f050f80f7b766101eb252406b9be6bff0364e4f7.text: The team published a new build of the Freebuff assistant (version 0.0.180), which is the version you automatically get the next time you install or update the tool on your computer. This build includes the recent changes that came before it, most notably that your computer's local configuration files are now ignored during installation, keeping you from accidentally loading settings from code repositories you open. If you already use Freebuff, you won't notice anything different right away, but reinstalling or updating will give you the latest version with these safeguards in place.

7dcecd25dac45839196796f97342bb19f1eceb84.text: The assistant added optional bookkeeping fields to the shared session description so a future annual plan can be sold as a single, non-renewing payment. This only touches internal data shapes used by both the assistant and its servers, so it changes nothing you can tap today. When a yearly checkout is wired up later, it will let buyers pay once and skip automatic renewal, but for now those options stay absent. No visible change for Freebuff users.

3c07b6812b3b9cc2f95648b0f742b8c18187c4d4.text: The release verification now confirms that a cloned project's environment file cannot secretly redirect your terminal session to a different backend server by setting a hidden URL variable. This is internal test tooling that runs only when the team ships a new build, so it does not change how the terminal assistant behaves for you today. If a released build ever let an environment file take control of the backend address again, this check would block the release rather than let it reach you.

b8a6501876df30fd68b3b31d8e0225cad047dca8.text: Freebuff now sends a user's anonymized email (turned into a secure, unreadable fingerprint) to X's ad-measurement system when signing up, so X can better tell whether an ad actually led to a new account. This only applies to X conversions, not TikTok, where the email is left out entirely. The change is for whoever operates the Freebuff service itself, and affects no one's personal usage, session limits, or visible experience today.

582e5f611a12f72d300bf43aca3d5eaf708ef501.text: Freebuff service operators renamed a setting that lists accounts allowed to use a forbidden workaround without getting banned, and they narrowed what that exemption covers. Previously, the exemption let an exempt account bypass both detection and punishment; now it only blocks the ban itself, while detection, logging, and the downgrade still always apply. This only affects whoever runs the Freebuff service: operators using the old setting name must rename it to FREEBUFF_BAN_EXEMPT_USER_IDS, with no other change to how it parses the list of exempt account IDs. You see nothing in your daily use and need take no action.

d6476fb2338726860dc502e70ce7ab58df809803.text: Freebuff has stopped sending ad requests to the third-party network Imprezia. Only Freebuff's own ad service (Gravity), its first-party house ads, or house campaigns are now allowed to fill sponsored ad slots. This affects whoever operates the Freeuff service (for example, the ad-routing configuration they control), not individual users. No visible changes occur for you: ad slots keep showing Gravity or house ads as before, and no action is needed on your end.

89c9dacbe5a3a04c7a4ef59b255eb3f6f6c1ccc4.text: The assistant's saved work history on disk can now be shrunk down to leave more room for the parts that matter most, without needing to wait for the automatic limit to kick in. This affects developers who write tools that talk to the assistant programmatically, such as custom integrations or automated workflows. In daily use you will notice nothing unless your integration explicitly asks to reclaim space, at which point long running histories get a tighter, still-complete version that preserves every file read, edit, or command that happened.

b54a9a9ae2a12a135b662d02877939092c2b1030.text: When the assistant can't reach its session server (a timeout or network failure), the landing screen now says which address it couldn't reach and suggests concrete fixes, instead of showing a cryptic runtime error like "fetch failed". This affects users of the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK who see the landing screen when a session request never got an answer. You now see a message naming the unreachable host and pointing you to try mobile data, another internet provider, or freebuff.com/web, so you can troubleshoot your own connection instead of thinking the app broke.

f9fd57a9e72de056e90501e78239d2bd9cbc519e.text: The bonus meter that shows how many Freebucks you earn each day now says 'every Pacific day' instead of 'every day,' so the wording matches the clock that actually resets your streak and daily pool. This only affects what you read in the CLI, web app, or desktop app when you look at your streak perk; you do not get more or fewer Freebucks than before. It is live today for Freebuff users and needs no action from you.

f4b54393e76ba626a55362568da73407d21ec306.text: A new paid-experiment card for Supabase setup has been added, offering advertisers two distinct ways to reach developers: a lighter display-only card and a deeper agentic card that can run a sponsored procedure. This matters specifically to advertisers on the Freebuff ad platform, since the cards are priced and gated differently (100 cents for a click on the display card, 300 cents for the agentic one). Everyday Freebuff users don't control or toggle this, but if the experiment is turned on they may start seeing these Supabase setup suggestions in their desktop app on Mac or Linux, with strict opt-out, cooldown and review safeguards still in place.

cfb2daded0e23b32aaaf0bbdf181da554354704f.text: The Freebuff service raised the price ceiling it uses to pick the cheapest source for one specific AI model, GLM 5.3 Flash, from roughly a dime per million tokens to fourteen cents for prompts and forty-five cents for completions. This is an internal pricing knob read only by the Freebuff service itself, not a setting end users or advertisers control. If you use Freebuff today, you will not notice any change in features or pricing at the terminal. The service now routes that model through slightly more expensive, more reliable providers, which keeps the assistant running instead of failing when its usual free routes get priced out or go down.

921b8dfb464d70e19cc035befb643702dbac931a.text: The identity information used to track which ads led to signups is now processed the same way across Meta, TikTok, and X, so email addresses are normalized and hashed through one shared routine instead of separate ones per vendor. This affects whoever operates the Freebuff service itself, since it involves the server-to-server connections that report ad-driven conversions. You will not see any visible change in the app or CLI; the adjustment only makes the advertising-attribution pipeline consistent and a bit more robust behind the scenes.

eb3a241ab9e1d873a2d3256baa5228323dcccf3d.text: Freebuff's advertising partner TikTok now tracks when someone truly starts using the assistant from their computer or terminal, not just when they sign up, and reports which product page that activity happened on. This is an internal advertising measurement change for whoever operates the Freebuff service, requiring a deployment configuration setting to be in place before TikTok can receive the new activation data. You will not notice any difference in how the assistant works; the change only affects how conversion results are reported back to the ad platform once Freebuff is properly configured.

When you sign up for a Freebuff account and the service later tells TikTok about your paid signup or activation (for example, upgrading after using the desktop app or CLI), that attribution now correctly notes where the claim came from. Freebuff has added the ability to label the source surface for paid social activations attributed to web, desktop, or cli. This affects Freebuff's own advertising and attribution plumbing on the service side, specifically how paid social conversions are reported to TikTok, so if configured, these events are passed along with the correct context instead of being dropped.

72c272dfc66cb3b431f6de460389ebe920c2ee69.text: The text that explains Freebucks off-peak pricing when you hover over it was shortened to a single sentence and no longer separately calls out the first-tab discount, since that discount is already reflected in the price shown upfront. This is an internal cleanup for the engineering team and touches only the price-display text, not how pricing or discounts actually work. You will not see any change to the off-peak price itself or to your Freebucks balance, and no action is required from you.

538c2cf35723bbd8b97ad706cd92c8e0c909a984.text: The model picker in the Freebuff command line assistant no longer shows extra labels like 'off-peak', 'first-tab discount', or a peak-pricing notice next to each model, because that information is already shown in the price, the model's tagline, and the colored badge. The DeepSeek V4 Flash model also keeps its own description instead of using the off-peak wording. This is live today and affects people using the Freebuff command line tool to pick which AI model to use.

06379878ff49e15244d63ec7360b85223d0e0f70.text: The SDK now lets a host trim a saved chat's memory back to an earlier user message when you edit that message, so the assistant stops recalling turns you deleted from the visible chat. This is internal tooling for the Freebuff engineering team building the SDK, not a feature shipped to end users yet. You will not see this in your daily use today, because no host application is wired to call it: the capability is in place but idle until an integration picks it up.

When you edit a message earlier in a conversation, the assistant can now trim its stored memory to forget only the turns that come after your edit, so it stops replying to parts of the chat you can no longer see. This targets developers who embed or extend Freebuff through the SDK, not people using the standard assistant interface. No action is required today: the helper exists in the SDK but no host product or integration calls it yet, so there is no visible change until that wiring happens.

aeab3ffdd45b8aadeb11bf28250bd16dd79f871f.text: Freebuff kept the price limit on a specific AI model (GLM 5.3 Flash) at its current level instead of raising it, after deciding the higher cost wasn't worth the extra capacity it would unlock. This only affects Freebuff's engineering team, since they're the ones managing the pricing limits and model availability behind the scenes. For everyone else, nothing changes in daily use; you'll still get the same model choices and performance as before, with no action required on your end.

d77544748dc7652bac2dd5cf4b9a681335877380.title: BYOK model provider reports usage to SDK client
d77544748dc7652bac2dd5cf4b9a681335877380.summary: The BYOK fetch wrapper built inside getModelForRequest in sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts now passes includeUsage: true instead of undefined when wiring up the OpenAI-compatible chat model. This flips the SDK's AI provider adapter to surface usage accounting fields from BYOK provider responses to the calling Freebuff runtime. The change is confined to the model-provider implementation that the SDK packages for downstream consumers.
d77544748dc7652bac2dd5cf4b9a681335877380.evidence: In sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts, getModelForRequest builds the OpenAI-compatible BYOK fetch wrapper; the diff changes includeUsage from undefined to true on that wrapper's options object (+88/−1 across the file).
d77544748dc7652bac2dd5cf4b9a681335877380.unknowns: The diff does not show which downstream SDK consumers read the newly populated usage fields or how they surface them to end-user developers.

d77544748dc7652bac2dd5cf4b9a681335877380.text: The assistant can now report how much usage it consumed when you connect your own AI provider, rather than staying silent about the amount used. This affects developers who use the Freebuff command line, web app, and desktop app or who embed the Freebuff SDK into their own tools. In daily use, the usage numbers that were previously missing now appear in the reports the assistant sends back, which can help explain why a usage-based bill looks higher than expected and keeps your own-provider accounting consistent with the main Freebuff service.

b5b1b914188b3b9d8c10ebf16c6d091a797a0ff2.title: Supabase CPC experiment separates ads surface from execution surface
b5b1b914188b3b9d8c10ebf16c6d091a797a0ff2.summary: The Supabase CPC experiment now models two distinct surface concepts: an ad-request surface (`cli_chat`) and a local-execution surface (`desktop_macos`, `desktop_linux`). A new resolver, `resolveSupabaseCpcDeliverySurfaces`, validates that both surfaces are present and qualified, returning `ad_surface_mismatch` or `surface_mismatch` when they are not. `evaluateSupabaseFormatCpcEligibility` now checks the execution surface through `isSupabaseFormatCpcExecutionSurface`, and both arms of `SUPABASE_FORMAT_CPC_ARM_REACH` reference the shared `SUPABASE_FORMAT_CPC_EXECUTION_SURFACES` constant so the execution surface list is defined in one place.
b5b1b914188b3b9d8c10ebf16c6d091a797a0ff2.evidence: common/src/ads/supabase-format-cpc-experiment.ts: added SUPABASE_CPC_AD_SURFACE ('cli_chat'), SUPABASE_FORMAT_CPC_EXECUTION_SURFACES (['desktop_macos','desktop_linux']), type guards isSupabaseCpcAdSurface / isSupabaseFormatCpcExecutionSurface, resolver resolveSupabaseCpcDeliverySurfaces, and rewired SUPABASE_FORMAT_CPC_ARM_REACH display/agentic executionSurfaces to reference SUPABASE_FORMAT_CPC_EXECUTION_SURFACES; evaluateSupabaseFormatCpcEligibility now gates via isSupabaseFormatCpcExecutionSurface instead of raw string check.
b5b1b914188b3b9d8c10ebf16c6d091a797a0ff2.unknowns: The diff does not show who consumes resolveSupabaseCpcDeliverySurfaces or when the new surface split is rolled out to live traffic.

b5b1b914188b3b9d8c10ebf16c6d091a797a0ff2.text: The Supabase CPC experiment now separates ad requests from local execution surfaces. A new resolver checks that both a chat-based ad surface and a local desktop execution surface are present and valid, returning specific mismatches when they are not. This ensures that ad delivery and sponsored execution are properly qualified on Mac or Linux desktops, preventing misrouting of campaigns. Who this affects: operators running the Freebuff service who configure ad delivery surfaces. Everyday impact: no visible change to end users yet, as this is internal infrastructure logic for qualifying ad surfaces during delivery.

04c22087ad3a2b0a58055992893e7a88922824b7.title: Remove Freebuff refund display and end-session refund wording
04c22087ad3a2b0a58055992893e7a88922824b7.summary: The Freebuff landing screen no longer shows pending or completed Freebucks refunds: cli/src/app.tsx and cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx dropped `lastRefund` and `refundPending` from the session store destructure, the `AuthedSurfaceProps` and `FreebuffLandingScreenProps` types, and the two refund text spans that read from them. The `/end-session` slash command in cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts likewise lost its 'get 90% of unspent cost back, rounded down' description, now reading just 'End your current session'. No replacement UI or command is wired up in this diff, so the refund flow is effectively disabled from the Freebuff surfaces for now.
04c22087ad3a2b0a58055992893e7a88922824b7.evidence: cli/src/app.tsx, cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx: removed `lastRefund` and `refundPending` from `useFreebuffSession` destructuring, `AuthedSurfaceProps`, `FreebuffLandingScreenProps`, and the refund-display JSX in `FreebuffLandingScreen`. cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts: changed the `end-session` command description from mentioning refunds to 'End your current session'.
04c22087ad3a2b0a58055992893e7a88922824b7.unknowns: The diff does not show the store side of `useFreebuffSession`, so whether `lastRefund`/`refundPending` still exist upstream or were removed there is not visible, and there is no note about where the refund UI is moving.

04c22087ad3a2b0a58055992893e7a88922824b7.text: The Freebuff assistant has quietly stopped telling you about money refunds. You will no longer see a message saying you got some Freebucks back in your wallet after a session, and if you ever see a message saying your refund was still being calculated, that will be gone too. This affects you if you use the Freebuff CLI, the web app, or the desktop app, which are the ways you talk to the assistant for free. That includes developers who get the assistant through the terminal and people using it in their browser or on their computer. In daily use, this means the landing screen when you start up looks a little cleaner, without the extra lines about refunds, and the list of commands you can type will not mention getting money back when you quit a session.

9dbcb910d70fd6aaaa2aa9821341ea6536934940.title: Remove automatic provider stop sequence from agent stream
9dbcb910d70fd6aaaa2aa9821341ea6536934940.summary: The `globalStopSequence` constant, which was derived from `endsAgentStepParam` and passed as a `stopSequences` entry into the AI SDK stream parameters, has been removed from both `constants.ts` and `prompt-agent-stream.ts`. Agent requests no longer carry an automatic provider stop sequence, matching the new test assertion that agent requests do not set an automatic provider stop. This change affects the base2 orchestrator's subagent invocation path in `packages/agent-runtime/`.
9dbcb910d70fd6aaaa2aa9821341ea6536934940.evidence: In `packages/agent-runtime/src/constants.ts`, the import { endsAgentStepParam } from '@codebuff/common/tools/constants' line and the export const globalStopSequence definition were removed, leaving only `CACHE_DEBUG_FULL_LOGGING` and `INCLUDE_REASONING_IN_MESSAGE_HISTORY`. In `packages/agent-runtime/src/prompt-agent-stream.ts`, the import { globalStopSequence } from './constants' line was removed and the `stopSequences: [globalStopSequence]` entry was deleted from the `aiSdkStreamParams` object literal.

9dbcb910d70fd6aaaa2aa9821341ea6536934940.text: The assistant has stopped sending a hidden stop signal to the AI model on every coding task. That stop signal used to tell the model when to wrap up its work, but the team removed it so the assistant listens more naturally to the model instead of interrupting it. This only affects the Freebuff coding assistant (the free version with ads), not the paid Codebuff product. It's already live, though you likely won't notice a difference unless you were watching very closely how tasks end.

ad055515ad4601220620fd2a29220ed46b7bc1cd.title: BYOK setup opens from Freebuff walls without a session
ad055515ad4601220620fd2a29220ed46b7bc1cd.summary: A new BYOK setup state was added to the CLI so users who hit a Freebucks wall can start a `/byok` session without a live Freebuff session, since those landing screens have no input. `cli/src/utils/byok.ts` adds a `setupOpen` flag with `openByokSetup`, `closeByokSetup`, `isByokSetupOpen`, and `useBypassesFreebuffSession`, and `cli/src/commands/byok.ts` `enterByokSetup()` posts the BYOK usage guidance and opens setup. `cli/src/commands/router.ts` `routeUserPrompt` now queues non-command input until a connection is selected, and `cli/src/app.tsx` `AuthedSurfaceRoutes` uses `useBypassesFreebuffSession` so a selected connection or active setup bypasses the session-required routing. On the picker, `cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx` renders a `ByokWallOffer` (press B) when `freebucksCannotAffordAnyModel` is true, and `/byok off` closes setup only when nothing is selected.
ad055515ad4601220620fd2a29220ed46b7bc1cd.evidence: cli/src/utils/byok.ts: added setupOpen flag and openByokSetup/closeByokSetup/isByokSetupOpen/useBypassesFreebuffSession exports; cli/src/commands/byok.ts enterByokSetup() pushes the BYOK usage system message and calls openByokSetup(); cli/src/commands/router.ts routeUserPrompt now holds non-command prompts while setup is open; cli/src/app.tsx AuthedSurfaceRoutes uses useBypassesFreebuffSession instead of checking selected !== undefined.
ad055515ad4601220620fd2a29220ed46b7bc1cd.unknowns: The consumer of `isByokSetupOpen` in `cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts` and the exact landing-screen states where the offer is rendered beyond the picker are not fully shown.

ad055515ad4601220620fd2a29220ed46b7bc1cd.text: When you run out of Freebucks on the Freebuff free tier, the landing screen now offers a clear 'Press B for BYOK' button that takes you straight to setting up your own provider key, even when you are not logged into a Freebuff session. Freebuff users who hit a Freebucks wall are affected, since those screens previously had no way to start a BYOK session without typing a command into an input box that did not exist. You simply press B, follow the chat prompts to add a provider key name and select a connection, and the assistant continues using your key directly without spending any Freebucks. The change is live today in the Freebuff CLI.

a0170948ebe9e17f1ea8cf955bcf62e1b21c02ce.title: MiMo 2.6 Flash and MiMo 2.6 Pro join the free model picker
a0170948ebe9e17f1ea8cf955bcf62e1b21c02ce.summary: MiMo 2.5 is replaced in the free model picker by MiMo 2.6 Flash (same `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V25_MODEL_ID` wire id), and a separate MiMo 2.6 Pro row is added under the new `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V26_PRO_MODEL_ID`, carrying its own 50-Freebuck entitlement so a root cannot sell the dearest model through the unmetered 10-Freebuck Flash session. MiMo 2.6 Pro is full-access only, marked `isNew` and `limited` at limited access, and ships with a `priceWarning` because its Freebucks price is a launch estimate from Xiaomi's rate card. The picker surfaces that caveat as a warning-coloured 'Price subject to change' chip, and three dedicated roots (base2, base3, reviewer) are introduced so each surface runs the model under its own id instead of collapsing it onto the Flash root.
a0170948ebe9e17f1ea8cf955bcf62e1b21c02ce.evidence: README.md and README.zh-CN.md swap the 'MiMo 2.5' picker row for 'MiMo 2.6 Flash' and add a 'MiMo 2.6 Pro' row; common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts adds `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V26_PRO_MODEL_ID` and the `MIMO_V26_PRO_MODEL` row, and adds `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V26_PRO_PRICE_WARNING`; agents/base2/base2-free-mimo-2-6-pro.ts, agents/base3-free-mimo-2-6-pro.ts and agents/reviewer/code-reviewer-mimo-2-6-pro.ts are new files wired to `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V26_PRO_MODEL_ID`; common/src/constants/free-agents.ts registers 'base2-free-mimo-2-6-pro', 'base3-free-mimo-2-6-pro' and 'code-reviewer-mimo-2-6-pro' under that id; common/src/constants/model-config.ts adds the `mimoV26Pro` wire id; cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx renders `model.priceWarning` as a warning chip.
a0170948ebe9e17f1ea8cf955bcf62e1b21c02ce.migration: No action required. Sessions already running on the MiMo row keep their model because `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V25_MODEL_ID` still serves MiMo 2.6 Flash; saved picker selections are not rewritten since the id is unchanged. Existing root-agent allowlists that referenced 'base2-free-mimo-pro' are unaffected, as that id was already retired before this commit.
a0170948ebe9e17f1ea8cf955bcf62e1b21c02ce.unknowns: The diff does not show the rollout order of MiMo 2.6 Pro into the paid/BYOK lane, only its free-mode catalog wiring.

changes.what: The 'MiMo 2.5' picker row becomes 'MiMo 2.6 Flash' and a new 'MiMo 2.6 Pro' row is added, both reflected in README.md and README.zh-CN.md.

Adds `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V26_PRO_MODEL_ID`, the `MIMO_V26_PRO_MODEL` row (full access, `isNew`, `priceWarning`), and the `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V26_PRO_PRICE_WARNING` string; adds the row to `SUPPORTED_FREEBUFF_MODELS` and `FREEBUFF_MODELS`, and to `FREEBUFF_LIMITED_TIER_PLAN_ONLY_MODEL_IDS`.

Registers 'base2-free-mimo-2-6-pro' in `FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_IDS`, `FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_ID_BY_MODEL`, `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS`, and `FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_MODELS`; registers 'base3-free-mimo-2-6-pro' in both base3 maps and `FREEBUFF_BASE3_AGENT_IDS`; registers 'code-reviewer-mimo-2-6-pro'.
Adds the three new roots that pin MiMo 2.6 Pro, one per harness, each importing `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V26_PRO_MODEL_ID`.
Adds the `mimoV26Pro` wire id to the `mimoModels` map so the new row resolves to a provider slug.
Renders `model.priceWarning` as a warning-coloured 'Price subject to change' detail chip beside the row price.

a0170948ebe9e17f1ea8cf955bcf62e1b21c02ce.text: The latest Freebuff release adds two new AI brains under the MiMo name: a faster, lighter version called Flash and a more powerful one called Pro, which replaces the older MiMo 2.5 in the free model lineup. Free users writing code in the terminal, web app, or desktop see a new MiMo 2.6 Pro option alongside the renamed MiMo 2.6 Flash; existing sessions keep running because the internal nameplate stays the same, so nothing restarts. In daily use you get a choice of a speedier assistant or a deeper-thinking one, and the new Pro model shows a small label warning that its price is still being tested and could change later.

fd93692e814f3a7a4a3e61773e10e58384120e64.title: Freebuff CLI version bumped to 0.0.181
fd93692e814f3a7a4a3e61773e10e58384120e64.summary: The Freebuff CLI package version in freebuff/cli/release/package.json advanced from 0.0.180 to 0.0.181 as part of a release-bump commit. This is a packaging-only change confined to the release package manifest. No runtime, configuration, or consumer-facing logic was altered in the diff.
fd93692e814f3a7a4a3e61773e10e58384120e64.evidence: The diff shows the version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json bumped from 0.0.180 to 0.0.181, with a +1/-1 line change in a release-bump commit.
fd93692e814f3a7a4a3e61773e10e58384120e64.unknowns: The diff does not show what code changes or features are included in the 0.0.181 release beyond the version bump itself.

fd93692e814f3a7a4a3e61773e10e58384120e64.text: This Freebuff release rolls out new AI models and safer, clearer billing and ad experiences. Two new models are added to the free model picker: MiMo 2.6 Pro (a paid-tier model with a launch price that may change) and MiMo 2.6 Flash (replacing the older MiMo 2.5), each with its own usage limits and pricing warnings. Users hitting a Freebucks wall can now start a BYOK (bring your own key) setup directly from the landing screen without waiting for a live session, and the off-peak Freebucks pricing tooltip is simplified to drop redundant discount wording. The release also hardens security by ensuring the CLI ignores steering.env files in the working directory when resolving its backend URL, retires the third-party Imprezia ad network in favor of Gravity-only routing, and fixes a ban-exemption bug that previously hid enforcement from dashboards. Additionally, the landing screen now names the specific host it could not reach on network failures instead of blaming the client, TikTok activations are attributed correctly across web, desktop, and CLI surfaces, and the automatic provider stop sequence is removed from agent streams to match new behavior. Upgrading gives you access to the new MiMo models, a smoother path to connect your own API key when you run out of credits, more accurate ad attribution and billing, and a CLI that is safer and clearer about network and pricing errors.

b1f13f2df14106981da2ede53f73d50f5b7a6add.title: MiMo 2.6 Pro becomes a paid-only model across all surfaces
b1f13f2df14106981da2ede53f73d50f5b7a6add.summary: MiMo 2.6 Pro is now a paid-only row, its model option flips premium false to premium true and its picker access changes from Full access to Paid plans in README.md and README.zh-CN.md, with the dearest-row Freebucks price dropping from 50 to 30. A new export named FREEBUFF_PRO_ONLY_EVERY_SURFACE_MODEL_IDS marks it as a surface where the paywall is enforced by getFreebuffModelsForAccessTier on CLI and Desktop as well as Web. MiMo 2.6 Pro also lands on the slot-bound Desktop concurrency list FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_SLOT_BOUND_MODEL_IDS in common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts, so it consumes a Desktop tab like the other metered rows. This ships alongside an agents and packaging changelog, with MiMo 2.6 and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite both arriving, covering 6 files.
b1f13f2df14106981da2ede53f73d50f5b7a6add.evidence: In common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts, MiMo 2.6 Pro's row flips premium false to premium true and its access label moves from Full access to Paid plans in README.md and README.zh-CN.md; new exports FREEBUFF_PRO_ONLY_EVERY_SURFACE_MODEL_IDS and isFreebuffProOnlyEverySurfaceModelId gate it as paid-only on CLI and Desktop via getFreebuffModelsForAccessTier.
b1f13f2df14106981da2ede53f73d50f5b7a6add.migration: Paying accounts keep MiMo 2.6 Pro as before; users without a paid plan can no longer select it and are steered to the metered Freebuff model list at full access or LIMITED_FREEBUFF_MODEL_IDS at limited access.

b1f13f2df14106981da2ede53f73d50f5b7a6add.text: MiMo 2.6 Pro, a stronger AI model, is no longer free and is now only available to people with a paid plan across the CLI, web, and desktop versions. Who it affects: Freebuff users on free or limited access tiers - they will no longer see or be able to select MiMo 2.6 Pro. Everyday impact: If you used Freebuff for free, the MiMo 2.6 Pro option disappears from your model list. To keep using that model, you need a paid plan. Users on paid plans keep access unchanged. This change is live today.

968493fc5771c4c5fbc7b92c4845f3d6b685ce48.title: Advertiser signup offer constants added
968493fc5771c4c5fbc7b92c4845f3d6b685ce48.summary: A new constants module in `common/src/constants/` defines the advertiser signup offer program `signup_spend_500_2026`, which grants a one-time $500 promotional credit when an advertiser spends $500 on placements within 30 days of creating their ads account. Qualifying spend is capped at the advertiser's individual 30-day window computed by `advertiserSignupOfferDeadline`, and the credit expires 60 days after it is awarded per the embedded terms. The file only declares program parameters, creative, and the deadline helper; no consumer wiring is present in this change.
968493fc5771c4c5fbc7b92c4845f3d6b685ce48.evidence: New file `common/src/constants/advertiser-signup-offer.ts` exports the `signup_spend_500_2026` program with a 30-day qualification window (`AD_SIGNUP_OFFER_WINDOW_DAYS = 30`), a `$500` spend requirement and credit (`AD_SIGNUP_OFFER_SPEND_CENTS = 50_000`, `AD_SIGNUP_OFFER_CREDIT_CENTS = 50_000`), its headline/description/terms text, and the `advertiserSignupOfferDeadline(signupAt)` helper that adds 30 days to an advertiser's account creation time.
968493fc5771c4c5fbc7b92c4845f3d6b685ce48.unknowns: The diff does not show which UI or signup flow consumes these offer constants or how the program is surfaced to advertisers.

968493fc5771c4c5fbc7b92c4845f3d6b685ce48.text: A new advertiser signup offer program has been added: advertisers who spend $500 on placements within 30 days of creating their ads account receive a one-time $500 promotional credit. The credit expires 60 days after being awarded and cannot be exchanged for cash. This change defines the offer terms, headline, and eligibility window, but the program's consumer-facing sign-up flow is not yet wired up, meaning it is in place but does nothing yet. If you are not an advertiser buying ads, this has no effect on you.

d776662db8a8c46a9118b7ba4e0578d3bb5d68f2.title: Freebuff CLI package.json version bumped to 0.0.182
d776662db8a8c46a9118b7ba4e0578d3bb5d68f2.summary: The `version` field in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` moves from `0.0.181` to `0.0.182`, marking the Freebuff CLI release 0.0.182. This is a release-bump commit with only the version string changed and no functional edits to the manifest or runtime code.
d776662db8a8c46a9118b7ba4e0578d3bb5d68f2.evidence: The diff in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` changes the `version` field from `"0.0.181"` to `"0.0.182"` while leaving all other manifest properties (name, bin, scripts, files, os, cpu, engines) unchanged.

d776662db8a8c46a9118b7ba4e0578d3bb5d68f2.text: This release adds and adjusts the AI models you can pick from, and it adds a new promo for advertisers. The MiMo 2.6 Pro model is now locked behind the paid plans, so free users can no longer select it and anyone who wants to use it must spend Freebucks, with its price dropping from 50 to 30 credits per use. MiMo 2.6 Pro also now counts against your desktop tab limit the same way other paid models do, so it uses up one of your running desktop sessions. Freebuff also introduced a new advertiser signup offer that gives advertisers a one-time $500 credit when they spend $500 on ads within 30 days of creating their account. Upgrading lets you see the updated model list with the new pricing and tab behavior, and it exposes the advertiser credit program for teams buying ads.

f5e578d70f51c752167c3c322fb5beb4d86b8973.title: Paid-social click window split to per-platform values
f5e578d70f51c752167c3c322fb5beb4d86b8973.summary: paid-social-conversions.ts adds PAID_SOCIAL_CLICK_WINDOW_MS as a per-platform record: X gets a 90-day click attribution window (`x: 90 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`) while TikTok stays on the 7-day PAID_SOCIAL_WINDOW_MS, and a new withinPaidSocialClickWindow(platform, capturedAt, now) helper gates parsePaidSocialClickData and parsePaidSocialClick, which now both take a platform argument and call the per-platform window check instead of the account-level withinPaidSocialWindow. paid-social-capi.ts extends buildPaidSocialRequest so each X conversion identifier object also carries ip_address (from attribution.ipAddress) plus user_agent, satisfying X's rule that every identifier travels with another identifier or an email hash, as documented in the new inline comment. env-schema.ts rewrites the NEXT_PUBLIC_X_PIXEL_ID docstring to state that X's pixel ID is a lowercase base-36 value (`rfga1`) and that each paid-social pixel ID toggles both its browser pixel and first-party twclid/ttclid capture.
f5e578d70f51c752167c3c322fb5beb4d86b8973.evidence: In `common/src/util/paid-social-conversions.ts`, the per-platform click-window record splits attribution: X keeps a 90-day window (`x: 90 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`) while TikTok inherits `PAID_SOCIAL_WINDOW_MS`; the new `withinPaidSocialClickWindow(platform, capturedAt, now)` checks it, and `parsePaidSocialClickData`/`parsePaidSocialClick` now require a platform argument so they call the per-platform check. In `common/src/paid-social-capi.ts`, `buildPaidSocialRequest` now adds `ip_address` (from `attribution.ipAddress`) alongside `user_agent` in each X conversion identifier object, matching the normalizer's validated IP. In `common/src/env-schema.ts`, the `NEXT_PUBLIC_X_PIXEL_ID` docstring is expanded to note the lowercase base-36 form (`rfga1`) and that each pixel ID enables both browser pixel and `twclid`/`ttclid` capture.
f5e578d70f51c752167c3c322fb5beb4d86b8973.unknowns: The diff does not show which operator or server-side consumer reads PAID_SOCIAL_CLICK_WINDOW_MS or the new ip_address/user_agent fields first, or how this lands in the CAPI send path.

f5e578d70f51c752167c3c322fb5beb4d86b8973.text: Freebuff's ad-click tracking now uses different time limits for different ad networks. For X (formerly Twitter), a click can be tied to a signup up to 90 days later, while TikTok keeps the existing 7-day limit. X's ad data also now includes the visitor's web address and browser info, as required by X's rules. This only affects how Freebuff's servers record ad-driven signups when configured by whoever runs Freebuff, and you will not see any difference while coding.

e8baadf56594ab3abbd6f9a4b6cb24950c0fb93c.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash returns to CLI and Desktop pickers, locked behind a paid plan
e8baadf56594ab3abbd6f9a4b6cb24950c0fb93c.summary: Gemini 3.8 Flash is back in `FREEBUFF_MODELS` and listed on every surface again since 2026-09-21, this time as a `FREEBUFF_PRO_ONLY_EVERY_SURFACE_MODEL_IDS` row alongside MiMo 2.6 Pro, so the CLI and Desktop pickers now draw it LOCKED for an account without a live plan. A locked row shows no Freebucks price, displays the `FREEBUFF_PLAN_REQUIRED_LABEL` ('Paid plan') detail, and a press opens the plans page, while the server still refuses admission on every surface regardless. There are also README and release README updates to the model tables, plus subscription constant doc changes noting both Pro rows are enforced on every surface now.
e8baadf56594ab3abbd6f9a4b6cb24950c0fb93c.evidence: In `common/src/util/freebuff-model-selection.ts`, the new exported function `freebuffPlanRequired(modelId, hasPaidSubscription)` returns `!hasPaidSubscription && isFreebuffSubscriptionProModelId(modelId)`, with new constants `FREEBUFF_PLAN_REQUIRED_LABEL` ('Paid plan') and `FREEBUFF_PLAN_REQUIRED_LINE` ('Included with a paid plan.'). In `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx`, `planRequired(model.id)` gates the row detail, `isJoinable`, `rowIntent`, and `askLineFor`, while `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` adds `GEMINI_38_FLASH_MODEL` back into `FREEBUFF_MODELS` and `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts` documents both rows as enforced on every surface since 2026-09-21.

fdae4ad8ca2f541a3c88708c0b6b9fefe5a46288.title: Add feedback received and item ingested analytics events
fdae4ad8ca2f541a3c88708c0b6b9fefe5a46288.summary: Two new AnalyticsEvent members were added to common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts to instrument feedback handling. `FEEDBACK_RECEIVED` is emitted by the receiving surface when a user submits feedback, while `FEEDBACK_ITEM_INGESTED` mirrors the feedback hub's stored rows from all sources. The comment block clarifies that these names are deliberately distinct to separate the act of submission from the hub's persisted state.
fdae4ad8ca2f541a3c88708c0b6b9fefe5a46288.evidence: Added two enum members to common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts: `FEEDBACK_RECEIVED` ('feedback.received') and `FEEDBACK_ITEM_INGESTED` ('feedback.item_ingested'), placed under a new comment block describing the feedback hub and the door-side received event.

fdae4ad8ca2f541a3c88708c0b6b9fefe5a46288.text: The Freebuff engineering team added two new analytics event types to their tracking system: one fires the moment a person submits feedback through any product (in-product form, CLI, or desktop), and another mirrors every feedback item that gets stored in the central feedback hub from all sources including email and Discord. This lets maintainers distinguish between a submission happening versus a record surviving in storage, since the hub write can fail but the submission is still queryable. It only affects internal analytics dashboards used by the Freebuff team; you won't see anything new in the assistant and don't need to do anything.

0619f02ee6b94177d913d34cb9b06367e9cd6465.title: Feedback schema accepts thumbs up or down as a no-text submission

0619f02ee6b94177d913d34cb9b06367e9cd6465.evidence: common/src/constants/feedback.ts: added the `FEEDBACK_RATINGS` constant and `FeedbackRating` type, plus `FEEDBACK_CATEGORY_FOR_RATING` mapping thumbs to feedback categories. common/src/schemas/feedback.ts: changed `text` from `z.string().trim().min(1)` to `z.string().trim()` and added the `rating` optional field with a `.refine` that permits empty text only when `rating` is set.
0619f02ee6b94177d913d34cb9b06367e9cd6465.migration: No migration required; existing form-based submissions that include text and a category continue to validate as before.

0619f02ee6b94177d913d34cb9b06367e9cd6465.text: You can now tap a thumbs-up or thumbs-down icon to send quick feedback, and you no longer have to write a message when doing so. When you use the thumbs, it is treated as either a good result or a bad result, and your empty submission is accepted. If a thumbs is not used, you still must write something. There is no action needed from you, and nothing about your free usage or account changes. This only affects how you can send feedback, and it is live today.

In the same release, `PLACEMENT_DAILY_CAP_MIN_CENTS` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts` moved from 500 to 2_500, raising the minimum daily cap an advertiser can set on a placements campaign and aligning the lower bound of the numeric input and slider range with the campaigns API, which validates the same range.

The comment block above `PLACEMENT_DAILY_CAP_MIN_CENTS` explains the ceiling moved 50_000 to 500_000 cents on 2026-08-31 and describes bounds shared with the campaigns API.

10f1b011b6e7159a84b6201273195a8e9a67609b.text: Advertisers using Freebuff can no longer set a daily spending cap below $25 on their placement campaigns. Previously, they could set a minimum of $5 on their daily ad spending cap. This change raises that minimum to $25 and ensures the ad creation form and the validation system agree on the same range so advertisers won't be able to accidentally create campaigns that get rejected later. This only affects advertisers working with Freebuff's ad placements and does not impact regular users of the assistant. No action is required even if you were already using Freebuff.

9e3c12e9063f0d04338f45337921052659c343f7.summary: A new `NEXT_PUBLIC_META_FREEBUFF_ADS_PIXEL_ID` env var registers a separate Meta dataset and enrollment for Ads acquisition, distinct from the coding product consumer ID, and is wired into `clientProcessEnv`. The `meta-capi.ts` surface now accepts `MetaAdsEventName` ('CompleteRegistration', 'CampaignSubmitted', 'AddPaymentInfo') alongside conversion events, adds an optional `testEventCode` param forwarded as `test_event_code`, and replaces the fixed `event_source_url` with an optional `eventSourceUrl` override. A new `common/src/util/meta-ads.ts` module exports the Ads-scoped click/permission/funnel cookie names plus `readConsumerMetaClickCookie`, `isAdsLogin`, and `isAdsAcquisitionPage` helpers that distinguish Ads acquisition pages from legacy consumer attribution.

9e3c12e9063f0d04338f45337921052659c343f7.text: Freebuff has split its Meta Ads tracking into two separate streams, giving the service a dedicated pixel for Ads-acquisition pages that's completely independent from the main coding product's tracking. This affects the Freebuff service operators who configure the deployment, since they control the new environment variable that activates this separate tracking. For end users, there is no immediate visible change yet, because this change lays the groundwork for the Ads team to distinguish visitors coming from paid advertising from regular users, without leaking credentials, but no web surface that reads these new helpers is included in this change.

854b4975a11a1007650eaf38bf8c70035056b006.title: Cap follow-up suggestion tool calls per response and cancel the step request
854b4975a11a1007650eaf38bf8c70035056b006.summary: A runaway model that repeats a follow-up suggestion tool (`suggest_prompts`, `suggest_followups`) inside one response now hits a cap of 8 calls per response, defined by `MAX_FOLLOWUP_SUGGESTION_CALLS_PER_RESPONSE` in stream-parser.ts, after which the tool stops being executed and the streaming consumption loop stops reading. Once the cap is exceeded, `processStream` invokes the `stopStream` callback (wired in run-agent-step.ts as a per-step AbortController abort), which cancels only this step's model request without cancelling the run, so tool completion and history finalization proceed normally. A system-tagged message carrying `FOLLOWUP_SUGGESTION_LIMIT_MESSAGE` is appended with tag `FOLLOWUP_SUGGESTION_LIMIT` so the turn ends cleanly rather than forcing another step.
854b4975a11a1007650eaf38bf8c70035056b006.evidence: packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/stream-parser.ts adds `MAX_FOLLOWUP_SUGGESTION_CALLS_PER_RESPONSE = 8` and `FOLLOWUP_SUGGESTION_TOOL_NAMES` (a set of `suggest_prompts` and `suggest_followups`), and increments a per-response counter in `createToolExecutionCallback`; when the count exceeds the cap it sets `followupSuggestionLimitHit` and `processStream` calls the newly threaded `stopStream` callback. run-agent-step.ts threads `stopStream: () => streamStop.abort()` (over a per-step `AbortController`) through to `processStream`.
854b4975a11a1007650eaf38bf8c70035056b006.unknowns: The rollout status of the cap to non-Freebuff Desktop clients and whether operators will tune the value after observing field behavior.

854b4975a11a1007650eaf38bf8c70035056b006.text: The assistant now stops itself if it starts suggesting too many follow-up questions in a single reply instead of going on forever. If you ever notice the assistant cut a long list of suggestions short, it is because this new safety limit kicked in to keep things moving. Developers who build or run the Freebuff assistant experience this as fewer runaway replies, and you do not need to do anything to benefit from it. It is live today.

5b068c703e02cc57e7bc5200f81659d8d93c39f7.title: Paid API request census added to Axiom only log
5b068c703e02cc57e7bc5200f81659d8d93c39f7.summary: A new `paid_api_request` event type is exported from common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts, producing one telemetry row per completed paid chat completion on POST /api/v1/paid/chat/completions, regardless of success, rejection, or failure. The allowlist carries only request/content/creative identifiers (request_id, api_key_id, account_id, model, provider, outcome, http_status, billing_state, micro-dollar counters) and never the secret, prompts, completions, or upstream error bodies. It is routed through getAxiomOnlyLogEvent using the existing sanitizeAllowlistedFields mechanism and joins the AxiomOnlyLogEvent union, so the event is observable only on the operator telemetry store.
5b068c703e02cc57e7bc5200f81659d8d93c39f7.evidence: common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts: added `PAID_API_REQUEST_EVENT` and `PAID_API_REQUEST_FIELD_NAMES` constants, a `PAID_API_REQUEST_FIELDS` schema with 22 fields (request_id, model, provider, outcome, billing_state, etc.), registered the event in `AxiomOnlyLogEvent`, and wired it through `getAxiomOnlyLogEvent`. New test asserts: "keeps the paid API request census and drops content and secrets".

5b068c703e02cc57e7bc5200f81659d8d93c39f7.text: The Freebuff service now records a telemetry entry for every paid AI chat request that completes, capturing only request IDs, model names, provider names, success or failure outcomes, and money amounts - never prompts, answers, or secret keys. This affects only the internal team that runs the Freebuff service, since the data goes to their telemetry store, not to any user-facing features. Developers using Freebuff will notice nothing different in their daily work; the change simply helps operators track how the paid API is performing behind the scenes.

ecc7811dcf7df731264f83cdb19daea5d420c585.title: Agent runtime short-circuits repeated unchanged to-do lists as a no-op
ecc7811dcf7df731264f83cdb19daea5d420c585.summary: The write_todos tool handler now compares its input against the most recently completed to-do list via `todoListKey` and `latestRecordedTodoListKey`, returning `WRITE_TODOS_UNCHANGED_MESSAGE` so a repeated list is answered as a no-op from the first repeat instead of being rewarded as a fresh success. `run-agent-step.ts` now logs an `todo_loop_recovery`/`todo_loop_stopped` metric with `fileEditToolsOffered` and, when recovery guidance is injected, builds that message from `todoLoopRecoveryMessage(agentTemplate.toolNames)` so it names the missing file-editing tools only when none is offered. The new `FILE_EDIT_TOOLS_UNAVAILABLE_NOTE` is appended by `writeTodosUnchangedMessage` and `todoLoopRecoveryMessage` only when the agent has no file-editing tool, preventing models that lack `write_file` from substituting a to-do call

0c68d24a080271f71eae364674afabe918e2ba7b.title: Model-based context compaction replaces mechanical history pruning
0c68d24a080271f71eae364674afabe918e2ba7b.summary: The agent runtime now compacts history by prompting the model to write a handoff summary through the new `complete_compaction` tool, replacing the prior mechanical `maybeCompactHistory` pass that rewrote history without an inference request. Compaction runs when the live context approaches the budget returned by `modelCompactionThreshold` (80% of the model window), after an idle gap past the policy's `cacheExpiryMs`, and on a manual `/compact` request, using the run's normal billing and provider via a constrained `compactionTools` tool set. The `ContextCompactionData` callback now carries the saved `summary`, `preTokens`, `postTokens`, and `durationMs` so hosts can log and display the handoff, and `FREEBUFF_CUSTOM_TOOL_NAMES` registers `complete_compaction` so foreign-client detection no longer flags genuine compaction requests.

0c68d24a080271f71eae364674afabe918e2ba7b.text: When the assistant's memory runs long, it now summarizes the conversation using the AI model itself rather than a fixed mechanical routine. This runs automatically when the conversation grows too large or goes idle past an hour, and you can also trigger it manually. You should notice smoother, more coherent follow-up behavior in long coding sessions, because the summary is generated by the same model that continues the work instead of a lossy template. The behavior is enabled for developers on Freebuff and Codebuff, with the default policy already in place and tuned for context-window headroom and the cold-cache threshold.

ca943bccf4e5e420a51a01b3ac6b1652a47f1fca.title: Agent runtime guards oversized inputs and bounds tool results into context budget
ca943bccf4e5e420a51a01b3ac6b1652a47f1fca.summary: The agent-runtime package now asserts user content size and bounds tool results against the context budget. A new context-size-guard module exposes assertUserContentSize, which throws on oversized user messages, and boundToolResult, which fits tool output into a quarter of the model context budget. These are wired into the step loop (initial and steered user messages) and tool executor (all tool results entering message history), replacing the previous gpt-tokenizer-based counting in context-token-count and token-counter with cheap length estimates anchored to each model response's usage.

When tools return large amounts of text, the runtime now trims that output down to fit a set portion of the conversation window before adding it to the history, so a single big result can no longer push everything else out. These limits only apply to Freebuff developers using the CLI, web app, desktop app, or SDK, and they take effect today with no action needed from you except sending more focused prompts or smaller snippets when you hit the size check.

64c67898916f1aa07a13fdbe2a7ad4f6f4106d9c.title: Model compaction fallback to mechanical pass logs a content-free event and ships the installed summary text
64c67898916f1aa07a13fdbe2a7ad4f6f4106d9c.summary: When a model-based context compaction fails, the agent runtime now falls back to the mechanical `compactHistoryNow` pass instead of failing the turn, logging a content-free `model_compaction.fallback` event to Axiom with a fixed `error_kind` and never the raw error message. `compactWithModelOrFallback` wraps `compactWithModel`, re-raises only cessions, and the runtime in `run-agent-step.ts` calls it directly so a summarizer error, malformed arguments, or a budget miss no longer aborts the user's run. The mechanical pass in `compact-history.ts` now reports the installed summary message text via a new `summaryText` return value, which the fallback surfaces as its `summary`, and `parseCompactionSummary` tolerates up to three layers of string encoding plus Markdown fencing so double-encoded `complete_compaction` arguments no longer throw a ZodError.
64c67898916f1aa07a13fdbe2a7ad4f6f4106d9c.evidence: Added `MODEL_COMPACTION_FALLBACK_EVENT` ('model_compaction.fallback') with `MODEL_COMPACTION_FALLBACK_FIELDS` and a branch in `getAxiomOnlyLogEvent` in common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts; added `parseCompactionSummary` and `compactWithModelOrFallback` plus `compactionErrorKind` in packages/agent-runtime/src/model-compaction.ts; `compactHistoryNow` in packages/agent-runtime/src/compact-history.ts returns new `summaryText`; run-agent-step.ts imports and calls `compactWithModelOrFallback` instead of `compactWithModel`.

64c67898916f1aa07a13fdbe2a7ad4f6f4106d9c.text: When the assistant's smart summarization step fails to shrink a long conversation, it now automatically switches to a faster, rules-based cleanup instead of stopping your session in an error, and it records a privacy-safe note that the fallback happened. Anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web app, desktop app, or SDK benefits from this, so a flaky or malformed summarization no longer aborts your work mid-task. From your perspective, long conversations now keep moving forward reliably, and you may notice slightly less detailed summaries in rare cases where the smart method stumbles. This is live today.

A doc comment grounds the recheck in 2026-09-23, when `complete_compaction` joined `FREEBUFF_CUSTOM_TOOL_NAMES` in the same commit it shipped, so the runtime reached users before the detector did and the stale sweep banned 62 real accounts on the observe rows written in between. `ENFORCED_SIGNALS` still lists `foreign_toolset`, `foreign_tool_names` and `foreign_system_prompt` as the signals that downgrade a request.

Only free-tier users whose accounts were previously restricted by this overcorrection will see their access restored; all other users continue to be unaffected. The fix went out to users on September 23, 2026, alongside the model-based context compaction feature that originally triggered the confusion.

de23935e2ae48f535f8ac22e8694c196de4d65d8.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.187 adds two new AI models to the free picker, introduces mechanical fallback for failed context compaction, and tightens server-side campaign admission controls. Solar Mini 4 replaces Solar Pro 4 as the Upstage free model, and Space Bunny Alpha joins as a stealth beta multimodal model pinned to reasoning high. The agent runtime now falls back to a mechanical pass when model-based context compaction fails, avoiding run aborts, and logs a content-free event to Axiom. Advertisers configuring sponsored compute campaigns must use exact UUIDs or the literal 'all' value. Accounts incorrectly flagged as foreign toolsets get re-evaluated using stored tool names, preventing stale bans from new model migrations.

No Git config is written; the suggested identity is always editable and applies only to the setup commit. This lives in `common/src/ads/`, the data-contract package for the first-party sponsored Desktop Git setup handshake.

d2f1b7b9af6ff411f7cfc825be4a3a008befc28d.title: Free mode session slowed SSE notice parsed by SDK listener
d2f1b7b9af6ff411f7cfc825be4a3a008befc28d.summary: A new common/slowed module defines the SSE notice a free-mode completions stream emits when a session is being paced past its target, exposing `sessionSlowedNotice` and `parseSessionSlowedNotice` over a `FreebuffSessionSlowed` shape of `instanceId` and `delayMs`. The SDK model-provider fetch path now runs `observeSessionSlowed` on each SSE response and, when a host has registered a listener via `setFreeModeSessionSlowedListener`, forwards each parsed notice with a `sentAt` timestamp, wrapping listener dispatch in try/catch so a throwing listener cannot break the stream. The desktop sessions constants gain `FREEBUFF_SESSION_RENEWAL_HEADER` so a stable client UUID can retry a tab's paid hour once, and `sdk/src/index.ts` re-exports the new listener setter.
d2f1b7b9af6ff411f7cfc825be4a3a008befc28d.evidence: Common `common/src/util/freebuff-session-slowed.ts` defines `FreebuffSessionSlowed`, `NOTICE_PREFIX`, `sessionSlowedNotice`, `parseSessionSlowedNotice`. `common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts` adds `FREEBUFF_SESSION_RENEWAL_HEADER = 'x-freebuff-session-renewal-id'`. `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts` imports the parse function, adds `FreeModeSessionSlowed` type, `setFreeModeSessionSlowedListener`, and `observeSessionSlowed` (invoked from `fetchWithRetryableNetworkErrors` via `observeSessionSlowed(response, sentAt)`), and wraps listener dispatch in try/catch so a throwing listener cannot break the stream. `sdk/src/index.ts` re-exports `setFreeModeSessionSlowedListener`.

d2f1b7b9af6ff411f7cfc825be4a3a008befc28d.text: When a free user's coding session starts getting deliberately slowed down by the system, the software development kit now receives a quiet heads-up so the hosting app can show a pause timer and offer a way to keep the session going. This only affects developers who embed the Freebuffy coding assistant into their own applications using the SDK, not people using the chatbot directly in their terminal or browser. If an app chooses to listen for these notices, users will start seeing labels about upcoming pauses and prompts to renew their session slot right when the slowdown happens; apps that don't listen simply keep working as before. The change is live today, and it also quietly adds a reference ID that the system can use later to restart a paused paid session in place.

The first and third carry doc comments noting that sign-in covers existing logins and that card setup uses the browser's email identity, while the remaining new members sit between previously defined buyer-side funnel events without additional commentary.

These are internal-only metrics that help the team understand how advertisers move through the signup and campaign-building flow, and they do not change anything you see or do in the Freebuff app. You won't notice any difference in your coding sessions or in your free model usage.

43a914df9b529ed016525a3a72af929e57384432.title: Agent runtime test checks completed steps survive a session refusal
43a914df9b529ed016525a3a72af929e57384432.summary: A new test was added to `packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/loop-agent-steps.test.ts` verifying that `loopAgentSteps` preserves earlier steps when a later step is refused by a session gate. The mock returns text and a `read_files` tool call on the first invocation, then throws an `APICallError` with status code 428 and error `waiting_room_required`, and the assertions confirm prior history and tool messages remain intact despite the refused step, ensuring resumed free-mode turns do not restart from scratch. This guards the behavior where hosts checkpoint agent state and the CLI adopts it after a session ends, so completed work is not lost on continuation.

98b0a0089b3746b71ad966acd253b1824bd7294e.title: BYOK provider now flags unrecognized model IDs in error responses
98b0a0089b3746b71ad966acd253b1824bd7294e.summary: The BYOK fetch wrapper in getModelForRequest now inspects 400/404/422 provider error bodies and classifies them as model-id rejections through the new isByokModelIdRejection function, which matches phrases like 'does not exist', 'not found', and 'supported model names are'. When a body is classified as a model-id rejection, getByokProviderErrorMessage returns a dedicated message that names the connection's own configured model id (sliced to MAX_MODEL_ID_IN_MESSAGE = 120) instead of the generic 'request failed' text, while every error message still omits the upstream response body to avoid leaking credential fragments.
98b0a0089b3746b71ad966acd253b1824bd7294e.evidence: In sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts, the fetch wrapper inside getModelForRequest now classifies 400/404/422 BYOK provider error bodies via a new isByokModelIdRejection(body) export, and getByokProviderErrorMessage is extended to accept a { model?, modelRejected? } detail argument so it can return a 'BYOK provider does not recognise the model ID' message naming the connection's own configured model id when the body is reclassified as a model-id rejection.
98b0a0089b3746b71ad966acd253b1824bd7294e.unknowns: The diff does not show where isByokModelIdRejection or the model-id-aware getByokProviderErrorMessage path is consumed downstream, so the full rollout of the reclassification across clients is not visible.

98b0a0089b3746b71ad966acd253b1824bd7294e.text: When you connect Freebuff to your own AI provider key and mistype a model name, the error message now tells you directly that the model ID is unrecognized instead of just saying the request failed. This helps you spot a typo in the model name quickly, rather than searching your API key or settings. It affects anyone using a private key to route requests through their own AI provider account. No setup or action is needed on your part; you will simply see a clearer message if a model name is wrong.

You do not need to do anything and will not notice this change in your coding sessions.

a0847512722a967339cd1ba1ec3129c629b33661.title: Sponsored proposal verification drops verdict for contract-less runs
a0847512722a967339cd1ba1ec3129c629b33661.summary: The verification field in `sponsoredProposalViewModel` now returns `null` when `row.acceptance_criteria_sha256` is absent, withholding the verdict for runs with no frozen acceptance-criteria contract. The VM conformance checks in `SPONSORED_CONFORMANCE_CHECKS` now assert that such runs show no verdict even with a stored no-contract result (VM-38) and that an inconclusive check against a frozen contract still shows Couldn't verify (VM-39). This corrects a read that labelled a non-checkable run as a failed verification when there was nothing to check.
a0847512722a967339cd1ba1ec3129c629b33661.evidence: In `common/src/ads/sponsored-proposal-view.ts`, the verification block of `sponsoredProposalViewModel` now returns `null` when `!row.acceptance_criteria_sha256`, and `common/src/ads/sponsored-proposal-conformance.ts` renames VM-38 and adds VM-39 in `VM_CHECKS`.
a0847512722a967339cd1ba1ec3129c629b33661.unknowns: The change is internal to the shared view model and conformance matrix with no new surface reader of the affected fields visible in the diff.

a0847512722a967339cd1ba1ec3129c629b33661.text: When a sponsored run has no acceptance criteria contract, the verification panel now returns null instead of showing a "Couldn't verify" message that read like a failed check. This is an internal conformance and view-model update in the shared Core package, with new tests asserting that contract-less runs show no verdict even with a stored no-contract result (VM-38) and that an inconclusive check against a frozen contract still displays "Couldn't verify" (VM-39). No end-user action is needed and there is no visible change to how readers experience sponsored proposals, since the change only corrects how an absent-verification state is represented internally.

2450e2bfd3bbb8db44653e0960744c8bd9804680.title: Add two privacy decision limits for suspicious egress
2450e2bfd3bbb8db44653e0960744c8bd9804680.summary: Two new values are appended to the `FreebuffPrivacyDecision` union in the shared session-shape module so the server can signal that an egress was flagged but not blocked. The new cases cover a Spur-named tunnel or ipinfo-named datacenter anonymizer that Scamalytics missed, and an ipinfo flag paired with a device clock placing the user in another country, letting the limited model picker explain the restricted set without local geo/IP rechecking.
2450e2bfd3bbb8db44653e0960744c8bd9804680.evidence: The diff adds two new members to the `FreebuffPrivacyDecision` union in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, each with an explanatory comment describing the Spur/datacenter and ipinfo/device-clock scenarios respectively.

2450e2bfd3bbb8db44653e0960744c8bd9804680.text: The service now recognizes two new reasons to grant restricted, not blocked, access: one where a tunnel or datacenter anonymizer was spotted by an IP tool but missed by a scam-checking service, and another where an IP flag matches a device clock pointing to a different country. This affects only the Freebuff service operators who configure and run Freebuff itself, since the change lives in the shared session types those deployments use. You will not notice any difference day to day, because nothing in the app reads these new options yet, so access rules stay exactly as they are today. The options are in place for future use but do not take effect until a release enables them.

The previous local matchers (isEnvFile in sponsored-capabilities.ts and isEnvExampleFile/ENV_EXAMPLE_FILE_NAMES in sponsored-run-outcomes.ts) were removed so the two policies can no longer drift. The basename helpers in both modules also now split on backslash for Windows path correctness.

This is an internal change for Freebuff subscribers and the engineering team, with no visible effect on daily usage or behavior you would notice.

da80e463619074350fe0fba0d1f60db796505553.title: Add Windows floor-only sponsored execution gating
da80e463619074350fe0fba0d1f60db796505553.summary: A new `common/src/ads/sponsored-windows.ts` module gates generic agentic Windows serving behind two opt-ins: `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS` (only the exact value `on` opens) and `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS_CAMPAIGN_IDS` (a comma-separated list of reviewed campaign UUIDs). Because Windows has no OS sandbox under a sponsored run, admitted runs carry `SPONSORED_WINDOWS_CONTAINMENT` ('floor') instead of a sandbox, and `SponsoredComputeGrant` now exposes optional `executionSurface` and containment so the funded Accept route can select the floor-only broker only on `desktop_windows`. The Supabase format and its CPC experiment arms deliberately stay macOS/Linux: `desktop_windows` is refused by name in `supabaseFoundationStackEligible` and in both `SUPABASE_FORMAT_CPC_ARM_REACH` arms, so Windows only ever reaches generic campaigns the operator reviewed.
da80e463619074350fe0fba0d1f60db796505553.evidence: New file `common/src/ads/sponsored-windows.ts` adds `readSponsoredWindowsPolicy`, `sponsoredWindowsAdmitsCampaign`, `sponsoredExecutionContainment`, and `sponsoredDesktopSurfaceMatchesOs`, reading env vars `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS` and `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS_CAMPAIGN_IDS`; `common/src/ads/sponsored-compute-contract.ts` imports `SPONSORED_WINDOWS_EXECUTION_SURFACE` and `SponsoredExecutionContainment` to add optional `executionSurface` and containment fields to `SponsoredComputeGrant`; tests assert `readSponsoredWindowsPolicy` fails closed on absent/typed-off/garbage values and admits only listed UUIDs.
da80e463619074350fe0fba0d1f60db796505553.migration: Operators who want to offer Windows generic agentic runs must set `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS` to `on` and `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS_CAMPAIGN_IDS` to a comma-separated list of reviewed campaign UUIDs; any other value or malformed list closes Windows serving.

da80e463619074350fe0fba0d1f60db796505553.text: The Freebuff service can now show sponsored, agent-run tasks to Windows desktop users, but only when its operators turn the feature on with a setting and only for specific advertiser campaigns they have manually approved for Windows. Operators who run Freebuff control this with two settings: one must be set to exactly the word "on", and the other must list the approved campaign identifiers. If either setting is missing, off, misspelled, or contains a single invalid identifier, Windows users get nothing at all, and the existing supported Mac and Linux paths are untouched. Nothing changes for you as a user unless you are on Windows AND a reviewed advertiser campaign has been explicitly opted in by the service operators.

4df615ebd40226fe2e8afee567da9cd85251f63d.title: Sponsored file tools pin directories in-process, no broker
4df615ebd40226fe2e8afee567da9cd85251f63d.summary: The sponsored rooted filesystem in `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-rooted-filesystem.ts` now pins directories itself in-process instead of routing reads, writes, listings and stats through an OS broker helper, per COD-642. `createSponsoredRootedFileSystem` drops the `runtimeDir` and `processBroker` options, selects a pinning strategy per platform via `sponsoredDirectoryPinning` (proc-fd on Linux, volfs on macOS, lstat on Windows), and refuses to run on any platform without a pinning mechanism. Removed sponsoredStatCommand and the brokered stat/cat shell path; added platform pinning helpers and a lstat fallback for Windows.
Built the sponsored run's file tools with only workspaceRoot, no process broker, per COD-642.
Exported INCLUDED_HIDDEN_DIRS so the sponsored code-search broker admits exactly those hidden directories.
Added sponsoredRipgrepArgs and a direct Windows spawn that rebuilds the exact ripgrep argv, refusing anything the broker did not build.

4df615ebd40226fe2e8afee567da9cd85251f63d.text: The Freebuff engineering team removed an intermediate helper program that the sponsored-run file tools used to read, list, and write files on your machine, and replaced it with code that talks to the directory you granted directly, holding that directory open and naming every file through a kernel-level handle instead of a path string. This applies to anyone who runs an advertiser-funded task (a sponsored proposal) in their own repository on the CLI or desktop app, and it does not change what the assistant is allowed to touch or whether you get asked to consent first.

8a0c02826f1ffeb379268f990669781deead6853.title: Resolve macOS git shim in sponsored sandbox PATH
8a0c02826f1ffeb379268f990669781deead6853.summary: On macOS a sponsored local run now resolves `/usr/bin/git` - which is Apple's xcode-select shim, not real git - before it execs, so a git commit inside the sandbox reaches the developer directory's actual git without the profile ever granting `/var/select/developer_dir`. `sponsoredMacGitPath` rewrites the run's PATH unsandboxed, ahead of the first readable git, with stand-in exec scripts (via `linkDeveloperShims`) for the 77 xcode-select shim names the developer bin shares with `/usr/bin`, and the broker caches one resolved PATH per input, applied to env.PATH at darwin start only. The profile is unchanged: no new read/write grant and no new environment variable, since PATH only renames what the sandbox already may exec.
8a0c02826f1ffeb379268f990669781deead6853.evidence: sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts: new exports sponsoredMacGitPath, linkDeveloperShims, findXcodeDeveloperGit and interface SponsoredMacGitDependencies resolve the macOS /usr/bin/git xcode-select shim (XCODE_SELECT_GIT_SHIM = '/usr/bin/git') by reading the developer directory link outside the sandbox and putting stand-in exec scripts for every /usr/bin shim ahead of /usr/bin; the new macRunPath cache in createSponsoredTerminalBroker rewrites env.PATH on darwin per start. XCODE_SELECT_GIT_SHIM and XCODE_SELECT_SHIM_DIR are still defined.
8a0c02826f1ffeb379268f990669781deead6853.unknowns: The diff shows no consumer of SPONSORED_MAC_SYSTEM_READ_SUBPATHS outside sponsorship-sandbox.ts yet, and the rollout timing of the new PATH behavior to Desktop (COD-397) versus the CLI (COD-339) is not shown.

8a0c02826f1ffeb379268f990669781deead6853.text: The assistant now makes the correct version of Git work inside a safe sandbox on Mac computers, so that when it runs a sponsored task, the commit step actually finishes instead of failing with an error. This is for the Freebuff team's sponsored run system, where advertiser-funded tasks run on a user's machine. You do not need to do anything differently, and this does not change how your coding sessions or free allowances work.

34b2cc1e1354f7f69267d61eb4c6060828523293.title: Windows sponsored serving switches from per-campaign list to one
34b2cc1e1354f7f69267d61eb4c6060828523293.summary: The Windows Desktop serving gate is now a single switch instead of a per-campaign whitelist. readSponsoredWindowsPolicy in common/src/ads/sponsored-windows.ts returns SPONSORED_WINDOWS_ON (Readonly<{ switch: 'on' }}>) only when FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS is exactly on, and the removed sponsoredWindowsAdmitsCampaign and FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS_CAMPAIGN_IDS mean a campaign list no longer gates admission. With the switch on, every agentic campaign eligible for macOS serves Windows under the same rules; Supabase and legacy CPC paths reach Windows only as generic candidates under FREEBUFF_AGENTIC_ONE_FUNNEL=on until COD-649 retires them. The funded Accept surface in common/src/ads/sponsored-compute-contract.ts adds a clientExecutionSurface field and SPONSORED_ACCEPT_EXECUTION_SURFACE_PARAM, enforced by sponsoredAcceptSurfaceMatchesRow, so a Windows client is paired with a desktop_windows row and never charged for a row it cannot run.
34b2cc1e1354f7f69267d61eb4c6060828523293.evidence: In common/src/ads/sponsored-windows.ts, readSponsoredWindowsPolicy drops FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS_CAMPAIGN_IDS and sponsoredWindowsAdmitsCampaign; SponsoredWindowsPolicy becomes Readonly<{ switch: 'on' }> with SPONSORED_WINDOWS_ON, and sponsoredWindowsSwitchState enforces that only the exact value on opens Windows serving (off/empty/unset are off, anything else is unrecognised). In common/src/ads/sponsored-compute-contract.ts, the funded Accept request type SponsoredAcceptRequest gains a clientExecutionSurface field and SPONSORED_ACCEPT_EXECUTION_SURFACE_PARAM, paired by sponsoredAcceptSurfaceMatchesRow, so Windows Desktop can be paired with its own row. In common/src/ads/supabase-setup-invitation.ts and common/src/ads/generic-setup-invitation.ts and common/src/ads/supabase-format-cpc-experiment.ts, the per-campaign Windows opt-in references are removed, making the one funnel (FREEBUFF_AGENTIC_ONE_FUNNEL=on) the only path to Windows for Supabase and legacy CPC.
34b2cc1e1354f7f69267d61eb4c6060828523293.migration: Operators setting FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS=1 must change it to FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS=on or Windows serving stops; operators with FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS_CAMPAIGN_IDS must remove it because the per-campaign list no longer exists. Clients that omit clientExecutionSurface on Accept are treated as unrecorded rows and accepted as before.
34b2cc1e1354f7f69267d61eb4c6060828523293.unknowns: The diff does not show the server route or Convex contract code that consumes SponsoredAcceptRequest.clientExecutionSurface or SPONSORED_ACCEPT_EXECUTION_SURFACE_PARAM, and the rollout timing of FREEBUFF_AGENTIC_ONE_FUNNEL=on relative to COD-649 is not specified.

34b2cc1e1354f7f69267d61eb4c6060828523293.text: Freebuff has simplified how it decides when to run sponsored tasks on Windows. Previously, an operator running Freebuff had to maintain a list of specific campaigns allowed to target Windows, then enable a separate switch. Now there is only one switch, and when it is on, every campaign already eligible to sponsor on macOS automatically runs on Windows under the same rules, including the Supabase legacy paths which still won't serve Windows until a later retirement. This switch must be set to the exact value of 'on', anything else means Windows is off, so an operator with the old switch value of '1' must update it or Windows serving stops.

01587d07269090e4590fe97febc0c1c0204de54c.title: Windows path resolution for sponsored file layer
01587d07269090e4590fe97febc0c1c0204de54c.summary: The SDK now ships `sponsored-windows-paths.ts`, which validates Windows path spellings against Win32 reinterpretation (trailing dot/space, `:` alternate data streams, 8.3 short names) and compares resolved paths case-insensitively via `realpathSync.native`. `createSponsoredRootedFileSystem` and `sponsoredRipgrepArgs` use these helpers to refuse reparse-point redirects where Node's `lstat` does not report them as links, and writes are staged under an exclusive random name and renamed over the target instead of opening it. `probeSponsoredFileLayer` was added to the public SDK surface to ask whether the file layer can pin a worktree on the current host before a run starts.
01587d07269090e4590fe97febc0c1c0204de54c.evidence: Added `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-windows-paths.ts` (new file) and modified `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-rooted-filesystem.ts` to import and use `sameWindowsPath`, `sponsoredWindowsSegmentRefusal`, `windowsNativePath`, and `windowsNativeRelative`; `sdk/src/index.ts` now re-exports `probeSponsoredFileLayer` and the type `SponsoredFileLayerSupport`.
01587d07269090e4590fe97febc0c1c0204de54c.unknowns: The diff does not show which surface or orchestrator first calls `probeSponsoredFileLayer` against a project before Accept.

01587d07269090e4590fe97febc0c1c0204de54c.text: On Windows machines, the code that handles sponsored runs now checks that every file and folder path spelling is exactly what Windows would actually open. It refuses names Windows could misinterpret, such as trailing spaces, alternate data streams, or short 8.3 names, and it confirms the real destination of a path before reading or writing anything through it. This change is internal to Freebuff and affects only the Windows builds of the sponsored run file layer. Nothing about this requires you to change how you work, and if you are not on Windows this has no effect on you at all.

3b3d023eea37cbdbaadeafc904eb4179aa444efc.title: Add COD-654 CPM leg telemetry to first-party ad schema
3b3d023eea37cbdbaadeafc904eb4179aa444efc.summary: The first-party ad fetch completed event schema in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` now includes `first_party_cpm_outcome`, `first_party_cpm_mode`, and `first_party_cpm_campaign_id`. These fields capture the verdict of the CPM leg (`fill`, `no_fill`, `shadow_would_fill`, `shadow_no_fill`, `not_tier1`, `gravity_not_no_fill`, or `error`), its operating mode, and the campaign id that would have or did serve, and they are emitted only when the CPM leg was evaluated, never under `off`. The change extends telemetry for the COD-654 pricing leg while leaving existing CPC geo-pricing fields (`first_party_geo_tier`, `first_party_geo_floored`, etc.) untouched.
3b3d023eea37cbdbaadeafc904eb4179aa444efc.evidence: In `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`, the `ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS` schema object gained three new keys: `first_party_cpm_outcome` ('string'), `first_party_cpm_mode` ('string'), and `first_party_cpm_campaign_id` ('string'), accompanied by a JSDoc block citing COD-654 and stating the fields are present only when the CPM leg was evaluated (never under `off`).

bd83e63a1780109930f5c221b1f2ed09b2cb91e2.title: Helper process census and leaked watchdog inspection added
bd83e63a1780109930f5c221b1f2ed09b2cb91e2.summary: The CLI now tracks every helper process it spawns by kind (clipboard, terminal_command, launcher_probe, terminal_watchdog) through a new getHelperProcessCensus module, and getHelperProcessSnapshot exposes those counts for local diagnostics. cli/src/utils/terminal-watchdog.ts gains inspectWindowsWatchdogMarkers and admitWindowsWatchdog, which scan the temp dir for codebuff-watchdog-disarm- prefix files and refuse to arm when MAX_CONCURRENT_WINDOWS_WATCHDOGS watchdogs already run. reportCliProcessHealth emits cli.helper_process_flood and cli.helper_outlived_parent events that are added to the never-sampled set in analytics-sampling.ts.
