f670fdb7932f87bef16edeb24cf73db2b5d6077d.title: Halve PAID and PRO PLUS credit limits and add Stripe customer
f670fdb7932f87bef16edeb24cf73db2b5d6077d.summary: The `CREDITS_USAGE_LIMITS` map in `common/src/constants.ts` now sets PAID to 5,000 and PRO_PLUS to 27,500 credits for production users (halved from 10,000 and 55,000), with matching reductions in the local overrides. A new script `scripts/migrate-stripe-customers.ts` migrates existing Stripe customers from the $99/month tier to a new price using `env.STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID` and `env.STRIPE_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID`, records prior usage via `billing.meterEvents.create` with `event_name: 'credits'`, and applies coupon `wwu4ER94` with `proration_behavior: 'none'`. These changes align with the commit message 'Cut costs and credits by half' and update billing documentation in `backend/src/billing/billing.knowledge.md` and `web/knowledge.md` with migration best practices. The pricing page in `web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx` also adjusts displayed prices, now showing Pro at $49/month, Pro Plus at $249/month, and Team at $99/seat/month.
f670fdb7932f87bef16edeb24cf73db2b5d6077d.evidence: The diff in `common/src/constants.ts` edits `CREDITS_USAGE_LIMITS` for both local and production branches, halving PAID from 10,000 to 5,000 and PRO_PLUS from 55,000 to 27,500 (production) and from 10,000,000 to 5,000,000 and PRO_PLUS from 55,000,000 to 27,500,000 (local). It also adds a new script `scripts/migrate-stripe-customers.ts` that reads `env.STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID` and `env.STRIPE_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID`, updates Stripe subscriptions for customers on the $99/mo plan, records usage via `billing.meterEvents.create` with `event_name: 'credits'`, and applies a coupon `wwu4ER94` with `proration_behavior: 'none'`.
f670fdb7932f87bef16edeb24cf73db2b5d6077d.migration: Existing subscribers on the $99/month tier must be migrated using the new script `scripts/migrate-stripe-customers.ts`, which reads STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID and STRIPE_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID; users on higher tiers will see their credit allowances halved, and operators should verify coupon and price IDs before running.
f670fdb7932f87bef16edeb24cf73db2b5d6077d.unknowns: The actual rollout status of the new Stripe price IDs and whether the coupon applies to all customers or only a subset.

changes.what: Halved PAID and PRO_PLUS credit limits in CREDITS_USAGE_LIMITS for both local and production environments.
Added migrate-stripe-customers.ts to migrate Stripe subscriptions to new price IDs, record usage via meter events, and apply a coupon.
Added documentation on subscription migration best practices including usage preservation and pagination.
Updated displayed pricing tiers for Pro, Pro Plus, and Team plans.
Expanded documentation on Stripe integration including subscription updates and item handling.

73b3e16cdc03da2402d2a3eed7e3bbec76b073f1.title: /reasoning command sets per-model thinking effort in Freebuff
73b3e16cdc03da2402d2a3eed7e3bbec76b073f1.summary: /reasoning [level] is a new Freebuff-only slash command that reads or sets how hard the selected model thinks, validated against the model's local ladder and persisted per model in settings.json as freebuffReasoningEfforts. It is freebuff-only because the ladder it reads is the FREEBUFF catalog's, and the metadata it sets is honored only for free-mode traffic (isFreebuffOriginatedRequest); on Codebuff the command takes a value and silently drops it. On send, cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts attaches the override as freebuff_reasoning_effort on extraCodebuffMetadata so it lands on the next message without restarting the session, while cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx memoizes picker width on reasoningEffortByModel and marks user-chosen rungs with a '*' suffix. Three supporting changes carry it: the store, the settings persistence, and the command/slash-command registration. The server re-clamps whatever the client sends against the model that actually runs the turn, so the effort is a request and not a final command.
73b3e16cdc03da2402d2a3eed7e3bbec76b073f1.evidence: New file cli/src/commands/reasoning.ts exports handleReasoningCommand, added behind a freebuff-only command registration in cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts and cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts; cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts now reads getSelectedFreebuffReasoningEffort() and attaches it as freebuff_reasoning_effort on extraCodebuffMetadata; cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx memoizes row width on reasoningEffortByModel and renders a '*' suffix for user-chosen rungs; cli/src/state/freebuff-model-store.ts adds reasoningEffortByModel state plus getFreebuffReasoningEffortForModel/getEffectiveFreebuffReasoningEffort/getSelectedFreebuffReasoningEffort; cli/src/utils/settings.ts adds freebuffReasoningEfforts persistence and validates it against each model's ladder on load.
73b3e16cdc03da2402d2a3eed7e3bbec76b073f1.migration: If you use the Freebuff CLI, you can run `/reasoning [low|high|max]` to override the thinking effort for your current model, or `/reasoning default` to return to the model's catalog default; overrides are stored per model, so switching models does not carry a rung across.
73b3e16cdc03da2402d2a3eed7e3bbec76b073f1.unknowns: The consumer on the server side that resolves freebuff_reasoning_effort against the running model is not visible in this diff, and the rollout scope beyond the Freebuff CLI is not shown.

changes.what: New handleReasoningCommand(args) reads or sets the thinking effort for the selected Freebuff model, validating against the model's ladder and offering clear words ('default', 'auto', 'reset', 'clear', 'none') to drop the override.

The /reasoning command (aliases /effort, /think) is registered as freebuff-only, excluded from Codebuff via the FREEBUFF_ONLY_COMMANDS and FREEBUFF_ONLY_COMMAND_IDS gates, and wired to post its message into chat history.

Each Freebuff send now reads getSelectedFreebuffReasoningEffort() and, when non-null, attaches freebuff_reasoning_effort to extraCodebuffMetadata so the override reaches the requests layer for the next message.

The picker subscribes to reasoningEffortByModel so row-width memoization stays current, and renders a '· Reasoning: <rung>*' suffix where the '*' marks a rung the user chose, falling back to the catalog reasoningEffort otherwise.

Added reasoningEffortByModel state, setReasoningEffort (persisting per model), and the getFreebuffReasoningEffortForModel, getEffectiveFreebuffReasoningEffort, and getSelectedFreebuffReasoningEffort helpers, re-checking saves against the current ladder on every read.

Added freebuffReasoningEfforts to the Settings schema, loadFreebuffReasoningEfforts/saveFreebuffReasoningEffort accessors, and validation on load that drops any stored rung not offered by the model's current ladder.

175ea48e5f9acebbb528cd76425d4f268f0d947c.title: Add /byok command and direct provider inference
175ea48e5f9acebbb528cd76425d4f268f0d947c.summary: A new `/byok` slash command (aliases `/provider`) lets Freebuff users run inference directly through their own OpenRouter or OpenAI-compatible provider instead of the Freebuff session. The command, implemented in cli/src/commands/byok.ts and registered as Freebuff-only in cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts and cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts, supports list/add/update/validate/select/remove/off subcommands and parses quoted names literally without evaluating shell syntax. Backing storage lives in cli/src/utils/byok.ts (`useByokSelectionStore`, `resolveByokConnection`, `saveSelectedByokConnection`) and sdk/src/byok.ts (`createBunByokConnectionStore`, `ResolvedByokConnection`, `byokCompletionUrl`), which keep keys in OS credential storage or named environment variables and never persist secret values into chat messages or command history. The change ripples through the SDK run path: client.ts, run.ts, impl/agent-runtime.ts, impl/llm.ts, and impl/model-provider.ts thread a run-scoped `byok` connection through `CodebuffClientOptions`, `RunOptions`, and `getModelForRequest`, while run.ts adds a non-secret inference pin to `RunState` so resumed conversations refuse to switch providers mid-turn. Qualification of the native credential adapter is covered by two new scripts under sdk/scripts/.
175ea48e5f9acebbb528cd76425d4f268f0d947c.evidence: New `handleByokCommand` in cli/src/commands/byok.ts (new) with subcommands list/add/update/validate/select/remove/off; backed by cli/src/utils/byok.ts (new) exposing `useByokSelectionStore`, `resolveByokConnection`, `saveSelectedByokConnection`; registered Freebuff-only in cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts and cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts; SDK layer in sdk/src/byok.ts (new) added `createBunByokConnectionStore`, `ResolvedByokConnection`, `byokCompletionUrl`, plus sdk/src/client.ts, sdk/src/run.ts, sdk/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts, sdk/src/impl/llm.ts, sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts carrying `byok` through run config and provider selection; qualification harness added as sdk/scripts/qualify-byok-credentials.ts and sdk/scripts/qualify-byok-credentials-worker.ts (new).
175ea48e5f9acebbb528cd76425d4f268f0d947c.unknowns: The diff does not show the rollout plan or whether the native credential store qualification is gated behind a feature flag.

changes.what: /byok command adds direct OpenRouter/OpenAI-compatible inference with local credential storage and literal quoted-name parsing.
Wiring skips auth and Freebuff session admission when a BYOK connection is selected, and reports the provider/model in the idle status bar.
CodebuffClient and run() accept an optional run-scoped byok connection that bypasses the Codebuff backend and validates against the provider directly.
Adds a qualification harness that exercises the production Bun credential adapter across source and compiled Bun runtimes.
Adds an explicit maxContextLength override to compactContext and applies it during history compaction and programmatic steps.

98e174e577d764b45973ff8a4091cb3b3d6196d8.title: Add /dashboard slash command and account hub usage types
98e174e577d764b45973ff8a4091cb3b3d6196d8.summary: A new `/dashboard` slash command opens `${LOGIN_WEBSITE_URL}/account` via `safeOpen` and prints a system message announcing streaks, activity, tokens, sessions and settings across CLI, Desktop and web; it is Freebuff-only (registered in `FREEBUFF_ONLY_COMMANDS`), while Codebuff keeps its separate `/usage` banner. The dashboard reuses the `usage` alias because Freebuff removes the old `/usage` command, leaving users without an answer to how much they have used. Two new files wire the account hub: `common/src/types/freebuff-usage.ts` adds the cross-surface summary interfaces, and `common/src/util/freebuff-usage-summary.ts` adds pure functions `buildFreebuffUsageSummary`, `calculateLongestFreebuffStreak`, and `buildFreebuffUsageGrid`, driven by new constants `FREEBUFF_USAGE_MAP_DAYS = 365` and `FREEBUFF_RECENT_TOKENS_DAYS = 7` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`.
98e174e577d764b45973ff8a4091cb3b3d6196d8.evidence: The diff adds a dashboard command definition in `cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts` (in `ALL_COMMANDS` and added to `FREEBUFF_ONLY_COMMANDS`), and a matching dashboard entry in `ALL_SLASH_COMMANDS` in `cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts` with aliases `usage`, `stats`, `streak`. The handler builds `${LOGIN_WEBSITE_URL}/account` and calls `safeOpen(url)` after posting a system message. New files `common/src/types/freebuff-usage.ts` and `common/src/util/freebuff-usage-summary.ts` define wire types and pure summary functions (`buildFreebuffUsageSummary`, `calculateLongestFreebuffStreak`, `buildFreebuffUsageGrid`) backed by new constants `FREEBUFF_USAGE_MAP_DAYS` and `FREEBUFF_RECENT_TOKENS_DAYS` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`.

changes.what: Defines the Freebuff-only `dashboard` command which opens `${LOGIN_WEBSITE_URL}/account` and prints a system message about the cross-surface account hub.
Registers the `dashboard` slash command with aliases `usage`, `stats`, `streak` and adds it to `FREEBUFF_ONLY_COMMAND_IDS`.
Adds wire types for the account hub usage summary shared by web, CLI and Desktop.
Adds pure functions `buildFreebuffUsageSummary`, `calculateLongestFreebuffStreak`, and `buildFreebuffUsageGrid` that assemble the hub summary from active dates.
Defines `FREEBUFF_USAGE_MAP_DAYS = 365` and `FREEBUFF_RECENT_TOKENS_DAYS = 7`.

3dc7ec2306d94243ab2ba83ab457b59bcd4713c1.title: /queue opens an in-place editor for the message queue
3dc7ec2306d94243ab2ba83ab457b59bcd4713c1.summary: A new /queue slash command (alias /queued) opens an editable, reorderable panel in place of the chat composer, backed by the QueuePanel component and the queue-panel-store, with edits, deletes and moves routed through the existing message-queue runtime actions. The panel takes over the composer surface the way the review screen does, restores keyboard focus on close, and auto-closes when the queue drains or the session ends, closing itself on an empty queue instead of flashing. Ctrl+Q also opens the panel when messages are queued, and the help banner now lists that shortcut.
3dc7ec2306d94243ab2ba83ab457b59bcd4713c1.evidence: New `queue` command registered in `cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts` returning `openQueuePanel`, and matching { id: 'queue', ... } entry added to `cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts`; panel surface is `QueuePanel` exported from new `cli/src/components/queue-panel.tsx`, driven by `cli/src/state/queue-panel-store.ts` zustand store, wired into Chat render and `useChatKeyboard` `onOpenQueuePanel`.
3dc7ec2306d94243ab2ba83ab457b59bcd4713c1.migration: No migration required, but opening /queue now switches the input area to the editor instead of leaving the composer behind.
3dc7ec2306d94243ab2ba83ab457b59bcd4713c1.unknowns: The rollout flag or gating for the queue editor surface is not visible in this commit.

changes.what: Added a `queue` command (alias `queued`) that returns `openQueuePanel` in the command result.
Added QueuePanel component with select, reorder, edit, delete and close actions, driven by queue-panel-store state.
Wired QueuePanel into Chat render behind queue-panel-open state, restored keyboard focus on close, and auto-closed on session end or empty queue.
Added open-queue-panel keyboard action and Ctrl+Q binding, disabled chat keyboard while panel is open, and updated help banner shortcut text.
Exposed editQueuedMessage, removeQueuedMessage, moveQueuedMessage from the queue runtime into Chat props.

538c2cf35723bbd8b97ad706cd92c8e0c909a984.title: CLI model selector drops off-peak detail chip, off-peak helper returns

ce02985fc2dae21a5d6635d933952781273e3b33.title: /copy serializes conversation to clipboard
ce02985fc2dae21a5d6635d933952781273e3b33.summary: Added a `/copy` slash command (aliases `/copy-chat` and `/export`) that serializes the full conversation - user text, assistant text, reasoning blocks, tool calls with inputs and outputs, and sub-agents - into Markdown and writes it to the system clipboard. Over SSH the OSC 52 payload caps at 32 KB (`OSC52_TEXT_BUDGET_BYTES = 22_000`), so `serializeConversation` progressively drops the largest tool results then tool inputs, replacing them with omission notes, and falls back to hard truncation via `keepTailBytes` when the remaining content still exceeds the budget; local sessions use pbcopy/xclip with no size cap and always copy the full transcript.
ce02985fc2dae21a5d6635d933952781273e3b33.evidence: New file `cli/src/commands/copy-conversation.ts` defines `serializeConversation`, `SerializedConversation`, and `handleCopyConversationCommand`; the `copy` command is registered in `cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts` with aliases `['copy-chat', 'export']` and added to `cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts` with description 'Copy the full conversation (messages + tool results) to the clipboard'.
ce02985fc2dae21a5d6635d933952781273e3b33.unknowns: The diff does not reveal how `copyTextToClipboard`, `isRemoteSession`, or `showClipboardMessage` in `cli/src/utils/clipboard` are implemented or whether the OSC 52 path is exercised on all remote sessions.

73b3e16cdc03da2402d2a3eed7e3bbec76b073f1.text: When you use Freebuff, you can now type `/reasoning low`, `/reasoning high`, or `/reasoning max` into your chat to tell the assistant how much extra thinking to do before it replies, and you can check what it is currently set to by typing `/reasoning` with no argument. This only works if you are on the Freebuff free tier, it only affects the model you are currently using, and your choice is remembered for that model the next time you start a session. The change is live today for Freebuff users; if you are on the paid Codebuff plan, the command does nothing.

175ea48e5f9acebbb528cd76425d4f268f0d947c.text: The assistant can now be pointed at your own AI provider account instead of the default free service. In the terminal you type /byok, then tell it which environment variable holds your key, and it switches your conversation to that provider - stopping any ad-supported session and routing all requests through your account. It is for Freebuff users who want to use their own OpenRouter or OpenAI-compatible key, and it is live today; the status bar now shows which provider and model you are using.

fd93692e814f3a7a4a3e61773e10e58384120e64.text: This release brings the free version of the coding assistant to version 0.0.181 and adds new features, model options, and safety fixes. The main additions include a new AI model called MiMo 2.6 Pro that you can use for free, support for annual prepaid subscriptions that let you pay once a year instead of monthly, and better protection so cloned projects cannot secretly change where your assistant connects. It also improves advertising tracking so signups from web, desktop, and command-line surfaces are recorded correctly, and it makes the model picker show only safe public models while hiding unapproved network traffic. Upgrading gives you access to the new model, a simpler way to manage payments yearly, clearer error messages when your internet connection drops, and stronger protections against sneaky repository settings trying to redirect your work.

98e174e577d764b45973ff8a4091cb3b3d6196d8.text: The Freebuff assistant now offers a /dashboard command, which opens your account page in the browser and shows a summary of your activity - your streak, how much you've used tokens, which models you picked, and your session counts - consistent across the CLI, desktop app, and web. This is for Freebuff users only, since the separate Codebuff product keeps its own usage view. In daily use, typing /dashboard (or /usage, which Freebuff redirected to the new page) prints a short message with your account link and tries to open it for you, so you can check how much you've used without leaving the chat.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: GLM 5.3 Flash is now the default AI model when you start a new task in Freebuff, replacing the previous default on CLI, web, and desktop. A new /reasoning command lets you control how hard the model thinks on each task, with choices like low, high, and max. The free model picker now includes Solar Pro 4 as a limited-time trial option. Clipboard copying in the CLI now falls back to a terminal-compatible method when your usual copy tool is missing, and aborts stale copy operations. Daily spend limits are now applied per region with a single shared message for restricted users, and signup flows now support reCAPTCHA as an option. The new subscription tier catalog defines Starter, Plus, and Pro plans with daily, five-day, and monthly session pools, and a shared plan summary now renders in the CLI model picker. GLM 5.3 Flash carries a native reasoning effort ladder and is unmetered, while GPT-5.6 Luna session caps were removed from the per-model table. New first-party ad routing and Imprezia chat ads integration let the platform fill inventory with advertiser content, with bounded telemetry logged to Axiom.

6e392721fb79228f970577ee7d957562e282073f.text: This release adds a /copy command that saves your full conversation to the clipboard, including tool calls and reasoning, and lowers the GitHub account-age requirement for referral sign-ups so newer accounts can qualify sooner. Premium Gemini Pro calls are now restricted to specific thinker helper agents, and the model picker shows the reset countdown for premium sessions even when you have not used any yet. The CLI removes the queued/waiting-room step, moving straight from model selection to active chat, and now detects Windows AVX2 support once and caches the result to speed up launches. Other changes include a new desktop thread agent ID, daily project-creation caps for limited-tier web users, and additional analytics events for tracking usage and login funnels.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This Freebuff CLI release adds the GPT-5.6 Luna model to the free model picker, introduces a new /diagnostics command, and improves how the app handles model switches and installer errors. The GPT-5.6 Luna model joins the free tier of models you can select without charge, and its tagline now includes ' & Slow' to reflect its performance profile. A new /diagnostics command shows you your machine's resource usage and lists the processes running behind your terminal sessions. When you try to switch to a model that is already in use by a stale session, the app now ends the old session and lets you continue on your chosen model instead of silently reverting. The installer now retries downloads that time out or return busy-server errors and cleans up corrupt partial downloads automatically. New analytics track desktop autorun settings and project management actions, while the CLI landing screen adjusts its layout based on your terminal size to prevent display crowding.

ce02985fc2dae21a5d6635d933952781273e3b33.text: You can now type /copy (or /copy-chat or /export) at the prompt to turn the entire chat, including your messages, the assistant's replies, hidden reasoning, and any tool results, into a clean Markdown transcript and send it straight to your clipboard. This works everywhere the chat runs, but when you're connected over SSH the system automatically trims the largest tool outputs and inputs if the transcript is too big for the remote clipboard's size limit, then hard-cuts the oldest lines as a last resort, and it tells you when it had to trim. Local sessions copy the full transcript with no size limit. This is live today, applies to Freebuff and Codebuff users, and needs no setup.

61f50f7e2be156def198dac02c70318d621c4120.text: A routine release of the Freebuff coding assistant is published with no new features for users. What updating to this version gives you is the bundled launch of a capped free trial of a premium model the assistant can now pick at no charge, even if your account is on the free tier: where the assistant previously ignored such a trial pick and swapped it back to the default model, it now honors it through both the model selection logic and the session admission checks. This widening of who can use a limited-offer model already took effect for free-tier users, so today's audience is existing Freebuff CLI, web, desktop, and SDK users who want an explicit pick of a capped premium trial to stick instead of falling back to the default model.

3dc7ec2306d94243ab2ba83ab457b59bcd4713c1.text: You can now type /queue (or press Ctrl+Q) to open an in-place editor that lets you view, reorder, edit, or delete messages you've sent that are waiting to be processed by the assistant. This panel takes over the chat input area the way the review screen does, and it automatically closes when the queue empties or you switch chats. It only appears when there are actually queued messages, so pressing Ctrl+Q with an empty queue does nothing rather than flashing an empty panel. Live today: Freebuff/CLI users who queue messages while the assistant is busy.

538c2cf35723bbd8b97ad706cd92c8e0c909a984.text: The CLI model selector no longer renders an inline off-peak detail chip for Freebucks pricing, removing its call from the rowDetails callback and dropping the import of `freebucksOffPeakCopy` from `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx`. The shared helper in `common/src/util/freebuff-off-peak-price.ts` now returns only active, badge, and tooltip fields, removing the terminal-specific detail field entirely. This collapse of off-peak presentation to the badge plus tooltip matches the badge-owned-quote model where the resolved price already carries the row's price line. The change affects Freebuff CLI users selecting models with off-peak pricing, and they will no longer see the secondary off-peak detail text inline on pricing rows, only the badge and tooltip.

f377278c442149319ba818d05791b4012b9cf3b5.text: The Freebuff coding assistant now suggests a different AI model by default when you first open it. Instead of starting on MiniMax M3, new users see DeepSeek V4 Pro highlighted as the recommended choice, with the model list still falling back to the faster DeepSeek V4 Flash when the daily premium quota is full. This affects anyone who opens the Freebuff terminal, web, or desktop interface and is live today, so users should notice a different default model card when they start a session.

8ac94a54affac0eea3470c33444b18393683fa02.text: New accounts created today now start with 500 free credits added automatically the moment signup finishes, credited once and never expiring. These signup credits go to anyone who makes a brand-new account using the assistant, and you will see them reflected the next time you check your usage or visit the pricing page. Monthly recurring credits for existing users are unchanged, since new signups no longer get them by default.

98ffa6c38ece5e15ad14bfa2d018fcfdc9a9b014.text: A new automated release process was added that lets the team build and publish a free-only version of the coding assistant called FreeBuff to npm, creating a downloadable package installers can grab. This is internal tooling for the Freebuff engineering team, not something end users see or act on. The change also flipped an internal debugging constant on so developers can log full AI requests while fixing prompt caching, with no effect on your daily use. Nothing requires your attention today.

eb47be392d867a2a8a0235cb993ff4d2af6d6c09.text: The Freebuff team added a new required secret called IPINFO TOKEN that the service must have configured, and it now uses that token to check whether a free user is connecting through a VPN, Tor, or a hosting provider before letting them into free mode. This is a change for whoever runs the Freebuff service itself, who must make sure that token is set in the environment before starting or updating to this version, otherwise the service will refuse to start and free-mode logins will fail.

f7461e3885e81bf95a5058142b2754174f13eb43.text: The referral program has been removed from both the terminal assistant and the web sign-up flow: the command to enter or redeem a referral code, the in-assistant referral input mode, and related web pages and links are all gone. Anyone using the paid Codebuff assistant no longer sees the refer-friends command or referral credits, while Freebuff users (the free tier) never had it and are unaffected. If you previously tried to sign up with a referral code or link, that path no longer works, but your existing account balance and access are unchanged. No action is needed from users; this is already live today.

ab87eb2287659131d7dcc6e88f70971ab7161251.text: The internal label for a specific agent output mode has been renamed from 'json' to 'structured_output'. This is an internal code refactor used only by the Freebuff engineering team and does not change any user-facing behavior. You will not see a different feature, new option, or changed behavior because of this.

7b17f6ed1a64395d1a122323932488f7bd0c21cc.text: The SDK that developers use to build on top of Freebuff has been reworked to talk to Freebuff through a real-time connection instead of launching a separate program. The old way of connecting is still around but is now marked as outdated, and the new approach lets developer tools react instantly to what the assistant is doing, like streaming responses and running tools, while automatically reconnecting if the connection drops. This is an internal update for developers who integrate Freebuff into their own applications, and it does not change what you see or experience when using Freebuff directly.

7c98630f058946cec393077942e0d9217d856554.text: The system that stores and shares custom AI helper configurations was rebuilt and renamed from "agent template" to "agent config", and the part that links those helpers to the person who made them now connects directly to you's account instead of using an extra publishing profile. This is now available for anyone to use. If you publish a custom helper, it will be saved under your own account with automatic version numbers, and others can fetch a specific version or the latest version of your helper over the network without any extra setup.

b9c4a393b92b8814c33c7952356a3d0145ed9a72.text: Freebuff has switched from monthly usage allowances to a credit-based billing system where you pay 1 cent per credit once your free monthly credits run out. When your balance drops below a threshold you set, the system can automatically charge your saved card to add more credits, and it will pause auto-top-up if a payment fails. This affects Freebuff users who run out of credits and need to keep working without manually buying more each time. In daily use, you'll see a credit balance and balance breakdown instead of a usage quota, and you can turn on auto-recharging from a new payment flow in the web app.

f050f80f7b766101eb252406b9be6bff0364e4f7.text: The Freebuff engineering team published a new build of the Freebuff command-line tool, moving it from the previous version number to a new one. This is a behind-the-scenes release step used only by the Freebuff team, not something individual developers or end users need to take action on. Nothing about how the assistant behaves in your terminal changes because of this, and you do not need to update anything yourself.

663ba6dc6110c21286c3f0c2de6893729e5323d9.text: Freebuff can now bill a company group instead of just you, and charge that group's credit pool when you work inside one of its approved code repositories. Teams can now sign up for shared credit billing, buy credits as a group, enable auto-recharge with a company card, and see usage and invites through an org dashboard. If you open a repository that a team has claimed, your work draws from that team's credits instead of your personal allowance. This started rolling out on June 4, 2025, with new backend tables, API, and web/CLI surfaces.

f670fdb7932f87bef16edeb24cf73db2b5d6077d.text: Paid subscribers on the old $99/month plan are having their subscriptions moved to a lower price, and everyone on the Pro and Pro Plus tiers is getting half as many monthly credits as before (for example, Pro drops from 10,000 to 5,000). The pricing page already shows the new rates of $49/month for Pro and $249/month for Pro Plus. Subscribers need no action because the move happens automatically in the background, but you will notice your credit allowance is smaller the next time your plan renews.

25f1d61530c6d58db394b59db12e97c113e9322d.title: Launcher detects Bun AVX2 crash via stderr on Windows code 3
25f1d61530c6d58db394b59db12e97c113e9322d.summary:
The Freebuff launcher now reads Bun's stderr tail and matches it against two new constants, BUN_NO_AVX2_FEATURE (/^Features:[^
]*\bno_avx2\b/m) and BUN_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION_PANIC (/^panic(?:\([^)\n]*\))?: Illegal instruction at address 0x[0-9a-f]+/im), to confirm a missing AVX2 instruction set. Previously the Windows baseline fallback only fired on STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION (0xC000001D) or the startup abort 0xC0000409, but a Bun native crash on a pre-AVX2 CPU exits with plain code 3 and the reason is only visible in its stderr. tryFallbackToBaseline() now treats stderrReportsMissingCpuFeature as a confirmed illegal-instruction event and records the machine as lacking AVX2 before downloading the baseline binary, while ordinary exit 3 passes through untouched.
25f1d61530c6d58db394b59db12e97c113e9322d.evidence: In cli/release-core/launcher.js, stderrReportsMissingCpuFeature() tests Bun's stderr tail against BUN_NO_AVX2_FEATURE and BUN_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION_PANIC regexes, and attachExitHandler() now captures stderrTail for any non-zero exit (code !== 0 || signal) instead of only Windows native crash codes, feeding it to tryFallbackToBaseline().
25f1d61530c6d58db394b59db12e97c113e9322d.migration: Freebuff, Codebuff, and Codecane users on pre-AVX2 Windows CPUs no longer hit a crash-loop on the optimized build and are automatically moved to the baseline binary on the next launch.

25f1d61530c6d58db394b59db12e97c113e9322d.text: When you start Freebuff or Codebuff on an older Windows PC that lacks AVX2 (a common CPU feature), the launcher now reads Bun's crash output and recognizes the exact phrase Bun prints when it detects that missing feature. This stops a restart loop on pre-2013 CPUs, where the optimized build crashed on every launch. Developers using the Freebuff CLI or desktop app on such machines are automatically moved to the slower, compatible baseline build on the next launch, with no action required. The fix is live for anyone updating to the current version.

01e5a44d74437dcbcf3d5950cc678cc3913fb33a.title: Release launcher verifies download sha256 before extraction and pins
01e5a44d74437dcbcf3d5950cc678cc3913fb33a.summary: The shared launcher (`cli/release-core/launcher.js`) now resolves an expected sha256 per target from the wrapper's own `binaryChecksums` map or the registry document, and `downloadAndExtract` runs `verifyFileSha256` against the partial archive before gunzipping or extracting it. A new `write-binary-checksums.js` stamps one hex digest per key in `PLATFORM_TARGET_KEYS` into each product package's `package.json` during the release publish job, and `verifyChecksums` fails the publish if any target is missing or malformed, so the launcher fails closed on an unverifiable archive. The package index files (`cli/release/index.js`, `cli/release-staging/index.js`, `freebuff/cli/release/index.js`) now forward `packageJson.binaryChecksums ?? null` into `createLauncher`, and `http.js` adds `evaluateRedirect` plus the `REDIRECT_ALLOWED_HOST_SUFFIXES` allowlist so follow-up redirects may only land on `*.githubusercontent.com` (plus the explicit hosts). This is the snapshot's most user-relevant change because it gates every self-update and install through an npm-trusted checksum rather than the download origin. It is accompanied by three other changes: a CLI trust gate for repository `.agents` directories, a `--trust-agents` opt-in flag and `CODEBUFF_TRUST_AGENT_DIRS` env var wired through `cli-args.ts`/`index.tsx`, SDK exports of `listLocalAgentFiles`, `getDefaultAgentDirs`, and `MCP_CONFIG_FILE_NAME` so hosts can build their own gates, and a documentation section in `docs/agents-and-tools.md`.

9904cc1e3ed78b5d42266bbab905cb6dc7deef7a.title: CLI clamps credentials.json and config dir to owner-only permissions
9904cc1e3ed78b5d42266bbab905cb6dc7deef7a.summary: The CLI now writes `credentials.json` with mode `0o600` and creates the config directory with mode `0o700` in `cli/src/utils/auth.ts`, so the bearer token stored in `credentials.json` is restricted to owner read/write on POSIX systems. Because `writeFileSync` only applies `mode` when creating a file, a new `tightenCredentialsFileMode` helper runs `fs.chmodSync` after each write and again on read inside `getUserCredentials`, so existing installs with a umask-wide file are repaired on the next launch. The chmod is skipped on Windows (where POSIX mode bits do not apply) and wrapped in try/catch so a failed chmod never costs a user their login.
9904cc1e3ed78b5d42266bbab905cb6dc7deef7a.evidence: In `cli/src/utils/auth.ts`, the diff adds two constants `CREDENTIALS_FILE_MODE = 0o600` and `CONFIG_DIR_MODE = 0o700`, and applies them in `saveUserCredentials` (via `writeFileSync` { mode } and `mkdirSync` { mode: CONFIG_DIR_MODE }) and `clearUserCredentials` (via `writeFileSync` { mode }), plus a new `tightenCredentialsFileMode` helper that calls `fs.chmodSync` after each write and on every read inside `getUserCredentials`.

The `hollowToolNames` field is added to `ForeignClientVerdict` and populated via `isHollowSignatureTool` for logging.

fd93692e814f3a7a4a3e61773e10e58384120e64.text: Freebuff's assistant now works even when you hit a paywall or lose your connection, and the free model lineup gets two new AI options. The Freebuff CLI lets you start a BYOK (bring-your-own-key) session right from the paywall screen, so you can keep going with your own model key without needing a Freebuff session, and landing screens now tell you which server name they couldn't reach instead of just blaming your connection. The free model picker drops the old MiMo 2.5 model and gains MiMo 2.6 Flash (replacing 2.6) plus a separate MiMo 2.6 Pro entry that carries a launch-time price warning and a 50-Freebuck entitlement so cheaper sessions can't be used to access the dearest model. Ad attribution also gets more accurate: TikTok and Meta events now share a single email-matching path and TikTok activations are attributed to whether you signed up on web, desktop, or via the CLI rather than erroring on non-registration events. Upgrading means you get clearer error messages when the service is unreachable, a smoother paywall escape hatch with BYOK, two fresh AI model choices with transparent pricing caveats, and more precise ad-attribution tracking that doesn't break on desktop or CLI signups.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release centers on launching Freebuff's advertiser marketplace and a new trust-based rewards system, where users earn credits for engaging with promoted content and can trade those credits for free or premium AI coding sessions. The free model picker now leads with GLM 5.3 Flash as the default model across the CLI, web, and desktop apps, while Solar Pro 4 joins as a limited-time trial option with a 500,000-token context window. A new /reasoning slash command lets you control how deeply your selected model thinks before responding, with choices like low, high, or max, and these preferences save per model in your settings. Spend limits are now per-account and region-based instead of a flat $50 cap, with daily budgets that taper down as they get used up and special low ceilings for users on privacy-focused networks like VPNs or Tor. Desktop users on paid plans can now run up to three premium and eight unlimited sessions at once, and the model selector correctly respects your subscription status so paid models no longer get swapped out for limited ones before you even start a session. The desktop app is now out of beta, and behind the scenes the system tracks database health more carefully and cleans up abandoned tool calls so conversations don't get stuck. Upgrading gives you a more responsive, less error-prone coding assistant with clearer pricing, better model availability, and a new way to earn free usage through the ad engagement program.

f4b54393e76ba626a55362568da73407d21ec306.text: Freebuff has introduced a new paid experiment that controls how advertisers are charged for a specific type of discovery card shown to developers. This experiment splits eligible users into two groups at random (a display group and an agentic group) and charges the advertiser a fixed fee only when a user clicks through the agentic arm's first call to action, with a shared daily spending cap. Access is limited to authenticated Freebuff developers who are reached via the existing Supabase setup invitation flow, and the agentic arm additionally requires a compatible client version to bill. This is live today as an opt-in experiment for Freebuff's advertising partners and has no effect on free users or free-tier development sessions.

d6476fb2338726860dc502e70ce7ab58df809803.text: Freebuff's developers removed the Imprezia ad network entirely, so sponsored ads now come only from Gravity, Freebuff's own first-party promotions, or house campaigns. The change is on Freebuff's servers today, and it only affects Freebuff's internal ad-serving machinery. Users of the assistant will not notice any difference in their coding sessions, since ad placement is transparent and no personal usage limits, free-tier quotas, or billing were tied to the removed network.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This release adds a new /diagnostics command that shows you what the assistant is running and how it is using your computer's resources, and it adds GPT-5.6 Luna as a new free AI model you can pick in the model selector alongside a refreshed DeepSeek V4 Flash build that is now the recommended default. When you switch between chats or quit a session, the assistant now stops any work it was doing so your conversation history is not accidentally overwritten, and the installer can now download through HTTP proxies and safely resume interrupted downloads. New analytics events let the team see when desktop turns stall or get recovered, and model-locked rejections now show a clear message telling you to end the old session before picking a different model. Upgrading means you get a safer, more stable download and install process, clearer feedback when a model switch fails, and one more free model option to choose from in the picker.

3c07b6812b3b9cc2f95648b0f742b8c18187c4d4.text: The team added a guard to the release checklist that proves a cloned project's dotenv files can no longer hijack which backend the assistant talks to: the released binary is launched from a temp folder packed with steering.env files and asked to print its backend URL, which must match the clean directory's value. A new internal-only flag makes the binary print that resolved URL and exit before the normal menu loads, and the list of environment variables that are allowed to override the backend URL is now shared in one place so the checklist and the app agree on the rule. This is internal release tooling only (the maintainers' pre-ship test), so you don't need to change anything and you won't notice it while working.

776646ec33c0cf58d84bfabccd9d125332f6a73d.text: Freebuff operators can now configure the service to report paid sign-ups and engagement directly to X and TikTok through a server-to-server channel, alongside the existing Meta integration, using new dataset IDs and either simple token authentication or OAuth for X. These settings only take effect when the Freebuff operator has configured them at deployment time, and because nothing in the service currently calls this new code path, the feature is in place today but not yet active for any conversions. You do not need to change anything and will not see any difference in Freebuff as an end user.

bb25dfd2ea548ab5c4601c9468b64d19620936ab.text: The code that decides whether a free user is allowed to run a model has a new safety check: it now refuses any free-mode request that tries to sneak in a hidden 'paid' flag while claiming to be one of Freebuff's own agents, closing a gap that let some free attempts quietly bypass the ad-supported rules. Only the Freebuff engineering team can change the list of accounts that get special reporting treatment, and that list is read from a setting the operator configures, not from anything an advertiser or everyday user controls. For you as a reader there is nothing to change or notice, because the guard lives inside the shared core library and the wiring that actually applies it is being added in a separate step that is not part of this code drop.

b4bfaad3a07d6aa1d05f8a2fb2e7091083d67ddb.text: Freebuff added a fixed, version-controlled checklist and an independent fact-checker for sponsored coding tasks, so that when an advertiser's AI assistant claims a job is done, two things are now true: the checklist a reviewer signed off on is frozen and hashed (so it can't be quietly changed afterward), and a separate verifier runs the same deterministic checks on the actual repo output instead of trusting the assistant's word or any text embedded in source files. This is internal infrastructure for Freebuff's sponsored integration product that advertisers pay for, so everyday users of the Freebuff coding assistant are not affected and will not see new UI, model features, or changes to their sessions, quotas, or ad experience from this change right now.

5f884d4393da759d031d6ef7aed8c34cad19e2e3.text: Freebuff added the ability to report certain user actions, like signing up or subscribing, to Meta's ad tracking system. This is configured by whoever runs the Freebuff service through a setting that holds a Meta pixel ID; if that setting is not provided, the reporting feature stays off. When configured, Freebuff can send these events to Meta while respecting users' privacy choices like Do Not Track. You do not need to do anything and will not notice any change in how you use Freebuff.

621d00924062d5807e2963de2d49517bf669f02d.text: When a request for free AI coding help comes in, the system now checks not just that a tool has one of our recognizable names, but also that it carries the real parameter structure we define for that tool. This stops resale services from slipping in a fake tool with a correct name but an empty or wrong shape to bypass the check. The change is for the Freebuff engineering team only and is internal security plumbing: it strengthens a fraud-prevention gate so third-party proxies can no longer pretend to be a genuine Freebuff client. You will not see or do anything differently when using the assistant.

7c820ad975a16751494d83c24168fa7c22011fbc.text: The Freebuff pricing display now shows an off-peak discount line on model rows during hours the service considers cheaper for developers, and the model picker stays accurate even if you leave it open across the on-peak to off-peak transition. Freebuff developers using the CLI, web, or desktop app see a clearer price tag (with the normal price crossed out where a first-tab discount also applies) and a short note like 'Off-peak 5 Freebucks/hour until 10:00 AM' beside the model, while an already-running session keeps the price it started with, so nothing surprises you mid-session. This behavior is live today through a server-provided schedule, so you don't need to take any action to benefit from it.

9904cc1e3ed78b5d42266bbab905cb6dc7deef7a.text: The assistant's login file - where your secret access token lives - now automatically locks itself to be readable and writable only by you, so other people who use the same computer (or other programs running there) can no longer see or change it. This repair happens quietly whenever you sign in or out, and it also clears out an old, unused piece of data from a long-removed feature, but you will not see any new buttons or prompts. If you use the Freebuff CLI in your terminal, your saved login is already safer today with no action needed on your part.

6c663def758eed32ed8ae629a9f387204afb775e.text: When you open the model menu in the Freebuff CLI and a first-tab discount is active on a row, you now see the regular price crossed out next to the discounted one, so it is clear which models got the promotion and what the original cost was. This only affects Freebuff users who reach the model picker with the first-tab offer in effect; rows the discount did not move look the same as before. The discount itself and the prices you pay have not changed, only how the savings are shown.

dc653bb55aeb2a3a8e3e8b081ee7054e0638af9d.text: The Freebuff team added internal wiring that lets the desktop app ask you, step by step, before it sets up a Git repository for a sponsored task, showing you the files involved without ever reading their contents, and then records the non-billable events of that setup flow, like whether you accepted or declined. This change is intended for Freebuff's engineering team only and is not yet wired up to any customer-facing feature, so you will not see anything new or different in your daily use.

bfead8065f4f0e68f6247fa51973c73185d00525.text: The free assistant now offers GPT-5.6 Luna as a new choice from the model picker. Anyone using the free tier of Freebuff on the desktop, web, or terminal will see GPT-5.6 Luna appear as an available model when starting a new session or building a project. In everyday use, you can pick GPT-5.6 Luna from the model list and the assistant will use it for that task, including running it at a higher thinking level so it can reason through problems more deeply. The option is live today for all Freebuff users.

7129d45870e6486850aca5729015b555653ca7d1.text: A new advertiser marketplace is in place where companies pay a flat $0.50 for each real engagement (like, comment, or repost) when you interact with a promoted post on the Earn page, with campaigns buying daily budgets in $5 steps between $5 and $1000. In parallel, an earned-trust ladder of 11 levels was added so that engaging with promoted posts builds up your standing and unlocks extra free and premium sessions, raising the daily session ceiling to 7 on both pools. The free-tier base limits also shifted: the premium pool dropped from 5 to 4 sessions per day and the limited-region pool from 6 to 3, though those who earn a level climb back above where they started. This affects Freebuff's free users who see the Earn page, and it is live now through the updated README and release notes.

10ec4e5ad003a6c5bd72ba98ad322469581d3d69.text: The assistant's file-editing tools can now open, read, patch, and browse folders located anywhere on your computer, not just inside the folder you are currently working in. If you ask the assistant to look at a file using a full path on your machine or a path that steps outside your project, it will now do so and keep going, whereas before it would refuse and report the file as out of bounds. This matters when a task legitimately needs the assistant to inspect something outside the project, and the only thing you need to do is make sure the path you give is the one you want changed. Nothing in your free allowance, model access, or daily limits is affected by this change.

a35a239f7d9c26ba75a870f6d34022ce4dba9933.text: The engineering team added a strict data template that defines how non-billable 'discovery' invitations for reviewed generic advertiser offers must be structured, recording campaign metadata, framework and surface, setup reason, expiration, and policy and decision identifiers. This is internal-only work for the Freebuff engineering team; no parts of the application read this template yet. Nothing you see or do in your daily sessions changes today, and your coding sessions, free allowances, or personal quotas are not affected.

b1b3f20f9f48afaf5e8d5044f38be17e6eb442b7.text: The SDK now checks the app URL override against a security rule before using it: only encrypted web addresses (https) are accepted on any server, while non-encrypted ones (http) are only allowed on your own computer (localhost). If an unapproved address is found, it's ignored and a clear warning is shown once, then the software safely falls back to its built-in default. This is internal hardening for the developer toolkit, so you won't notice it unless you were trying to point the assistant at a custom local development server, in which case your http://localhost address will still work exactly as before.

06379878ff49e15244d63ec7360b85223d0e0f70.title: SDK exports rewind run state to the point of an edited user message
06379878ff49e15244d63ec7360b85223d0e0f70.summary: The SDK adds a function that cuts a stored run's `messageHistory` back to the user turn a host is editing, aligning the persisted `RunState` with the transcript a host shows when a user edits an earlier message. 4b2b9ba193f215d52fdda833622d4929ab3b2be8.title: Agent runtime reserves space for system, tools and step prompt before
4b2b9ba193f215d52fdda833622d4929ab3b2be8.summary: A new `fitToolResults` helper in `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/fit-tool-results.ts` clips fresh `read_files` contents and oversized JSON tool results so the latest tool calls and their results fit the remaining token budget after older history has been compacted. The runtime now passes a `fixedTokenCount` into `maybeCompactHistory` (system prompt, tool schemas and the step prompt plus its scaffolding), so the context budget is sized against the live request overhead rather than only against summary text. `compactRequestHistory` preserves the newest historical entries that fit the actual remainder, keeps steering prompts together, and reserves a legacy request as historical memory when the current prompt is absent.

The `loopAgentSteps` call site in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` now passes `fixedTokenCount` composed of `countTokens(system) + countTokensJson(toolsForTokenCount) + (stepPrompt ? ... : 0)`.

8ae0c9c1da31404dd515238cb4e196c13c2872fc.title: Stop agent runs stuck repeating an unchanged to-do list
8ae0c9c1da31404dd515238cb4e196c13c2872fc.summary: The agent runtime now detects when an assistant emits the same completed `write_todos` list repeatedly without any other tool use. When the tail of `agentState.messageHistory` contains three identical completed calls, a tagged recovery message is injected; at six, `TodoLoopError` is thrown and surfaced as a failed turn, preventing budget exhaustion on models like GLM that loop silently. The comparison keys on the task/status pair rather than object key order or provider call IDs, and only matched, completed calls are counted so interrupted or failed tool execution cannot masquerade as progress.
8ae0c9c1da31404dd515238cb4e196c13c2872fc.evidence: New file `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/todo-loop.ts` defines `trailingIdenticalTodoCalls`, `TodoLoopError`, and thresholds `TODO_LOOP_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD` (3) and `TODO_LOOP_STOP_THRESHOLD` (6); `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` calls `trailingIdenticalTodoCalls(agentState.messageHistory)` after tool results and throws `TodoLoopError` when consecutive identical `write_todos` calls reach the stop threshold, otherwise injects a tagged recovery user message.
8ae0c9c1da31404dd515238cb4e196c13c2872fc.migration: No migration is required; existing runs that were already looping will now terminate, and users may retry with a different model or reasoning level after the stop message appears.
