872fc2305848cdcdd0e5d4199e211b9f82831fe1.title: Advertiser reason redaction adds country exclusion codes in v2
872fc2305848cdcdd0e5d4199e211b9f82831fe1.summary: The advertiser reason redaction vocabulary versioned as advertiser_reason_redaction_2026_09_v2 now classifies country_excluded and country_unresolved eligibility reasons as show rules, surfacing them in the ADVERTISER_SAFE_REASON_CODES set without altering the generalize or hide boundaries for other reasons. These additions let the CAPI projection layer report country-based refusals as distinct, advertiser-owned facts rather than folding them into a generic temporarily_unavailable fallback. The change is confined to the operator eligibility projection table in common/src/constants/advertiser-reason-redaction.ts.
872fc2305848cdcdd0e5d4199e211b9f82831fe1.evidence: In common/src/constants/advertiser-reason-redaction.ts, ADVERTISER_REASON_REDACTION_VERSION changed from advertiser_reason_redaction_2026_09_v1 to advertiser_reason_redaction_2026_09_v2, and the ADVERTISER_OPERATOR_REASON_CODES and ADVERTISER_SAFE_REASON_CODES arrays plus the ADVERTISER_VISIBLE_REASONS map gained new country_excluded and country_unresolved entries with 'show' kind.

54ce330ea151686b4a999b1318617b6c6a069644.title: Freebucks header shows daily reset countdown
54ce330ea151686b4a999b1318617b6c6a069644.summary: freebucksHeaderLine in cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts takes an optional nowMs argument and appends a 'resets in 4h 12m' countdown via the new freebucksResetCountdown helper, which formats remaining time as days, hours and minutes, or 'now' once the window has passed. The picker in cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx passes its now clock into freebucksHeaderLine(freebucks, now) so metered accounts see the countdown alongside the daily balance, wallet and monthly allowance figures already rendered as a single string.
54ce330ea151686b4a999b1318617b6c6a069644.evidence: In cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts, freebucksHeaderLine gained an optional nowMs parameter that appends a freebucksResetCountdown(freebucks.daily.resetAt, nowMs) segment to the header line. In cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx, the metered header text now passes now (the picker's clock) to freebucksHeaderLine(freebucks, now).

f3857f1b81fa3b21e59eba6564a47a8edb64c5f3.title: Advertiser reason redaction and placement CPC band added
f3857f1b81fa3b21e59eba6564a47a8edb64c5f3.summary: Adds a new common/src/constants/advertiser-reason-redaction.ts module that projects operator eligibility reasons into a closed advertiser-safe set via projectAdvertiserReason, generalizing request-context and viewer-limit reasons while hiding holdout, no-campaigns, and aggregate verdicts, and failing unknowns closed to temporarily_unavailable. Adds advertiserPlacementCpcBand (AD_PLACEMENT_CPC_SELF_SERVE_CEILING_CENTS = 1_000) to freebuff-topups.ts so an operator ceiling only narrows the editable band, with a conservative $10 default when none is supplied. Adds a new ads.campaign_ingress_evidence_v1 event in axiom-only-log.ts carrying opaque advertiser and campaign ids to distinguish independent ingress binding from a join learned after click resolution, with raw click, event, and email fields excluded from the schema. The reason-redaction and ingress-evidence modules are definitions placed in common with no visible internal caller in this diff, so they have no runtime effect until a consumer reads them.
f3857f1b81fa3b21e59eba6564a47a8edb64c5f3.evidence: New file common/src/constants/advertiser-reason-redaction.ts defines ADVERTISER_OPERATOR_REASON_CODES, ADVERTISER_SAFE_REASON_CODES, ADVERTISER_VISIBLE_REASONS, and export projectAdvertiserReason; modified files common/src/constants/freebuff-topups.ts adds AD_PLACEMENT_CPC_SELF_SERVE_CEILING_CENTS and export advertiserPlacementCpcBand, and common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts adds ADS_CAMPAIGN_INGRESS_EVIDENCE_EVENT plus ADS_CAMPAIGN_INGRESS_EVIDENCE_FIELDS and the corresponding branch in getAxiomOnlyLogEvent.
f3857f1b81fa3b21e59eba6564a47a8edb64c5f3.unknowns: The consumers that will read projectAdvertiserReason and ADS_CAMPAIGN_INGRESS_EVIDENCE_EVENT are not present in this diff, so the rollout timing and which ad-reporting or campaign-health service ingests them remain unclear.

a852b83bdfb6dbc2fdc996eb33eecc2e1fbb2489.title: Ads fetch completed exports field names for decision-contract test
a852b83bdfb6dbc2fdc996eb33eecc2e1fbb2489.summary: The `ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS` schema in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` gains a DEPRECATED ALIAS of `inclusion_probability_ppm` plus new `inclusion_reason`, `user_key_version`, and `inclusion_probability_ppm` fields for COD-367. It also exports `ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELD_NAMES` so the decision-contract test can assert the Axiom half of the warehouse contract, which was previously pinned nowhere and could be edited without notice on a stream several dashboards and the yield read rely on.

17106e2e4b02aee3ffa07db72fad3327df43b1b2.title: End session refunds and pending receipts land in the Freebuff session
17106e2e4b02aee3ffa07db72fad3327df43b1b2.summary: The Freebuff session lifecycle now owns refund receipts in `cli/src/state/freebuff-session-store.ts`, which gained `releaseSlot` and `refreshRefund` methods after `releaseFreebuffSlot` and `endFreebuffSessionBestEffort` were removed from `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts`. Commentary on GLM_V53_FLASH_REASONING_EFFORTS updated to document that the removal of max is half of a fix; the other half is the reasoningEffort pin, and that MERGE_EFFORT_ALIASES still preserves max for BYOK and direct-API callers.

12f8f2bb5b72969b7114cec9f24ae47e7e5e4500.title: Token totals and rendering added to common util
12f8f2bb5b72969b7114cec9f24ae47e7e5e4500.summary: A new `common/src/util/tokens.ts` module introduces `totalTokens`, `freshInputTokens`, and `formatTokens` as the single definition for every surface that reports how many tokens Freebuff moved. `totalTokens` sums `inputTokens` plus `outputTokens` and fixes a prior double-count where cache reads were added again on top of `prompt_tokens`, which already includes the cached prefix. `freshInputTokens` subtracts `cacheReadTokens` from `inputTokens`, clamped at zero for providers that over-report cache reads, and `formatTokens` renders exact counts below 10,000 and abbreviated counts from thousands up to trillions.
12f8f2bb5b72969b7114cec9f24ae47e7e5e4500.evidence: New file `common/src/util/tokens.ts` defines `totalTokens`, `freshInputTokens`, and `formatTokens` and exports them; no existing reader is modified in this commit, per the module doc comment that says this figure is reported on more than one surface and once had two variants that disagreed.
12f8f2bb5b72969b7114cec9f24ae47e7e5e4500.unknowns: The commit adds the shared token utilities with no reader wired up yet, so which Freebuff surface will consume `totalTokens`, `freshInputTokens`, and `formatTokens` first is not shown in the diff.

dcc6b662d492759a0776826bd0ee32e36480baa4.title: Placements daily cap ceiling raised to 5000 dollars with shared bounds
dcc6b662d492759a0776826bd0ee32e36480baa4.summary: The placements daily cap maximum moved from 50_000 to 500_000 cents ($5,000/day) in common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts, and the bounds plus a clamp function plus a ladder of slider rungs plus a nearest-rung index were promoted to shared constants so the campaigns API and the builder validate the same range. The ceiling was previously sized around fixture campaigns ($25-$50/day) with headroom, and the shared definition fixes the two-hand-agreed literals that let the form offer a cap the API would reject. Whole-cent clamping and ladder-only slider resolution keep the numeric entry and the API both valid.
dcc6b662d492759a0776826bd0ee32e36480baa4.evidence: Added constants PLACEMENT_DAILY_CAP_MIN_CENTS (500), PLACEMENT_DAILY_CAP_MAX_CENTS (500_000), PLACEMENT_DAILY_CAP_DEFAULT_CENTS (2_500), and functions clampPlacementDailyCapCents, PLACEMENT_DAILY_CAP_LADDER, placementDailyCapLadderIndex in common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts; the ceiling comment notes the move from 50_000 to 500_000 cents on 2026-08-31.
dcc6b662d492759a0776826bd0ee32e36480baa4.unknowns: The diff shows the constant and helper definitions but does not show the campaigns API or console UI that now reads PLACEMENT_DAILY_CAP_MAX_CENTS to enforce the new ceiling. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

fcb16dec8af815505ae1dcc2d4f8be9c907fc814.title: Solar Pro 4 capped at one session a day in Freebuff free tier
fcb16dec8af815505ae1dcc2d4f8be9c907fc814.summary: Solar Pro 4 (`upstage/solar-pro4`) gains a per-model session cap of 1 per day in `FREEBUFF_PER_MODEL_SESSION_CAPS`, backed by a $0.50 per-session dollar ceiling in `FREEBUFF_PER_MODEL_SESSION_SPEND_CAPS`, because the uncapped row multiplied daily spend roughly seventyfold within fourteen hours on 2026-08-31. The catalog now exposes `SOLAR_PRO_4_OPENROUTER_ENDPOINT = 'upstage/zdr'` to pin the provider-tagged zero-data-retention route, and three new helpers (`freebuffModelLabel`, `isFreebuffExperimentalModel`, `getFreebuffPerModelSessionSpendCap`) plus `freebuffSessionSpendNotice` let refusals name the model as an experimental trial. `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` now describes Solar Pro 4 as an experimental, 1-session-a-day trial, and the comment marks this as a measurement window meant to come off once cache rate and $/msg stabilize.
fcb16dec8af815505ae1dcc2d4f8be9c907fc814.evidence: The diff adds a per-model session count cap for Solar Pro 4 in `FREEBUFF_PER_MODEL_SESSION_CAPS` (limit 1, pool `solar_pro4`) in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, adds `SOLAR_PRO_4_OPENROUTER_ENDPOINT = 'upstage/zdr'`, and adds a parallel per-session dollar ceiling in `FREEBUFF_PER_MODEL_SESSION_SPEND_CAPS` ($0.50) with helpers `freebuffModelLabel`, `isFreebuffExperimentalModel`, `getFreebuffPerModelSessionSpendCap`; it also adds `freebuffSessionSpendNotice` in `common/src/util/freebuff-model-availability.ts` and updates `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` to call Solar Pro 4 an experimental trial capped at 1 session a day.
fcb16dec8af815505ae1dcc2d4f8be9c907fc814.migration: No migration is required; Freebuff users on eligible sessions should pick another model if Solar Pro 4 stops mid-session, and the cap lifts automatically if the model graduates from its trial.
fcb16dec8af815505ae1dcc2d4f8be9c907fc814.unknowns: The diff does not show which gate or surface consumes `SOLAR_PRO_4_OPENROUTER_ENDPOINT`, nor when the measurement window will close and the cap lift.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds a new way to save your conversations to a file, brings two new AI models into the free tier (Muse Spark 1.3 across CLI/Desktop/Web/Cloud, and Solar Pro 4 in limited access), and switches the default free model to GLM 5.3 Flash. You can now type /export to save a chat as a Markdown or JSON file in your project folder, the model picker shows a currency-style Freebucks balance so you can see how many paid-model credits remain before hitting a paywall, and a one-time intro card explains Freebucks on first metered launch. Safety and accuracy improvements include geo-aware ad routing that keeps click-fraud floors intact, a monthly Freebucks allowance shown alongside today/week limits on the rate-limited screen, and day-scale wait formatting for monthly resets so refusals read like '26 days' instead of '622h 18m'. Upgrading gives you the /export command, the new default model, Muse Spark 1.3 availability across all surfaces, and a metered balance display that stops hiding your remaining paid-model credits behind a session counter.

17106e2e4b02aee3ffa07db72fad3327df43b1b2.text: When you end a Freebuff coding session, you now get a clearer, real-time update on your refund. The system keeps track of your session while it shuts down, so if something goes wrong (like the CLI closing while a session is still being cleaned up) it can retry and recover the correct refund amount, rather than guessing or losing your credit. Users on the free tier will notice that if they close their session or quit the app, the landing screen now shows a clear message when a refund is pending (like 'awaiting final usage') and then tells them exactly how many Freebucks were returned to their wallet once it's complete. The `/end-session` command also now clearly states you get 90% of your unused time back as a credit.

f3857f1b81fa3b21e59eba6564a47a8edb64c5f3.text: A new privacy filter has been added that automatically rewrites internal ad-placement reasons into a safe, simplified set of messages before showing them to advertisers. This only affects advertiser-facing reporting tools, so most users won't see anything different. The filter keeps sensitive details like 'you're in a holdout group' hidden, while still telling advertisers the essentials like 'your campaign is paused,' 'out of budget,' or 'temporarily unavailable.' Since it is brand new, it does not actually take effect anywhere yet until the reporting systems start using it.

a852b83bdfb6dbc2fdc996eb33eecc2e1fbb2489.text: Engineers added a safety net to their ad-tracking code so they can confirm that two separate reporting systems record exactly the same details about each ad opportunity. They also marked one old field as deprecated while keeping it around temporarily so existing dashboards don't break. This is internal test-suite and schema-maintenance work for Freebuff's engineering team, not a new feature or visible change. You will not notice any difference in how Freebuff behaves today.

01e5a44d74437dcbcf3d5950cc678cc3913fb33a.text: When the assistant updates or installs itself, the installer now checks a fingerprint (called a sha256 checksum) for the download before unpacking it, and it gets that fingerprint from the npm package registry, not from the download website. This prevents a compromised download server from secretly swapping in a different binary. You don't need to do anything; the verification happens automatically during installs and updates. The release packaging also gained a trust gate so repository-owned agent folders must be approved before the assistant loads them, and a --trust-agents flag you can set for non-interactive (for CI) runs.

8221e333895c0933b2ab58d669ac40272c339eb8.text: Freebuff now gives each paying plan its own hard daily spending limit, which replaces the old blanket regional limit for accounts on the new Freebucks meter. This applies to subscribers whose plan sets a daily dollar ceiling, while restricted-risk accounts still compose under that same base entry by minimum. If you hit your plan's ceiling, you see a specific refusal message explaining today's limit rather than a generic capacity notice, and the same leeway multiplier that lets an open session finish now applies to your plan's small ceiling. For everyone else, there is no visible change today: the feature is in place but only activates once the Freebucks meter is enabled for an account.

4ff67e17e1d2980de3411ac0f573e20160b845d8.text: The assistant has a new way to ask a sponsoring code change to commit its work safely. When an advertiser-sponsored task runs and writes code to a branch in your own repository, the sandbox now hands git the exact, minimal files it needs - the branch ref, the reflog, the commit lock and the object store - while keeping your hooks, config, packed-refs, other branches and other worktrees strictly read-only. A separate fix keeps the offer card watching a run that is still in progress, instead of stopping the moment it leaves the offered state. You will notice only that the sponsored thread you accepted stays open and updates until it is genuinely finished, and that its commits land in a branch you can open a pull request from.

48b5fee79a1016800772e01eafa8ceb3db346f98.text: The number of free daily sessions available to users in limited-access regions (such as those using a VPN or located outside supported countries) has been raised from 3 to 6 per day. This affects Freebuff users in those limited regions who rely on the MiMo model, which is the only model available to them without a paid plan. You will now get twice as many free one-hour coding sessions each day while in limited mode, and the updated session count is also reflected in the Freebuff command-line installer release notes.

6edee52fa9c4ab5511163f99269dd8613f0669f2.text: When Freebuff runs an advertiser-paid coding suggestion on your own computer (instead of in a remote, throwaway sandbox), a new local safety layer now decides which tools and files the suggestion is allowed to touch, then runs whatever does get approved inside a locked-down subprocess that gets the user's real home directory, SSH keys and credentials stripped out, a private scratch space of its own, and no ability to talk to your own machine over the local network. The rules refuse to start the run at all on Windows or on any machine where the OS-level sandbox cannot be set up, instead of silently running an uncontained process. This only affects the local-sponsored-task path that was just shipped; your normal Freebuff sessions are untouched.

0d2d7a08594e7172e82d0f59a6a4c8a6bcc001b4.text: The Freebuff assistant removed a strict daily limit that was limiting how often you could use the Solar Pro 4 AI model, so it now works just like the other premium models, letting you pick how to spend your daily premium usage across any of them. If you had hit that one-a-day wall yesterday while trying to use that specific model, youll no longer be blocked by it today, though the overall shared premium limit still applies. This change is live now for Freebuff users.

5d679590800f31569758fe1002a5ef087668f7b7.text: The assistant's behind-the-scenes helper that thinks hard about your request switched from an expensive Google model to a cheaper DeepSeek model, after the free credits that paid for Google ran out (live today). It still does the same job: breaking down your request quietly before answering, but it now takes fewer resources so the service can keep it running. You notice nothing changes in how the assistant answers you. The model name shown internally stays the same even though the engine under the hood is different.

358336a18e557894e7bbdd623c43e34f1bc54f6f.text: This release updates the Freebuff free-tier AI coding assistant with new ad features, model changes, and spend-management updates. Sponsor break headlines can now have one highlighted word in accent color while staying within the character limit for ad slots, and Freebuff Pro sponsor breaks include new hero image assets. The free model picker switched from Muse Spark 1.3 to Muse Spark 1.2 because the newer version kept returning model_not_found errors. A new Freebucks daily reset countdown shows how long until your balance refreshes. Hard monthly spend limits were replaced with softer session pacing that pauses usage rather than blocking it. Premium sessions can now use up to five models, and the limited-tier plan now recommends GLM 5.3 Flash as its leading option while keeping DeepSeek V4 Flash as the fallback choice. The turn spend limit error message was simplified to remove confusing diagnosis. A pending refund notice now appears when ending a session, showing any unspent-cost refund, and the same key press can no longer dismiss the Freebucks intro card and accidentally start a session on the cheapest model.

321907165f73f9a66f780f275f38e27092f87aa9.text: The Freebuff engineering team added a new internal setting that lets the company's own ad system get first look at premium ad slots in top-tier countries, before passing the request to an outside ad partner. The setting defaults to off and no external ad surface has wired it up yet, so it has no effect on anyone today. When a surface eventually enables the setting, the new telemetry now records that Freebuff's own ad filled the slot, instead of marking the request as skipped for the outside partner. This is purely internal ad-routing logic and does not touch user accounts, Freebucks, or free model access.

b6775f5c3e83b041816b59b2c2bb6dcadadf9f91.text: The preview that shows advertisers how their ad will look in the terminal now uses three common widths instead of the old set. The new choices are 48, 80 and 100 columns, which are the sizes most people actually use, replacing the previous 20, 48 and 60. The very narrow 20-column case is still supported behind the scenes so a real terminal that is that small still renders the ad correctly, but it is no longer offered as a preview option. This affects only the advertiser preview tool and does not change what you see in your own terminal.

70f1d8d632956affcf4ef483ae0c317dfd8d9403.text: The default AI model that new users get when they start a coding task has been slowed down by default, so it thinks and reasons more carefully before taking action. This change affects the Freebuff free tier (the one funded by ads), which uses this AI model to drive every developer session on the CLI, web, and desktop. Most of the time you will not notice the difference except that your first task may finish using less trial-and-error and come out cleaner, since the assistant now takes slightly longer to start and plan before running tools, instead of jumping straight into them.

fcb16dec8af815505ae1dcc2d4f8be9c907fc814.text: Freebuff has added a new AI model called Solar Pro 4 to its free tier, but you can only use it for one coding session per day. This is a test period so the team can see how much it costs to run before deciding if it stays. If you try to use Solar Pro 4 and it stops after one session, switching to another model will let you keep working right away. No action is needed unless you were hoping to use Solar Pro 4 heavily, in which case it is temporarily limited while the company monitors expenses.

12f8f2bb5b72969b7114cec9f24ae47e7e5e4500.text: A single, shared way to count and display how many tokens the assistant processed in a conversation was added to the Freebuff codebase. It fixes a prior bug where cached tokens were counted twice, and it shows both the total token figure and the smaller figure for tokens the assistant actually had to read for itself. This change is internal: it sets up the counting rules now, but no screen or report in the Freebuff app currently uses it yet, so you will not notice anything different in daily use. It only takes effect once a future release wires these helpers into the usage display.

dcc6b662d492759a0776826bd0ee32e36480baa4.text: Advertisers can now set a campaign's daily spending limit as high as $5,000 per day, up from $500, and that same limit is now checked in one shared place so the form and the billing system always agree. This affects only the advertisers who buy and manage ad campaigns in the Freebuff console; it does not touch your free coding assistant experience. If you run an ad campaign, you'll see the higher ceiling right away with no action needed, and the slider you use to pick a daily cap now moves in bigger steps at higher amounts so you don't lose fine control where you need it.

2f0ded02ccab4cb1346a9f602d6391424b860994.text: After an advertiser-funded coding run finishes and commits its changes, the assistant now shows a 'Setup → verify' section in the terminal. That section repeats the advertiser's landing link as plain copyable text and walks through the next steps to connect the project and confirm it works. This applies to developers using the Freebuff CLI who run sponsored proposals that reach the committed, landed, or merged states. Nothing changes for already-finished or failed runs, and the new guidance only appears once local code changes exist.

54ce330ea151686b4a999b1318617b6c6a069644.text: The Freebuff balance line now shows a live countdown of how long until your daily Freebucks pool refills, for example 'resets in 4h 12m', alongside your current balance, wallet, and monthly usage figures, so metered accounts can see exactly when the next fresh pool arrives. It only affects you if you are on the pay-per-session (metered) plan; free accounts, which use session windows instead of a balance, see nothing new, and the countdown appears only in the CLI's model picker, matching what the web and desktop apps already show. Today, when you open the model picker in the terminal, the balance header now carries the countdown as a single line that cannot wrap, keeping the layout stable while still updating with the real time remaining until midnight Pacific.

e1792f99509f9abc40904b9f4dad683d57510329.text: A new set of rules was added for deciding when an ad truly counts as 'seen', specifically that at least half of it must stay on screen for a full second while the page is in the foreground. This is for internal use by the Freebuff engineering team, since it establishes the standard for measuring ad viewability across the web and desktop apps. It does nothing on its own yet, because the change only sets up the measuring stick and no part of the app is wired to read it, so you will not notice any difference in daily use.

1bb18115cb107d956fa0026d5b9ae840db62b72e.title: Block sensitive files with strikethrough UI
1bb18115cb107d956fa0026d5b9ae840db62b72e.summary: A new FileFilter in createRunConfig blocks sensitive files (.env, .pem, id_rsa, credentials, etc.) and tags .env.example/.env.sample/.env.template as example-only; getFiles applies that filter, returns FILE_READ_STATUS.IGNORED for blocked files and prepends FILE_READ_STATUS.TEMPLATE to example content. The CLI read_files component renders blocked paths in strikethrough with '(blocked)' and example paths with '(allowed - example only)'. FILE_READ_STATUS.IGNORED is renamed to '[BLOCKED]' and a TEMPLATE status is added to common/src/old-constants.ts, and the SDK now exports getFiles plus the FileFilter and FileFilterResult types.
1bb18115cb107d956fa0026d5b9ae840db62b72e.evidence: cli/src/utils/create-run-config.ts defines isSensitiveFile (matching SENSITIVE_EXTENSIONS, SENSITIVE_BASENAMES, SENSITIVE_PATTERNS) and isEnvTemplateFile (ENV_TEMPLATE_SUFFIXES), and createRunConfig wires a FileFilter returning {status:'blocked'} / {status:'allow-example'} that sdk/src/tools/read-files.ts getFiles consumes, prepending FILE_READ_STATUS.TEMPLATE to example files. cli/src/components/tools/read-files.tsx now renders sensitive files with strikethrough and '(blocked)' via FilePathsDescription, while sdk/src/index.ts exports getFiles, FileFilter, and FileFilterResult. common/src/old-constants.ts renames FILE_READ_STATUS.IGNORED to '[BLOCKED]' and adds TEMPLATE: '[TEMPLATE]'.
1bb18115cb107d956fa0026d5b9ae840db62b72e.unknowns: The diff does not show consumers outside the CLI and SDK read_files path for the new FileFilter, nor whether blocking is enforced server-side or only on the client.

changes.what: read_files tool renders sensitive files in strikethrough with '(blocked)' and env templates with '(allowed - example only)' via FilePathsDescription in read-files.tsx, backed by isSensitiveFile and isEnvTemplateFile from create-run-config.

getFiles applies an optional FileFilter, returning IGNORED for blocked files and prepending the TEMPLATE marker to example files; run.ts threads fileFilter through requestFiles and requestOptionalFile.
FILE_READ_STATUS.IGNORED renamed to '[BLOCKED]' and a new TEMPLATE: '[TEMPLATE]' status added to old-constants.
getFiles, FileFilter, and FileFilterResult exported from sdk/src/index.ts.

31cf16f7e26bd33459b002c33bc55747baf8b2ca.title: Rename str replace replacement fields to old String and new String
31cf16f7e26bd33459b002c33bc55747baf8b2ca.summary: The str_replace and propose_str_replace tool parameter schemas were updated so the replacement objects use `oldString` and `newString` instead of the short `old` and `new` keys. The change spans the type declarations in `.agents/types/tools.ts`, `agents/types/tools.ts`, and `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/tools.ts`, the zod schemas in `common/src/tools/params/tool/str-replace.ts` and `common/src/tools/params/tool/propose-str-replace.ts`, the alias normalization in `common/src/tools/params/utils.ts`, the runtime destructure in `packages/agent-runtime/src/process-str-replace.ts`, the validation hints in `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts`, the SDK result messages in `sdk/src/tools/change-file.ts`, and the agent instruction prompts baked into `agents-graveyard/editor/reviewer-editor.ts`, `agents/editor/best-of-n/editor-implementor.ts`, and `agents/editor/editor.ts`. The CLI rendering side was simplified in `cli/src/components/tools/str-replace.tsx`, which drops its inline `extractValueForKey` parser and instead delegates to the shared `extractDiff`, `extractFilePath`, and `isCreateFile` helpers imported from `../../utils/implementor-helpers`, so the component now guards the diff viewer with `diffText.length > 0`.
31cf16f7e26bd33459b002c33bc55747baf8b2ca.evidence: The diff renames the `old`/`new` replacement fields to `oldString`/`newString` in the `StrReplaceParams` and `ProposeStrReplaceParams` schemas within `.agents/types/tools.ts`, `agents/types/tools.ts`, and `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/tools.ts`; updates agent instruction prompts in `agents-graveyard/editor/reviewer-editor.ts`, `agents/editor/best-of-n/editor-implementor.ts`, and `agents/editor/editor.ts` to reference `oldString`/`newString`; and rewrites `cli/src/components/tools/str-replace.tsx` to remove its local `extractValueForKey` parser and instead call `extractDiff`, `extractFilePath`, and `isCreateFile` from `../../utils/implementor-helpers`.
31cf16f7e26bd33459b002c33bc55747baf8b2ca.migration: If you use the str_replace or propose_str_replace tool, update any integration that reads or emits the old `old`/`new` keys to use `oldString`/`newString` instead.

changes.what: Renamed the str_replace and propose_str_replace replacement fields from `old`/`new` to `oldString`/`newString`.
Updated the zod schemas and alias normalization so the replacement objects use `oldString`/`newString`.
Destructured the replacement objects as `oldString`/`newString` in the str_replace processor.
Adjusted the change-file tool to produce the new success and failure result messages.
Removed the local diff parser in str-replace.tsx and reused the shared implementor-helpers extractors.
Updated editor agent instruction prompts and examples to use the new field names.

6b1963707ad3659f9d2308535dff59f317cd8174.title: Desktop E rows observed, CLI waivers unchanged, commit attribution
6b1963707ad3659f9d2308535dff59f317cd8174.summary: The Desktop `SPONSORED_CONFORMANCE_ACCEPTED_WAIVERS` table drops E-3, E-4 and E-7 (now measured by a real Desktop accept walk and a real PR) and keeps E-5 wived as 'not deliberately driven'; the CLI block still lists E-3, E-4 and E-7 as 'no execution' alongside E-1, E-2 and E-6, because the CLI still has no producer that inserts a card into a transcript. The conformance comment also restates that one macOS/loopback run is neither reliable nor a Linux/Windows/production claim, and that E-5's incidental `failed` rows are not a deliberate measurement. In parallel, the agent template types (`agent-definition.ts`, `agent-template.ts`, `dynamic-agent-template.ts`), the runtime tool assembly (`run-agent-step.ts`, `prompts.ts`) and the commit guidance (`run-terminal-command.ts`) gain a `suppressCommitAttribution` field that serves a trailer-free `run_terminal_command` description, and `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts` adds a literal grant for `/private/var/select/sh` so `/bin/sh`'s shell-selector noise does not reach the model as tool error output.
6b1963707ad3659f9d2308535dff59f317cd8174.evidence: The diff to common/src/ads/sponsored-proposal-conformance.ts replaces the previous Desktop waiver block (which listed E-3, E-4, E-5, E-7 as 'never run...') with a retained Desktop waiver for only E-5, and adds an extensive retained CLI waiver block that lists E-3, E-4, and E-7 (alongside E-1, E-2, E-6) as 'no execution' - these CLI entries are unchanged from the pre-existing block, not removed.
6b1963707ad3659f9d2308535dff59f317cd8174.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer that reads AgentTemplate.suppressCommitAttribution in a dynamic/publish path, or any rollout flag for the Desktop E-row measurement. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Desktop waiver block now keeps only E-5; E-3, E-4, E-7 remain waived on cli as 'no execution'
Adds the suppressCommitAttribution opt to the user-facing agent definition type
Mirrors suppressCommitAttribution onto the backend AgentTemplate type
Mirrors suppressCommitAttribution onto the dynamic agent definition schema
Reads suppressCommitAttribution off the template and forwards it into getToolSet
getToolSet swaps in runTerminalCommandNoAttributionDescription when suppressCommitAttribution is true

f9b0815704eb34ebed2b8852b1a27c4902664d58.title: Add Freebucks balance types to session responses and bump release
f9b0815704eb34ebed2b8852b1a27c4902664d58.summary: The freebuff session response now carries a freebucks block on the `none`, `active`, and `ended` states, backed by the new `FreebuffFreebucksInfo` (with `balance`, `daily`/`weekly`/`monthly` `FreebuffFreebucksWindow`s, `bindingWindow`, optional `planDaily`, and `prices`) plus the `getFreebucksInfo` accessor, so clients can render Freebucks spendable balance and per-model session prices from the session wire shape rather than a separate call. This rides every state for the same reason subscription does, since the balance is shown in the picker, mid-session and after it, and the detail field `planDaily` only appears for subscribed plans. The freebuff release `package.json` version is bumped from `0.0.162` to `0.0.163`.
f9b0815704eb34ebed2b8852b1a27c4902664d58.evidence: In `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, the diff adds `FreebuffFreebucksWindow`, `FreebuffFreebucksInfo`, and `getFreebucksInfo`, and threads `freebucks?: FreebuffFreebucksInfo` through the `none`, `active`, and `ended` branches of `FreebuffSessionServerResponse`. In `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, `version` changes from `0.0.162` to `0.0.163`.
f9b0815704eb34ebed2b8852b1a27c4902664d58.unknowns: The server-side producer of the new `freebucks` block and its rollout audience are not shown in these files.

changes.what: Adds Freebucks window, balance, and accessor types and wires the freebucks field into session states.
Bumps the Freebuff CLI release version from 0.0.162 to 0.0.163.

c3521fd87fc4c8f683e73c08251772dc976ca8ec.title: Add HMAC-shielded account deletion proof for Convex purges
c3521fd87fc4c8f683e73c08251772dc976ca8ec.summary: The `common` utility `account-deletion-proof.ts` introduces `createAccountDeletionProof` and `verifyAccountDeletionProof`, which derive an HMAC-SHA256 over a payload that length-prefixes the `PROOF_VERSION`, identity subject, and deletion code so each field cannot collide in the encoded string. The signing secret must be at least 32 characters, and verification uses a constant-time comparison over fixed-size hex signatures. As noted in the JSDoc, the proof is minted only after Adbuff reports an active suppression fence and is presented on each bounded Convex purge pass, never returned to the browser.
c3521fd87fc4c8f683e73c08251772dc976ca8ec.evidence: New file `common/src/util/account-deletion-proof.ts` defines `PROOF_VERSION = 'v1'` and exports `createAccountDeletionProof` and `verifyAccountDeletionProof`, using HMAC-SHA256 over a length-prefixed payload bound to the identity subject and deletion code.
c3521fd87fc4c8f683e73c08251772dc976ca8ec.unknowns: The diff does not show the Next route that mints the proof or the Convex purge consumer that verifies it, so the exact server-side integration is not visible.

d88c688727818ebcf7ce9bdcdcc18ba16d7946a2.title: Placement CPC floor override validators added to common constants
d88c688727818ebcf7ce9bdcdcc18ba16d7946a2.summary: Two exported functions, `isValidPlacementCpcFloorOverride` and `effectivePlacementCpcFloorCents`, are added to `common/src/constants/freebuff-topups.ts` so the four layers that price a campaign (admission validators, the `/r/` click-recording guard, the reprice clamp, and the table CHECK) can agree on a single floor. `effectivePlacementCpcFloorCents` resolves an operator-set override through `isValidPlacementCpcFloorOverride` and falls back to `AD_PLACEMENT_CPC_FLOOR_CENTS` (100) otherwise, so out-of-range or malformed overrides fail SAFE by raising the floor back to $1. This lives beside the constant rather than next to any caller because two of those layers sit in `packages/internal` and two in `freebuff/web`.

The existing constant `AD_PLACEMENT_CPC_FLOOR_CENTS` (100) is retained as the rate-card floor, and the new `effectivePlacementCpcFloorCents` function resolves any override through `isValidPlacementCpcFloorOverride` before falling back to that global floor.
d88c688727818ebcf7ce9bdcdcc18ba16d7946a2.migration: If you maintain the placements rail, no migration is required because `effectivePlacementCpcFloorCents` replaces any local copy of the floor-resolution predicate with a single shared export from `common/src/constants/freebuff-topups.ts`.

443f19f0eae03bcbc0dfb3ac6a5cd869fb9dcbae.title: Mid-turn /plan /interview /review and /skill queue instead
443f19f0eae03bcbc0dfb3ac6a5cd869fb9dcbae.summary: The `/plan`, `/interview`, and `/review` commands previously called `sendMessage()` directly without checking whether a run was in progress, which forced `registerActiveRun` to stop the in-flight run (root cause: a user report in #1211 where a mid-turn message overwrote the active job instead of queuing). This commit routes all of those - plus `/skill:<name>` - through `dispatchSkillPrompt`, which mirrors the busy-check-then-queue-else-send logic already used by `/skill:<name>` inline args, so a mid-turn submit waits its turn instead of interrupting. A new `cli/src/utils/steering-buffer.ts` mailbox lets the router echo a bubble immediately and hand mid-turn plain text to the active run at its next step boundary, falling back to the queue for anything steering can't carry (attachments, slash commands, pending bash output, a non-empty queue, or no active run). `use-send-message.ts` wires `activateSteering`, `drainSteeringMessages`, and `deactivateSteering` into the SDK run lifecycle via `RunOptions.drainSteeringMessages` and a new `pauseQueue` option, so undelivered steering text is retracted and requeued rather than lost. There are six other supporting changes in the same area: `prompt-builders.ts` adds `buildSkillPrompt` for byte-identical prompts across the args and input-mode entry paths; `chat-store.ts` adds `pendingSkillName`, `setPendingSkillName`, and `enterSkillMode`; `input-modes.ts` adds a `skill` mode config; `chat-input-bar.tsx` labels the skill-mode banner with the pending skill name; `status-bar.tsx` renders context usage via a new `format-token-count.ts`; and `chat.tsx` passes `hasQueuedMessages` through to the router.
443f19f0eae03bcbc0dfb3ac6a5cd869fb9dcbae.evidence: command-registry.ts adds `dispatchSkillPrompt`, routes `/skill:<name>` bare invocation into skill input mode via `enterSkillMode`, and queues mid-turn; router.ts calls `dispatchSkillPrompt` from the skill-mode branch and adds `canSteer` logic in `routeUserPrompt`; new files `cli/src/utils/steering-buffer.ts` and `cli/src/utils/format-token-count.ts` provide the steering mailbox and token formatting; chat-store.ts adds `pendingSkillName`, `setPendingSkillName`, and `enterSkillMode`; status-bar.tsx imports `formatContextUsage` to render context usage; chat-input-bar.tsx reads `pendingSkillName` to label the skill mode banner.

bd4a417e32556ffb2004437274d0cdd893ad3907.title: Agentic ad funnel event vocabulary added for sponsored proposals
bd4a417e32556ffb2004437274d0cdd893ad3907.summary: A new dependency-free module `common/src/constants/agentic-ad-events.ts` defines the event vocabulary for sponsored proposals surfaced through the first-party placements rail, covering stages from `proposal_offered` through `tool_used`. Of these, only accepted is billable, and it settles as a CPC click through the existing first-party click path (`settleFirstPartyClick`) rather than via funnel-event recording; all other stages are telemetry for pricing the next campaign. A second subset, `AGENTIC_POSTBACK_EVENT_TYPES`, restricts which events an advertiser may report via the S2S postback (`POST /api/ads/agentic/postback`) to `account_created` and `tool_used`.

872fc2305848cdcdd0e5d4199e211b9f82831fe1.text: The reason list was updated so that country-based refusals are now reported as two separate, advertiser-owned facts instead of being lumped into a generic fallback. Only the Freebuff engineering team maintains this change, which affects how ad-attribution messages are shaped internally. You will not notice anything different in daily use.

6b1963707ad3659f9d2308535dff59f317cd8174.text: The assistant's built-in guidance for making git commits now gives agent authors a way to turn off the automatic "Co-Authored-By: Codebuff" and "Generated with Codebuff" lines that normally get appended to commit messages, so an agent writing code into someone else's project can keep its commits free of that branding. The feature is wired through the agent definition and runtime tool set, but it only takes effect when an agent is explicitly configured to use it - no published agent in the catalog does so yet, and a normal user run is unchanged. Alongside it, the macOS sandbox that runs sponsored (advertiser-backed) tasks stops every command from printing a repetitive permission error about the shell selector, while still keeping that boundary in place.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: Freebuff 1.0.687 adds a new export-to-file slash command, a Freebucks currency-based model picker, Solar Pro 4 model access, and a sponsor dock detail panel, while removing FutureSearch deep research and withdrawing Gemini 3.8 Flash from the free model picker. You can now save any chat to a file (markdown or JSON), see your AI usage priced as Freebucks currency instead of session counts on metered accounts, and pick Solar Pro 4 as an unmetered option. The CLI landing screen shows day-scale wait times for monthly resets, hides the legacy session counter when metered, and surfaces a one-time Freebucks intro card. A Ctrl+O shortcut opens an expandable sponsor ad panel with Escape-to-close, and 429 rate-limit errors now stop retrying and show the server's message instead of a countdown. Upgrading gives you the new model choices, the file export feature, clearer metered-usage pricing, and the sponsor panel without the withdrawn Gemini model.

a71de944590b9d02d5c182133e8c17de5e600db0.text: The assistant's default thinking depth for a specific free model has been turned back up to its deepest setting, after it was briefly lowered to avoid the model getting stuck repeating itself. The few users who choose this model on the free plan will now see it think more carefully by default, but may occasionally see it repeat the same step in a task. This is live today.

f9b0815704eb34ebed2b8852b1a27c4902664d58.text: When you open the Freebuff assistant, the session info now includes your current Freebucks balance and the price per model, so the interface can show how many paid sessions you can still start and which models those credits will cover. This affects anyone using Freebuff who has Freebucks credits, and it appears in the model picker, during a session, and after a session ends. The change is live today and requires no action from you; older versions of the app simply ignore the new information and continue to work as before.

f3e97864f5d12d3df41f0bc10e08b5afd66dd101.text: Freebuff moved the user-facing parts of account standing (the names, labels, and descriptions for levels like Getting Started, Verified, Established, and Core) into a new file, while keeping the internal scoring and limits that determine which level an account earns in a separate, non-public file. This is an internal reorganization of how the product stores and shares account-standing text, so Freebuff engineers can update the user-visible wording without also exposing the numerical limits that attackers could target. It affects no one outside the Freeuff engineering team; there is no visible change for users today.

443f19f0eae03bcbc0dfb3ac6a5cd869fb9dcbae.text: When you ask the assistant to plan, interview, or review something while it is already working on a previous request, your message now waits its turn instead of cutting off what is in progress. This only affects you if you submit one of those commands mid-turn - your typing will be queued and run in order rather than interrupting. You do not need to change anything; the fix is live today and just makes mid-turn submissions behave consistently with every other message you send.

d88c688727818ebcf7ce9bdcdcc18ba16d7946a2.text: Operators can now set a lower per-click price for a specific ad campaign, but if that custom price is missing, zero, or outside the allowed range, the system automatically falls back to the standard one-dollar minimum instead of letting the campaign run at a broken price. This only affects the ad-placement pricing engine that advertisers use to buy slots in the Freebuff interfaces, so it does not change anything for people writing code with the assistant. No action is required from users or advertisers, and the visible day-to-day experience is unchanged.

a67e89052816db2de4de5bc42c4b6c318f91797a.text: Paid subscribers can now run more Freebuff Desktop sessions at the same time: three premium sessions and eight unlimited sessions, up from one and three for free users. This only affects people on a paid plan, who previously were limited to one premium tab at a time. If you subscribe, you can now have several of the more capable models open side by side, while free users continue to see the tighter limits.

bd4a417e32556ffb2004437274d0cdd893ad3907.text: Freebuff added a shared list of names that track how a sponsored, AI-powered task moves from being shown to a developer, through being accepted and turned into a code change, to later results the advertiser reports. The team that buys and measures these sponsored tasks now has one consistent vocabulary to record every stage, but only the moment a developer accepts the task counts as a billable click, settled through the same existing payment path as a normal ad click. For everyone else, nothing in your daily experience changes: this is internal bookkeeping that helps price future campaigns, and it is already live today.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release makes a new AI model called GLM 5.3 Flash the default choice for free users across the CLI, web, and desktop apps, and adds Solar Pro 4 as another free model option. The free model list now leads with GLM 5.3 Flash (unmetered and uncapped), followed by Solar Pro 4, with DeepSeek V4 Pro and MiniMax M3 removed from the free picker. A new /reasoning slash command lets you control how hard the selected model thinks on each task, persisting your preference per model. Per-account daily spend ceilings replace the old flat $50 limit, using region, email, and privacy-network signals to flag abuse while keeping suspicious traffic flowing through honeypots for stronger evidence. Privacy-focused traffic (VPN, proxy, Tor) now lowers the restricted daily ceiling to $0.50 and triggers a shared refusal notice naming 'VPN' and 'connecting directly' instead of leaking detection signals. The CLI model selector now shows local-time return windows for off-peak-only models, and subscription tiers were resized with Starter at 3/10/50 and Plus at 7/20/125 daily/5-day/monthly sessions, both now topping up the free base pool instead of replacing it.

477b0e47facf165557cca9b60a070dacc3f6f9d9.text: When a paying subscriber chooses a premium model from the picker, the CLI now keeps that selection all the way through to session start instead of swapping it back for a free model. This affects only Freebuff subscribers whose plan includes paid models. In practice, subscribers who explicitly pick their plan model will now start their session on that model, rather than being quietly downgraded before the session begins.

72fffec8570aebd6a07ae1fce403fcdedee01dbd.text: The assistant has removed the daily usage limit on GLM 5.3 Flash, making it a free-to-use model for everyone on Freebuff. This change affects Freebuff users on all plans, and it means you can now use GLM 5.3 Flash without worrying about it counting against your premium allowance or session caps. Starting today, GLM 5.3 Flash joins MiMo and DeepSeek V4 Flash as completely unmetered options, so you can switch to it freely whenever it is best suited for your task, just like any other free model on the list.

31cf16f7e26bd33459b002c33bc55747baf8b2ca.text: The assistant renamed the field names used when replacing text in a file from the short labels "old" and "new" to the clearer "oldString" and "newString", so the same edit operation still works but uses unambiguous names everywhere the assistant, its helper agents, the terminal display, and the developer tools read these fields. Developers, agent authors, and tools that directly read or send these edit fields need to use the new names. In daily use nothing looks different to you - edits still apply the same way - but any custom integration that still uses the old short names should switch to the longer ones.

1bb18115cb107d956fa0026d5b9ae840db62b72e.text: Freebuff can no longer read sensitive files in your project. When you ask the assistant to look at files like your.env, private keys, password files, or SSH keys, it will refuse instead of showing their contents, displaying the file path with a strikethrough and a (blocked) label. Files that are safe examples (.env.example,.env.sample,.env.template) will still be readable but clearly tagged as (allowed - example only), so the assistant can see the structure without touching your real secrets. This applies to everyone using the Freebuff CLI, web app, desktop app, or SDK right now.

dc18d1a2063a92cc1939648a0280c0847a662c73.title: /diagnostics command inspects CLI and terminal tool processes
dc18d1a2063a92cc1939648a0280c0847a662c73.summary: A new /diagnostics slash command (aliases diag, processes) appends a runtime diagnostics report to the chat via formatProcessDiagnostics(collectProcessDiagnostics()). The report shows CLI version, runtime, platform, uptime, CPU, memory, parent and CLI PIDs, the terminal watchdog state, and PIDs of in-flight terminal tool processes, while omitting command lines and environment variables for safety. Supporting exports getActiveTerminalCommandProcesses and ActiveTerminalCommandProcess were added to the SDK so the CLI can enumerate processes owned by in-flight terminal tools, and getTerminalWatchdogDiagnostics exposes the watchdog state. Process tracking in sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts now uses taskkill.exe to terminate the full descendant tree on Windows and delays removing a child from liveChildren until its process group is confirmed gone, so diagnostics still see orphaned grandchildren.
dc18d1a2063a92cc1939648a0280c0847a662c73.evidence: New /diagnostics command handler in cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts invoking collectProcessDiagnostics and formatProcessDiagnostics from the new cli/src/commands/process-diagnostics.ts, registering it in cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts, and exposing getActiveTerminalCommandProcesses and ActiveTerminalCommandProcess from sdk/src/index.ts via sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts. The chat store reset in cli/src/state/chat-store.ts no longer restores inputFocused/isFocusSupported, and cli/src/utils/terminal-watchdog.ts adds getTerminalWatchdogDiagnostics. sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts adds taskkill.exe tree kills on Windows and keeps liveChildren tracked until the process group is gone.
dc18d1a2063a92cc1939648a0280c0847a662c73.unknowns: The rollout of the diagnostics report to non-Freebuff builds and any future surface that consumes getTerminalWatchdogDiagnostics or getActiveTerminalCommandProcesses beyond the CLI chat.

changes.what: Added /diagnostics command that prints a runtime diagnostics report into the chat, registered in the command registry and slash command list.
Added new module collecting runtime, watchdog, and active terminal tool process information and formatting it into a human-readable report that excludes command lines and environment variables.
Reset now preserves terminal focus support and detected capabilities so a new chat does not re-enable animation while the app is still unfocused.
Added read-only diagnostics for the watchdog's armed, external, and pid state.
Exported getActiveTerminalCommandProcesses and ActiveTerminalCommandProcess and switched Windows termination to taskkill.exe for full descendant tree kills.
Header animation now also requires input focus, gating the ChatHeader animationEnabled flag on inputFocused.

57c010db236b4b5ffba7030cb4eff4bb50a4a333.title: Plan summary renders paid-subscription windows and block reasons
57c010db236b4b5ffba7030cb4eff4bb50a4a333.summary: A new shared reader `freebuffPlanSummary` converts a live subscription into `today` / `5-day` / `month` windows and an optional blocking limit with its reset instant, so the CLI picker, Desktop and the web usage page name the same binding limit and reset. The picker imports `formatPlanWindows` and `freebuffPlanSummary` from `common/src/util/freebuff-plan-summary.ts`, renders a single muted line below the catalog and, when the plan is currently blocking, a second row carrying the limit's label and a countdown, preventing the blocked row from being clipped on a short terminal. Because the plan line adds real rows, the picker's height estimate now counts them too, so a blocking user can see the limit that bars them.
57c010db236b4b5ffba7030cb4eff4bb50a4a333.evidence: New file `common/src/util/freebuff-plan-summary.ts` exports `FreebuffPlanWindow`, `FreebuffPlanSummary`, `formatPlanUnits`, `formatPlanWindows`, and `freebuffPlanSummary`. In `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx`, `planSummary = freebuffPlanSummary(subscriptionInfo)` is derived and rendered as a muted line and a separate blocking-limit row below `sectionsContent`, with the height estimate (`estimatedModelHeight`) now adding `SECTION_GAP + 1` plus one more row when `planSummary.blocked` is set.

changes.what: Defines `FreebuffPlanWindow`, `FreebuffPlanSummary`, `formatPlanUnits`, `formatPlanWindows`, and `freebuffPlanSummary` to read a paid subscription's usage, windows, blocked limit, reset instants and month-to-date spend into one shared object.

Imports and calls `freebuffPlanSummary` on the session's subscription info, then renders the plan windows line and a separate blocking-limit row below the catalog and folds their heights into the picker's row estimate.

590e6d257bf4128557f1e5823077c586bb424138.title: Ad taper pacing moves to a trailing-hour ceiling
590e6d257bf4128557f1e5823077c586bb424138.summary: The ad budget tapering code in `common/src/constants/freebuff-ads.ts` now computes each hour's delivery ceiling from a trailing one-hour window, via `deliveryWindowLimit`, instead of the prior cumulative share-of-day model in `pacedDailyAllowance`. The `glideHash` helper gains a lowbias32 avalanche finalizer so the seeded jitter spreads across the whole 32-bit word rather than clustering in its low bits, and a new `DELIVERY_PACE_WINDOW_MINUTES = 60` export names the trailing-window length. This keeps a tapering campaign's cap flat from 00:01 to 23:59 so no clock-aligned burst can empty it at Pacific-day boundaries.
590e6d257bf4128557f1e5823077c586bb424138.evidence: In `common/src/constants/freebuff-ads.ts`, `glideHash` adds a lowbias32 avalanche finalizer after the FNV-1a pass, and `deliveryWindowLimit` replaces `pacedDailyAllowance` computing a trailing-window ceiling over `capEngagements`, `seed`, `windowKey` and `jitterBps`, exporting the `DELIVERY_PACE_WINDOW_MINUTES = 60` constant.
590e6d257bf4128557f1e5823077c586bb424138.migration: Advertisers or services calling the removed `pacedDailyAllowance` must call `deliveryWindowLimit` with `capEngagements`, `seed`, `windowKey`, and `jitterBps` instead, using `DELIVERY_PACE_WINDOW_MINUTES` as the window length.

8f390e940d2f9457ea52bca4567f727f0a049277.title: Think-tag-stream splits leaked reasoning out of content at flush
8f390e940d2f9457ea52bca4567f727f0a049277.summary: processStream now routes text deltas through a new ThinkTagStream (packages/agent-runtime/src/util/think-tag-stream.ts), classifying paired open/close, bare opens, and orphan closes into reasoning vs text before reaching a surface. The implicitOpen flag is armed only when historyLeaksThinkTags finds an unclosed open in the last assistant turn, so a step's head is held until a close arrives or the 4000-char IMPLICIT_OPEN_BUDGET_CHARS budget expires, after which it is released as text. stream-parser.ts releases any held content on flush and on abort paths so speculation never swallows an answer, and a native reasoning chunk disarms any implicit open. This is the Freebuff agent runtime's content/reasoning split for lanes that emit thinking models without populating the native reasoning field. freebuff/cli/release/package.json bumps the CLI version to 0.0.159 to ship it.
8f390e940d2f9457ea52bca4567f727f0a049277.evidence: New file `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/think-tag-stream.ts` introducing `ThinkTagStream`, `historyLeaksThinkTags`, `stripThinkScaffolding`, `IMPLICIT_OPEN_BUDGET_CHARS` (=4000), and `ThinkStreamSegment`; `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/stream-parser.ts` imports and wires these so text deltas pass through `thinkTagStream.push` and `flush` and reasoning/`content` chunks trigger `disarmImplicitOpen`, with `implicitOpen` armed from `historyLeaksThinkTags(agentState.messageHistory)`; version field in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumped from 0.0.158 to 0.0.159.
8f390e940d2f9457ea52bca4567f727f0a049277.unknowns: The end-user-visible rendering behavior depends on a Freebuff agent runtime consumer of the exported segments; the diff only shows the agent-runtime wiring, not the surface that renders reasoning_delta vs text.

changes.what: Added think-tag-stream.ts implementing ThinkTagStream, historyLeaksThinkTags, stripThinkScaffolding, IMPLICIT_OPEN_BUDGET_CHARS, and ThinkStreamSegment for splitting leaked thinking out of a content stream.

processStream now constructs a ThinkTagStream armed by historyLeaksThinkTags, routes text deltas through push/flush and disarms the implicit open on native reasoning chunks, releasing held content at step end and in the finally block.
Release version bumped from 0.0.158 to 0.0.159 in the CLI release manifest.

cb3ef3135c27c68f08c1c3e92290607a08732afc.title: GLM 5.3 Flash cap removed from per-model session limits
cb3ef3135c27c68f08c1c3e92290607a08732afc.summary: The single per-model session cap in `FREEBUFF_PER_MODEL_SESSION_CAPS` - the 2-a-day ceiling on `FREEBUFF_GLM_V53_FLASH_MODEL_ID` - has been removed, and the table comment now records that the measurement window closed at 93.7% cache on its pinned Merge vendor and 6.25x under the OpenRouter route it replaced. The `freebuff-models.ts` comment also restates the invariant that being in some pool is required, since `FREEBUFF_STANDARD_MODEL_IDS` is derived by filtering `!premium` and a premium model absent from every pool becomes unlimited. The companion update in `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts` edits the `FREEBUFF_SUBSCRIPTION_PRO_MODEL_IDS` comment to reflect that GLM 5.3 Flash shipped as a free premium row whose 2-a-day ceiling came off once its lane was measured. The `common/src/util/freebuff-model-availability.ts` notice `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` is rewritten to drop the GLM 5.3 Flash per-model cap number, and the `common/src/constants/spend-providers.ts` file adds the `merge` billing counterparty with the Merge Gateway label.
cb3ef3135c27c68f08c1c3e92290607a08732afc.evidence: The `FREEBUFF_PER_MODEL_SESSION_CAPS` table in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` is emptied of its only entry, the `[FREEBUFF_GLM_V53_FLASH_MODEL_ID]: { limit: 2, pool: 'glm_v53_flash', poolLabel: 'GLM 5.3 Flash' }` row, and the comment block beside it is updated to record that the measurement window closed at 93.7% cache on its pinned Merge vendor and 6.25x under the OpenRouter route it replaced.
cb3ef3135c27c68f08c1c3e92290607a08732afc.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer reads the emptied `FREEBUFF_PER_MODEL_SESSION_CAPS` table to enforce the new shared-pool-only metering, or whether a follow-up step is required to complete the migration. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

2f4829e864d268f1cd6987537fd7956f6c67d0dc.title: Add Freebuff Pro house ad copy for last-resort slot fill
2f4829e864d268f1cd6987537fd7956f6c67d0dc.summary: A new module `common/src/constants/freebuff-house-ad.ts` defines the marketing copy and creatives for the house ad that fills Freebuff ad slots when no paid or first-party campaign can serve. The entry price is read from `FREEBUFF_SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS[0]?.priceUsd ?? 8` instead of being hardcoded, and each surface (`cli_chat`, `waiting_room`, `freebuff_web_chat`, `chat_assistant`) plus a `HOUSE_AD_DISPLAY_CREATIVE` card variant route readers to `${FREEBUFF_WEB_URL_PROD}/plans`. No serving logic ships in this change; the consumer in `@codebuff/internal/ad-serving/house-ad` is responsible for enforcing coverage over the declared `HouseAdSurface` set.
2f4829e864d268f1cd6987537fd7956f6c67d0dc.evidence: New file `common/src/constants/freebuff-house-ad.ts` (116 lines) defines `HOUSE_AD_DESTINATION_URL`, `ENTRY_PRICE_USD`, `HouseAdSurface`, `HOUSE_AD_CREATIVES`, `HOUSE_AD_DISPLAY_CREATIVE`, with the file doc noting it is copy only and the serving mechanism lives in `@codebuff/internal/ad-serving/house-ad`.
