changes.what: Rewrote the credited and not-yet-used branches of getFreebuffStreakBonusStatus to avoid mislabeling east-of-Pacific credits as "today's" and "in your wallet", and aligned the docstring and comment to "already credited".

08dafc32a020452b6a2c4511b46848c605258460.title: SDK file read override now receives full content flag on edit-path
08dafc32a020452b6a2c4511b46848c605258460.summary: The SDK's `readFiles` override now sets a `fullContent` flag when reading a file to compute an edit, because the hosted read override was truncating files at ~65K characters and str_replace calls past that offset failed to match. The flag is sent only on the edit path (via `requestOptionalFile`), so model-facing reads keep the override's read budget while edit reads return whole files. This lets `str_replace` match content anywhere in large files on hosted surfaces.
08dafc32a020452b6a2c4511b46848c605258460.evidence: In `sdk/src/run.ts`, the `read_files` override handler type adds a new `fullContent` field, and the `readFiles` function forwards `fullContent` to the override when `limitContent` is `false` (the edit path via `requestOptionalFile`), across both the `!enforceEnvPolicy` and env-policy branches; `packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/process-str-replace.test.ts` asserts regex metacharacters match literally past 65,536 chars, and `sdk/src/__tests__/run-file-filter.test.ts` asserts the override receives `fullContent` as `true` only on the edit-path read.
08dafc32a020452b6a2c4511b46848c605258460.unknowns: Whether the hosted override actually implements the full-read budget the new flag asks for on this revision.

changes.what: Added a `fullContent` field to the `read_files` override type and forwarded it when `limitContent` is false on the edit path.
Added a test asserting str_replace matches regex metacharacters literally and $ patterns verbatim past 65,536 chars.

84be4d3a3c3b59fec71dd61bbe93f10c3291b5c6.text: When you use the assistant to work through a big task, Freebuff now keeps a running summary of where things stand so you don't lose track of earlier steps. If the AI skips its normal summary step, the assistant can still build that summary from the last reply it wrote, and it will keep the summary even if it is a little longer than originally planned, as long as the overall context stays within size limits. The assistant also records when this summary happens so developers can see it in their logs, and two new checks were added to make sure this behavior stays consistent.

4cdbbb8e228beaa638fe937d7fec9a9c3d15f1c1.text: This Freebuff CLI release upgrades the free model catalog, updates how spawned helper agents report back, and tightens security and accuracy across referral tracking, streak bonuses, and release downloads. The standout user-visible changes are: Muse Spark 1.2 is removed from the free model picker and replaced by Muse Spark 1.3 (1.2 is now paid-only), the onboarding referral question now asks about Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook as separate choices instead of one combined chip, and a new status line under your streak note tells you whether today's Freebucks streak bonus has landed and when the next one resets in your local time. Behind the scenes, the release hardens the download process so release files only load from trusted freebuff.com or codebuff.com addresses, the release launcher rejects versions that aren't proper version numbers, and terminal output now strips invisible or control characters before display so remote text can't hijack your terminal. Upgrading keeps your free AI model access current, makes referral credit and streak bonuses easier to read in your local time, and locks down where the CLI will pull its update files from.

89abfa4a12586730d5ac44f74b877173a6d2ea56.text: The assistant now recovers from a specific mistake a few AI models make when summarizing a long coding chat: some models write the summary directly into their reply text instead of using the proper tool call, and previously this caused the summary to be discarded. Now, when that happens, the system recognizes the reply text as a valid summary if it contains the right section headings and installs it, allowing the conversation to continue with a reduced context window. This affects only the backend behavior of the Freebuff coding assistant and requires no action from you; long coding sessions that previously lost progress may now be summarized and continued more reliably.

fa6729bf4c2f8809a3d8afb07f6e976176db09bc.text: The status message that shows how many Freebucks you have left from your daily streak bonus no longer claims the credit is "in your wallet". Instead it now says the bonus was credited, and tells you when the next one will arrive. This matters most for users east of the Pacific, whose daily bonus can land before their local day resets, making the old wording misleading. The wording also changed for users who haven't earned today's bonus yet, from "for today's" to "to earn". If you see these status lines, they now describe what happened and when the next credit is due, not what is sitting in your wallet.

227e3fdb0d096fd532844dddbfc0fae41cd4b9d6.text: When you're already working with the assistant on a task and you type a quick note or follow-up, the assistant now treats it as a continuation of what it's doing rather than a brand-new request, so it won't drop what it was in the middle of. The message gets wrapped with an internal label that tells the assistant this came in while it was working, and that label is stripped out when the assistant later needs to recall the original words. This is live for anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, or desktop app who sends a message while the assistant is still busy. You'll notice that sending a message mid-task now adds to the running task instead of silently replacing it, and the input box will tell you that Enter adds to the current task rather than queueing a new one.

2b6d2607c0b7d9a2feb2e48138c059713c1387eb.text: The record the assistant keeps of each answer now also stores the raw token counts exactly as the provider reported them, while leaving out the billing numbers the service actually charges you in credits. This is for the Freebuff engineering team only, so nothing you see changes today, and there is no action for you to take.

08dafc32a020452b6a2c4511b46848c605258460.text: When the assistant needs to edit a file (for example, to find and replace a piece of text), it now reads the entire file instead of only the first portion. Previously the read was capped at roughly 65,000 characters, which caused edits targeting text later in large files to fail because the text wasn't there to be matched. Now any edit operation gets the complete file contents, so search-and-replace can reach anywhere in the file. This only applies to the internal edit path; ordinary reads the assistant does while chatting are unchanged, and no action is required from you.

f9d3f018008ec79a9d70c0c67f8af3966fed1587.title: Prompt-error returns a state snapshot instead of the live session
f9d3f018008ec79a9d70c0c67f8af3966fed1587.summary: When local agent templates fail validation, the runtime sends a prompt-error action and returns early instead of proceeding to the main prompt loop, so no model call, tools, or further chunks occur. The SDK's run() now resolves that prompt-error path with cloneSessionState(initialSessionState), a JSON round-trip copy of the live state the host passed in, rather than the live object itself. This snapshot is what the host keeps and resends, preventing post-error writes from bleeding into the persisted state.
f9d3f018008ec79a9d70c0c67f8af3966fed1587.evidence: packages/agent-runtime/src/main-prompt.ts: in callMainPrompt, validationErrors from assembleLocalAgentTemplates now triggers a 'prompt-error' sendAction and an early return of a new sessionState object instead of continuing; sdk/src/run.ts: handlePromptResponse for 'prompt-error' now resolves with cloneSessionState(initialSessionState) instead of the live initialSessionState. Confirmed by sdk/src/__tests__/run-prompt-error-snapshot.test.ts asserting result.sessionState.mainAgentState is not the same reference as the runtime object and excludes late writes.

changes.what: callMainPrompt exits early via a prompt-error action when assembleLocalAgentTemplates reports validationErrors, returning a fresh sessionState object instead of continuing to mainPrompt.
handlePromptResponse resolves prompt-error with cloneSessionState(initialSessionState) so the host receives an isolated snapshot of the state it provided rather than the live object.
Test asserts that after a prompt-error the resolved sessionState is a distinct object from the runtime's and does not contain late writes pushed onto the runtime's mainAgentState.
Test verifies that an invalid local agent template produces a prompt-error and halts with no model call, tools, or further chunks.

f9d3f018008ec79a9d70c0c67f8af3966fed1587.text: When you configure the assistant with a malformed local agent template (for example, a missing or invalid agent definition file in your project), the system now stops cleanly and returns a fresh, independent copy of your session state instead of handing back the live, in-progress session object that the runtime is still mutating. This affects developers who use the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or embed the Freebuff SDK to build their own integrations. You will not notice this during normal use, but if you hit a configuration error, your saved session is no longer at risk of being corrupted by later writes from the failed run, and the run no longer keeps going in the background after the error is reported.

9a87cf853a482411f6667fa4ad554c38b077e4fc.title: Head think tag is released as text when model ends step
9a87cf853a482411f6667fa4ad554c38b077e4fc.summary: The ThinkTagStream now distinguishes a head open tag from one appearing after visible text: a head block streams live as reasoning but, if still open when the step ends, is re-emitted as text only when the model finished the step itself, while a cut-off step (output limit, tool call, abort) keeps it as a truncated thought. A mid-answer is now held and released verbatim as text if no close arrives within MID_PROSE_THINK_BUDGET_CHARS (= 1000), fixing the answer-swallowing bug where any unclosed tag sent the rest of the step to the thinking box. This required wiring the model's finish reason through run-agent-step into processStream so the split can tell a completed step from a cut-off one.
9a87cf853a482411f6667fa4ad554c38b077e4fc.evidence: packages/agent-runtime/src/util/think-tag-stream.ts adds MID_PROSE_THINK_BUDGET_CHARS = 1000 and ThinkStreamFlushOptions with a stepCompleted flag; packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/stream-parser.ts passes streamFinishReason (read from the new onFinishReason callback wired in run-agent-step.ts) to thinkTagStream.flush({ stepCompleted }) so a head open tag still blocking at step end is re-emitted as text only when the model ended the step itself.
9a87cf853a482411f6667fa4ad554c38b077e4fc.unknowns: The exact rollout path for lanes that already pair their tags, and whether the new stepCompleted branch interacts with existing stream-recovery retries on reasoning-only steps.

9a87cf853a482411f6667fa4ad554c38b077e4fc.text: When the assistant thinks out loud before answering, it now uses a special tag to wrap its reasoning so that the thinking portion stays in a separate "thinking" panel, instead of bleeding into the visible answer. This is aimed at Freebuff's developer users who interact with the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK. You'll notice fewer instances where the assistant's hidden reasoning leaks into the main response, showing up as stray markers or cutting off the visible reply.

6c9b69c3627e831b66cd81e672aaf74939a417c5.title: README docs replace legacy session allowance with Freebucks daily
6c9b69c3627e831b66cd81e672aaf74939a417c5.summary: The Freebuff, Freebuff Chinese, and CLI release READMEs swap the documented free-access model from the legacy session system (six one-hour daily sessions, earnable to seven) to a 25-Freebucks-per-day allowance (20 on VPN/proxy) that is spent first on every model, with earned Freebucks used from the wallet afterward. This reflects the shipped Freebucks-based metering so the public docs match the current product surface rather than the retired session buckets.
6c9b69c3627e831b66cd81e672aaf74939a417c5.evidence: README.md, README.zh-CN.md, and freebuff/cli/release/README.md each replace a paragraph describing Freebuff's free-access and pricing model: the old text described the legacy session system (six one-hour sessions per day, earnable up to seven, with Freebucks pricing for accounts on Freebucks), while the new text describes a 25-Freebucks-per-day allowance (20 on VPN/proxy) spent first on every model including GLM, with earned Freebucks from the wallet used afterward. The freebuff/cli/release/README.md FAQ also replaces one model-listing sentence fragment with the limited-mode allowance text, and the old text stating GLM 5.3 Flash 'costs no session at all' and is 'always available no matter how much you have used' is gone.

d0ee7b0acaec39142ef7af945c3735e6f2aa4369.title: Freebuff 0.1.7 export is Beijing Weekend for peak-hour weekend gating
d0ee7b0acaec39142ef7af945c3735e6f2aa4369.summary: Freebuff 0.1.7 is published by bumping the version in freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.1.6 to 0.1.7. In common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts, isBeijingWeekend is exported (previously module-local) so the shared peak-hour definition, which both billing and model-availability code read from this same file, gates DeepSeek's weekend rule that took effect on 2026-08-22T16:00Z. The export exists so consumers can call the weekend check, which is also covered by the new 'the Beijing weekend boundaries' tests.
d0ee7b0acaec39142ef7af945c3735e6f2aa4369.evidence: Diff hunk in common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts flips isBeijingWeekend from a module-local function to an exported function and adds a JSDoc block stating it gates instants on or after 2026-08-22T16:00Z (when DeepSeek's weekend rule took effect); Diff hunk in freebuff/cli/release/package.json bumps "version" from "0.1.6" to "0.1.7"; New test describe block 'the Beijing weekend boundaries' in common/src/__tests__/freebuff-peak-hours.test.ts asserts isBeijingWeekend across Fri 16:00Z-Sun 16:00Z edges. isBeijingWeekend is consumed by deepseekPricingWindow and isDeepSeekExpensiveWindow in the same peak-hours module, and the pricingWindow logic is shared by billing and model-availability code per the file header comment.

changes.what: isBeijingWeekend is changed from a module-local function to an exported function with added JSDoc describing the Fri 16:00Z to Sun 16:00Z Beijing weekend window and the 2026-08-22T16:00Z rule start.
A new 'the Beijing weekend boundaries' test block asserts isBeijingWeekend at the edges where the UTC and Beijing days disagree.
The version field is bumped from 0.1.6 to 0.1.7 as the release-bump commit nature.

d0ee7b0acaec39142ef7af945c3735e6f2aa4369.text: The Freebuff team published version 0.1.7, which is mainly a labeling update for their release files. Inside that release, they made a small adjustment to how the system decides whether a given day counts as a weekend for DeepSeek's pricing windows, and they added tests to lock in the exact weekend boundaries. This is an internal engineering change: it keeps the billing and model-availability logic in sync, but it does not change what you see or do when using Freebuff.

93f5e6d99c94f55caa8bc4c067196475a1f732d5.text: When you run the Freebuff assistant in your terminal and a new version of the app is installed while you're using it (like an automatic update that restarts your CLI), your current session is now resumed cleanly instead of dropping you back to the model picker. Freebuff now remembers which model you were using and keeps your existing session slot alive during the update restart, so you don't lose your paid time or get interrupted by a fresh login screen. This only applies to the free tier of the assistant; Codebuff users and the web/desktop apps are not affected. No action is needed from you, and the change is live today.

4cdbbb8e228beaa638fe937d7fec9a9c3d15f1c1.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.5 ships with the newer Muse Spark 1.3 model now available in the free model picker (1.2 moved to paid-only surfaces), along with a streak-bonus status line that shows when your daily Freebucks credit has landed and when the next one resets in your local time zone. Other user-visible fixes include the release launcher now refusing downloads unless the source is a trusted first-party host, a terminal text sanitizer that strips invisible or malicious control characters from text drawn from remote sources, and sponsored-run crash recovery so a run that dies mid-task is reported rather than lost. Upgrading gives you the current free model, clearer streak status, safer downloads and terminal output, and a model-availability notice that mentions Freebucks when you are on a VPN.

This release swaps the free Muse Spark 1.2 model for Muse Spark 1.3 in the model picker you see when choosing a free AI model, and adds a time-limited deal badge to the GLM 5.3 Flash model row indicating a price change and a September 30 deadline. It also fixes the streak bonus status line so users in time zones east of Pacific Time no longer see misleading wording about today's bonus being in their wallet, instead showing the actual credited amount and when the next bonus arrives after their first message. Finally, it tightens security around the release download process by enforcing HTTPS-only download URLs and sanitizing all remote text shown in the terminal to strip hidden control characters and invisible Unicode.

f8ed82aaaa4ed3c5776a04b6c7423b894b294f74.text: Ox Alpha, an experimental coding model, is now selectable as a real option in the free picker instead of only being available on certain web pages. Users on the CLI and desktop app, including those in limited-access regions, can now pick it directly. In daily use you will see a new 'TEST' badge on the Ox Alpha row, and if you pick it the assistant will run using that model along with its matching code reviewer.

98ffa6c38ece5e15ad14bfa2d018fcfdc9a9b014.text: The Freebuff team finished publishing the Freebuff free-tier package as its own downloadable app: they added the release package files (a small wrapper script, install and cleanup helpers, and a version manifest), a build helper that produces the free-only binary, and an automated release workflow that builds the binaries and publishes them. This is the first public release, so the app is live on npm now. It only affects people who install Freebuff from npm and does not change anything for the engineers maintaining the agent runtime.

df596975d3847f148250d348fada73ef08f30465.text: When you start the Freebuff CLI and you are not already signed in, the app now shows a built-in login screen instead of asking you for an API key up front. Pressing Enter opens your web browser to a sign-in page hosted on the Freebuff website, and after you complete that step the CLI confirms the login in the background and lets you right into the chat. This applies to Freebuff CLI users who are signing in for the first time or have logged out, so if you have never signed in before you can now use a normal browser-based login flow. You will notice the change the first time you open the CLI without existing credentials: you will see a branded welcome screen with a link and instructions instead of a blank prompt.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This Freebuff CLI release ships a new Freebucks pay-as-you-go credit system, adds a /export command to save conversations to a file, and promotes several models in the free picker. You can now save any conversation to a markdown or JSON file using the new /export slash command, and the model picker shows your remaining Freebucks balance and per-model prices instead of legacy session counters. DeepSeek V4 Flash and GLM 5.3 Flash remain the headline free models with Solar Pro 4 and Meta Muse Spark 1.3 newly available, and Solar Pro 4 is capped at one session per day while unmetered at full access. The CLI landing screen now offers a direct upgrade path when you hit rate or spend limits instead of a dead end, and account deletion requests are protected with a signed HMAC proof verified in constant time before any data purge runs. Upgrading gives developers a clearer picture of their free tier usage, a way to persist conversations, and direct links to paid plans when they need more than the free allowance.

9f81f91397709452f3b757a035fb9e93d0ab9454.text: The team that decides which AI models Freebuff subscribers can use cleaned up how those model lists are maintained, so the list of models a paid plan can spend its allowance on is now defined in one place instead of being copied and at risk of drifting out of sync. Gemini 3.8 Flash is now both available for paying subscribers to use and counted as one of the costliest models that gets a daily spending cap, so that no single user can run it for every session and deplete the pooled allowance for everyone on that plan. This affects Freebuff subscribers and anyone building against the Freebuff SDK, because the set of models a subscription can pay for is now pulled from the canonical model catalog.

443f19f0eae03bcbc0dfb3ac6a5cd869fb9dcbae.text: If you submitted a plan, interview question, review request, or skill while the assistant was already working, the old message used to be killed and replaced by the new one. Now, those requests wait their turn in a queue instead of interrupting whatever the assistant was doing. When you type a plain text message mid-turn, it is also handed directly to the running task so you can steer the assistant without restarting the whole turn. Developers using the terminal app will notice that mid-turn messages no longer cancel each other out, and the status bar now shows how full the conversation context is with a compact token count like '14.2K (7%)'.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds a new free model called Muse Spark 1.3 to the picker alongside an updated Freebucks credit system that shows prices as wallet balances in the CLI. A new /export command lets you save your full conversation to a markdown or JSON file, mid-turn /plan, /interview, and /review commands now queue instead of interrupting ongoing runs, and the thinker-gemini agent switched to DeepSeek V4 Flash for cost reasons. The CLI now shows a one-time Meet Freebucks intro card and renders price/balance for metered models, while the model picker reorders GLM 5.3 Flash back to the default lead position. For daily use, you get clearer credit balances, the ability to export conversations, queued commands that no longer clobber your in-progress work, and the new Muse Spark 1.3 option when other models are busy.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release adds a new default AI model, GLM 5.3 Flash, which replaces GPT-5.6 Luna as the primary Freebuff model with faster and deeper reasoning capabilities. You can now use the /dashboard slash command to view your account activity, usage tokens, sessions, and streaks in one place. The release also introduces a new /reasoning command that lets you control how deeply the AI thinks on a per-model basis with low, high, and max effort settings. GLM 5.3 Flash is now capped at 2 sessions per day in the free tier, though the default recommendation is now uncapped for this model. The model picker interface has been reorganized to show GLM 5.3 Flash first and includes clearer availability window labels for when models are temporarily unavailable.

8f390e940d2f9457ea52bca4567f727f0a049277.text: The assistant now properly separates its thinking or reasoning content from its direct answers, so when it shows how it arrived at a conclusion, that thinking appears in its own dedicated section instead of mixing with the final response. This affects users of the Freebuff coding assistant in their terminal, web app, or desktop app. You'll see cleaner output where the AI's line of thinking is clearly distinguished from its actual answer, making responses easier to read and understand. No action is required on your part - the improvement is automatic and applies whenever you use the assistant starting today.

05c9164d5a35b3f002dfaae7943d2bad11aa4002.title: Add bugs url to Freebuff release package.json
05c9164d5a35b3f002dfaae7943d2bad11aa4002.summary: A "bugs" field was added to the Freebuff CLI release manifest at `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, pointing to https://github.com/CodebuffAI/freebuff/issues. This surfaces a standard npm reporting destination in the freebuff package metadata so package consumers can file issues against the Freebuff CLI release.
05c9164d5a35b3f002dfaae7943d2bad11aa4002.evidence: The diff adds a top-level "bugs" field with "url": "https://github.com/CodebuffAI/freebuff/issues" to `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, immediately after the "homepage" field and before the existing "publishConfig" block.
05c9164d5a35b3f002dfaae7943d2bad11aa4002.unknowns: The downstream consumer of this field (npm UI, CLI tooling) is not shown in the diff.

05c9164d5a35b3f002dfaae7943d2bad11aa4002.text: The Freebuff release manifest now includes a "bugs" field that points to the project's GitHub issues page, making it easier for anyone inspecting the package to find the right place to report problems. This is an internal packaging detail, so it does not change how the assistant behaves or what features are available. Most users will notice nothing different.

c9517264c3b4a0143773266f7c0e88e954a69f3b.title: Remove tier change notice constant from landing screen
c9517264c3b4a0143773266f7c0e88e954a69f3b.summary: The `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` constant was deleted from `common/src/util/freebuff-model-availability.ts` and dropped from the imports in `cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx`, so the full-access branch of `belowPickerNotices` now yields `[]` instead of rendering that notice line.
c9517264c3b4a0143773266f7c0e88e954a69f3b.evidence: diff --git a/cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx: removed `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` from the import and from `belowPickerNotices` (the full-access branch now yields `[]`), and diff --git a/common/src/util/freebuff-model-availability.ts: deleted the `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` constant definition.
c9517264c3b4a0143773266f7c0e88e954a69f3b.unknowns: The diff does not state why the notice text was removed or whether any consumer beyond the landing screen referenced it.

changes.what: Deleted the `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` constant that held user-facing release-note copy.
Removed `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` from the import and from the full-access branch of `belowPickerNotices`, which now returns an empty array.

c9517264c3b4a0143773266f7c0e88e954a69f3b.text: A small informational line that used to appear on the Freebuff landing screen has been removed. This affects only the Freebuff engineering team and the internal tooling that maintains that screen, so it is an internal cleanup. You will not see any difference in your daily use of Freebuff; the picker still shows your models and availability notices behave exactly as before, just without that extra note. The change is live today.

ac2a035d604166a86390a7272dd56b60efd8a556.text: The free coding assistant has switched its default model back to DeepSeek V4 Flash, which is now available at all hours of the day. DeepSeek V4 Pro, the most powerful model, is now only available outside peak times (roughly five in the evening to three in the morning Pacific time) and is limited to one session per day. This affects developers using the Freebuff CLI, web app, and desktop app who want the strongest model for deep reasoning tasks, but the change is automatic and requires no action from users.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release makes Freebuff's free AI coding assistant default to GLM 5.3 Flash as its main model, adds a new /reasoning command to control how hard the AI thinks, and introduces a /dashboard command to view your usage, streaks, and account settings. The DeepSeek V4 Flash and GPT-5.6 Luna models are now unmetered so they no longer count against daily session limits, while the ad-supported system got more precise controls: ads now use a daily subscription model, referrer links go directly to your referral status page, and new safeguards block stale clipboard copies from overwriting newer ones. You also get clearer error messages when a model is temporarily unavailable (with a specific return time), better handling of interrupted tool calls so conversations don't break, and the CLI now shows accent-colored focus for the dashboard button with clearer streak progress markers. Upgrading means you'll see GLM 5.3 Flash as the first model option, can check your account stats from within the app, and get more predictable behavior when models are rate-limited or unavailable.

7fec1c348df816ea7456827338d370cd25a3b1a2.title: Add fatigue-layer aggregates to first-party decision allowlist
7fec1c348df816ea7456827338d370cd25a3b1a2.summary: Eight new scalar fields are appended to the `ADS_FIRST_PARTY_DECISION_FIELDS` allowlist in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` so fatigue-layer aggregates can pass through the content-free operational-event filter into the `ads.first_party_decision` event stream, while the comment notes that campaign- or user-level identifiers remain excluded by keeping the fields aggregate-only. The change exists so fatigue-signal visibility is captured on the operational telemetry stream without re-introducing identifiers the allowlist deliberately excludes.
7fec1c348df816ea7456827338d370cd25a3b1a2.evidence: In `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`, eight new scalar fields are appended to the `ADS_FIRST_PARTY_DECISION_FIELDS` allowlist schema: `ranker_fatigue_status`, `ranker_fatigue_read_ms`, `ranker_fatigue_history_len`, `ranker_fatigue_normalization`, `ranker_fatigue_fatigued_candidates`, `ranker_fatigue_min_ppm`, `ranker_fatigue_mean_ppm`, and `ranker_fatigue_disagreements`, each typed as 'string' or 'number'.
7fec1c348df816ea7456827338d370cd25a3b1a2.unknowns: The diff shows only the allowlist addition; it does not show the F fatigue layer emission logic that populates these fields on the operational telemetry stream.

7fec1c348df816ea7456827338d370cd25a3b1a2.text: The team added a few new reporting fields to the internal telemetry that tracks how Freebuff’s built-in ads are selected. These fields only describe broad, aggregate stats about how often the ad system pauses showing the same ad to avoid overexposure, and they still exclude any per-campaign or per-user details. This is strictly for whoever operates and monitors the Freebuff service, so you do not need to do anything and will not notice any difference in your coding sessions.

afc8351b5b724273614569816b30691f1fecf536.text: The web search tool no longer offers a deeper, multi-step research mode; it now performs only standard web searches. This affects anyone writing or relying on prompts that passed the removed research options to web_search, who must drop those parameters since the tool performs standard web search only. In daily use, you simply get a regular web search instead of the deeper research mode when you ask it to search.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds a new export command to save your full conversation to a file, promotes Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 to the free model picker across the CLI, Web, and Cloud, and makes DeepSeek V4 Flash and GLM 5.3 Flash the default models depending on the surface you use. The CLI now shows a one-time Meet Freebucks intro card and renders your remaining compute credits as a currency label with per-model prices, including a special Labor Day promotion that makes Solar Pro 4 free through Sep 7. Mid-turn messages to /plan, /interview, and /review no longer overwrite an in-progress run, instead queuing behind it, and plan mode now blocks file-editing tools to keep planning turns read-only. Account deletion proofs are now HMAC-signed and verified, and a new geo-aware ad routing layer serves inventory based on your location, with the house advertising suppressed for paid subscribers. Upgrading gives you the export command, the updated model catalog with Muse Spark 1.3 available, the Freebucks credit meter and pricing in the picker, the corrected default model behavior, and the safer mid-turn and plan mode interactions.

2afc2b2dfac9a0bcb48e18ccc0c1f720f6f2e6a7.text: The assistant now sends your request to the model provider it prefers first, and only switches to a backup if the first one is too expensive, instead of always sticking to one locked provider. If a provider refuses your request by returning a specific error, the assistant now correctly notices that error instead of silently acting like the connection just dropped and asking you to check your network. This is a live change for everyone using the assistant today.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release makes GLM 5.3 Flash the recommended free AI model across the CLI, web, and desktop apps, and adds a new /reasoning command that lets you control how hard that model thinks. A new /dashboard slash command opens your account hub where you can see streaks, token usage, sessions, and settings across all surfaces. Freebuff subscriptions (Starter and Plus tiers) now top up your free sessions instead of replacing them, and subscribers in limited regions can run premium models like GPT-5.6 Luna. A new Solar Pro 4 model joins the free picker as a limited-time trial option. Ad inventory is now served through first-party placements with creative sanitization that strips terminal-control sequences and enforces safe https destinations before serving. Live sessions are never interrupted by daily spend caps, since spend ceilings only apply to fresh sessions.

a29a854c99017a698e7c8c673e870465919ec957.text: The CLI now includes a built-in agent manager that lets developers list, create, and switch between custom AI agents right from their terminal, using a new menu opened with the 'agents' command. Developers who build custom agents get a guided chat assistant and template system that writes the agent files for them, and agent naming now resolves more reliably whether or not a prefix is used. No action is required, but anyone using custom agents in the CLI will see a more flexible and forgiving experience when adding or referencing them.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds a new /export slash command so you can save your full conversation to a file (as markdown by default, or as raw JSON if you name it.json), and it also makes the Freebucks pay-as-you-go credit meter the main way metered models are shown in the picker, with per-row prices, a wallet balance, and a one-time Freebucks intro card instead of the old session counter. Behind the scenes, the default free model flips back to GLM 5.3 Flash across CLI and Web, Muse Spark 1.3 is promoted into the free picker (with a 1,000,000-token context and DeepSeek V4 Flash as its fallback when busy), and Solar Pro 4 becomes an unmetered limited-access model with a 1-session-per-day trial before moving into the shared premium pool, while Gemini 3.8 Flash is withdrawn from the free picker entirely and paused so existing sessions can drain. The upgrade experience matters here: rate-limited and spend-limited landing screens now show an upgrade call-to-action (with day-scale wait times like '26 days' instead of '622h 18m') so you aren't stuck on a dead-end free wall, and /plan, /interview, /review and /skill submissions now queue instead of overwriting an in-progress run, with mid-turn plain text handed to the active run at its next step boundary via a new steering buffer. For security and data integrity, sponsored proposal runs gain a sandboxed local execution boundary (capability vocabulary, per-OS environment scrubbing, and an OS sandbox broker) plus a linked-worktree grant so a sponsored run can reach your real.git for commits while refusing writes to hooks and config, and the CLI's direnv handling drops steering variables from cloned.envrc files to prevent a checked-in repository from hijacking where the assistant connects. You also get better observability into what's happening: ad events now carry a client-minted event id and a clamped render-delay header on every first-party impression and click, the ad-fetch telemetry logs geo tier and decision-outbox status, and model token totals are corrected so cache reads no longer inflate the count (~1.8x at high cache-hit rates), so the usage you see in the UI and usage reports actually matches what was billed.

f7828c2c4b5a55de46b00f0484ed047e091d0964.text: The Freebuff team added a new separate worker service that runs Freebuff coding sessions on dedicated machines, instead of running them through the shared cloud functions where they used to run. This is internal infrastructure work by the Freebuff engineering team, so free users will not notice anything different in their daily use today. The new worker is turned on by default for Freebuff, Codex, and Claude Code sessions, and it is designed to start running those sessions through the new system instead of the old one.

b3e55023aff056482671e824ebabbf1cb3940ee8.text: This release improves the Freebuff AI coding assistant with better stability, advertising tracking, and agent behavior. A runaway AI model that kept suggesting prompts repeatedly now gets automatically capped at 8 attempts per response, preventing infinite loops. Advertisers get more accurate tracking with a separated Meta pixel system that distinguishes ad-acquisition signups from regular coding users. The assistant's to-do list handling now detects and stops unproductive busy-work loops where it repeats the same unchanged task list. Developer telemetry now captures more detailed but privacy-safe logging of paid AI requests. The agent also better recognizes when it lacks the tools needed to complete tasks and can give clearer guidance. Upgrading gives you fewer stuck or looping AI sessions and better overall reliability.

2e6752b1c89a822c6efecf6e1ba0f6b1c95da554.text: Freebuff added a new set of analytics events to its internal tracking system, specifically designed to monitor the advertiser signup and campaign creation flow. This is internal telemetry work for the Freebuff advertising team, not something end users will notice. The new events let Freebuff measure how advertisers move from the initial pitch page through campaign creation, including signups, onboarding steps, campaign builder interactions, and payment setup, while avoiding the capture of sensitive advertiser data like emails or URLs. Since these are backend tracking definitions, nothing changes in how you use Freebuff or your development experience.

ecc7811dcf7df731264f83cdb19daea5d420c585.text: The change makes the assistant stop itself when it keeps resubmitting the exact same to-do list instead of doing actual work, answering that repeat as a no-op right away rather than treating each copy as fresh progress. It is live for anyone whose session runs the agent runtime today, so if an assistant gets stuck echoing itself, you see a quicker, explicit pause and a clearer hint suggesting it move on. No action is needed from you, and on turns where the to-do list actually changes the behavior is unchanged.

da80e463619074350fe0fba0d1f60db796505553.text: Operators can now switch on Windows support for generic ad-sponsored coding sessions, but only when the service is configured with a specific toggle and a reviewed list of campaign identifiers. Because Windows lacks an OS-level sandbox, these sessions run in a restricted floor mode instead of a normal sandbox when the configuration is active. No advertiser or individual user controls this setting, so if you are a Freebuff user there is nothing for you to change and no visible difference in your daily experience.

4a8b060def270c1beedad8f4d70b9233fdaa50eb.text: Freebuff 0.0.189 adds official support for running assistant tasks on Windows desktops (previously macOS and Linux only), and makes the free tier of AI models easier to understand when a session is being slowed down by a pacing notice shown in the desktop app and SDK. The release also retires the old free-mode model downgrade system (which automatically swapped to a tiny model when it thought you were a foreign client), adds clearer error messages when you bring your own AI key (BYOK) and pick a model ID the provider does not recognize (naming your configured model instead of a generic failure), and expands the list of premium AI models available to provisioned accounts (like GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna Pro, Claude Opus 5.5, and others, each on its own dedicated starting agent). On the safety side, sponsored file tools now pin directories directly without routing through a separate broker process, Windows paths are checked against tricky edge cases like trailing spaces and short names before being executed, and the CLI now keeps track of helper processes it spawns so it can detect runaway watchdogs. Upgrading mainly matters if you are a Windows desktop user, a developer bringing your own AI provider key, or a provisioned account using one of the newer model tiers, since these groups will actually see new surfaces and behaviors open up.

d2f1b7b9af6ff411f7cfc825be4a3a008befc28d.text: When you use the free version of the assistant and your conversation gets throttled because you've hit a spending target, the app can now detect that slowdown message coming from the server - it used to be ignored. You, as a free-tier user, don't need to do anything different, and you won't see a new setting. The change just lets desktop hosts react quietly: when your tab is being slowed down, they can now label that pause instead of leaving it unexplained, and retry a paid hour exactly once instead of accidentally paying twice.

3180425d0b41feb1359a31abcf39ab569f241c95.text: When the assistant tries to look up information about your project's version history, it now handles errors more gracefully instead of crashing. This change affects developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, or SDK who work with projects that have git repositories. In everyday use, this means the assistant will keep working smoothly even on Windows systems where it previously might have failed when checking git history.

1bd6ccee9aa99ed5177e9a14441e2449c70e824c.text: This release extends Freebuff's optional sponsored features to Linux desktop alongside the existing Windows support, so advertisers can offer sponsored AI-assisted tasks tailored to each operating system (with Linux requiring a bwrap sandbox to qualify). The desktop experience now adjusts what optional sponsored actions appear based on whether you are on Windows or Linux, using simple on/off switches that the service can toggle remotely. Behind the scenes, a bug that caused the helper fetching your repository's recent changes to fail entirely on Windows whenever a particular formatting flag was present has been fixed, so prompts that depend on that context no longer break unexpectedly and instead degrade gracefully. Upgrading means sponsored desktop prompts reach you on the right platform with the right gating, and repository-aware tasks stay reliable on Windows where they previously could fail mid-run.

ab6bf9cb6c21a1501dd4f76f4be2cfffcee2207b.text: The price shown for the first paid model in your session now comes from the same purchase account that's paying for your current session, instead of a separate legacy price list. When you're actively using the assistant and have a valid session, the discount is read from the desktop purchase store; older trial sessions keep using the single-session store. This means the price you see quoted at the top of the model picker matches the account actually being charged, so ordinary claims no longer pull prices from the wrong place. The new behavior is live today for active desktop sessions.

5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.text: This Freebuff release updates the version number and includes several practical improvements for users of the free AI coding assistant. The biggest change is how the app handles updates: instead of replacing the running program while you work, it now waits patiently until you close your session to install any new version, so your in-progress work is never interrupted by an upgrade. Also improved is how the built-in search tool (ripgrep) is unpacked onto your computer, which is now done more safely by writing to a temporary location first and only moving it into place once it is fully and correctly installed, falling back to a user cache folder if there are permission issues, preventing broken or partial installations. For users who look back at past conversations, a new History shortcut (press 'h') lets you easily browse your chat history from the main screen, and old transcripts can be viewed in a read-only mode that lets you revisit and pick a model to continue from, without the usual input box. Lastly, the pricing shown for the first-tab discount is now correctly tied to your own active session, so users see and are charged the right price instead of a generic single-user rate. In daily use, upgrading to this version means updates won't disturb your work, the search tool installs more reliably, and reviewing past chats or applying discounts works as expected.

8d7a935e56beac4db2faa5f2421e2af0f1c6a905.text: Ox Alpha, an experimental anonymous AI model that was temporarily free to use through Freebuff, has been fully withdrawn from every model picker and session list as of August 27, 2026, because its anonymous host ended the free promotion. This affects developers and users who use the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK, particularly those on free or limited access tiers who may have previously selected Ox Alpha from the model list. In everyday use, you will no longer see Ox Alpha as an option in any Freebuff model picker, and any existing sessions that were started on that model before August 27 will still finish normally but no new sessions can be started using it; the system now quietly redirects any leftover references to the default free model instead.

9d0e435b3802e4b6b833c1ed349d604e5b804f0d.text: The Freebuff assistant on the web and cloud can now use a new experimental AI model named Ox Alpha, which gives it a large one-million-token memory for longer conversations. Only the hosted web and cloud versions of Freebuff can use this model, not the downloadable CLI or desktop app, because its creator is still testing how reliably it performs. The model is offered for free at a zero-dollar price cap, which stops it from being used for paid services or resold by other providers. You can try it now when talking to the assistant on freebuff.com or in the cloud workspace.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release makes GLM 5.3 Flash the new default AI model across the CLI, web, and desktop, while adding a new /reasoning command that lets you control how deeply each model thinks before it responds. The model picker now displays per-row wait times when models close during busy hours, and it correctly shows remaining sessions for shared premium pools instead of mislabeling quota counts. A first-party ad rail now serves house ads for the Pro subscription plan, and you can see which premium models your plan unlocks when you check the model picker if you have a paid subscription. The release also fixes several long-standing bugs: clipboard copies no longer hang waiting on a broken display server, stale tool calls cannot poison a resumed session, and directory creation now handles timing races on Windows cloud filesystems. Your daily use benefits from a model that is now uncapped on the free tier, clearer admission messages that name a replacement model when one is withdrawn, and ad revenue that no longer routes traffic to paid networks when configuration is missing.

bb4c8ba7c39a35a6514781f05ae534d40f2db56f.title: Streak bonus moves to the daily allowance
bb4c8ba7c39a35a6514781f05ae534d40f2db56f.summary: The streak bonus now lives in the daily Freebucks allowance (never the wallet) and the client renders when it lands and when the allowance reset removes it. `bonusExpiresAt` is threaded from `FreebuffStreakResponse` through `getFreebuffStreakBonusStatus` and the CLI layout forwarder, while `FreebuffFreebucksWindow` gains `streakBonus` so the pool can report what today's streak added, and the `limit` comment now says `plus streakBonus`. This corrects copy that described the bonus as a wallet credit and explains the 2026-09-27/28 reports where users east of Pacific saw the bonus as missing.
bb4c8ba7c39a35a6514781f05ae534d40f2db56f.evidence: Diff to `common/src/types/freebuff-streak.ts` adds bonusExpiresAt?: string | null to `FreebuffStreakResponse` and rewrites the comment on `todayCredited` to say the bonus is added to the daily allowance rather than the wallet; diff to `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` adds `streakBonus?: number` to `FreebuffFreebucksWindow` and updates the `limit` comment to mention `plus streakBonus`; diff to `common/src/util/freebuff-streak-line.ts` adds `bonusExpiresAt` to `getFreebuffStreakBonusStatus` params and rewrites its copy to render the bonus against the daily allowance and its reset; diff to `cli/src/utils/freebuff-streak-line.ts` forwards `bonusExpiresAt` from `FreebuffStreakResponse` into the shared status function.
bb4c8ba7c39a35a6514781f05ae534d40f2db56f.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side writer that populates `bonusExpiresAt` or `streakBonus`, so the rollout consumer is not visible. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Adds `bonusExpiresAt?: string | null` and rewrites the `todayCredited` doc to describe the daily allowance instead of the wallet.
Adds `streakBonus?: number` to `FreebuffFreebucksWindow` and updates the `limit` comment to reference `plus streakBonus`.
Accepts `bonusExpiresAt` in `getFreebuffStreakBonusStatus` and rewrites the status copy to describe the bonus against the daily allowance and its reset.
Forwards `bonusExpiresAt` from `FreebuffStreakResponse` into the shared `getFreebuffStreakBonusStatus` call.

bb4c8ba7c39a35a6514781f05ae534d40f2db56f.text: The streak bonus you earn for coding every day now adds to your daily Freebucks allowance instead of your wallet, and it leaves that allowance (not your balance) when your daily pool resets. This only affects Freebuff users who get Freebucks streak rewards on the Freebuff service, and if you're in that group you will notice the bonus no longer piles up between days - it resets cleanly each day along with your allowance. The change is live today and also fixes earlier confusion where users east of the Pacific time zone saw their daily streak bonus as missing.

f7461e3885e81bf95a5058142b2754174f13eb43.text: The Freebuff CLI has removed the old "refer friends for free credits" command - you can no longer type /refer-friends or redeem referral codes in the terminal to get free compute credits, since that growth program was shut down in April 2026. What remains is a simpler creator-attribution feature: if someone shared a special invite link with you, your signup is still credited to them as a thanks, but no credits change hands and nothing shows up in the CLI anymore. Existing referral codes continue to work on Freebuff's website and backend, so anything you previously earned is still honored.

9904cc1e3ed78b5d42266bbab905cb6dc7deef7a.text: Freebuff now locks its login file so only your user account on the computer can open it, instead of letting every program or person who can reach the file read your login token. This affects anyone using the Freebuff terminal app on a Mac or Linux machine. If you already use Freebuff, the next time you open it the login file will be made private automatically, so nothing changes for you except the extra protection; on Windows the behavior stays the same as before.

7c820ad975a16751494d83c24168fa7c22011fbc.text: The model picker in the CLI now shows you when a model is running at an off-peak price, with an inline chip and a timed message like "Off-peak, normally 15/hr until 6 PM". This only affects people who have been moved onto the Freebucks pay-per-use meter, so if you are on the free tier you will not see it. The picker also stays up to date if you leave the terminal closed or sleeping, and the displayed price is locked in once you start a session, so what you see is exactly what you pay.

6edaba95110f54cfee58529bbb0cfe1e19d95f5d.text: The SDK now rewrites certain AI chat requests on the fly, right before they are sent, so third-party connections work more smoothly. A new BYOK request transform is active today and adjusts how requests look depending on the destination endpoint, with developers who bring their own API keys to Freebuff being the audience that benefits. In daily use, direct connections to a specific model drop unsupported settings and swap in compatible ones, while anonymous traffic routed through a popular gateway now gets consistent, credential-based attribution on every call, and all other requests pass through unchanged.

eb3a241ab9e1d873a2d3256baa5228323dcccf3d.text: TikTok ad campaigns that pay per signup or per use of the coding assistant now correctly record activity that happens on a computer desktop or in the terminal, not just on the website. Advertisers running these paid campaigns are the ones affected. Daily use of the assistant is unchanged and no action is needed.

fd93692e814f3a7a4a3e61773e10e58384120e64.text: Freebuff 0.0.181 adds support for prepaid annual subscriptions, lets users start a BYOK session directly from the landing screen when they run out of Freebucks, and introduces MiMo 2.6 Flash and MiMo 2.6 Pro as new free model options. The ban exemption list is renamed and narrowed so it only waives specific punishment actions instead of disabling enforcement entirely, email hashing is consolidated for Meta and paid-social conversions, and TikTok activation events now report on the surface's public product page. The model selector drops the off-peak detail chip in favor of a badge plus tooltip, the off-peak price tooltip is simplified to one sentence, and usage data from BYOK providers is surfaced to the SDK client. The landing screen names the session host on network failures instead of blaming the client, the GLM 5.3 Flash price ceiling is held at $0.14/$0.45 after a rejected raise, and automatic provider stop sequences are removed from agent streams. An on-demand SDK compaction API and manual history compaction are added, the Supabase CPC experiment separates ad-request and local-execution surfaces, and refund display and end-session refund wording are removed from Freebuff surfaces. Upgrading gives you prepaid annual checkout options, direct BYOK access from walls, new MiMo models, clearer error messages, and consistent ad and attribution handling.

8870810f21a3f99ee8e7f349bd10e1dce92488d2.text: Freebuff has widened what model choices appear when using the web version of the assistant from certain locations, specifically excluding one particular premium model. This change is live today and only affects users of the Freebuff web interface who are located in regions where access was previously limited. These users now see more model options in their selection menu than before, including cheaper alternatives they were previously blocked from, while one specific paid model remains locked behind a subscription requirement.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds a new export feature so you can save your full chat conversations to a file (in markdown or JSON), and the model picker now shows how many free sessions you have left today, this week, and this month instead of just a daily count. The assistant now routes mid-turn messages through a queue instead of interrupting what is running, so commands like /plan, /interview, /review, and /skill wait their turn rather than overwriting the active job. Sponsored proposal tasks now run in a sandboxed worktree with a one-sentence consent prompt and proper device-node grants, and the CLI landing screens now offer an upgrade path when you hit rate or spend limits. The default free model swaps back to GLM 5.3 Flash with a migrated picker order, Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor is added across CLI/Desktop/Web/Cloud, and Gemini 3.8 Flash is withdrawn from the picker. Upgrading gives you safer mid-turn behavior, clearer free-tier metering, an export button for conversations, and sandboxed sponsor tasks that cannot escape their worktree.

48b5fee79a1016800772e01eafa8ceb3db346f98.text: Freebuff restored the daily free session allowance for users in limited regions back to six, after it had been cut to three. If you use Freebuff from a region that gets limited access (typically outside the US, Canada, UK, and EU, or while using a VPN), your daily free sessions for MiMo went back up from three to six. No action is needed: the change is already live, and your existing saved preferences and level are unaffected since they are calculated relative to this base.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release swaps the default free AI model back to GLM 5.3 Flash for new sessions while adding Muse Spark 1.3 as a selectable option across the CLI, desktop, web, and cloud. A new /export command lets you save a conversation to a file as either markdown or raw JSON, and the CLI now shows a one-time "Meet Freebucks" introduction card plus a metered model picker that lists per-model prices and your remaining balance instead of a session quota. Mid-turn messages to /plan, /interview, /review, and /skill commands now queue behind an in-progress run instead of interrupting it, and the CLI rate-limit and spend-limit screens render day-scale wait times and carry your Freebucks balance so refusals stay accurate. Sponsored proposal tasks gained in-terminal /ads accept, pull-request, and remove-worktree commands plus a rewritten single-sentence consent dialog, while model reasoning ladders and spend ceilings were clamped so metered models stay within their daily and per-session caps. Upgrading means the assistant defaults to a different model on startup, the picker shows prices and balance for paid-beyond-free work, you can export chats without copying text by hand, and mid-turn commands wait their turn instead of overwriting your active job.

70f1d8d632956affcf4ef483ae0c317dfd8d9403.text: The assistant's default model for Freebuff, GLM 5.3 Flash, no longer offers its deepest reasoning option in the picker, dropping the 'max' rung so it now only lets users choose 'low' and 'high'. At the same time, the model is now hard-set to 'high' by default, which prevents a problem where untouched conversations were running at an even deeper setting than 'max' and getting stuck in loops of re-reading files and re-planning steps instead of making progress. This change is live today and affects every Freebuff user who starts a new conversation on the free tier, web, desktop app, or CLI, since those surfaces have no effort control of their own and now consistently run at 'high' rather than the previously unset, deeper default.

25fab627e738eaf5ca5c596187c62fc2e12c5649.title: Add invoiced CPM delivery value field to PlacementTotals
25fab627e738eaf5ca5c596187c62fc2e12c5649.summary: An optional `invoicedValueCents?: number` field was added to the `PlacementTotals` interface in `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts`. The JSDoc describes it as the delivery value of invoiced CPM impressions (COD-677), billed outside the product, which the ledger never sees and the reconciliation between spend and delivery figures must not either. The field is optional and absence is treated as zero.
25fab627e738eaf5ca5c596187c62fc2e12c5649.evidence: The diff adds an optional `invoicedValueCents?: number` field to the `PlacementTotals` interface in `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts` (line 613), with a JSDoc comment describing it as delivery value of invoiced CPM impressions (COD-677) billed outside the product, noting absence means zero.
25fab627e738eaf5ca5c596187c62fc2e12c5649.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer of the new field or how the console uses it in spend and result pricing.

1654e2212f8267b7b9bebccea8ec5a4992d638d8.title: Muse Spark OpenRouter lane pinned to meta with 0.15/0.3 price ceiling
1654e2212f8267b7b9bebccea8ec5a4992d638d8.summary: Adds MUSE_SPARK_OPENROUTER_UPSTREAM_ORDER and MUSE_SPARK_OPENROUTER_MAX_PRICE in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts to pin the Muse Spark OpenRouter lane to the meta endpoint at $0.10/$0.20 list pricing. The lane exists because Meta's direct key was user_blocked about fourteen minutes after 1.3 went paid-only on 2026-09-28, sending every pick to the DeepSeek fallback, so OpenRouter is used as a separate account with its own rate limit. The price ceiling sits strictly above the $0.10/$0.20 card so a repriced or mislabelled host becomes unroutable rather than billed.
1654e2212f8267b7b9bebccea8ec5a4992d638d8.evidence: In common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts the added block defines MUSE_SPARK_OPENROUTER_UPSTREAM_ORDER = ['meta'] as const and MUSE_SPARK_OPENROUTER_MAX_PRICE = { prompt: 0.15, completion: 0.3 } as const, with the comment stating the direct Meta key was user_blocked about fourteen minutes after 1.3 went paid-only on 2026-09-28, so OpenRouter is used as the lane.
1654e2212f8267b7b9bebccea8ec5a4992d638d8.unknowns: The diff does not show the reader or runtime enforcement of MUSE_SPARK_OPENROUTER_MAX_PRICE and MUSE_SPARK_OPENROUTER_UPSTREAM_ORDER, so it is unclear who consumes these new constants in this commit.

1654e2212f8267b7b9bebccea8ec5a4992d638d8.text: The Freebuff team added a price cap to the OpenRouter route that the assistant uses to reach the Muse Spark model, so that if Meta ever changes its pricing, the request will be rejected instead of silently costing more. This only affects Freebuff engineering operations and does not change anything you see in your daily coding sessions today.

25fab627e738eaf5ca5c596187c62fc2e12c5649.text: Freebuff added a new reporting column to its advertiser console that records the dollar value of ad impressions billed separately through a sales contract. This only affects the internal tools Freebuff staff and advertisers use to review campaign results. Advertisers will now see this invoiced value added into their spend and pricing numbers where applicable, with missing data treated as zero.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds a new Freebucks pay-as-you-go meter that lets you spend beyond your free allowance, a once-only "Meet Freebucks" intro card the first time you open the model picker, and a new /export slash command that saves your full conversation to a markdown or JSON file in your project root. The model picker now lists Meta Muse Spark 1.3 (which falls back to DeepSeek V4 Flash when busy) and drops Gemini 3.8 Flash, while the default free model is now GLM 5.3 Flash across the CLI and Web. Sponsored ad proposals gained a two-step consent flow with dedicated slash commands (/ads:accept-proposal, /ads:pull-request) that run advertiser tasks in a separate git worktree with a sandboxed terminal, and the CLI now surfaces upgrade calls-to-action right on rate- and spend-limit screens so a blocked free session can reach a paid plan without dead-ending. You also get clearer Freebucks pricing, day-scale wait labels for monthly resets, house-ad suppression for subscribers, and new telemetry so the service can track ad fills and sponsored-run outcomes more accurately. Upgrading gives you spendable credits past the free tier, a real way to export conversations, safer sandboxed ad runs, and a smoother path from free limits to paid plans.

6b1963707ad3659f9d2308535dff59f317cd8174.text: The Desktop app now runs real end-to-end checks for sponsored (advertiser-funded) tasks: accepting a task, editing code in a sandbox, committing on a branch, and opening a pull request were all verified live against one macOS machine on one test repo, so the Desktop conformance table drops those rows from its 'waived' list and only keeps one (E-5, the failure rendering, which was only seen incidentally). The CLI still shows nothing yet, because no code path actually displays sponsored tasks in your chat, so its existing 'no execution' and 'no producer' waivers stay the same.

f9b0815704eb34ebed2b8852b1a27c4902664d58.text: The session response that the assistant's CLI, web, and desktop apps receive now includes a Freebucks balance block on every authenticated state, so clients can display your spendable Freebucks credits and the per-model session prices directly from the session reply instead of making a separate lookup, with the balance and prices shown in the model picker, during a session, and after it ends. This ride on every state for the same reason subscription data does: the balance is visible in the picker, mid-session, and after it finishes. This release label version bumps the Freebuff package to ship these new balance and pricing types to users today, with no action needed from you.

477b0e47facf165557cca9b60a070dacc3f6f9d9.text: When you open the Freebuff coding assistant and a model you had picked is still valid for your account, the assistant now keeps that model selected instead of silently switching you back to the default free model. This is for subscribers on limited or paid plans whose saved model choice should stay in place across a new session. As a result, you won't see your model unexpectedly revert to the free tier the moment you rejoin or refresh, and your last choice stays saved for your next start. The fix is live today for Freebuff CLI users on limited-access or paid subscriptions.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release makes GLM 5.3 Flash the default AI model for free users, adds Solar Pro 4 as a new available model, and introduces a /reasoning command for controlling how thoroughly the AI model thinks through tasks. The model picker now shows when time-limited models will return and names the time zone so you know when they reopen. Clipboard copying now has a timeout that prevents the terminal from freezing when a display server is broken, and a newer copy will no longer be overwritten by an older one waiting in the background. Streak progress display was made more readable with clearer filled-versus-empty indicators, and the dashboard buttons use accent colors for better focus visibility.

57c010db236b4b5ffba7030cb4eff4bb50a4a333.text: When you subscribe to a paid Freebuff plan, the model picker in the CLI now shows a single muted line below the catalog with the plan's own windows - today, 5-day, and month usage - and, if a limit is currently blocking you, a second row naming that limit (e.g. today's plan sessions are used) with a countdown to its reset. The same shared summary that drives this line also powers the Desktop and web usage page, so all three surfaces name the same binding limit and the same reset instant. The picker's height estimate now counts these plan rows too, so a blocked user on a short terminal no longer has the blocking row clipped off the first frame. Live today for paid subscribers; free-tier users see nothing new since freebuffPlanSummary returns undefined when there is no entitling plan.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release overhauls the Freebuff free AI model lineup and adds new spending and ad features. The free model picker now leads with GLM 5.3 Flash (an unmetered, uncapped reasoning model) and includes Solar Pro 4, while DeepSeek V4 Pro, MiniMax M3, and Ox Alpha are withdrawn from the free tier. You can now use a new slash command, /reasoning, to set how deeply the selected free model thinks before responding, with your choice saved per model. Freebuff introduces a Trust engagement feed where ad interactions convert into free and premium session bonuses, and paid subscription tiers (Starter, Plus) are added with daily/weekly/monthly session allowances that top up your free pool. The CLI model picker now shows return-time labels for time-gated models and preserves your selected premium model when you have a paid plan. Ad delivery shifts to a live first-party rail with real inventory across chat surfaces, with new creative safety filtering and operational telemetry. Upgrading gives you a refreshed free model catalog led by GLM 5.3 Flash, a way to control reasoning depth inline, and access to paid subscription tiers that add sessions to your free allowance.

a4837a425cd7f9ac57d590d53a9ef1bc20fa63f6.text: The SDK team swapped out the old bundled code-search tool (from version 14 to 15) and added support for Windows computers running on ARM processors, like the new Surface laptops. This is internal maintenance for the Freebuff engineering team, so you won't notice any difference in how the app works today, and no action is needed on your end. Behind the scenes, the new version of the search tool is now downloaded and packaged for all supported platforms, including ARM64 Windows which was previously missing, and the way the app figures out which binary to use on your machine has been cleaned up into a single lookup table instead of a long list of conditions. There's no visible change to the app's features or performance for end users.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release adds the new GLM 5.3 Flash model as the default AI for Freebuff, along with Solar Pro 4 as a trial option, and gives you a new /reasoning command to control how deeply the AI thinks per model. The model picker now shows when time-limited models reopen, you can earn Trust points by engaging with first-party ads that convert into free and premium session bonuses, and a house ad fills slots when no paid campaign can serve. For daily use, you get clearer model-availability labels, a less negative Trust score that decays slower than it builds, and subscription tiers (Starter, Plus, Pro) whose free-session pools now top up rather than replace your free allowance, plus monthly spend ceilings so a plan stops billing once it hits its cap. The ad system moved to a flat daily subscription model with new placements and creative sanitization, and the SDK now bundles ripgrep 15.2.0 for code search.

e30c58d37ea03426da0f01a727c5acff3895a462.text: If you're a developer who uses the Freebuff CLI, here is what happened. When a model you picked gets permanently removed from the free tier while you are trying to start a session, the tool now tells you the model is gone and that you should use the default fallback model instead, then it quietly switches your session to that fallback so you are not sitting there waiting on nothing. Your saved model preference is remembered for next time, so a one-off withdrawal does not hijack all of your future sessions. This only affects Freebuff free-tier users on the CLI, and you will notice it as a plain chat message explaining the switch instead of the session just vanishing or hanging.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release puts GLM 5.3 Flash (z-ai/glm-5.3-flash) at the front of the Freebuff free model picker as the new default model across the CLI, Web, and Desktop, after removing it from the premium metered pool so it runs uncapped. DeepSeek V4 Flash reopens full availability again after its peak-hours closure was removed, while DeepSeek V4 Pro, MiniMax M3, and Ox Alpha remain withdrawn from the free picker. A new /reasoning slash command lets you read or set how hard the selected model thinks before it answers, validated against the model's local ladder and persisted per model in your settings. The spend-ceiling system switched from a flat 50 USD daily limit to a per-region ceiling table with a 50 cent restricted cap and a 2x hard live-session multiplier, and the referral-abuse list grew by five disposable email domains. Ad delivery moved to a first-party delivery plane with creative sanitization that strips terminal-control characters from ad copy and enforces absolute https destinations, while a resilient acknowledgement transport with best-effort retries now carries first-party ad impressions. Upgrading gives you GLM 5.3 Flash as the unmetered default hero, control over model thinking effort, and a less aggressive spending gate that only pauses fresh sessions instead of interrupting the one you are using.

d9e94b083c24c9e1fa9655b0e55f5cdfc6506865.text: Freebuff removed a daily limit it used to impose on the GPT-5.6 Luna model, so that model now shares the same overall daily session allowance as the other premium models instead of having its own separate cap. The limit had been based on a pricing estimate that turned out to be incorrect, with Luna actually costing less per session than the competing model, so the developers decided to drop the extra restriction. This affects developers who use the Freebuff command-line tool, web assistant, or desktop app to pick and run AI models, since their usage now counts entirely against their normal daily allowance rather than a model-specific bucket.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release makes GLM 5.3 Flash the default AI model when you use Freebuff in your terminal, browser, or desktop app, replacing GPT-5.6 Luna as the first model shown in every picker. You can also now control how deeply a model thinks using a new /reasoning command, so you can ask for lighter or deeper reasoning per model and have your choice remembered in settings. The ad-supported free tier got a new advertiser marketplace with a $0.50 engagement price and seven-day campaign limits, plus a Trust engagement feed that converts ad clicks and sign-ups into free bonus sessions. Behind the scenes the CLI now explains when a model you picked has been permanently withdrawn (naming a replacement instead of silently swapping it), shows when peak-hour models reopen using your local time zone, and no longer freezes if a clipboard tool or a stalled tool call is left hanging. Users on paid plans see their remaining subscription sessions surfaced directly in the model picker, and the app will no longer claim a referral gave you an extra session once you have hit your daily cap. If you upgrade, you get a clearer, ad-funded free experience with more predictable model availability and a couple of new controls (reasoning depth and subscription-aware model selection) that make the same free allowance go a little further.

161b864dd4f665957ded8250837935b5f8612cfc.text: A new shared set of rules was added so that every part of the app agrees on what a sponsored AI coding task can offer you and how it should be described, including the safest way to handle links and logos that come with it. This affects the Freebuff engineering team only, since the actual screens that show these proposals are not part of this change. For now there is nothing you will notice differently, because nothing else in the app reads these new rules yet.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds a new AI model (Muse Spark 1.3) to the free model picker and makes GLM 5.3 Flash the default model across the CLI and Web surfaces, while removing Gemini 3.8 Flash from the picker and Solar Pro 4's session cap. It introduces a Freebucks pay-as-you-go credits system with a meter in the model picker and new rate-limited/spend-limited landing screens that show your remaining balance and upgrade prompts. You can now export your conversations to a file with a new /export command that writes markdown or JSON. The CLI also gains support for sponsored proposal tasks that run sandboxed in a linked worktree, plus new ad event telemetry and consent dialog improvements. Upgrading gives you a refreshed model list with Muse Spark 1.3 available, pay-as-you-go pricing via Freebucks with real-time balance display, conversation exports, and safer handling of mid-turn messages and sponsored runs.

c235ded0aec8696b8af0e9fbb9e7fe1529e8bf1f.text: The title bar of your chat input box and the queue panel now act like buttons you can click. When messages are waiting in line, you can click the preview text at the top of your composer to open the queue panel, and click the panel's title bar to close it again. This affects anyone using the Freebuff CLI or desktop app to chat with the assistant. You'll notice that instead of seeing a hint telling you to press Ctrl+Q, you simply click the queue summary to see and edit your pending messages.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.title: Freebuff CLI 0.1.8 adds launch-intent partner ad slot
f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.1.8 is released by bumping the version in freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.1.7 to 0.1.8, packaging a new partner ad slot that fires when a draft is about launching, shipping or deploying rather than opening a PR. `cli/src/chat.tsx` now picks `CLI_PARTNER_PLACEMENT_IDS.composerLaunch` via the new `mentionsLaunchKeyword` from `common/src/ads/partner-triggers.ts`, which shares the whole-word tokenizer `mentionsAnyWord` with the existing PR trigger so the two slots never collide. The registry in `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts` registers the `Desktop-Partner-Composer-Launch` and `CLI-Partner-Composer-Launch` slots as available: false partner placements labeled 'Composer (launch intent)', so the composer row can render one advertiser's chrome next to a launch-focused draft.
f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.evidence: cli/src/ads/partner-ads.ts adds `composerLaunch: 'CLI-Partner-Composer-Launch'` to `CLI_PARTNER_PLACEMENT_IDS`; cli/src/chat.tsx routes the composer row to that slot when `mentionsLaunchKeyword(inputValue)` matches instead of only `mentionsPrKeyword`; common/src/ads/partner-triggers.ts introduces `LAUNCH_INTENT_KEYWORDS` and `mentionsLaunchKeyword` sharing the whole-word tokenizer `mentionsAnyWord`; common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts registers the two new `Desktop-Partner-Composer-Launch` and `CLI-Partner-Composer-Launch` partner slots and labels them 'Composer (launch intent)'; freebuff/cli/release/package.json bumps version 0.1.7 -> 0.1.8.
f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.unknowns: The diff does not show the ad policy or operator agreement that authorizes a campaign onto the new LAUNCH slot.

changes.what: Compser partner row now auctions the launch slot when the draft mentions launch, ship, deploy, demo or related keywords, falling back to the PR slot only when the PR keyword matches.
Adds the LAUNCH_INTENT_KEYWORDS set and mentionsLaunchKeyword helper built on the shared whole-word tokenizer, plus the two new partner placement ids and their display labels.
Bumps the published freebuff CLI manifest version from 0.1.7 to 0.1.8.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.text: A second ad slot now appears above the input box when the assistant is writing about launching, deploying, or showing off finished work, sitting beside the existing sponsorship slot that appears for pull-request-related drafts. This only affects advertisers who have paid for placement in the CLI and the desktop app, both of which already supported the matching launch-intent slot.
