You will not notice anything different unless an advertiser has an active campaign, and no action is required.

85fe163fd7843afe7dc3d07df57d2ac8eade07c4.text: Three test-only AI models (two named Greg and one named Ling) and a fourth model called HY3 have been removed from the code that controls which AI models Freebuff developers test with internally. These were never available to regular Freebuff users in the app picker, and HY3 was already cut from user-facing lists earlier in August. The developer-facing tools now use a different test model named Kimi K3 in their place. You see nothing new or different in your Freebuff sessions from this change: it only affects the internal menu that Freebuff's engineering team uses to test models before they are offered to you.

fbf092f424327cab5a5086a0cf209d9199dcac73.text: When you open the model picker in the Freebuff assistant and look at the list of models to choose from, each model now shows you how much 'thinking effort' it uses, like 'Reasoning: high'. The picker now shows this information directly on each row, including the effort level the model actually runs at. If you are a developer using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK, you can now see the reasoning effort level for models like DeepSeek V4 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and GPT-5.6 Luna before committing to use them. No action is needed on your part; this is simply an added piece of information shown when you view the available models.

a47be121a650358f747794cf743870e75d35e6b3.text: The engineering team renamed two helper scripts that manually run the browser-use and librarian agents, changing their file names from names ending in 'test' to names starting with 'run', because the previous naming caused the test runner to crash while scanning all test files at once. This affects only the internal development tooling used by the Freebuff engineering team and has no impact on how the application behaves for users.

92a6961b894204c5620f9dd77cd2606e54b9a397.text: The Freebuff CLI has added a way for developers to create skills that only you can start manually, keeping them hidden from the assistant's automatic tool discovery. If you write a skill and add the flag `disable-model-invocation: true` in its SKILL.md frontmatter, the assistant will refuse to use it on its own and show an error saying 'can only be invoked by the user.' Developers who author skills now need to add this flag if they want to restrict a skill to explicit user invocation. Additionally, the suggestion menu that pops up as you type now syncs better with what's actually in the input box, so selecting a skill inserts it correctly instead of lagging behind what you typed.

f28ecce37f526a75beecd2e0c8d82da50630abba.text: Freebuff removed the MiMo 2.5 Pro model and a second GLM 5.2 route from its free service. This is a backend change for Freebuff operators, not something you trigger yourself. If you used MiMo 2.5 Pro on a recent Freebuff client, it is no longer offered; the regular (non-Pro) MiMo 2.5, and referral-earned access to GLM 5.2, are unchanged. No action is required from you, but saved preferences for the removed model will stop working.

f56844fd118df56422c40c55968c247d6253c562.text: When the assistant runs a command in your terminal on Windows, it now briefly turns off the terminal's mouse and keyboard focus signals before that command starts, then turns them back on again only after the command finishes. This keeps command programs from writing stray control codes like `^[[<35;187;32M` directly over the assistant's screen. The change is live today for Windows users of the assistant; Mac and Linux users do not notice anything different. You do not need to enable or change anything, and the assistant's own interface and keyboard input keep working normally while a command runs.

51e08c800533ae4206e4e740eade9b700d2b7d9f.title: Drop the Freebuff web chat house ad surface

This narrows the checked-in floor creatives the ad-serving package requires to be total over every surface, reducing the surface set from five to four. 51e08c800533ae4206e4e740eade9b700d2b7d9f.text: Freebuff removed one of its built-in ad slots, the one that previously appeared in the web chat interface, so there is now one fewer place the app tries to show a fallback house advertisement. Maintainers only: this trims a constant and a couple of matching creatives from the shared copy file, leaving four surfaces instead of five. For anyone using Freebuff today there is nothing to update and no moment you will notice, since the web chat slot was not actively serving anything visible anyway.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This release adds a new AI model called GPT-5.6 Luna to the free model picker, switches the recommended model on the CLI to DeepSeek V4 Pro, and makes several reliability and advertising changes. The update ensures that when you deliberately pick a model from the landing screen, the session re-claims on that model instead of silently reverting to a previous choice, and it adds an IP-capped status path so too many shared users on one network are routed to the landing screen instead of erroring. Ads now wait two response nodes before showing the first placement, then appear every three nodes, and a new shared ad user-agent makes the CLI report a consistent browser-like identity when fetching ads. Under the hood, the SDK now auto-retries interrupted streams (up to three times) and caps subprocess output at 10 million characters to prevent crashes, while the context pruner tracks separate budgets for user and assistant messages instead of a single cutoff. Upgrading means you get the new Luna model as a selectable option, a more dependable recommended default, fewer mid-task crashes from huge command outputs or dropped streams, and clearer handling when you or others share an IP. The streak GLM bonus now grants one session per day for full-access referrals with no read-time ceiling, and the daily free session limit rose from 5 to 6.

32405d54b26ef83e80be7c091a8c9610c6bf3b8a.text: The Freebuff CLI now uses a single, dedicated terminal-protocol manager to safely run shell commands, replacing the older Windows-specific guard. When you run a bash command from the assistant on Windows, the protocol manager briefly disables the terminal's mouse and keyboard-reporting features so the command can't accidentally paint stray control characters over the user interface, then turns them back on only after the command's full process group has exited. This only affects Freebuff CLI users on Windows who run terminal commands; there are no new user-facing features or settings to change, but the command runner behaves more reliably, failing closed with an actionable message if terminal isolation cannot be established.

7c831448a6e554c45b87894487ebe7421385045f.text: On Windows, the SDK no longer falls back to the Linux-style bash that comes with WSL when looking for bash to run commands. Instead, it checks only the standard Linux-for-Windows install (Git Bash), the user's own pointed-to bash, and bash/Git programs already on the system path, and it stops treating Windows-built-in bash as a safe choice. If you are a Windows user who does not have Git Bash (or any real bash) installed, commands that need bash will now fail with a clear message instead of attempting a flaky WSL fallback that could break silently. For Windows users who already have Git Bash installed, the change is invisible: everything still works as before.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: Freebuff CLI 1.0.685 ships a larger free daily session quota (6 per day instead of 5) plus weekly GLM streak bonuses that now scale with how long your streak is, and the CLI's recommended hero model now defaults to DeepSeek V4 Pro. Downloads and installs now happen through a staged, rollback-safe flow so a failed update won't leave a half-written binary, and a shared exponential-backoff retry with a redirect cap makes network fetches more resilient. The CLI now aborts an in-flight agent run before you switch chats so a run can't keep writing into the wrong conversation's transcript, and spend-limited sessions route you to a landing screen with a countdown timer instead of an opaque error. New models joined the free picker including GPT-5.6 Luna and Ling 3.0 Flash, while Kwaipilot/Kimi K2.7 Code were retired from free mode and MiniMax M3 moved into the premium pool so it now flips to a fallback when the paid pool is exhausted. Ads in streamed responses now wait two nodes before the first placement and then space every three, and the model selector moved the session counter and referral banner inside its scrollbox so the layout no longer steals viewport rows. On upgrade you get a safer binary update path, accurate spend- and rate-limit messaging, cleaner multi-chat isolation, and an expanded free model catalog with clearer guidance on which model is recommended by default.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: The default AI model you write code with switched to GLM 5.3 Flash, which now leads every picker as an unlimited, uncapped free model across the CLI, web, and desktop, replacing GPT-5.6 Luna as the first choice you see. DeepSeek V4 Pro and DeepSeek V4 Flash are back to always-available with no per-model daily caps, GLM 5.3 Flash gained a reasoning-effort ladder you can tune with /reasoning [level], and the model picker gained new /reasoning slash command support. Safety improvements include new spam and referral-abuse domain blocks, a per-process exception budget that stops PostHog log spam, hardened ad-creative sanitization that strips terminal control sequences, and on-device path translation that maps Git Bash POSIX paths to native Windows paths in the SDK. For daily use, this means fewer rejected requests during peak hours, clearer refusal messages when a model is closed or withdrawn, a single house-ad copy source of truth for the subscribe prompt, and spending limits that now pause at a half-dollar daily ceiling for VPN/proxy egress instead of silently coercing you to another model.

cef358330ebed218abe3c1d8df88a8d4bb8315db.text: A new rule was added so that when a model leaves the free limited tier, the system quietly swaps in the tier's remaining model instead of charging the user. This only affects free-tier users whose session was admitted on a model that has since been removed from their tier. If you are on a free tier and your session's model was withdrawn, the assistant will now run a different model at no charge rather than silently starting to burn your credits or blocking the turn. No action is needed from you, and the change is already live for affected sessions.

65f20efb85fbaa7d2ec42f484fbbf9b39c57f751.text: The crofAI-powered GLM 5.2 model is now directly choosable from the web and cloud model picker instead of being hidden behind an experimental-only gate, so if you have full access to Freebuff's web or desktop experience you can select GLM 5.2 just like any other premium model. It now carries its own separate one-session-per-day limit rather than drawing from the shared premium pool, meaning your regular premium sessions remain untouched when you use it. Users in limited regions still cannot select it, and no action is required - the change is already live today.

3b7ce89c8102761014eafbe97cced66d9a22ec88.title: GPT-6.1 Sol added to the free model picker
3b7ce89c8102761014eafbe97cced66d9a22ec88.summary: GPT-6.1 Sol lands in the Freebuff catalog as a new `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` row with a temporary 100-Freebucks promotional price, free in the US and plan-locked elsewhere, so the picker can offer OpenAI's flagship alongside the existing US-or-paid rows. New base2/base3 roots (`base2-free-gpt-6-1-sol`, `base3-free-gpt-6-1-sol`) and a same-model reviewer (`code-reviewer-gpt-6-1-sol`) wire the model into the CLI and Desktop agent allowlists, and `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts` adds it to the premium sub-capped and plan-metered sets. The row carries a promotional badge rendered from `GPT_61_SOL_PROMOTIONAL` so released clients show the same temporary-price copy on both the catalog and the Freebucks price notice.
3b7ce89c8102761014eafbe97cced66d9a22ec88.evidence: New file `common/src/constants/freebuff-sol-promo.ts` exports `GPT_61_SOL_PROMOTIONAL`; `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` adds `FREEBUFF_GPT_61_SOL_MODEL_ID` ('openai/gpt-6.1-sol') and a `GPT_61_SOL_MODEL` entry to `SUPPORTED_FREEBUFF_MODELS` and `FREEBUFF_MODELS`; new files `agents/base2/base2-free-gpt-6-1-sol.ts`, `agents/base3-free-gpt-6-1-sol.ts`, `agents/reviewer/code-reviewer-gpt-6-1-sol.ts` register the matching base2/base3 roots and reviewer, and `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts` wires `base2-free-gpt-6-1-sol` and `code-reviewer-gpt-6-1-sol` into `FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_IDS` and `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS`; READMEs and the model selector surface the row for US (free) and other regions (paid).
3b7ce89c8102761014eafbe97cced66d9a22ec88.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side admission/coercion consumer that enforces the US-or-paid gate from `planRequiredModelIds`, so the runtime path that decides whether a given viewer can actually open a session is not visible here.

changes.what: Adds the GPT-6.1 Sol model id, price ceiling, upstream order, reasoning effort, and a promotional badge constant to the catalog and subscription sets.
Adds base2/base3 roots and a same-model code reviewer for GPT-6.1 Sol, and registers them in the free-mode allowlist and root-id lists.
Renders the promotional badge on the model row's second line so the temporary-price warning is visible in the picker.
Adds GPT-6.1 Sol to the Desktop slot-bound concurrency list because it is the dearest quota-metered row.

3b7ce89c8102761014eafbe97cced66d9a22ec88.text: OpenAI's newest flagship model, GPT-6.1 Sol, is now available to pick from Freebuff's model list, at least if you are in the United States. If you are outside the US, you can still see it offered, but selecting it will prompt you toward a paid subscription. The model is priced at a temporary promotional rate of 100 Freebucks per session (its normal cost is higher), and carries a 1 million token context window with image support. This is live for Freebuff users starting 2026-09-29 as part of the model catalog update, with the promotional label appearing alongside the price in the picker.

c8e487a6246813b34d1f8a6942bef69352c80bc4.text: The Freebuff Cloud custom-stack planner now uses the MiniMax M3 model for planning, while the build phase after 'Start building' switches to DeepSeek V4 Pro, with a new 12-turn limit on planning conversations to prevent runaway free sessions. Three supporting functions were added to safely select and validate the build model per access tier and client request, and the required_integrations field now defaults to an empty list so planners that cannot cite a specific recommendation can still finalize instead of blocking the build button. This affects only internal Freebuff engineering maintainers working on the shared Core package; no Freebuff, Codebuff, or end-user-facing behavior changes for you, and there is nothing you need to do or will notice in daily use.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: Version 1.0.685 ships a major refresh of the Freebuff free tier, adding new AI models to the picker, making the landing screen adapt better to your terminal size, and tightening ad placement so ads appear less often in short answers. The recommended free model is now DeepSeek V4 Pro (it already shows the data-use/training notice), a dated DeepSeek V4 Flash 07/31 row is called out as new, and MiniMax M3 and DeepSeek V4 Pro are de-emphasized with a supersede notice so the list steers you toward Flash. The referral GLM 5.2 reward is now a daily +1 session pool (instead of weekly), and qualified referrals grant one GLM session per day with no read-time ceiling. Behind the scenes the CLI now aborts an in-flight run before switching chats, downloads the binary as a staged partial archive with rollback so a failed update won't leave a half-written binary, and caps redirect chains plus retries transient download errors. Other user-visible improvements include a compact image indicator ('Images') on every model row, a centered supersede notice, and the session counter moving inside the model selector's scrollbox so the layout no longer reserves dead viewport rows. For developers the SDK now forwards an acting-user id header, auto-retries interrupted streams up to 3 times, caps subprocess output at 10M characters to prevent crashes on huge git diffs, and routes Windows terminal redirects through bash-compatible /dev/null. A fresh session that hits a free-session cap now lands on a dedicated screen explaining the limit and showing when you can try again, and the daily free quota moved from 5 to 6 sessions per day.

8e956567928c769287011b3a1b8974d8d646631a.text: The engineering team made the automated test suite more reliable when run on a fresh checkout of the codebase. Previously, running tests locally could fail silently on up to 371 tests because two helper modules were missing until a separate setup step ran; now each package runs a small setup step that builds those modules first, so a plain test command works anywhere without manual prep. Documentation was updated to explain the rule that every package needs this setup, and a flag was added so test code never accidentally sends data to the live analytics backend. This is an internal change for developers maintaining the codebase and has no effect on the assistant's behavior.

c9bdd9c7b58e05b498d296cf64fcaaa3db54890d.text: When a developer asks the AI assistant to do a task and then retries the same task after something went wrong, the system used to get confused and fail completely because it saw the same work result twice. Now the assistant quietly skips over results it has already seen, so retrying a failed task no longer breaks the conversation. This change is live in the agent runtime and affects no setup on your part. If you develop with the Freebuff SDK and resend results after an error, your retry now works instead of stalling the conversation.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This Freebuff CLI release updates the model catalog, session limits, and how free credits work. DeepSeek V4 Pro becomes the recommended default CLI model, GPT-5.6 Luna joins the free picker as a new selectable model, and Kimi K2.7 Code and MiniMax M3 are repositioned with superseded-model nudges and automatic preference migration toward Flash. The daily free session limit rises to six per day, the GLM 5.2 referral reward switches from weekly to daily reset, and MiniMax M3 moves into the shared premium pool. Ads are skipped after two nodes then shown every three nodes, and the binary download now uses staged downloads with rollback on failure. When too many users share one IP, the CLI no longer loops and instead shows a landing screen telling you how many are ahead and when to retry.

This release updates the Freebuff coding assistant's model lineup and refines how it handles sessions, ads, and agent behavior. Several models were reorganized: MiniMax M3 moved to the premium daily pool while GPT-5.6 Luna became a free model, the streak GLM bonus now refreshes weekly, and the daily free session limit rose from 5 to 6. The CLI now handles interrupted streams by retrying automatically, prevents stale runs from writing into the wrong conversation, and routes IP-capped sessions to the landing screen instead of looping endlessly. Ads in responses now wait two nodes before the first placement then space every three nodes, and read-files enforces a shared 100,000-character limit across all files in a single call. Upgrading gives you more predictable session limits, cleaner interruption handling when network hiccups occur, and a model picker that keeps your saved preferences up to date when models are deprecated.

0ff93e746badad951717b0a70386bf5b24701517.text: When an assistant is in the middle of a task and gets interrupted, it can leave behind a half-finished tool call with no matching result. Strict providers like DeepSeek reject these orphans with a 400, and because the history is persisted and replayed, that one orphan would fail every later turn. The runtime now cleans the history at the single point where each step's request is built, dropping any tool call that lacks a corresponding response, and writes the cleaned history back so the saved state stays valid. If the assistant finishes a turn cleanly and every tool call has its result, nothing is touched. This is internal maintenance work, so there is no visible effect for you: your sessions will just keep working instead of stalling on a stale, broken turn.

e78563f1e523d46e46a3234eeb84bb3e77cb9b4b.text: The CLI moved the chat's live session state (whether the assistant is thinking, streaming, or stopped) out of the chat view and into a background provider that survives when you switch chats or open history. Now when you jump to history and back, or start a new chat, the running session keeps its state instead of being torn down and rebuilt. You see fewer flickers where the assistant appears to restart or lose connection during normal navigation, and switching chats reliably stops the old conversation instead of leaving it streaming in the background.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This Freebuff CLI release focuses heavily on making the model picker, session management, and reliability more polished for daily use. You now get a dated DeepSeek V4 Flash option marked as newer and better, the landing screen shows your daily session counter inside the model list, and the recommended hero model defaults to DeepSeek V4 Pro. Ads in streamed responses now wait two nodes before the first placement and then space every three nodes, and the referral banner moved inside the model selector so the screen layout no longer desyncs on wrapped text. When the shared Freebuff spend budget runs out, the CLI routes you to a landing screen that explains the daily free limit and shows when you can try again instead of erroring out. Streamed AI responses now auto-retry on silent connection drops (up to three recoveries), and Ctrl+C now drains analytics logs before exiting so telemetry is less likely to be lost. A series of analytics events and layout tweaks land across Desktop and Web surfaces, including autorun toggles, project removal tracking, and turn-background-wait signals to separate long waits from real hangs, plus the read-files tool now enforces a shared 100,000-character and 20,000-token budget across all files in one call.

0b35949fad7bbaf605afbd048ca912c14d4a3173.text: The assistant can now mark a brand-new Freebuff Cloud project as ready for your approval once it has put together a complete plan. When you are using a blank Cloud project, the assistant can hand you a summary, the chosen tech stack, and a build brief, then signal that everything is settled and waiting on your go-ahead. Who this affects: developers working on blank Freebuff Cloud projects. What you notice: a 'Start building' confirmation that appears after the plan is finalized, instead of the task staying open-ended.

0a6df5765585fe3da17d92272fbce28be74bc127.text: Previously, each advertisement was anchored below one specific completed assistant answer and stayed pinned there in the conversation. Now, when you send Freebuff a prompt, a single batch of up to eight ads is fetched and the assistant's reply is laid out as a sequence of sections, with ad cards dropped in between those sections (roughly every four nodes), so a short one-liner shows no ads and a long, tool-using answer carries several. The rotating ad that sits just above your input box still exists, but it is now fetched through its own separate placement id so it keeps rotating on its own cadence and is tracked for reporting continuity.

99f8bdf7238772049723aee6d133b9e2af05e10c.text: When you ask for a recommendation for a developer service like an email or database provider, the assistant now passes along a tracked referral link that the system fills in automatically, so the button it shows always points to the exact sign-up link the service provider gave Freebuff, rather than a generic or possibly mistyped URL. This only affects you when you are using Freebuff Chat or the assistant suggests a service it found through Gravity Index. You just click the same "Get your API key" button as before, but the link behind it is now guaranteed to be the correct tracked one every time.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This release updates the Freebuff CLI coding assistant with new AI models, improved download reliability, and several user experience fixes. The Freebuff daily session limit increased from 5 to 6 sessions per day, giving you one additional free session each day, and new models including GPT-5.6 Luna and DeepSeek V4 Pro now appear in the free model picker alongside updated taglines for existing models. The app now handles interrupted network connections during AI responses by automatically retrying up to 3 times instead of stopping, and it shows a clear message when too many people on the same network share a free session rather than silently reloading. Ads in AI responses now appear after 2 nodes then every 3 nodes, the referral banner moved inside the model selector to free up screen space, and cross-chat data mixing is prevented by aborting in-progress tasks before switching conversations. The binary updater now downloads to a temporary file and installs with rollback, so failed updates restore the previous version instead of leaving a broken install, and the SDK caps subprocess output at 10 million characters to avoid crashes on large git diffs.

4afa065433a1f7c99574755052324ab24fc7bd1c.text: Freebuff has quietly prepared a new AI model called HY3 for its web-based version, adding the behind-the-scenes identifiers and configuration so that the web interface can eventually offer it as an option. This is an internal bookkeeping change for Freebuff's maintainers and does not appear anywhere users currently interact with the product, so the CLI and desktop apps remain unchanged. Nothing visible to you happens today because no user-facing feature has been turned on to call for the new model.

671c093077dc5cd74ab2b1892c7c134d84c8fbd8.text: The assistant now keeps a small summary card alongside each saved conversation, recording how many messages are in it, the first thing you asked, and a fingerprint of the file's size and last-updated time. When you open the list of past conversations in the CLI, the app reads just that tiny card to show each chat's message count and opening line instead of cracking open and parsing every full conversation file (which can be megabytes of text). If the summary card ever gets out of sync with its conversation file, or a chat is so old it predates summary cards, the app falls back to reading the full file so nothing disappears or shows stale data. Because of this, older chats still load as before and the full conversation history continues to be saved unchanged.

c4a838fedc84d87b1640d62047cc4aa7bff923b4.text: The download mechanism the assistant uses to fetch your CLI updates now handles two common internet hiccups automatically: it follows more types of web redirects and stops if a redirect loop gets too long, and it retries failed downloads a few times with short delays between attempts. This affects anyone installing or updating the assistant's CLI tool. In daily use, you are less likely to see a failed update due to a momentary network glitch or a misbehaving download server.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: Version 1.0.685 updates the AI models in Freebuff and improves how the app handles downloads, session limits, and ads. New and replacement models arrive in the picker: DeepSeek V4 Flash becomes the recommended free model, GPT-5.6 Luna joins the free picker, and the cloud planner switches to DeepSeek V4 Pro. Downloads now retry on failure and roll back safely if they break, so installs and updates are less likely to leave a broken binary. When your daily free sessions run out, a landing screen explains the limit and shows a countdown until you can try again, instead of failing silently. Ads in streamed responses now appear after two messages and then every three messages, spacing them more evenly. Keyboard focus and terminal layout fixes keep the model picker and referral banner behaving correctly as access tiers load.

28ccadc6687c271cf00e473547c11ed8a096c363.title: GPT-6.1 Sol daily session cap added to session limits table
28ccadc6687c271cf00e473547c11ed8a096c363.summary: GPT-6.1 Sol gains a per-account daily session cap, exposed as the export GPT_61_SOL_MODEL_ID ('openai/gpt-6.1-sol') with a value of 1 in FREEBUFF_DAILY_SESSION_LIMITS in common/src/constants/freebuff-sol-promo.ts, so debitAdmission can reject a second session once the day's un-refunded debits hit the limit, which is why the README rows now state GPT-6.1 Sol gives one session a day for every account, paid plans included. The change lets the promotional label and the picker documentation agree on the daily limit, because the promotion is the leaf constant the price map, the model catalog and the admission debit all read.
28ccadc6687c271cf00e473547c11ed8a096c363.evidence: common/src/constants/freebuff-sol-promo.ts adds export const GPT_61_SOL_MODEL_ID = 'openai/gpt-6.1-sol' and appends GPT_61_SOL_MODEL_ID: 1 to FREEBUFF_DAILY_SESSION_LIMITS; README.md, README.zh-CN.md, and freebuff/cli/release/README.md extend the GPT-6.1 Sol model table row with the phrase 'one session a day for every account, paid plans included', and the promotional constant short label changes to 'Promotional · 1 session a day'.
28ccadc6687c271cf00e473547c11ed8a096c363.unknowns: The rollout timing of debitAdmission enforcement against the new FREEBUFF_DAILY_SESSION_LIMITS value is not shown in the touched files. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Adds GPT_61_SOL_MODEL_ID and a FREEBUFF_DAILY_SESSION_LIMITS entry pinning GPT-6.1 Sol to one paid session per Freebucks day for every account, paid plans included.
Updates the GPT-6.1 Sol model table rows and CLI FAQ to state the one-session-a-day-per-account limit and the new 'Promotional · 1 session a day' short label.

45a2358b9acdb158b300963919271fb6f21c5f34.title: Update Freebuff subscription house ad copy
45a2358b9acdb158b300963919271fb6f21c5f34.summary: The subscription promotion copy in `freebuff-house-ad.ts` was refreshed, with a new creative added to the `waiting_room` surface and the checked-in floor kept in lockstep with variation 0 of each surface. The change is a copy-only edit to the house campaign's creative set and fallback floor, with no new consumer or serving logic.
45a2358b9acdb158b300963919271fb6f21c5f34.evidence: The commit modifies `common/src/constants/freebuff-house-ad.ts`, updating the subscription promotion copy and adding a new entry to the `waiting_room` surface's creative variation while keeping the floor identical to variation 0 across all surfaces.
45a2358b9acdb158b300963919271fb6f21c5f34.unknowns: The rollout timing and whether the web deploy gotcha noted in the file header was triggered are not shown in the diff.

28ccadc6687c271cf00e473547c11ed8a096c363.text: The GPT-6.1 Sol model now has a published rule that limits every Freebuff account, including paid subscribers, to one session per day. The label shown in the model picker and the behind-the-scenes limit enforcement now both point to the same single definition so they can't disagree. You notice this as an explicit note in the model picker reading 'one session a day for every account,' and a tooltip explaining the promotional price will rise when the promotion ends. This applies right now, so users picking GPT-6.1 Sol today are already bound by the one-session-per-day cap.

45a2358b9acdb158b300963919271fb6f21c5f34.text: The marketing copy shown to people waiting to use a full model was rewritten, and the new text was synced so the always-on backup message matches the first variation of every screen. Freebuff engineering maintains this copy only and it is not shown to subscribers, nor does it change how many coding sessions anyone gets.

e488d49ce54605dc40c2ec1c84a80ef495083786.text: The assistant now recognizes when a streaming reply gets cut off mid-sentence because the connection to the server was dropped, and treats it as a temporary glitch that can be safely retried, rather than a hard failure. This only matters for the version of the assistant that developers run directly in their own code using the software development kit, not for the regular command-line or web version. In daily use, if you are building with the kit and a model reply is interrupted, the kit now has a better chance of recovering or retrying instead of ending the turn with an error, and no action is needed from anyone else.

3af5ff1fb34c0c30677e09070c89dcfb5c18d7c4.text: This version of the Freebuff CLI improves how the assistant manages long conversations, handles dropped network connections, and registers external tools, while also cleaning up unused tracking events. When the assistant runs low on output space while summarizing a long chat, it now respects each AI model's real output limit instead of asking for more tokens than the model can produce, and it will reject a summary that gets cut off rather than silently losing the rest of your session. If a connection to an AI model drops partway through a response, the CLI now treats it as a temporary network problem and keeps going instead of ending your turn with an error. External tools (like those added through the Model Context Protocol) now register correctly without losing their input formats, and binary or non-image resources from those tools show up as descriptive text instead of failing to decode. The set of analytics events the app can send no longer includes the retired bookmark gate prompts, since that flow has been removed entirely. Upgrading means your long coding sessions are less likely to fail from truncated summaries or dropped streams, and plug-in tools you add from other developers will work more reliably without breaking the current chat.

73c6ceb590d8d56df307de723563cd09d01e2ea0.title: CLI post-click return label for ad clicks and prompts
73c6ceb590d8d56df307de723563cd09d01e2ea0.summary: A new CLI module implements the post-click RETURN label (COD-694), measuring whether a user who clicked a Freebuff ad comes back to the assistant. Because a terminal cannot see focus, the CLI's return signal is the user's next submitted prompt: `away_ms` is recorded as click to next prompt latency, an upper bound on time away, and a second ad click also resolves a pending click as a return. The watcher starts from `recordAdClick` in `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts` and resolves from `routeUserPrompt` in `cli/src/commands/router.ts` via `noteUserTurnForAdClickReturn`, while the shared machine and wire contract live in the new `common/src/ads/click-return.ts` as a clock-injected state machine with a 30-minute watch and no leave grace.
73c6ceb590d8d56df307de723563cd09d01e2ea0.evidence: New file `cli/src/ads/click-return.ts` exports `createCliClickReturn`, `postCliClickReturn`, `trackAdClickAck`, `watchAdClickReturn`, and `noteUserTurnForAdClickReturn`; `cli/src/commands/router.ts` imports `noteUserTurnForAdClickReturn` and calls it at the top of `routeUserPrompt`; `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts` imports `trackAdClickAck` and `watchAdClickReturn`, and `recordAdClick` calls `watchAdClickReturn(ad.impUrl)` before firing the click POST and passes that fetch promise to `trackAdClickAck(ad.impUrl, ack)`.
73c6ceb590d8d56df307de723563cd09d01e2ea0.unknowns: The server-side consumer of the `/api/v1/ads/click-return` endpoint is not visible in this diff.

changes.what: Adds the CLI half of the post-click return label, including the shared singleton watcher, the ack gate that delays the return report until the click POST settles, and the fire-and-forget return reporter posting to the click-return endpoint.
Hooks the CLI return watcher into the prompt path by calling `noteUserTurnForAdClickReturn` at the top of `routeUserPrompt`, so the next user-submitted prompt resolves any pending click as a return.
Starts the return watcher on every ad click and tracks the click POST promise so the return report waits for it instead of racing to the server.

Adds the shared wire contract and clock-injected state machine for the RETURN label, including client/signal/outcome constants, the body parser, the watcher, an ack gate, and a DOM binding for Desktop and Web.

bb46c52bc16e41ff79cb08aa459448643ab95ddb.title: Ad request forwards USER PROMPT, STEP PROMPT, TOOL CALL ERROR tags
bb46c52bc16e41ff79cb08aa459448643ab95ddb.summary: convertToAdMessages in cli/src/ads/ad-request.ts now exports and tags user-role messages with the subset of AD_MESSAGE_TAGS ('USER_PROMPT', 'STEP_PROMPT', 'TOOL_CALL_ERROR') that the message carries, filtering them through AD_MESSAGE_TAG_SET, while assistant messages never receive tags. adMessagesForRequest appends the just-typed UI user message wrapped in `<user_message>` and tagged ['USER_PROMPT'] so the Freebuff auction server can distinguish what the developer typed from runtime-injected user turns. The ad routes' schemas strip unknown keys, so an older server ignores the new field, and only these three tag names are forwarded. The change is consumed by the ad auction request built in buildAdAuctionRequest.
bb46c52bc16e41ff79cb08aa459448643ab95ddb.evidence: In cli/src/ads/ad-request.ts, convertToAdMessages is now exported and maps an AdMessage with an optional tags field; for user-role messages it filters tags through a new AD_MESSAGE_TAG_SET built from AD_MESSAGE_TAGS ('USER_PROMPT','STEP_PROMPT','TOOL_CALL_ERROR'), and adMessagesForRequest pushes the latest UI-typed user message with tags: ['USER_PROMPT']. Tests in cli/src/ads/__tests__/ad-request-tags.test.ts assert STEP_PROMPT and TOOL_CALL_ERROR are forwarded, INSTRUCTIONS_PROMPT and assistant tags are stripped, and 'assistant messages never carry tags'.
bb46c52bc16e41ff79cb08aa459448643ab95ddb.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side consumer of the new tags or the rollout timing of the change across the ad-serving pipeline. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

73c6ceb590d8d56df307de723563cd09d01e2ea0.text: When you click on an ad inside Freebuff's command-line tool and then continue coding (for example, by typing your next question), that action now gets logged as a signal that you came back to the app after visiting the ad. The tool watches for your next prompt after a click and sends a short report to Freebuff's servers, without slowing down your typing or changing how anything else works. This only affects how ad responses are measured for improving which ads get shown to Freebuff users. Nothing in your daily use changes otherwise.

bb46c52bc16e41ff79cb08aa459448643ab95ddb.text: The change tags each forwarded user message with a short label (USER_PROMPT, STEP_PROMPT, or TOOL_CALL_ERROR) so the ad-request builder can distinguish what you typed from messages the assistant generated itself, while assistant messages never get tagged and the live in-flight message is only attached when the run history does not already contain it. This is an internal CLI-only change for the Freebuff engineering team: ad-serving internals, not your coding session. You will not notice anything different today, and there is no visible effect in the terminal.

ed7485229b4d8f6492ea393d1c7d64d5e5455b8e.text: The assistant now signals both the start and the end of a context-summarizing pass to anyone watching the run from the outside (like the Freebuff CLI, web app, or a program using the SDK). Previously, hosts only got told when a summary was done, so a 'Compacting...' indicator could disappear before the new shorter conversation was in place, leaving a brief blank moment. Now the start and end events bracket the pass, and the end event is guaranteed to fire even if summarization fails, so a host can show a continuous 'Compacting...' state with no gap before the assistant hands back control. This affects anyone embedding Freebuff via the SDK or watching it in the CLI/desktop app, and you'll notice a smoother, steadier status while long conversations get summarized.

4cdbbb8e228beaa638fe937d7fec9a9c3d15f1c1.text: This release swaps the free AI model line-up, adds a live streak bonus tracker to the landing screen and chat header, puts a short warning badge on the GLM 5.3 Flash model row to flag its expiring deal, and splits the referral onboarding question so Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook are counted as three separate sources. It also tightens download security by checking the release origin and cleaning hidden terminal codes out of remote text, and fixes streak bonus text shown to users in time zones east of the Pacific.

Freebuff CLI 0.1.5 updates the free AI model lineup, tightens security around release downloads and terminal output, and improves how streak bonuses, sponsored runs, and model availability notices are displayed. The free model picker now offers Muse Spark 1.3 (1.2 is dropped from the free tier and moved to paid-only), a new status line shows when your daily Freebucks bonus lands and when the next one starts, and sponsored task runs now record crash-proof progress so a killed or closed app still gets reported correctly. Security improvements include the release downloader only accepting HTTPS URLs from official hosts, refusing non-standard version names, and sanitizing all remote text before printing it to your terminal to block hidden control characters. Model availability notices now explain that VPN users get a smaller free compute pool and must connect directly to unlock more models and Freebucks. The onboarding referral question was also split into separate Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook options so answers are tracked accurately.

774b13485d0c5b5d1e44ca41217bf35ab37aae2a.text: When you use the Freebuff terminal app and you've kept a streak of daily usage going for a week or more (and you're on the free Freebucks meter), a new line now appears right under the streak-perk note telling you whether today's bonus Freebucks already landed in your pocket and when the next streak day begins, all shown in your own computer's clock. Before this, the bonus note only said the perk was coming in a confusing 'every Pacific day' wording, which tripped up users in other timezones (like Singapore or Europe) who expected it at their own midnight. This fixes that by reading the actual reset time the server sends and showing it locally, so you can see 'today's +X is in your wallet' or 'send a message before 3:00 PM for today's +X' instead of guessing.

155c66375523b6e95e5af4ec6ff6f3ef71057bf7.title: GPT-6.1 Sol promotional copy notes free in the US
155c66375523b6e95e5af4ec6ff6f3ef71057bf7.summary: The `GPT_61_SOL_PROMOTIONAL.tooltip` copy in `freebuff-sol-promo.ts` is rewritten to state that GPT-6.1 Sol is free in the US, paid elsewhere, and capped at one session a day for every account. The picker reads the `promotional.short` label that this constant backs, so the Desktop and Web surfaces now print the updated wording beside the GPT-6.1 Sol row. The change is text only; no admission or paywall logic is added here.
155c66375523b6e95e5af4ec6ff6f3ef71057bf7.evidence: In common/src/constants/freebuff-sol-promo.ts, the `GPT_61_SOL_PROMOTIONAL.tooltip` string is rewritten from 'Temporary promotional price, limited to one session a day for every account, paid plans included. The price will go up when the promotion ends.' to 'Temporary promotional price: free in the US, a paid plan everywhere else, and one session a day for every account, paid plans included. The price will go up when the promotion ends.'. In common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts, the promotional field on the GPT-6.1 Sol catalog row is assigned the promotional text that the picker reads.

155c66375523b6e95e5af4ec6ff6f3ef71057bf7.text: The model picker now shows a New badge next to Muse Spark 1.3, the returning paid model that runs on every paid plan, so you can see at a glance that it is back and updated. If you browse the picker you will notice the extra New label with a tooltip describing the model, and GPT-6.1 Sol's price explanation now states the temporary price, the one-session-a-day limit, and the free-in-the-US detail all together, so the on-screen text matches the catalog. You do not need to do anything, the change is live when the release ships to the Desktop, web, and CLI pickers.

227e3fdb0d096fd532844dddbfc0fae41cd4b9d6.text: When you are running a task and type a message in the Freebuff CLI, that message now gets flagged as a mid-turn steer so the model keeps working on the original task instead of dropping it to answer your new message, and the input box even shows 'Add to the current task' to make that clear. You see no extra steps: if the system was already busy, your typing joins what it was doing, and if it was idle the prompt behaves as before. This is live today for Freebuff CLI users on free compute credits or pay-as-you-go (BYOK) connections, and it does not affect sponsored/ad-funded runs, which still queue your message. No configuration is required.

4cdbbb8e228beaa638fe937d7fec9a9c3d15f1c1.text: Freebuff 0.1.5 adds the newer Muse Spark 1.3 AI model to the free model list while moving Muse Spark 1.2 to paid-only status, so free users now get the latest Muse Spark automatically and existing 1.2 picks switch over on load. The daily Freebucks streak bonus now shows a clear status line telling you whether today's credit has landed and when the next day's bonus starts, with wording that no longer misleads people in time zones east of the Pacific. The referral-onboarding question splits the old combined Instagram/TikTok/Facebook choice into three separate options, and Facebook answers are now counted correctly instead of being lost. When you send a message while the assistant is still busy, it is treated as part of the running task instead of starting over, and the assistant announces it will be added to the current task. The release launcher only accepts downloads over HTTPS from Freebuff or Codebuff domains, and a new sanitizer strips hidden control codes and invisible characters from text coming from ads and external tools before it is shown in the terminal. A sponsored task that crashes or gets interrupted is remembered on disk and reported as failed when the CLI next starts, instead of vanishing silently. Upgrading gives you the new Muse Spark model, a clearer Freebucks streak indicator, safer downloads, cleaner terminal output, and reliable crash reporting for sponsored tasks.

88e05db4b26f8e58eca99dbae7cf8ef26f22d0a5.text: Freebuff added the internal tracking pieces for a new kind of ad: a full-screen 'sponsor break' that can pause what you're doing. The code defines three events (the break appears, gets closed, or gets clicked), sets up how users are sorted into test groups to measure whether these breaks help or hurt, and wires the new events into the logging system so the team can read the results later. Nothing has changed in your app yet: the events and test groups are in place and tested, but no part of the product actually shows or records these breaks today, so you will notice nothing different when you open the assistant.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release gives you a new `/export` command to save your full chat to a file (as markdown or JSON), adds a one-time Freebucks introduction card and Freebucks balance/pricing directly in the model picker and session screens, and makes mid-turn `/plan`, `/review`, and `/skill` submissions queue safely instead of interrupting an in-progress run. The Freebucks meter now shows currency-style balances and per-model prices, landing rate-limit screens render day-scale wait times, and the model picker lists Solar Pro 4 and Muse Spark 1.3 as available free-tier options. Upgrading lets you export conversations for the record, see exactly how your Freebucks credits and model prices are shaping up without extra calls, and avoid having a busy agent run clobbered by a mid-turn command.

9ac3cfaccbda1e5eefac4a136587406f1bf5fe83.text: Freebuff is a coding tool that reads project settings files (like.gitignore) to decide which folders and files to skip. This change adds a safety check so the tool verifies a file path actually lives inside your project folder before scanning any parent directories for rules, preventing it from accidentally walking out of your project into unrelated areas of your computer. The change is internal to Freebuff's shared file-scanning library. You do not need to do anything different when using Freebuff, but the tool is now more careful about only looking where it should.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: Freebuff CLI 1.0.685 ships a refreshed model picker and new daily/weekly session perks, tighter download and upgrade reliability, and clearer billing-state handling. The Freebuff Web and CLI model picker now defaults to DeepSeek V4 Pro and adds GPT-5.6 Luna as a free selectable model, while MiniMax M3 drops to a paid premium pool that auto-switches to DeepSeek V4 Flash when the shared 5/day quota is full; the daily free-session allotment rises from 5 to 6, streak rewards become a recurring weekly +1 GLM session that scales with streak length, and a new spend-limited landing screen shows exactly when your daily Freebuff limit resets before letting a fresh session start. Upgrades are now downloaded to a partial file first and installed with a transactional rename, so a dropped network connection or a failed update rolls back cleanly to the previous version instead of leaving a half-written binary, and in-flight agent runs are aborted before switching chats to stop a stale conversation from writing its messages into the wrong transcript. The installer now follows modern HTTP redirects, retries flaky downloads with exponential backoff, and accepts the same proxy settings as your shell, while a new safe JSON serializer ensures long chat checkpoints never get corrupted by circular references or oversized content. Taken together, this release cuts down failed installs and lost conversations, gives you one extra free session per day and a predictable weekly GLM bonus, and makes the model picker steer you to the recommended DeepSeek V4 Pro by default while still honoring any model you deliberately pick.

4f5a72d6b85c9521b28248e359c11719cf6d55c4.text: The Freebuff engineering team standardized how log data is formatted and how log severity levels are ordered, so that every part of the system that writes logs now produces them in the exact same way. This is internal maintenance work done by the Freebuff developers only, and it does not change any feature you can see or use. You will not notice anything different in your Freebuff sessions today, and no action is needed on your part.

0c8fa864774e716b4e711aafc612fa9b49aaecbf.text: A small change was made to the behind-the-scenes data that Freebuff sends to its apps about your daily Freebucks allowance, adding an optional note field that can carry a short explanation of why your daily pool is a certain size. At the same time, the message shown when your connection looks like it is coming through a VPN or proxy was updated so that it now plainly states that Freebuff loses money on VPN users and that more models and Freebucks are available on a direct connection, rather than just saying more models are available. These changes are internal for now: the new note field is only in place and is not used by apps yet, and the VPN notice is live wherever the notice is shown to people whose connection looks like it uses a VPN or proxy.

4cdbbb8e228beaa638fe937d7fec9a9c3d15f1c1.text: This release updates the Freebuff assistant to use the newer Muse Spark 1.3 model instead of the older 1.2 version, adds a countdown badge for a limited-time deal on the GLM 5.3 Flash model, and shows a new status line telling you when your daily Freebucks bonus has been added and when the next one arrives. The referral question that asked how you heard about Freebuff is now split into separate Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook options so your answer is counted correctly, and a Facebook answer no longer gets lumped in with TikTok. If you send a message while the assistant is still working, it is now treated as a follow-up to the current task instead of replacing what it was doing. Downloads are now locked down to only come from official Freebuff or Codebuff websites over a secure connection, and any text pulled from the internet is cleaned up before showing in your terminal to block hidden or malicious formatting. Upgrading gives you the updated model lineup, clearer feedback on your daily bonus timing, more accurate referral tracking, safer downloads, and fewer surprises when you interrupt a running task.

fa7f6a239db7ed3d74758432e00ac1acdbc847f4.title: UTM tagging for sponsored procedure links on export
fa7f6a239db7ed3d74758432e00ac1acdbc847f4.summary: A new module `common/src/ads/ad-link-utm.ts` appends Freebuff's default UTM tags to advertiser links inside agentic procedures, adopting the advertiser's own `utm_source`/`utm_medium`/`utm_campaign` from its landing URL when present and falling back to `utm_source=freebuff`, `utm_medium=paid`, `utm_campaign=<slug>` otherwise, while leaving any link that already carries a `utm_*` parameter byte-identical and skipping code spans, commands, API hosts, and non-page files. `tagSponsoredProcedureLinks` runs at procedure save time rather than serve time because the stored text is what the reviewer approves and what Desktop hashes for consent, so a byte-identical rewrite keeps execution, review and hashing aligned. The module doc comment cites Infisical (2026-09-29) reporting every visit from a sponsored run arriving untagged, since an agent-relaid URL carries no UTM and no `bfcid` token for campaigns with internal conversion authority.
fa7f6a239db7ed3d74758432e00ac1acdbc847f4.evidence: New file `common/src/ads/ad-link-utm.ts` defines `tagSponsoredProcedureLinks`, `withDefaultAdLinkUtm`, `adLinkUtmTags`, `adLinkUtmCampaign`, `advertiserLinkDomains` and exports `AD_LINK_UTM_SOURCE`, `AD_LINK_UTM_MEDIUM`, `AdLinkUtmTags`; modified `common/src/ads/supabase-format-experiment.ts` adds `SUPABASE_PINNED_PROCEDURE_SHA256S`. The module doc comment for `ad-link-utm.ts` states Infisical (2026-09-29) reported every visit from a sponsored run arriving untagged, because campaign links relayed by the agent carry no UTM and no postback token for campaigns with internal conversion authority.
fa7f6a239db7ed3d74758432e00ac1acdbc847f4.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer that calls tagSponsoredProcedureLinks on the procedure save path or where advertiserLinkDomains feeds its input, and the Supabase pair comment references that consumer as the only proof that stored procedure text hashes stay byte-stable across the UTM write.

fa7f6a239db7ed3d74758432e00ac1acdbc847f4.text: Links inside Freebuff-sponsored coding procedures now carry tracking tags so advertisers can see which visits came from the assistant's suggested steps. The tagging only applies to links a developer would open on an advertiser's own website, and it leaves links already carrying campaign parameters untouched, skipping code, commands, file downloads, and other companies' domains. This is a change for advertisers running paid placement campaigns, and it is live for procedures saved from September 29, 2026 onward. You will not notice anything different in your daily use, and your own coding sessions and credits are unaffected.

Only the version literal changed; nothing else about the package or release configuration differs in this diff.

afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.text: Freebuff CLI jumps to 0.1.9 with GPT-6.1 Sol available to pick for free in the US (and paid elsewhere) at a temporary 100-Freebucks promotional price, plus a daily one-session limit for everyone. The web chat house ad surface was dropped from ad serving, the subscription house ad copy and waiting-room creative were refreshed, and new post-click return tracking now reports whether you come back to the assistant after clicking an ad. Ad request history tags your real prompts versus runtime-injected messages so the ad auction can tell them apart, UTM tags are now auto-appended to advertiser links inside sponsored procedures, and Muse Spark 1.3 gets a prominent "New" pill in the picker. Upgrading gives you the headline model addition and cleaner ad attribution without changing your core coding workflow.

This release adds OpenAI's flagship GPT-6.1 Sol model to the free model picker, available at a temporary promotional price in the US and plan-restricted elsewhere, with every account getting one session per day. It also improves ad attribution by tagging the developer's actual prompts in the ad auction request history so the service can tell real user input apart from system-injected messages. The CLI now watches how long it takes you to return after clicking an ad and reports that post-click return timing back to the service. House ad creatives for the waiting room and subscription promotions were refreshed with new copy, and the returning Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor model gets a 'New' pill in the picker. Upgrading lets you try GPT-6.1 Sol for free (one session daily), gives you a clearer promotional label for the model's temporary price, and helps the service measure ad click effectiveness through post-click return tracking.

41c03830a5fb0af4241a56663cfadfa6cfa24a56.title: BYOK reasoning effort per run with per-provider dialects and rejection
41c03830a5fb0af4241a56663cfadfa6cfa24a56.summary: A new /byok effort command lets a Freebuff user pick low, medium, or high reasoning effort for BYOK runs, persisted in settings.json as byokReasoningEffort and resolved at run start via withByokReasoningEffort so the choice rides along the resolved connection without being stored on it. The request body is translated per provider dialect in byokRequestTransform: openrouter emits reasoning.effort, anthropic emits thinking.budget_tokens added to max_tokens, and openai-compatible endpoints emit reasoning_effort. A provider that rejects the field with a 400 naming it is retried once without it via byokReasoningRetryBody, remembered per connection revision so later steps skip it, because a BYOK run must still complete when the picked rung is refused.
41c03830a5fb0af4241a56663cfadfa6cfa24a56.evidence: The diff adds BYOK_REASONING_EFFORTS, ByokReasoningEffort, isByokReasoningEffort, withByokReasoningEffort, ByokReasoningDialect, byokReasoningDialect, BYOK_ANTHROPIC_THINKING_BUDGETS, ANTHROPIC_ANSWER_TOKENS, clearByokReasoningRejections, byokReasoningRetryBody, and applyReasoningEffort across common/src/constants/reasoning-effort.ts and sdk/src/impl/byok-request.ts; cli/src/commands/byok.ts adds an 'effort' case to handleByokCommand that persists byokReasoningEffort via saveSettings and validates input against isByokReasoningEffort; cli/src/utils/byok.ts resolves the connection through withByokReasoningEffort(loadSettings().byokReasoningEffort) and sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts calls byokReasoningRetryBody on 400/422 responses.
41c03830a5fb0af4241a56663cfadfa6cfa24a56.migration: No migration required; existing /byok sessions continue to send no reasoning field unless a user explicitly chooses /byok effort.
41c03830a5fb0af4241a56663cfadfa6cfa24a56.unknowns: The diff does not show a rollout gate or remote flag controlling whether byokReasoningEffort is offered, and the consumer of BYOK_REASONING_EFFORTS on Desktop is not present in these files.

changes.what: Added an 'effort' action to /byok that validates the picked rung against isByokReasoningEffort, persists it via saveSettings, and reports the current value, with a default choice that clears it.

resolveByokConnection now wraps the resolved connection with withByokReasoningEffort using loadSettings().byokReasoningEffort so the per-task pick is attached without mutating the shared frozen connection.
Added a byokReasoningEffort field to the Settings schema with an isByokReasoningEffort allowlist guard in validateSettings.
Added BYOK_REASONING_EFFORTS limited to low, medium, high, plus the ByokReasoningEffort type and isByokReasoningEffort validator, because these are the rungs every BYOK provider shape understands.
Added reasoningEffort to ResolvedByokConnection as a run-scoped, non-stored field and exported withByokReasoningEffort plus copyRuntimeFields to attach it while keeping the credential non-enumerable.

Added ByokReasoningDialect, byokReasoningDialect, BYOK_ANTHROPIC_THINKING_BUDGETS, ANTHROPIC_ANSWER_TOKENS, clearByokReasoningRejections, byokReasoningRetryBody, applyReasoningEffort, and stripReasoningEffort so effort is written in each dialect and a rejecting provider is retried once without it.

41c03830a5fb0af4241a56663cfadfa6cfa24a56.text: Freebuff now lets you tell the assistant how deeply to think on each response when you run it through your own provider key, using a new slash command. You pick a level like low, medium, or high, and Freebuff sends it to your provider in the right format for OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, or others. If a provider refuses that setting, Freebuff quietly retries without it rather than failing the task, and remembers to stop sending it for that connection. The choice applies only to your own-key runs, not to Freebuff's default model, and nothing changes if you never use it.

f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.title: Freebuff CLI release 0.1.10 with subscription billing interval helpers
f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.summary: Freebuff CLI release 0.1.10 published with version 0.1.9 -> 0.1.10 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`. The change adds `freebuffSubscriptionBillingInterval` and `freebuffSubscriptionMrrUsd` to `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts`, plus the `SubscriptionBillingIntervals` type in `common/src/types/subscription-costs.ts` that splits paying subscribers by billing cadence. These helpers exist so yearly plans count a twelfth of their annual charge toward MRR, with non-`yearly` cadence defaulting to monthly, and so the admin subscriptions surface can group paid subscribers by cadence, prepaid status, and tier.
f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.evidence: The diff adds two exported functions, `freebuffSubscriptionBillingInterval` and `freebuffSubscriptionMrrUsd`, to `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts`; adds the `SubscriptionBillingIntervals` type to `common/src/types/subscription-costs.ts`; and bumps the version field in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` from `0.1.9` to `0.1.10`. The `FreebuffSubscriptionBillingInterval` type already existed in the subscription constants file and is now imported into the costs types file to back the new `SubscriptionBillingIntervals` record.

changes.what: Added freebuffSubscriptionBillingInterval and freebuffSubscriptionMrrUsd exported helpers to compute billing cadence and per-subscription MRR.
Added SubscriptionBillingIntervals type and imported FreebuffSubscriptionBillingInterval to support cadence-split subscriber counts for admin reporting.
Bumped package version from 0.1.9 to 0.1.10 for the Freebuff CLI release.

f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.text: The Freebuff CLI has been released at version 0.1.10, which includes helpers for subscription billing intervals and monthly recurring revenue calculations. This change is internal, affecting how the service tracks paid subscribers by billing cadence (monthly or yearly), so yearly plans correctly count a twelfth of their annual price toward MRR. You do not need to take any action, and there is no visible effect on your daily use of the assistant. The release also packages other changes made elsewhere, but this commit only updates the version label itself.

e3d7701e9223662ede68d501c3bdc686168d36cb.title: Guard against file edits cut off mid-generation
e3d7701e9223662ede68d501c3bdc686168d36cb.summary: A new `truncated-write-guard.ts` module in `packages/agent-runtime/src/util` refuses two shapes of a file edit cut off mid-generation. The runtime's `parseRawToolCall` returns a truncated error when tool arguments stop mid-JSON (a bracket/string prefix that never closes), telling the model nothing was written instead of inviting a re-issue; `processFileBlock` refuses a `write_file` that would replace an existing file of 30+ lines with a copy under 60% of its size that leaves brackets open where the current file balances them. Both refusals log the new `FILE_WRITE_GUARD_EVENT` to Axiom via the allowlist added in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`, and the change adds tests and a docs section describing the guard.
e3d7701e9223662ede68d501c3bdc686168d36cb.evidence: New module `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/truncated-write-guard.ts` exports `isTruncatedJsonPrefix`, `detectTruncatedRewrite`, `truncatedToolCallMessage`, and supporting constants; `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts` calls `isTruncatedJsonPrefix` inside `parseRawToolCall` and adds a truncated branch in `executeToolCall` that emits a non-echoing error and logs `FILE_WRITE_GUARD_EVENT` with `metric: 'truncated_tool_call_refused'`; `packages/agent-runtime/src/process-file-block.ts` calls `detectTruncatedRewrite` and logs `FILE_WRITE_GUARD_EVENT` with `metric: 'truncated_rewrite_refused'`; `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` defines `FILE_WRITE_GUARD_EVENT` and `FILE_WRITE_GUARD_FIELDS` plus a `FILE_WRITE_GUARD_EVENT` case in `getAxiomOnlyLogEvent`; tests in `packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/tool-validation-error.test.ts` and `packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/truncated-write-guard.test.ts` assert the refusal paths; docs note added in `docs/agents-and-tools.md`.
e3d7701e9223662ede68d501c3bdc686168d36cb.unknowns: The production log site that emits the new event was added in this same change, but the operator dashboard or alert reading `file_write_guard` rows is not shown.

changes.what: New module that refuses tool calls cut off mid-JSON and rewrites that look like a cut-off copy of an existing file.
Parses raw tool calls for truncated JSON prefixes and emits a non-echoing error plus an Axiom log for cut-off arguments.
Calls the rewrite detector before applying a `write_file` and refuses cut-off copies with an Axiom log.
Adds the `FILE_WRITE_GUARD_EVENT` constant, its `FILE_WRITE_GUARD_FIELDS` allowlist, and a case in `getAxiomOnlyLogEvent`.
Documents the two cut-off edit refusals and that they log `file_write_guard`.
Asserts refused cut-off writes, truncated JSON detection, and legitimate rewrites passing the guard.

e3d7701e9223662ede68d501c3bdc686168d36cb.text: Freebuff now watches for two ways an AI-written file edit can get accidentally cut off, and when it spots either, it refuses to save that partial edit instead of leaving a broken file on disk. This helps anyone who uses the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK to edit files, because an over-limit or interrupted response can no longer silently truncate a file; the assistant is told nothing was written and what to do next. You do not need to change anything: the next time the assistant's file write gets cut off, Freebuff keeps the original file intact and asks for a smaller edit instead.

e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.title: Freebuff CLI release bumped to 0.1.11
e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.summary: The version field for the freebuff package in freebuff/cli/release/package.json was incremented from 0.1.10 to 0.1.11, aligning the published release with the version shipped in the release packaging manifest because release-bump commits exist solely to tag and publish a new CLI build.
e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.evidence: The diff in freebuff/cli/release/package.json changes the "version" field from "0.1.10" to "0.1.11" in the "name": "freebuff" package declaration, with no other logic altered.

e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.text: Freebuff 0.1.11 adds a safety net that prevents your files from being left half-written or corrupted when the assistant tries to save a file but the write gets interrupted. When an edit cuts off before it is complete, the program now stops and reports the mistake instead of saving a broken file that could make your project unusable. It also watches out for situations where a large file is suddenly replaced with a much shorter version that leaves code brackets unbalanced, refusing the change to keep your files valid. These protection checks log their activity into the service logs so problems can be tracked later. Upgrading means you are less likely to end up with damaged or incomplete files during coding sessions.

5d525143041ab63d8faf7aec68b3ef6eb11be287.title: Capped reasoning effort at high for Muse Spark, GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini
5d525143041ab63d8faf7aec68b3ef6eb11be287.summary: The Muse Spark default reasoning effort FREEBUFF_MUSE_SPARK_REASONING_EFFORT drops from 'xhigh' to 'high', and the GPT-6.1 Sol, Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor, and Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor rows switch their efforts arrays to EFFORTS_THROUGH_HIGH, because product capped them at high on 2026-09-29 after measuring that the xhigh rung bought ~8% more reasoning for ~26% more latency. The Gemini 3.8 Flash row fixes reasoningEffort to 'high' and uses the new EFFORTS_HIGH_ONLY ladder so the server clamps any other effort to high on every turn, per the same 2026-09-29 product decision. The GPT-6 Luna row drops 'max' from its ladder via EFFORTS_LOW_THROUGH_XHIGH while keeping its xhigh ceiling, also per the 2026-09-29 decision. The new EFFORTS_LOW_THROUGH_XHIGH and EFFORTS_HIGH_ONLY exports exist in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts.
5d525143041ab63d8faf7aec68b3ef6eb11be287.evidence: In common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts, FREEBUFF_MUSE_SPARK_REASONING_EFFORT changes from 'xhigh' as const to 'high' as const, with a new comment dated 2026-09-29 stating that the cap is by product decision because the top rung bought ~8% more reasoning for ~26% more latency. The GPT-6.1 Sol row switches efforts from EFFORTS_THROUGH_MAX to EFFORTS_THROUGH_HIGH with the comment 'Capped at high by product decision (2026-09-29): the dearest row, and reasoning bills as output at $5/M'. The Muse Spark 1.2 and 1.3 Contributor rows switch efforts from EFFORTS_THROUGH_XHIGH to EFFORTS_THROUGH_HIGH with the comment 'Up to high only (2026-09-29, by product decision)'. The Gemini 3.8 Flash row adds reasoningEffort: 'high' and switches efforts from EFFORTS_THROUGH_MAX to EFFORTS_HIGH_ONLY with the comment 'FIXED at high since 2026-09-29, by product decision: one rung, so the server clamps any other effort to it, and pinned so every turn sends it'. The GPT-6 Luna row switches efforts from EFFORTS_THROUGH_MAX to EFFORTS_LOW_THROUGH_XHIGH with the comment 'No max (2026-09-29, by product decision)'. Two exports named EFFORTS_LOW_THROUGH_XHIGH and EFFORTS_HIGH_ONLY are newly added.
5d525143041ab63d8faf7aec68b3ef6eb11be287.unknowns: The diff shows no reader of the new EFFORTS_LOW_THROUGH_XHIGH and EFFORTS_HIGH_ONLY exports within this commit, so their consumers are not visible here. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

5d525143041ab63d8faf7aec68b3ef6eb11be287.text: The assistant is turning down the 'deep thinking' level for a few of its most powerful free models. Three popular paid models (GPT-6.1 Sol, Muse Spark 1.2, and Muse Spark 1.3) are now capped at a medium-high thinking depth instead of letting them go all the way to maximum, and the Gemini 3.8 Flash model is locked to that same medium-high level on every turn. You are a Freebuff subscriber or someone using the assistant at full access on these specific paid models. You may notice these models feel slightly faster or respond with a touch less elaborate reasoning on very complex tasks, though the change is small enough that most daily coding work should feel the same.

51b40e3b7df6b180ed089d2204f6bb3a91f93c4f.title: Onboarding question order shuffled for role, intended use
51b40e3b7df6b180ed089d2204f6bb3a91f93c4f.summary: The role, intended use, and subscriptions onboarding questions now shuffle their option order on each form mount, matching the behavior already set on referral source, so every chip-list question distributes the first-position advantage evenly across options.
51b40e3b7df6b180ed089d2204f6bb3a91f93c4f.evidence: The diff to `common/src/constants/freebuff-onboarding.ts` adds `shuffleOptions: true` to the `role`, `intended_use`, and subscriptions questions in `FREEBUFF_ONBOARDING_QUESTIONS`, joining the existing `shuffleOptions: true` on `referral_source`.

51b40e3b7df6b180ed089d2204f6bb3a91f93c4f.text: The order of answer choices in three of the post-signup questions now changes each time you open the form. Questions about your role, what you plan to build, and your current subscriptions are now shuffled just like the "how did you hear about us" question already was. This affects anyone signing up for Freebuff who reaches the onboarding questionnaire. You will no longer see the same options appear in the same order every time, which is intended to stop the first-listed choice from getting picked more often by accident.

592b3211840b26f528305bfbea7954cdbc5ead5b.title: CLI Freebucks keeps the live session's purchase and prices model
592b3211840b26f528305bfbea7954cdbc5ead5b.summary: The Freebucks meter in cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts now returns the live session's Freebucks info directly when the session is active and the instance id is a CLI-owned attempt, so the running session keeps its hour reservation and first-tab discount instead of re-resolving off the single-session store. Legacy or ended single-session purchases still release their discount reservation via firstTabQuoteForSession with the 'single' surface, so a model switch quotes full price while the old purchase holds the discount. The server quote is reused for any replacement rather than promising a discount transfer to another model.
592b3211840b26f528305bfbea7954cdbc5ead5b.evidence: In cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts (diff @@ -53,6 +53,8 @@), freebucksOf returns getFreebucksInfo(state) unchanged when state.status is 'active' and freebuffCliAttemptId(state.instanceId) matches, and only then calls firstTabQuoteForSession with the literal 'single' for legacy/ended sessions; new tests assert 'GLM to Luna asks for 20 Freebucks while GLM retains the first-tab discount' and 'a CLI model switch quotes full price while its old purchase holds the discount' in __tests__/freebuff-premium-reset.test.ts and freebucks.test.ts.
592b3211840b26f528305bfbea7954cdbc5ead5b.unknowns: A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.
