verifyClaims.reason: Diff and file list only include changes to cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts; no test files (freebucks.test.ts or freebuff-premium-reset.test.ts) are listed

592b3211840b26f528305bfbea7954cdbc5ead5b.text: When a developer starts a new paid session in the CLI, the assistant now keeps the correct discount and hourly rate that came with that specific purchase instead of mixing it up with the older single-session discount logic. This affects developers using the free tier CLI who start fresh paid sessions. You will not notice anything different unless you are actively switching models or ending a paid session, in which case the price quote will match the purchase you are actually working on.

9a87cf853a482411f6667fa4ad554c38b077e4fc.text: The assistant can now tell the difference between its private chain of thought and the actual reply it wants to show you, so your screen no longer gets a half-empty answer box when the model runs out of room or stops mid-reasoning. When a thinking model starts writing its reasoning directly into the visible reply (which the backend lane sometimes does), the system now captures that text in the correct place instead of letting it spill into your answer, and if the model stops on its own, it treats the unfinished thinking block as part of the reply rather than discarding it. This works today for anyone using the Freebuff assistant, and you will notice replies appearing intact instead of showing up blank or cut off.

0c68d24a080271f71eae364674afabe918e2ba7b.text: The assistant now summarizes long conversations by asking the AI model itself to write a brief handoff summary, instead of mechanically deleting or truncating the conversation history. This affects developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK. You won't see a new button or setting; when a conversation gets very long, the assistant will spend a brief moment generating a summary so it can keep working without running out of memory, and the cost of that summary is billed like a normal question rather than happening for free.

de23935e2ae48f535f8ac22e8694c196de4d65d8.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.187 changes how the assistant handles long conversations, adds two new free AI models, and tightens some security and configuration rules behind the scenes. The assistant now asks the AI to write a summary of your chat when it gets too long, instead of mechanically trimming the history, and you can now pick Solar Mini 4 (which replaces Solar Pro 4) and Space Bunny Alpha from the free model list. It also guards against extremely large messages and tool results that could overwhelm the AI's context, so runs won't be cut off by oversized inputs. The agent runtime now recovers gracefully if summary generation fails, falling back to trimming instead of stopping your work, and previously banned users can be re-recognized by their tool usage. Upgrading keeps long sessions running, gives you two new models at no charge, and prevents oversized inputs from breaking the assistant.

8ac94a54affac0eea3470c33444b18393683fa02.text: The assistant now gives new accounts a single 500-credit signup bonus instead of 500 credits every month. Existing accounts that were already getting free monthly credits keep them, but brand-new accounts only get the one-time bonus. Who it affects: New Codebuff accounts created from today onward. Everyday impact: New users get 500 credits when they first sign up, which they can use right away without buying anything. Those credits do not expire, so they can be saved for later. New users no longer get a fresh monthly 500-credit refill. The usage display now shows signup bonus credits separate from any monthly credits that legacy users still receive.

40cdfe2fc4c97d351a6efa619960adacd714247e.text: The signup form now asks 'Where did you hear about Freebuff?' with separate Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook buttons instead of one combined button for all three. If you signed up before this change, your previous answer is still remembered but gets counted correctly behind the scenes. This helps the team understand which specific platform brings in new users, so they can see clearly where free signups are coming from.

7c98630f058946cec393077942e0d9217d856554.text: The Freebuff team added a way for developers to publish their custom AI agents to a shared store, so you can now save, share, and reuse your personalized agents across projects. This is for developers who build and customize agents using Freebuff's tools. If you don't create or use custom agents, you won't notice any difference in your usual workflow.

4cdbbb8e228beaa638fe937d7fec9a9c3d15f1c1.text: Freebuff 0.1.5 swaps Muse Spark 1.3 into the free model picker (replacing Muse Spark 1.2, which becomes pay-only) and adds a streak status line that shows your daily Freebucks bonus and the exact time your next credit arrives. The release also hardens the download flow by refusing non-HTTPS or non-first-party release URLs, blocks steering variables from hijacking the install, and sanitizes remote text rendered to the terminal so partner ads, error messages, and sponsored content can no longer inject terminal escapes or invisible Unicode. Onboarding now splits the combined Instagram/TikTok/Facebook referral chip into separate options so each platform's cost per activation can be tracked independently, with the legacy combined id preserved for existing tallies. A new GLM 5.3 Flash deal badge warns you when limited-time pricing ends, spawning agents return plain text answers instead of message arrays, and steering messages sent mid-run are framed as part of the current task so models keep going instead of dropping what they were doing.

663ba6dc6110c21286c3f0c2de6893729e5323d9.text: Freebuff's codebase now has the internal structure (new database tables and programming interfaces) needed to let businesses pay for and share credits that power the AI coding assistant across a team. The engineering team at Freebuff built the system that will later let organizations manage shared billing, but those screens, payments, and shared credits do not exist yet for anyone to use. Nothing you do today in your personal coding session changes because of this work.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release delivers a new sponsorship workflow, a fresh Freebucks pricing model that charges per model, and a reorganized ad-insertion system that shows house-sponsored tasks and spotlight breaks in the terminal. Specifically, you can now accept advertiser-funded proposal tasks that run sandboxed on your machine with a single consent screen, the model picker charges a per-session Freebucks price with a one-time intro card and monthly allowance, and new ad controls let you dismiss or report proposals plus skip sponsor breaks. Sponsored runs are contained to a linked worktree under your project's.freebuff directory with a macOS seatbelt or Linux bubblewrap sandbox, so advertiser code cannot touch your real repos without explicit consent. Upgrading means metered models now show their actual spend price, rate-limit waits display as days instead of hours, and mid-turn messages queue instead of overwriting an in-progress run.

3975224904d989f60ad8db9139bf51b7390e67c0.text: Freebuff now shows you small sponsored proposal cards inside your CLI chat. Each card is a real advertiser-funded task suggestion for your current repository, and you reach all of its controls through slash commands (`/ads:proposal` to open the menu, `/ads:dismiss-proposal` to decline, and others for reporting or never seeing an advertiser again), since the card itself binds no keys to avoid clashing with the live composer. This is live for Freebuff CLI users, and for now the card only lets you view, dismiss, or report the offer (Phase 1 ships no Accept). Nothing about your daily coding flow changes unless an offer appears: no new steps for you, and a declined or spent card stays in the transcript rather than disappearing so the history stays honest.

d9ee7bfc3e52b9156522bc86250fc7376f9fe955.text: Starting today, when you open Freebuff in your terminal or desktop app, the model it suggests first is now DeepSeek V4 Pro (a stronger, more capable model) instead of the previous default. If you've already used up your daily allowance of premium model sessions, Freebuff automatically switches the suggested model to DeepSeek V4 Flash, which is always available. Your saved model preference is remembered across sessions and only reset at launch if it's no longer available to start, so no action is needed unless you want to try Pro.

a29a854c99017a698e7c8c673e870465919ec957.text: The assistant can now build and edit its own helper programs that live in a special.agents folder, letting you create, tweak, and swap out custom AI assistants through a new interactive /agents menu right inside the terminal. This matters to anyone using Freebuff to code, because you can now design your own specialized agents for tasks like reviewing code, writing commits, or brainstorming ideas, and switch between them on the fly. In daily use, typing /agents opens a full-screen list where you can create a new agent with a guided setup, edit existing ones in place, or jump into any agent you’ve already made, all without leaving the chat.

f7828c2c4b5a55de46b00f0484ed047e091d0964.text: A new background worker called @codebuff/freebuff-runner was added under freebuff/runner/ so that Freebuff, Codex, and Claude Code agent turns execute off Convex action compute. It subscribes over websocket to runner-dispatched queued rows in freebuff_agent_runs, claims them with a CAS mutation, and streams batched events through recordRunEventBatch. Dispatch is gated by the freebuff_runner_enabled feature flag, which now defaults ON for those send types, with the legacy Convex action and workflow paths remaining as fallback. The event batcher ships every buffered delta in one mutation per ~2s and sends a 30000ms heartbeat to keep the run alive during long tool calls with no streamed output.

d22c969cee10470f88c1dce87c6091f4426d0b99.text: Freebuff 0.1.1 adds a Discord invite banner that shows after you sign in, so you can easily join the community from the CLI or web login, and it now shows a correct member count that is updated manually in the thousands. Research projects run by the built-in AI assistant now stop after 15 steps instead of running forever, which prevents one message from accidentally spawning thousands of tool calls, and the assistant writes a final answer when the step budget runs out. The list of AI models you can use for free has been published as the model table in the README, showing every model available at no charge in this version. When you bring your own API key to run a model, the app now asks the model provider for the real context window size instead of guessing, so it compacts your conversation far less often during long sessions. On the desktop side, the app now sends a small header that identifies a session as coming from Freebuff Desktop, giving the service a way to tell desktop sessions apart from CLI sessions. Keyboard shortcuts Up and Down now move through slash-command and mention menus instead of just scrolling your draft message, so navigating /ask and @-mentions feels normal when a menu is open. Error details are now preserved in logs, time-zone selection is validated to avoid crashes on unusual browsers, and CPU detection recovers gracefully when a system call fails. Upgrading gives you the Discord welcome banner and the new free-model picker table right away, stops runaway research loops, reduces needless conversation compaction when using your own API key, and fixes arrow-key menu navigation and login-time banner display.

71741fc79de88ca49a02602fe2b124a35d6a7361.text: After you sign up for the free tier of the coding assistant, a friendly banner now appears at the top of your chat window inviting you to join the Freebuff Discord community, with a clickable link and a message like 'Talk directly with our team and 7,000+ community members on Discord.' This banner shows up right after you complete the sign-in process in the terminal app, and the same invitation line is also printed when you log in using the plain-text command outside the terminal interface. It only appears for new sign-ins, not when you reopen the app later using your saved session, and the member count is updated manually over time as the community grows.

0d4d983708de983b28cd65e1727c595c48b46219.text: When you are using Freebuff for free and your session runs out while the assistant is still working, the CLI now stops the run and shows a clear message instead of leaving the cursor blinking, and a new attempt is admitted right after without needing to restart. A stuck-lock watchdog in the message queue now re-arms itself while an agent turn or a pending user question is still active instead of wrongly resetting the queue mid-run, and it can be configured to a custom duration. Additionally, the AI SDK's per-call v2 compatibility notice is dropped so it no longer floods the logs on every model call, while other warnings are logged only once per process.

d22c969cee10470f88c1dce87c6091f4426d0b99.text: Freebuff 0.1.1 shows a Discord community banner after you sign in, fixes model and research problems, and improves logging. After a fresh Freebuff login, you now see a banner inviting you to join the Discord community. The web researcher helper is now capped at 15 steps per message, preventing runaway research loops. Time zone handling is fixed so the app no longer crashes on unsupported zones from certain PlayStation or Windows browsers. Error logging now captures full details instead of empty data. Model ID mapping is fixed so OpenRouter models no longer fail at Anthropic's endpoint. CPU detection is more resilient when system info is unavailable.

c71604de74656272d8721f0f33e0cfe031eb23cb.text: The assistant stopped crashing when counting how many words are in a message for newer Claude models like Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5. The engineering team fixed a hidden lookup table inside the app that translates between two different naming systems, so requests that had been failing since late September now go through correctly. If you are a Freebuff maintainer running tests against model providers, your token-counting calls for these models now return results instead of errors. For everyone else, nothing changes in your day-to-day work.

9d0e435b3802e4b6b833c1ed349d604e5b804f0d.text: Freebuff added 'Ox Alpha' as a new AI model that you can only use on the Freebuff website and in the Cloud version, not in the Freebuff desktop app or command-line tool. If you use Freebuff in your web browser, you might see this new model in your list of choices, and it is free to use. People who run the Freebuff service for their own team, or anyone writing custom code that talks directly to Freebuff, cannot use this model on its own unless they are authenticated as the Freebuff Web service itself. Using a new AI model in your browser is safe and free today. Nothing changes for the Freebuff desktop app, the command-line tool, or any other way of using Freebuff. The change is live now.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release makes GLM 5.3 Flash the default AI model across the CLI, web, and desktop, and adds a /reasoning command so you can control how hard the model thinks before answering. DeepSeek V4 Pro now pauses during peak hours and falls back to a cheaper option, the model picker shows countdown timers for unavailable models, and Freebuff subscriptions now add to (rather than replace) your free daily sessions with new pay-as-you-go tiers. The first-party ad rail is now live with real inventory, ad creatives are sanitized for terminal safety, and the CLI no longer gets stuck when copying conversations or pasting from a broken clipboard backend. On the reliability side, the assistant now drops unanswered tool calls at session boundaries to prevent errors from replayed history, and the SDK translates Git Bash paths on Windows so agents that emit POSIX-style paths resolve correctly. Upgrading gives you a clearer, safer chat experience with transparent model availability, subscription sessions that stack on your free allowance, and no more frozen copy operations when the clipboard backend is unavailable. GLM 5.3 Flash is now the default free model across CLI, Web, and Desktop, with Solar Pro 4 added as a limited-time option and DeepSeek V4 Pro, MiniMax M3, Ox Alpha, and GPT-5.6 Luna removed from the free picker; new features include the /reasoning command, peak-hour pause notices with return timers, subscription tiers that top up free sessions, and a live first-party ad rail with sanitized terminal creatives.

f4b54393e76ba626a55362568da73407d21ec306.text: Freebuff has added a new, separate A/B test for its Supabase setup invitations, which charges advertisers a per-click fee when someone starts the setup flow. Each eligible user is quietly sorted into one of two test groups (a simple card, or a card that can run a small automated task), using a stable, fixed 50/50 split, so the company can compare how each format performs. This test is live now behind the scenes, but it does not change anything you see today unless you are part of the invited technical audience on Mac or Linux.

fd93692e814f3a7a4a3e61773e10e58384120e64.text: Freebuff 0.0.181 adds new AI models to the free model list, lets you start bring-your-own-key (BYOK) sessions without a live Freebuff session, and makes the assistant read your environment safely so cloned projects can't hijack where it connects. You can now pick the latest MiMo 2.6 Flash and MiMo 2.6 Pro models, and if you run out of Freebucks you can jump straight into a /byok setup from the landing screen instead of being stuck. The smoke test now proves that steering files in a directory cannot change the backend URL the CLI connects to, and the landing screen names the specific host it could not reach when a network failure happens. The refund display was removed from the landing screen and the /end-session command no longer mentions getting a partial refund back. The off-peak price tooltip now shows a single clear sentence instead of stacking multiple discount lines in the model selector. If you edit an earlier message, the SDK now rewinds the run state to that point so the conversation history stays aligned with what you are editing.

f7461e3885e81bf95a5058142b2754174f13eb43.text: The referral system that gave users bonus credits for inviting friends has been removed across the CLI, website, and mobile app. Users who previously earned credit bonuses through referrals will no longer receive them, and any codes or links used to claim those credits no longer work. Instead, the system now tracks which creators brought in new users, so you can see who referred you during sign-up, but without any credit rewards attached. This change is live today and affects anyone who was using the old refer-a-friend feature.

a7ea9ca1fdbf59aea2aedd91b557f4416f19695b.text: This change adds the wiring to run a small A/B test around a new ad showcase, deciding which visitors are shown the showcase versus a control group and recording when the showcase is actually presented, but it does not by itself turn the feature on for anyone. The test bucket is computed from a salted hash of the visitor so the split is stable and private, and presentation reports are re-checked on the server and quietly dropped when they are anonymous, malformed, or missing required identifiers. It is aimed at whoever operates the Freebuff ad service, not at people writing code or running their assistant, and it has no visible effect on your sessions today since nothing yet calls the assignment step that would tag you a treatment or control visitor.

7c5cc043fcad67cd82f362c61bc4c82cae553a78.text: The discount new subscribers get on their first month now scales with the size of the plan they pick: Starter saves $3 (first month $5), Plus saves $6 (first month $19), and Pro saves $15 (first month $45), instead of a flat $3 off every plan. When you sign up, your first payment now depends on which tier you start with. The first month is cheaper by an amount that matches the plan you picked.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release brings Freebuff a new free AI model to pick from and several improvements to how you run, manage, and pay for help. You can now use Meta Muse Spark 1.3 across the CLI, desktop, web, and cloud free tiers, and a new Freebucks meter in the CLI shows the per-model price and your available balance instead of hiding limits behind a session counter. The conversation controls were fixed so typing /plan, /interview, /review, or /skill mid-turn now waits for the current step to finish instead of overwriting it. You also get a new /export command to save a chat to a markdown or JSON file, day-scale wait times on monthly reset walls, and the referral banner now links to the account page. Sponsored proposal cards gained accept, pull-request, and worktree slash commands with an in-terminal consent screen, and account deletion proofs now use a signed HMAC with constant-time verification for safer data purges. Upgrading means your chats save correctly, your free-tier usage is shown as currency you can reason about, and new models and safer local execution paths become available.

e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.title: Freebuff 0.2.0 released with Tier-2 per-conversion telemetry
e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.summary: The Freebuff CLI release 0.2.0 was published by bumping the version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.1.11 to 0.2.0. A new first_party_tier2_per_conversion_outcome string field was added to the ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS allowlist in common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts so the Tier-2 per-conversion leg can report fill, no_fill, or error outcomes to Axiom. That leg only runs for campaigns that bill per conversion, and the field is emitted only when the leg actually executes.
e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.evidence: The diff adds the field first_party_tier2_per_conversion_outcome to the ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS schema in common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts (immediately after first_party_cpm_campaign_id), with a comment tying it to COD-713 and stating it is present only when the Tier-2 per-conversion leg ran; it also bumps the version from 0.1.11 to 0.2.0 in freebuff/cli/release/package.json.
e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.unknowns: The rollout status of the Tier-2 per-conversion leg and whether its consumers are already wired.

changes.what: Version bumped to 0.2.0 for the Freebuff CLI release package.
Added first_party_tier2_per_conversion_outcome to the Ads Fetch Completed telemetry allowlist.

e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.text: Freebuff 0.2.0 adjusts how much deep thinking certain AI models do before answering you, along with small changes to how new-user setup screens look and behave. Some newer models (Muse Spark, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Gemini) now take slightly less time to think through answers because the team found that the deepest thinking option only improved results by about 8% while making responses much slower. The signup surveys asking about your role and what you plan to use Freebuff for now shuffle their answer choices each time you see them, so no single option always appears first. If you use the newest GPT-6 Luna model, it keeps its previous ceiling on how deeply it can think. These tweaks mainly affect response timing for some models and fairness in how new-user questions are presented.

dc18d1a2063a92cc1939648a0280c0847a662c73.text: A new /diagnostics command lets you type a slash command in the chat to see a read-out of what the assistant is doing behind the scenes on your machine - how much memory and CPU it is using, how long it has been running, and which background terminal tasks are currently active. Freebuff and Codebuff developers using the terminal app can now type /diagnostics (or the shorter /diag or /processes) to get this report appended directly into the chat, which is handy for troubleshooting when something feels slow or frozen. The report intentionally leaves out command text and environment variables so you can safely paste it into a bug report or support thread without leaking secrets.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This release brings a new /diagnostics command to inspect your CLI and terminal processes, automatic retries for failed downloads, and safer handling when switching chats. The free model lineup changes: GPT-5.6 Luna joins as a selectable model while Kimi K2.7 Code is retired from the free picker, and daily free sessions rise from 5 to 6. Updates also stop stalled streamings, improve how ads appear in responses, and harden the model picker layout. Upgrading gives you more transparent diagnostics, steadier installs, and clearer messaging when free limits or IP caps are reached.

3623ca3ffeb9e8ed71a65207075c1d4d18e639f3.text: The text shown to people who see the Freebuff Pro subscription ad in the CLI and web app now automatically pulls the current price and session limits from the same pricing system, so it always matches what checkout actually charges instead of a number someone typed by hand. The Freebuff marketing team now has four different ad angles to test per placement (price, queue, model list, ads) instead of just one, and the cap on how many creative variants a single campaign can hold was raised from 10 to 25 to make room for those variants. This rolls out to anyone who sees those promotional slots while using the free tier, and they will notice the ad copy is now kept in sync with pricing automatically rather than drifting after plan changes.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release puts GLM 5.3 Flash at the top of the Freebuff free model picker and restores DeepSeek V4 Flash to 24-hour availability, replacing the previous peak-hour closures and per-model daily caps. The /reasoning slash command is now available so you can set a model's thinking effort per session, and the model picker now shows local-time return windows and a new off-peak-only label for closed rows instead of just greying them out. Ad delivery planes are now live on the Freebuff service with first-party inventory, campaign review gates, and a daily budget taper that paces delivery by the hour so campaigns no longer empty out at Pacific-day boundaries. The CLI now warns you by name when a model is withdrawn, switches you to a working fallback without forgetting your saved preference, and renders a plan-blocking limit with its reset instant directly below the catalog so you can see what is holding you back. Upgrading to this version gives you a stable default model that stays open all hours, clearer messages when a model is refused or paused, and a paid-subscription paywall that points you at the upgrade instead of leaving each client to write its own.

0ce5fb0b7d299ff3a646c2785016dd3287928df3.text: Freebuff's public project now has automated checks that run on every proposed change, so contributors get quick feedback instead of waiting in silence. It affects only people who submit changes to the Freebuff or Codebuff source code. In daily use this does nothing visible for you: the assistant, your sessions, and your projects behave exactly as before, but the project maintainers now have fewer messy or out-of-scope contributions to sort through.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: Freebuff's August 2026 release reshapes the free AI model catalog, changes how daily spending limits work, and adds new ad-delivery and billing plumbing that mostly runs behind the scenes. The free model picker now ships with GLM 5.3 Flash as the lead default model (it's unmetered and uncapped), Solar Pro 4 joins as a limited-time trial option, and GPT-5.6 Luna is un-premiumd; withdrawn models like DeepSeek V4 Pro, MiniMax M3, and Ox Alpha are no longer selectable. Daily spend ceilings are restructured into a per-region table with a $15 standard tier, a $5 limited tier, and special caps for flagged accounts or VPN/proxy traffic, while DeepSeek's peak-hour closures were introduced and then removed after re-measurement. On the ad side, the placements delivery plane goes live with sanitized creative copy, deterministic daily-budget tapering, and first-party ad routing that defaults to dark-deploy until explicitly enabled, plus new CPC-floor and campaign-length controls. Users gain a new /reasoning command to set per-model thinking effort, the CLI model selector now shows peak-hour return times for closed rows and explains withdrawn model picks with a fallback, and subscription paywalls now surface upgrade links and plan-window summaries. Under the hood, the agent runtime drops unanswered tool calls at persistence boundaries to prevent history-replay errors, the SDK bundles a newer ripgrep and translates Git Bash paths on Windows, and post-session banners and referral trackers now carry subscription data so the plan panel stops flickering. The net effect is that you get a simpler, more stable free tier with clearer refusal messaging, a working default model at every hour of the day, and fewer silent routing surprises when a model is paused or withdrawn.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.text: The Freebuff coding assistant added a second ad slot to its terminal chat. Where the earlier slot appears when you're talking about pull requests and code reviews, this new one appears when you're talking about shipping, deploying, demoing or announcing what you built. Both spots draw the same single branded row just above the text box, so at most one shows at a time, and nothing changes unless the feature is part of the assistant's launch flow.

32405d54b26ef83e80be7c091a8c9610c6bf3b8a.text: When you ask the assistant to run a command in your terminal, the screen's keyboard and mouse tracking get temporarily turned off while that command runs, then turned back on only after it fully finishes. This mainly affects Freebuff CLI users on Windows, whose terminal no longer gets garbled mouse and focus escape sequences like ^[[I painted over the interface when a command spawns a child process. Headless SDK consumers that don't render an interactive terminal simply skip the isolation step entirely, so their programmatic runs are unchanged.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release updates the free AI models you can choose from and adds finer control over how the assistant reasons while it works. GLM 5.3 Flash is now the default free model across the CLI, web, and desktop apps, and Solar Pro 4 has been added as a limited-time free option, while DeepSeek V4 Pro and MiniMax M3 are removed from the free picker. You can now use the new /reasoning command to set how deeply the selected model thinks before answering, with your choice remembered per model in settings. Spend limits for free users are now calculated per region (with Singapore and China on their own ceilings) and can drop further when traffic comes through VPN, proxy, or Tor, and the refusal messages explain the limit and when it resets. Ad delivery now runs real first-party ads when possible, with creative text and landing URLs sanitized to block terminal-control sequences, and the CLI clipboard copy no longer hangs on broken display servers and prevents a stale copy from overwriting a newer one. On supported models, the CLI now labels rows that only open during off-peak hours with a local return time, and the agent runtime drops unanswered tool calls at conversation boundaries to keep history valid when resuming.

389f40a9a9a113232c22a5e93ee40d01a4ee7b08.text: The Freebuff SDK now looks for Git for Windows bash in a smarter, more flexible way, checking many possible install locations derived from your computer's environment settings instead of guessing a fixed default path. Windows users benefit when the assistant needs to run terminal commands: installs in per-user folders, Scoop or Chocolatey package managers, non-C: drives, or installs done while the app was already open are now detected without restarting. There is no action needed from you; the program will simply find your existing Git install more reliably and stop wrongly claiming bash is missing when it is actually present.

4cdbbb8e228beaa638fe937d7fec9a9c3d15f1c1.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.5 updates the lineup of free AI models, adds clearer progress and status information to your terminal session, and tightens security around downloads and third-party integrations. The Freebuff model catalog now offers Muse Spark 1.3 while Muse Spark 1.2 moves to the paid-only section, and a deal badge flags the GLM 5.3 Flash model as ending soon on September 30. Your daily Freebucks streak bonus now shows exactly how much credit you earned and when the next one arrives, with wording adjusted so east-of-Pacific users no longer see misleading wallet messages. The release launcher blocks downloads from non-https or non-first-party origins and sanitizes all remote text before it reaches your terminal to prevent hijacking and malicious escape sequences. Sponsored task runs now survive crashes by recording state to disk, let you undo partial file edits, and report launch-time failures instead of silently vanishing. Steering messages sent while a task is running get framed as additions to the current work rather than new standalone requests, so the assistant keeps working on the task instead of restarting.

46813796ce87abb4b405325a7c3deffa3f6f8509.text: The assistant now remembers when it is helping you with an ad-sponsored task, even if the terminal unexpectedly quits, closes, or your laptop goes to sleep mid-task. If that happens, the next time you open the assistant it will find the unfinished task, report it as interrupted, tell you which files it had already edited, and offer a single Undo button to revert those changes instead of leaving you unsure what happened. It also reports each ad-sponsored task's outcome more accurately to the service, so interrupted tasks are counted as partial changes rather than successful ones.

155c66375523b6e95e5af4ec6ff6f3ef71057bf7.text: The label next to GPT-6.1 Sol in your model list now says it is free in the US, paid everywhere else, capped at one session per day for every account. This affects developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK who see the model picker. You will notice the updated wording beside the GPT-6.1 Sol row, but the free-in-the-US benefit only applies to viewers in the US, and the one-session-a-day limit applies to everyone including paid plans.

afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.text: Freebuff 0.1.9 adds a new free AI model, GPT-6.1 Sol, to the list of options you can use at no charge (it is free in the US and limited to one session per day for every account), and refreshes the in-app promotional copy so the messaging stays consistent across the picker and pricing notices. Key highlights: (1) GPT-6.1 Sol is now selectable as a free model, pre-wired for the CLI and desktop agents, and marked as a temporary promotional model capped at one daily session for all users; (2) a 30-minute watch was added so the app can report whether you return after clicking an ad, posting that result back to the ad service so a fast bounce is not lost; (3) user and step messages sent for ad auctions are now tagged by source (your prompt, a step prompt, or a tool error) so the ad server can tell your real input apart from injected runtime messages; and (4) links inside sponsored procedures are automatically tagged with campaign tracking parameters at save time, falling back to Freebuff defaults when the advertiser did not supply their own, so visits from these runs are no longer untagged. Upgrading gives you a fresh free model to try, more accurate ad-attribution reporting behind the scenes, and properly tagged promotion links so sponsored runs are trackable; the house ad creatives and subscription promo copy were also updated to stay in sync with the current messaging.

4cdbbb8e228beaa638fe937d7fec9a9c3d15f1c1.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.5 replaces the older Muse Spark 1.2 model with Muse Spark 1.3 for free users, while Muse Spark 1.2 becomes paid-only and is marked as superseded. The daily Freebucks streak now shows a status line telling you when your next bonus starts and whether today's credit has landed, rendered in your local time. Sponsored runs that crash before finishing now get marked as failed by the next launch and can report partial file edits with an Undo option, plus the release launcher now blocks fake download URLs, refuses non-semver versions, and sanitizes remote text so terminal hijacks and ANSI/OSC escape tricks are stripped. Ads and referrals were reorganized too: Facebook counts under its own label instead of being lost, and the picker warns when a GLM 5.3 Flash deal ends soon. For developers using the SDK, spawn-agents results come back as plain text instead of message arrays, compaction hooks now always fire start/end events around a compaction pass, and large file reads on edit paths return full content so str_replace works past the old ~65K truncation.

cef527925490255bcfcfb2dba4a125ae27f63d38.text: When you sign in to Freebuff from home internet that is being run through a bandwidth-sharing app (the kind that pays you to share your connection), Freebuff now tells you that is the reason in plain words, instead of offering VPN advice you cannot use. This only affects users whose connection is identified as a residential proxy, and they will see a clearer explanation next to the model list. Everyone else sees no difference today.

bb46c52bc16e41ff79cb08aa459448643ab95ddb.text: When you type a message to the assistant, that message now travels with a small label telling the ad server it is your own text, not something the program added itself. The assistant already sent along the back-and-forth of your conversation when asking for ads, but it no longer tagged whether your words started the talk, came back as a follow-up step, or appeared after a tool failed. The ad server uses these labels only to decide which ad fits the moment, so ads may feel a little more relevant to what you just typed. Nothing about your session limits, your free credits, or your access changes, and if your version of the service is older the extra label is ignored.

afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.text: This release adds OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol to the free model picker as a temporary promotional model with a 100-Freebucks price in the US and one free session per day for every account, and it refreshes the wording around that promotion so both the catalog and the Freebucks price notice show the same temporary-price copy. It also drops the web chat house ad surface from the ad-serving setup, updates the subscription promotion copy shown in the waiting room, adds UTM tags to advertiser links inside sponsored procedures so visits get attributed correctly, and tracks whether someone who clicks a Freebuff ad comes back by treating their next typed prompt as the return signal. Upgrading gives you a new flagship model option with a clear daily-session cap, slightly cleaner ad experiences, and better measurement of ad click returns, while the house ad surfaces and sponsored link tagging keep the free experience consistent and attributable.

73c6ceb590d8d56df307de723563cd09d01e2ea0.text: When you click on an ad inside Freebuff, the app now quietly watches to see if you come back by typing your next question. It measures how long it is between the click and your next prompt, using that gap as an upper-bound estimate of how much time you spent away, since a terminal can't directly tell whether you switched back to it. This only affects users who interact with ads in the Freebuff CLI while coding. You won't see anything new in your terminal, but these measurements help improve which ads are shown by telling whether clicks actually brought people back to keep using the assistant.

41c03830a5fb0af4241a56663cfadfa6cfa24a56.text: You can now tell Freebuff how much thinking effort your own AI provider should spend on each coding task, using the new `/byok effort` command with one of three levels: low, medium, or high. Freebuff translates that choice into the correct setting for whichever provider you connected, and if a provider rejects the setting, Freebuff automatically retries without it so your task still finishes. This affects only you when you run Freebuff with your own provider key, and it is live today; existing sessions that do not use this command behave exactly as before.

592b3211840b26f528305bfbea7954cdbc5ead5b.text: When you start a coding session with the Freebuff CLI and have an active Freebucks purchase, the running session now keeps its reserved hour and first-tab discount instead of re-checking a single shared store. If you switch models during that same session, you will be quoted the full price for the new model while your original purchase keeps its discount, and any replacement purchase uses the server's quote rather than transferring the old discount. The change also lets older, ended single-session purchases release their discount reservation through the single-session path.

e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.text: Freebuff 0.2.0 ships with lower reasoning effort on the most demanding Muse Spark and Gemini models, so those responses settle at 'high' rather than the previously automatic 'xhigh' setting. The onboarding flow now shuffles its role, intended use, and subscription questions each time you open the form, so no single option always appears first. The in-app Freebucks meter now reads the live session's pricing and purchase data directly through the cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts path, meaning your running session keeps its hour reservation and first-tab discount instead of being re-quoted at full price when you switch models, while older single-session purchases continue to release their discount reservation through the server quote reuse path. Freebucks top-ups and model-tier pricing are now kept consistent for the active session, and the off-peak pricing option for Freebucks rates is now exposed in the purchase meter. The update also exports EFFORTS_LOW_THROUGH_XHIGH and EFFORTS_HIGH_ONLY ladders in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts, so the server can clamp any out-of-range effort to high on every turn for the affected rows, per the 2026-09-29 product decision.

9a87cf853a482411f6667fa4ad554c38b077e4fc.text: The assistant now pays attention to whether a model stopped on its own or got cut off while it was thinking out loud in its reply. If the model finished a step with the thinking tags still open, the assistant treats what the model wrote inside those tags as part of the actual answer instead of hiding it. If the model was cut off before finishing, the thinking stays hidden as a truncated thought. You will notice fewer replies where the answer disappears behind an open 'thinking' tag that never closed, and fewer empty or cut-short replies where the model was trying to reason through something. Live today in the Freebuff CLI, web app, and desktop app.

e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.text: Freebuff 0.2.0 caps several high-end AI models at a 'high' reasoning level instead of the previous 'extra-high' setting, after measuring that the extra-high tier added only about 8% more reasoning for roughly 26% more wait time. This release also introduces new reasoning-effort options that let the service enforce these caps consistently across model families. The on-screen setup questions (role, intended use, subscriptions) now randomize their answer order on each form load, matching a change that was already in place for the referral source question. The Freebucks purchase meter in the CLI now reflects the live session's pricing and discounts instead of re-resolving them, so a running session keeps its hour reservation and first-tab discount rather than showing full price. Upgrading means the models you select no longer use the extra-high reasoning tier that cost you more waiting time for only a small gain, the setup form shows answer choices in a different order each time you open it, and any Freebucks purchase you make mid-session honors the discount you saw upfront rather than switching on you.

1d624b2aaf25302cafde35530631657767e4a5d3.title: OpenAI cyber risk 403 pattern and recovery message
1d624b2aaf25302cafde35530631657767e4a5d3.summary: Added the FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CYBER_RISK_ERROR_PATTERN regex and FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CYBER_RISK_MESSAGE constant to common/src/constants/freebuff-errors.ts, extending the provider-error catalog that already covers DeepSeek content filters and Codebuff out-of-credits 402s so this safeguard surfaces a recoverable message instead of an unrelated organization 401. The pattern is applied to the request's content, so the same conversation is refused again on retry, and the message points the user to OpenAI's Daybreak access form, which a Freebuff user cannot use. No consumer of these exports appears in the diff at this revision.
1d624b2aaf25302cafde35530631657767e4a5d3.evidence: Added FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CYBER_RISK_ERROR_PATTERN (/flagged for possible cybersecurity risk/i) and FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CYBER_RISK_MESSAGE in common/src/constants/freebuff-errors.ts, matching OpenAI 403s whose body says "This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk" on GPT-6.1 Sol (2026-09-30); these are new exports with no visible consumer in the diff.
1d624b2aaf25302cafde35530631657767e4a5d3.unknowns: The diff shows no consumer of the new error pattern and message, so it is unclear which handler surfaces them to users.

1d624b2aaf25302cafde35530631657767e4a5d3.text: The assistant now recognizes a specific refusal message from one of its AI model providers (OpenAI) that says content looks like a cybersecurity risk, and shows a clearer explanation instead of a confusing account error. This is internal setup work: the new message and detection rule are saved in a shared error list, but nothing in this change is wired up to actually show them to users yet. Today it does nothing visible; users will only notice a difference once a later change connects these rules to the assistant's error handling.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.text: This release updates the Freebuff coding assistant to version 0.2.1, adding clearer feedback when OpenAI blocks a request for policy reasons and improving how the terminal-based AI tool reports ad-related setup information. When OpenAI rejects a prompt due to content policies, the assistant now shows a specific, recoverable message explaining the issue instead of a confusing authorization error, and retrying will produce the same result since the prompt itself is the problem. The update also introduces new utilities for gathering client environment details and user input profiles, which help the system better understand how users interact with ads within the Freebuff interface. Upgrading to this version gives you more transparent error handling when model providers refuse requests, and lays groundwork for improved tracking of how people use the free tier funded by first-party advertisements.

b6925d1398492646733a7269207331d414e7a2b9.title: CLI sends terminal env and input profile in ad and run metadata
b6925d1398492646733a7269207331d414e7a2b9.summary: The CLI now ships a compact `v1;in=1;out=1;tp=iterm;term=1;ct=1;sz=120x40;ci=0;ssh=0;l=1;p=shell;g=terminal;osc=1 descriptor of its terminal environment under the x-freebuff-env` header on Freebuff session and ad requests, and the same descriptor plus per-prompt input counts into `codebuff_metadata` for each run. `clientEnvironmentHeaders()` is imported into `buildAdAuctionRequest` and the gravity ad path so ad requests carry env, device and trace pointers consistently, and `clientDescriptorMetadata` attaches `freebuff_client_env` and `freebuff_input_profile` to the Freebuff run config. A one-time ancestor-process probe starts at launch (reading parent and grandparent kinds, skipping the CLI's own launcher pid) and the colour-query reply is recorded, because ad networks bot-filter on the user agent while the server uses the descriptor to scope bot-filtering and billing.
b6925d1398492646733a7269207331d414e7a2b9.evidence: New modules `cli/src/utils/client-environment.ts` and `cli/src/utils/input-profile.ts` plus shared constants `common/src/constants/freebuff-client-descriptor.ts` produce compact `v1;key=value;...` descriptors; `clientEnvironmentHeaders()` is spread into session/ad headers in `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts`, `cli/src/ads/ad-request.ts`, `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts`, and `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-identity.ts`'s `clientDescriptorMetadata` adds `freebuff_client_env` and `freebuff_input_profile` into `codebuff_metadata`; `cli/src/index.tsx` kicks off `startClientEnvironmentProbe()` and calls `noteTerminalColorReply`; `cli/src/chat.tsx` calls `sealInputProfile` and wraps paste handling with `withPasteCount`; `cli/src/components/chat-input-bar.tsx` and `cli/src/components/multiline-input.tsx` wire `recordTypedInput` and `onTypedText` into the composer's key events.
b6925d1398492646733a7269207331d414e7a2b9.unknowns: The server-side consumer of the new metadata keys is not in the diff.

changes.what: Builds a compact `v1;...` terminal-environment descriptor and a `clientEnvironmentHeaders()` map that emits it under `x-freebuff-env` for Freebuff builds, probing ancestor process kinds asynchronously and never throwing.
Counts typed vs pasted characters, key events, and compose time per submitted prompt, sealing counts keyed by the trimmed text and encoding them as a `v1;...` profile.
Adds `clientDescriptorMetadata`, which attaches the env descriptor and any sealed input profile to a run's `codebuff_metadata`.
Spreads `clientEnvironmentHeaders()` into Freebuff session request headers.
Adds `clientEnvironmentHeaders()` to ad auction request headers so targeting/filtering sees the same descriptor.
Adds `clientEnvironmentHeaders()` to impression and click acknowledgement requests.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.text: This release updates the Freebuff version label to 0.2.1 and adds two new behaviors you'll notice during use. First, Freebuff now recognizes a specific error code returned by OpenAI when your request is blocked for cyber-risk reasons, and instead of showing a confusing login error, it explains that you need to apply for access through OpenAI's Daybreak form. Second, the CLI now sends a small profile of your terminal setup (like its size, whether you're using iTerm, and how many prompts you type) along with ad requests and run records; this helps the ad system better filter out bots and bill advertisers accurately, and it also attaches that same profile data to each coding session you run. Upgrading gives you clearer error feedback when OpenAI blocks a request, and ensures your terminal and usage context are properly recorded for both advertising and session tracking.

b6925d1398492646733a7269207331d414e7a2b9.text: The Freebuff CLI now sends a compact summary about your terminal setup (like what app you're using, how big your window is, and how you typed your message) whenever it asks for an ad or starts a coding task. This affects Freebuff's free-tier users and anyone seeing ads, since the service uses these details to tell real people apart from bots and to show relevant ads. You won't notice anything different day-to-day, but it helps make sure ads are shown correctly and billed properly when you're using the free version.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: Freebuff 1.0.686 adds a new slash command, a revamped ad engagement system, and significant changes to which AI models you can use for free. You can now type /reasoning to control how hard the model thinks on each request, and the free model catalog has changed: GLM 5.3 Flash is now the default free model, Solar Pro 4 has been added to the picker, while DeepSeek V4 Pro, MiniMax M3, and Ox Alpha are no longer available in the free tier. The ad system has been reworked so advertisers pay a flat daily subscription fee instead of per engagement, campaign lengths are capped at one week, and ad creatives are now sanitized for terminal safety. Your daily free session limits have been adjusted: most models share a pooled daily quota, GLM 5.3 Flash and DeepSeek V4 Flash are unmetered, and DeepSeek V4 Pro is capped at one session per day. The referral and trust system now uses a 11-rung ladder where engagements earn points toward free and premium sessions, with standard prompts costing zero trust and a zero balance floor so your score never goes negative. Signing up now supports Google reCAPTCHA in addition to Cloudflare Turnstile, and the CLI model picker shows peak-hour return times for models that close during expensive windows. Upgrading gives you access to the latest free model lineup with clearer limits, the new /reasoning control, and a more stable ad-supported experience.

9d0e435b3802e4b6b833c1ed349d604e5b804f0d.text: The assistant now has access to a new experimental AI model called Ox Alpha, but only when you use the Freebuff website or Cloud version - it does not appear in the terminal app or desktop app. This model is free to use right now, comes from an undisclosed provider who is testing it, and includes a hard safety lock that prevents you from ever being charged for it, even if the provider changes their pricing. If you use Freebuff in your browser, you will see this new model listed as an experimental option with a one-million-token limit, but if you use the terminal or desktop versions, you will not see it at all.

28ccadc6687c271cf00e473547c11ed8a096c363.text: The assistant has been taught that one specific AI model, OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol, can only be used once per day by any single account, and this limit cannot be bypassed by paying for a plan. Users who pick GPT-6.1 Sol will now see a clear message saying they get one session a day, so they know the limit before they begin. If GPT-6.1 Sol is free in your country, you can still only run it once each day; if you want to use it more often, you would need to choose a different model.

afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.text: This release adds OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol to the free model picker, offering it at no charge in the US with a temporary promotional price and a daily session limit of one per account for all users. GPT-6.1 Sol is now wired into the CLI and Desktop as a selectable model with a dedicated reviewer, and its promotional copy clearly notes the free-in-US, paid-elsewhere, one-session-per-day structure. The CLI now tracks post-click return behavior for Freebuff ads by measuring the time from an ad click to your next submitted prompt, with a 30-minute monitoring window and no grace period for leaving. Ad request messages now carry tags (USER_PROMPT, STEP_PROMPT, TOOL_CALL_ERROR) so the auction server can distinguish what you typed from runtime-injected turns, while assistant messages remain untagged. Sponsored procedure links exported by the agent now automatically receive UTM campaign tags at save time, preserving the advertiser's existing UTM parameters and keeping execution, review, and hashing aligned. The removed web chat house ad surface means the checked-in floor creatives now total across four surfaces instead of five, and the subscription promotion copy was refreshed with an updated waiting room creative.

9a87cf853a482411f6667fa4ad554c38b077e4fc.text: When the assistant writes out its private reasoning inside a hidden tag, the program now checks whether the model finished its answer or was cut off mid-sentence. If the model completed its response on its own, the hidden reasoning is released as the visible reply; if it was interrupted, it stays tucked away as thinking. This affects anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web app, or desktop app to chat with the assistant. In daily use, answers are less likely to appear empty or cut short when a model stops inside its reasoning tag.

5e1579a5cab63056ed76b338490991bc981e05b7.title: BYOK model ID rejection pattern narrows to model-as-subject matches
5e1579a5cab63056ed76b338490991bc981e05b7.summary: In sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts, the second pattern in `BYOK_MODEL_REJECTION_PATTERNS` was tightened so `isByokModelIdRejection` only classifies provider error bodies where the model ID itself is the subject of the rejection. It now demands `models?` followed by an optional single id token (bare, quoted, or backtick-quoted) and then phrases like does not exist / not found / not supported, which prevents capability refusals on valid IDs from being mistaken for bad model IDs.
5e1579a5cab63056ed76b338490991bc981e05b7.evidence: sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts: the regex at `BYOK_MODEL_REJECTION_PATTERNS[1]` was rewritten from a permissive sentence pattern to one that requires `models?` as the subject followed by an optional single id token and then the rejection phrase, so bodies like model x: image input is not supported no longer match.
5e1579a5cab63056ed76b338490991bc981e05b7.unknowns: The consumer of this stricter classification and what, if any, user-facing message path changes as a result.

5e1579a5cab63056ed76b338490991bc981e05b7.text: The matching rule that decides whether a failed request was caused by a wrong model name has been made more precise, so it now only flags errors where the model name itself is clearly stated as the problem. This is internal logic inside the software developer kit that connects to AI providers, so it does not change anything you see or do directly. The practical effect shows up later, when the tool gives you better, more accurate messages if a model you picked is not accepted by your provider.

b63254fdc6b1967224a0eaea03df93dd75c5724b.title: Client env descriptor reports proxy, TLS and timezone shape
b63254fdc6b1967224a0eaea03df93dd75c5724b.summary: The Freebuff CLI now reads ALL_PROXY and the proxy, TLS rejection, and CA certificate environment variables into CliEnv (cli/src/types/env.ts and cli/src/utils/env.ts) so they are available to the client environment descriptor. client-environment.ts adds bucketProxy to reduce each proxy URL to where it points (none, loopback, or remote), formatClientEnvironment now emits tzo, px, tls, ca and stz fields, and readSystemTimeZone reads the OS timezone from /etc/localtime or /etc/timezone so stz can carry the system zone only when TZ overrides it. The descriptor continues to send only presence flags, fixed bucket names and the OS zone, never raw proxy URLs, paths, or the proxy variable values themselves.
b63254fdc6b1967224a0eaea03df93dd75c5724b.evidence: Commit b63254fd modifies cli/src/types/env.ts, cli/src/utils/env.ts, and cli/src/utils/client-environment.ts to add proxy and TLS env vars (ALL_PROXY, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, and other proxy variants) to the CliEnv type and getCliEnv(), and adds bucketProxy, zoneFromZoneinfo, readSystemTimeZone, ProxyBucket, and zoneFromZoneinfo exports to client-environment.ts, wired into the x-freebuff-env descriptor via new tzo, px, tls, ca, and stz fields. New tests assert 'a MITM sidecar: TZ forced, loopback proxy, TLS off, extra CA', 'bucketProxy', and 'zoneFromZoneinfo' behaviors.
b63254fdc6b1967224a0eaea03df93dd75c5724b.unknowns: The consumer of the new tzo, px, tls, ca, and stz descriptor fields on the server side is not shown in this diff.

b63254fdc6b1967224a0eaea03df93dd75c5724b.text: The Freebuff CLI now gathers information about your network and timezone setup (like whether you're using a proxy, whether TLS certificate checks are turned off, and your system's timezone) and includes a summarized version of that in its environment report. This report goes to Freebuff's servers as part of session and advertising requests. You won't see anything new in the terminal, but the summarized information helps improve how Freebuff understands and supports different user environments. Developers using the Freebuff CLI who already configure proxies or adjust security settings in their environment are the ones this affects, and no action is required from them.

fc37ac10e299ace4c9055da809823202303a75c8.title: Caller deadline aborts reported as cancellation not idle timeout
fc37ac10e299ace4c9055da809823202303a75c8.summary: The agent runtime and SDK now distinguish a caller-initiated deadline from Bun's 5-minute fetch idle timeout. AbortSignal.timeout rejects with a DOMException named TimeoutError, the same name isFetchIdleTimeoutError matches, so loopAgentSteps and runOnce now check signal.aborted first and report a cancelled run instead of the idle-timeout user message when the caller aborted the run.
fc37ac10e299ace4c9055da809823202303a75c8.evidence: Modified run-agent-step.ts (catch block) and sdk/src/run.ts (runOnce .catch handler): both now check signal.aborted and treat an aborted caller signal as a cancellation instead of classifying a TimeoutError (the name AbortSignal.timeout rejects with) as the 5-minute fetch idle timeout.
fc37ac10e299ace4c9055da809823202303a75c8.unknowns: The diff does not show which exact caller surfaces set the 20-second title deadline that motivated this change.

changes.what: The catch block now checks signal.aborted alongside isAbortError so a caller deadline aborting the stream is treated as a cancelled run rather than a TimeoutError idle timeout.
runOnce's .catch handler now branches on signal?.aborted, returning the caller's abort reason message instead of the fetch idle timeout message when the caller aborted.

fc37ac10e299ace4c9055da809823202303a75c8.text: When a run is cut short by a caller-imposed deadline rather than by the assistant going quiet, the system now recognizes that deadline and reports the stop as a cancellation (the caller pulled the plug) instead of blaming a five-minute idle-timeout message. This affects developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK who pass their own abort deadlines into a run. In daily use you see an accurate "Run cancelled by user" message instead of a misleading "no data was received for 5 minutes" notice when your own timeout fires; no action is required on your part, it is live today.

9aede7717867ad17a5aeac24cb14ecddb12d1d68.title: Infer tool call index when OpenAI-compatible chunk omits it
9aede7717867ad17a5aeac24cb14ecddb12d1d68.summary: The OpenAI-compatible chat model now infers a tool call's index when an OpenAI-compatible server or proxy omits index from a tool_calls delta, using a new inferToolCallIndex export that falls back to matching an existing id or reusing the last unfinished call. Previously the missing field failed the whole chunk, so the tool call was silently lost; the chunk schema now accepts index as nullish, and the new tests 'assembles tool calls whose deltas carry no index' and 'keeps honoring an explicit index' cover both paths.

New tests in `byok-paste.test.ts` cover joined URLs, reported splits, and unknown provider types.

1654e2212f8267b7b9bebccea8ec5a4992d638d8.summary: A new OpenRouter lane for Muse Spark is pinned to the `meta` endpoint and capped by MUSE_SPARK_OPENROUTER_MAX_PRICE ({ prompt: 0.15, completion: 0.3 } per M tokens), so a second host or repriced endpoint cannot take the traffic or be billed. MUSE_SPARK_OPENROUTER_UPSTREAM_ORDER = ['meta'] as const records the single endpoint OpenRouter lists for each Contributor id. The lane exists because the direct Meta key was user_blocked about fourteen minutes after Muse Spark 1.3 went paid-only on 2026-09-28, sending picks to the DeepSeek fallback.
1654e2212f8267b7b9bebccea8ec5a4992d638d8.evidence: Diff hunk in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts adds three new exports after the MUSE_SPARK_CONTRIBUTOR_TPM block: MUSE_SPARK_OPENROUTER_UPSTREAM_ORDER = ['meta'] as const, MUSE_SPARK_OPENROUTER_MAX_PRICE = { prompt: 0.15, completion: 0.3 } as const, and a docblock comment explaining the OpenRouter lane default since 2026-09-29 due to the direct key being user_blocked by Meta.

a65a05b3511a4ba7bf8d838348796a1a58d45705.text: The session response now includes a country verification flag indicating whether the server has confirmed the request comes from an allowed country. This is information for the Freebuff engineering team as part of shared type definitions, not a change to your experience. Because no code reads this flag yet, it is in place but does nothing for you today. Your daily use is unchanged.

925bc3fc61b0927e0189685d5d1f0dfb0fee38c8.text: You can now scroll up and down through your earlier prompts in the assistant even after recalling one of them. Previously, pressing Up/Down on a recalled prompt only showed the most recent entry and ignored the rest of your history; now it keeps paging back through earlier prompts, the same way it behaves when the input box is empty. Left/right arrow keys still move the cursor inside a recalled prompt so you can edit it, and once you manually edit a recalled entry, Up/Down switch back to moving the cursor instead of paging history. This applies to anyone using the CLI assistant for prompt history navigation.

9aede7717867ad17a5aeac24cb14ecddb12d1d68.text: When the assistant talks to an AI model that returns answers piece by piece, some of those model services forget to label which part of a multi-step tool call (like editing a file) each piece belongs to. Previously that missing label made the whole piece get thrown away, so a task like writing a file would start but never finish. Now the system guesses the right slot based on the tool's name and any previous pieces, so tool calls that were silently failing now complete. Affected parties are Freebuff's engineering team, who maintain the model connection code; you may notice that AI models connected through certain third-party services now reliably finish tool-using steps instead of stopping midway.

a50d7e783cb6733fe7ac14503afb30f4c49748ba.text: When you add or update your own AI provider in the Freebuff CLI and paste a long command that the terminal wrapped across lines, the assistant now intelligently rejoins a pasted line break only when there is exactly one correct way to read it, instead of guessing. If you include more arguments than the command allows, it refuses with a clear message naming the extra words, rather than silently dropping them. If you leave off a required piece of the command, it tells you exactly what is missing instead of printing generic help. This applies to Freebuff CLI users adding or updating connections and is live today.

fc37ac10e299ace4c9055da809823202303a75c8.text: The assistant now treats a user's manual stop as a true cancel, not a timeout error, so interrupting it mid-sentence no longer logs a confusing 'server idle' message in your terminal or SDK logs. This is live today for anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web app, desktop app, or the developer SDK. You won't see a banner or popup, but a cancelled response will now report a clean cancellation reason instead of an idle-timeout warning in logs and return payloads. No setup or migration is needed.

51b40e3b7df6b180ed089d2204f6bb3a91f93c4f.text: The signup questionnaire now randomizes the order of the answer choices for four questions, so no option gets an unfair edge just from being listed first. This affects whoever maintains the questionnaire definition and the tests that guard it. For day-to-day use the questions still appear in the same place with the same choices, only the order you see them in is reshuffled each time; the one question that runs low-to-high (how much you code) stays in that order. Nothing else in the app changes.

b63254fdc6b1967224a0eaea03df93dd75c5724b.text: The Freebuff app now quietly notes whether you are using a web proxy (and where it points, without recording the full address), whether secure web certificate checking is turned off, and whether extra security certificates are installed, plus whether your clock zone has been manually overridden. This is internal diagnostic information the engineering team uses to understand how people run the app, so it does not change anything you see or change any settings you need to adjust.

bb46c52bc16e41ff79cb08aa459448643ab95ddb.text: When you see an ad in the Freebuff assistant, the request that gets sent now labels who actually wrote each message: it can tell which lines you typed yourself apart from the ones the assistant generated on its own (like error summaries or step-by-step notes). This is internal wiring behind the ad display, so it changes nothing about how the assistant feels to you and you do not need to do anything. Freebuff's team made this change today so they can serve more relevant, correctly targeted ads.

45a2358b9acdb158b300963919271fb6f21c5f34.text: The assistant's built-in house ad catalog no longer includes the Freebuff web chat promotion, so that ad surface and its fallback copy have been taken out of the catalog that runs the subscription promotion. This only affects the Freebuff engineering team's internal ad copy catalog and the campaigns it seeds. You won't see any difference in your daily use of the assistant, and nothing you do is affected.

51e08c800533ae4206e4e740eade9b700d2b7d9f.text: The wording of the built-in subscription promotion that fills in when no paid ads are available was revised in this internal constants file. This is a marketing-text tweak read only by Freebuff's ad-serving internals and the house campaigns that promote the paid subscription tier, so it affects no user-facing behavior, sessions, quotas, or ad serving for end users. There is nothing you need to do, and you will not notice any change in daily use. The copy change is live within the common package, while the actual campaign creative is stored separately and does not require a redeploy on its own.

25fab627e738eaf5ca5c596187c62fc2e12c5649.text: Advertisers buying ad space on Freebuff now see a new line in their dashboard called invoiced CPM value. This shows the dollar amount of ads they purchased through a separate billing process outside of Freebuff's normal pay-per-click system. The new field only appears for advertisers whose contracts use this invoiced pricing model, and it does not change what they are charged through Freebuff directly. Who it affects: Advertisers running campaigns billed via invoice rather than through Freebuff's standard click-based billing. Everyday impact: These advertisers will see an additional amount labeled as invoiced CPM value added to their displayed spend and result-pricing numbers, giving them a fuller picture of their total ad costs.

1654e2212f8267b7b9bebccea8ec5a4992d638d8.text: The Freebuff engineering team added a safety lock on the new Meta model (Muse Spark 1.3) so that when it is reached through OpenRouter, traffic can only go to Meta's own endpoint and cannot be silently rerouted to a cheaper or different host. A price ceiling is recorded so that if anyone tries to repackage or resell the model at a different rate, the request is refused instead of billed. The change is internal configuration that the routing code does not yet read, so it has no user-visible effect today, and nothing is announced to end users or advertisers.

fa7f6a239db7ed3d74758432e00ac1acdbc847f4.text: Sponsored-run procedures in the Freebuff monorepo now attach default UTM tags to links that send a developer to an advertiser's own site, while leaving the advertiser's existing UTM tags and code-block links untouched. It affects advertisers and sponsors who buy placements or run sponsored campaigns on the Freebuff platform. If you click a tagged link during a sponsored run, the advertiser's analytics can now plainly see it came from Freebuff, so untagged visits from sponsored runs should drop off. No action is needed from you; this is a backstage fix so Freebuff gets proper credit for the traffic it sends, and it only applies to advertisers' own domains.

6fc184b984516641b8193b07ae4188145c94583d.title: Freebuff auth token moves to OS keychain at login
6fc184b984516641b8193b07ae4188145c94583d.summary: The Freebuff CLI now stores the user auth token in the operating system keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service via `Bun.secrets`) instead of `credentials.json` in plaintext. `loadStoredAuthToken()` runs once at startup in `cli/src/index.tsx` to migrate or load the token, and `saveUserCredentials` in `cli/src/utils/auth.ts` calls `moveTokenToKeychain` to copy the token then strip it from the file, leaving a profile with `tokenStore: 'keychain'`. Reads remain synchronous through a cached token, and `clearUserCredentials` also removes the keychain item on logout. The change is guarded behind `IS_FREEBUFF` and never throws, so a missing or unusable keychain leaves the token in the owner-only file.
6fc184b984516641b8193b07ae4188145c94583d.evidence: cli/src/index.tsx calls loadStoredAuthToken() at startup before reading credentials; cli/src/utils/auth-token-store.ts defines the OS keychain store via Bun.secrets; cli/src/utils/auth.ts's saveUserCredentials calls moveTokenToKeychain and userFromJson falls back to getCachedKeychainToken when tokenStore === 'keychain'; tests in auth-keychain.test.ts assert token moves out of the file and is reloaded from the keychain at launch.
6fc184b984516641b8193b07ae4188145c94583d.unknowns: The rollout plan and whether the keychain item key or service name will stay stable across future binaries are not described in the diff. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

985c872eb8d43f538ab77d933ef7c43125d100ff.text: Freebuff release 0.2.3 is a packaging update that labels the current stable CLI version users download and run. This release ships the Freebuff command-line tool under version 0.2.3. It bundles the terminal interface, slash commands such as /ask, /undo, /diff, and /byok, plus the free model picker that shows which AI models you can use at no charge. The package includes the same first-party text ads and sponsored placements that fund the free tier, along with the spend ceilings and Freebucks credit system that govern your compute allowance. Updating to 0.2.3 simply installs the same Freebuff experience under its new version number, so the CLI behaves as it did in 0.2.2 while carrying the updated release label.

8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.text: This release updates Freebuff to version 0.2.4 and refreshes the package that powers the CLI. The assistant's model catalog (the list of AI models you can pick from at no charge) is now kept up to date through new catalog and store files in the CLI, so the models offered to you reflect the latest published free model picker. As a result, upgrading to 0.2.4 syncs the in-app model list you choose from with the current set of free models, so any newly added or removed options show up correctly when you start a new session.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff 0.2.2 refreshes the screen you see when you open the app, updating how the model picker and session-ended banner are shown. It expands the Bring Your Own Key flow so you can connect your own AI provider accounts in more ways and see clearer messaging during pay-per-use credit setup. The update also introduces a new reset path for premium model access and adjusts how the CLI reacts after a session ends. Upgrading gives you a cleaner startup experience, broader options for using your own AI keys, and clearer feedback when a session finishes.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.text: This Freebuff update adds support for reporting your terminal setup (like the type of terminal app, screen size, and input settings) on a single line sent with ad and session requests, so ad networks can better filter automated traffic and the service can match your environment accurately. The CLI now probes its parent launch processes once at startup and captures your terminal's color-support reply, adding these details to its metadata without changing your workflow. When you run a task, the CLI also includes a compact profile of how much you type and what kind of terminal you use, helping the service distinguish real user interactions from automated ones for billing and bot-filtering. Upgrading gives you more accurate ad targeting and bot protection, and keeps your terminal's real-world usage signals flowing consistently to the service that funds the free tier.

83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.title: Cap credentials parse/read log spam in cli auth
83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.summary: Because `getUserCredentials` runs on every render of the app shell (`useAuthQuery` / `useAuthState`) and a 0.2.4 CLI that moved the token to the keychain left pre-0.2.4 builds failing `userSchema` validation with `authToken` required, an unparseable `credentials.json` logged an error on every frame (about 11 per second). The new `logCredentialsFailureOnce` helper deduplicates failures by key (`parse:${profileName}:${errorMessage}` and `read:${message}`) and caps the set at `MAX_LOGGED_CREDENTIALS_FAILURES = 20`, so each distinct failure logs once instead of per read.
83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.evidence: cli/src/utils/auth.ts introduces `loggedCredentialsFailures`, `MAX_LOGGED_CREDENTIALS_FAILURES = 20`, the `logCredentialsFailureOnce` helper, and exports `resetCredentialsFailureLogForTests`; `userFromJson` and `getUserCredentials` now call `logCredentialsFailureOnce` with distinct keys instead of `logger.error`.
83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.unknowns: The `loggedCredentialsFailures` set and `resetCredentialsFailureLogForTests` are consumed only by the new tests, so it is not visible whether non-test callers will rely on the reset export.

e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.text: AI Model Limits Adjusted: Freebuff 0.2.0 caps the deepest thinking level for several popular models so responses stay predictable and don't take much longer for minimal gain. The update sets Muse Spark and GPT-6.1 Sol models to use the high thinking level by default instead of the higher setting, after measuring that the extra thinking added 26% more wait time for just 8% more reasoning benefit. Gemini and GPT-6 Luna models also get their thinking capped to the same level on every turn, so all these models behave consistently across conversations. You get responses that finish sooner while keeping the same level of thoughtful answers.

e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.text: This release adds a safety check that stops half-finished file edits from overwriting your real files. When an AI response gets cut off mid-writing, the system now detects incomplete instructions (like a message that stops in the middle of typing a bracket or string) and treats it as if nothing was written, instead of letting a broken partial version replace your full file. It also blocks attempts to overwrite an existing file of 30 or more lines with a much shorter copy that leaves brackets open where the current file had them balanced. The system logs when these protections trigger and includes tests and documentation explaining how the guard works. Upgrading means you're less likely to lose work when the AI is interrupted mid-edit.

83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.text: The assistant's helper that checks who you are has been quieted down so it no longer spams the log file when it struggles to read your login information, instead logging each separate problem just once. This is internal maintenance work for the engineering team that builds the Freebuff coding assistant, and it has no noticeable effect on your daily use of the app.
