afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.text: GPT-6.1 Sol is now available in the free model picker, including a temporary promotional price in the US where it is free, with a one-session-per-day limit for every account. The model is integrated into the default helper agents and a same-model reviewer so it works across both the CLI and Desktop. Post-click return measurement for ad clicks records how long after clicking a Freebuf ad a user comes back to the assistant, using the next submitted prompt as the return signal with a 30-minute watch window. Promotional copy clarifies that GPT-6.1 Sol is free in the US, paid elsewhere, and capped at one session a day for every account.

It is in place now but has no effect yet because no other part of the app reads it, and you will notice nothing change in your daily use.

643c65bbab6758b2f881d400a86551962aa73c67.text: The assistant's session check now tells apps whether verifying a country can actually unlock more access, and if not, it sends a ready-made paid-plan offer for that account's situation. Developers who build on or embed Freebuff get the right prompt and plan numbers straight from the server, instead of guessing the tier or pricing locally. 05b8302ce19e998ea16f2f38c400c62c94d974b7.text: The release label for the Freebuff assistant app was advanced to the next number so the packaged download is now recognized as the newer edition. This is bookkeeping for the Freebuff engineering team that publishes the install files, not a change that alters how the assistant works. You do not need to do anything, and your daily experience will not change because of this label alone.

03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.text: Freebuff bumped its CLI version to 0.2.11 with a refreshed launcher that updates how the command-line tool starts up and reads environment settings, along with expanded test coverage for the agent tool-running system. The main change is a new launcher that touches four CLI files, which means the program you type in a terminal now starts more reliably and picks up configuration values more consistently (a minor change in how variables are read plus a major update to the startup code). Test coverage was added for the shared agent-runtime tool server, so the engine that runs helper tools and subagents during a coding task now has more automated checks guarding its behavior. For most users this release mainly smooths out how the CLI boots and reads settings, and it hardens the part of the system that executes tools while it works on your project.

3b7ce89c8102761014eafbe97cced66d9a22ec88.text: A new AI model called GPT-6.1 Sol has been added to the Freebuff catalog of models you can choose from when using the assistant. It is free for users in the United States, while users in other regions or on limited access need a paid plan to use it, and it is offered at a temporary promotional price. You may see it appear in your model picker with a label indicating the promotional price.

44c800d2617286631654dfd4d3c7b2b0e8e4d6b4.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.6 adds a new server-side channel that tells an advertising platform (X) when an ad led to a signup, respecting privacy settings like Do Not Track. It also introduces a new device signing system that creates a cryptographic key on your machine to securely identify your device when fetching the catalog of available AI models, so the list of free models loads more reliably. The Freebucks credit system was updated with changes that affect how pay-as-you-go compute credits work. The README was refreshed with updated model tables and documentation in both English and Chinese, along with improvements to the model selector interface.

8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.text: The Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 release updates the Freebuff version label to 0.2.4 in the release packaging files and binary distribution configuration, keeping the published Freebuff package aligned with the current build number. This update includes a new internal catalog helper and model catalog utilities that support how the Freebuff model picker and catalog store are structured, plus session-related type changes in the shared core code. The CLI also adds new authentication token storage utilities and updates the index and auth modules accordingly. For users, this primarily means the released Freebuff package and its version identifier are updated to 0.2.4, with the underlying changes remaining internal to the codebase.

055e9c3cd792ca332c6838f1f47c12415c638f54.text: The Freebuff CLI now greets you with a new landing screen when you start it up, giving you a clear place to begin before you start working on code. The way you sign in has also been reorganized, updating how authentication works so your login stays active across uses. If you open the CLI, you will see the new landing screen right away. If you sign in, you will use the updated login flow the next time you start a session.

2b4fd7db6a35ecfa22bbfdcdcce6913119b55120.title: SDK add model reuses endpoint and key with independent limits
2b4fd7db6a35ecfa22bbfdcdcce6913119b55120.summary: A new addModel method on the ByokConnectionStore type lets a saved BYOK connection spawn a sibling model entry that reuses the same provider endpoint and credential with its own independent limits and lifetime. The create logic was extracted into a standalone function so addModel can call it under the metadata lock, and an environment-backed source credential is preserved as a reference rather than copied as a key value. A failed model save rolls back its copied key while keeping the source connection usable.
2b4fd7db6a35ecfa22bbfdcdcce6913119b55120.evidence: The diff to sdk/src/byok.ts adds a new addModel method to the ByokConnectionStore type and refactors create into a standalone function; the addModel implementation calls exclusive() and create(), copying the source connection's provider, baseUrl, and credentialRef or apiKey only when the source is not environment-backed. New tests assert that adding models reuses the endpoint and key with independent limits and lifetimes, preserves an environment reference, and cleans up a copied key on a failed save.
2b4fd7db6a35ecfa22bbfdcdcce6913119b55120.unknowns: The diff does not show the CLI or web surface that calls addModel or how a user triggers a sibling model from a saved connection. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

985c872eb8d43f538ab77d933ef7c43125d100ff.text: Freebuff CLI version 0.2.3 ships a reworked keyboard input system for the chat interface, making typing and navigating conversations feel more responsive and predictable. The chat keyboard handling now supports richer key bindings across the chat input, key interception logic, and keyboard action processing, so slash commands like /ask, /undo, /diff, and /byok respond more reliably when you type them. Users will notice that pressing keys while composing or editing messages in the terminal behaves more consistently, with fewer dropped or misrouted keystrokes, especially when using shortcuts that previously conflicted with the input field. These changes only affect the terminal-based chat experience, so users who primarily interact through the web or desktop apps will see no difference from this release.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff 0.2.2 brings improvements to using your own AI model key and managing your free-tier sessions. The BYOK (bring your own key) feature works more consistently across the command-line tool, the agent runner, and your saved settings, making it easier to switch between your personal AI provider and Freebuff's free models. Free-tier users get better tracking of their daily allowance and reset timing, with clearer banners showing when sessions end or when premium access is full. The model picker refreshes correctly after premium access resets, and the landing screen and session-ended notices stay up to date. Only users who bring their own AI keys or rely on the free daily allowance are affected by these changes.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.1 ships an improved advertising system that sends a detailed snapshot of your terminal setup to Freebuff when you start a session or when an ad is shown to you. That snapshot includes things like your terminal size, whether the window was resized, and whether you are connected over SSH, and it is passed along with how many keys you typed so far. Freebuff attaches this info to both ad requests and run records, which lets it check that ad views and paid compute time really came from a real person rather than an automated script, and it uses the same terminal details to bill advertisers accurately. The release also corrects a collection of shared error messages used across Freebuff when something goes wrong. You do not change anything in how you write or run code, but your ad-funded Freebuff sessions now carry the extra terminal context that helps prevent misuse, and the corrected error messages make problems easier to read.

e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.0 caps AI reasoning effort at high for several models after measuring that pushing to xhigh bought only about 8 percent more reasoning for roughly 26 percent more wait time. The Muse Spark default reasoning effort drops from xhigh to high, and GPT-6.1 Sol, Muse Spark Contributor variants, and Gemini 3.8 Flash now clamp reasoning to high so every turn stays within that ceiling. GPT-6 Luna also drops the max setting from its ladder while keeping its xhigh ceiling, matching the same September 29 product decision. Behind the scenes the freebucks utility got a larger refresh that affects how pay-as-you-go compute credits are handled. The onboarding experience gets a small shared update across the codebase. The net effect is that users choosing these models will see consistently high reasoning without occasional xhigh slowdowns, and credits behavior updates for anyone running models past the free allowance.

e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.text: This release adds a safety net that stops the assistant from saving files when its writing is cut off mid-sentence. When the assistant starts rewriting a file but the text gets unexpectedly cut off before finishing, the system now detects that interruption and refuses to write the incomplete version, so you don't end up with a broken or partial file saved to disk. If the assistant tries to overwrite a longer existing file with a much shorter version that leaves code brackets unclosed, that attempt is also blocked. These refusals are recorded internally in the service logs so they can be tracked. The goal is to keep your files from being silently corrupted when the assistant's output is interrupted unexpectedly.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.1 ships with two user-visible improvements. First, the CLI now reports a compact snapshot of your terminal environment (including its dimensions, whether you are on SSH, and the terminal type) in a structured string, and it attaches that snapshot plus per-prompt input counts to both ad requests and run metadata. This lets ad networks and the Freebuff service distinguish real users from automated traffic and apply consistent, environment-aware billing and bot filtering. Second, the shared set of user-facing error constants was extended and adjusted in a backwards-compatible way, giving the CLI clearer internal signals to surface meaningful errors to you. The release also bumps the packaging version label on the Freebuff CLI line. The main day-to-day effect is that ad and session requests now carry your terminal environment consistently, which improves bot filtering and ensures billing context follows your actual setup.

70a78466da2239b118a3891b0ccced51e1ac07bc.title: CLI chat scroll no longer swallows wheel input at bottom
70a78466da2239b118a3891b0ccced51e1ac07bc.summary: useChatScrollbox in cli/src/hooks/use-scroll-management.ts now routes every `scrollbox.scrollTop` write through a `setScrollTop` helper that sets `programmaticScrollRef` only for the duration of the assignment. The scroll-change handler no longer flips `autoScrollEnabledRef` to true on programmatic scroll, so OpenTUI's synchronous but no-op-quiet scroll events no longer clear the bottom guard and swallow the user's next wheel event. `animateScrollTo` also accepts the literal `'latest'` instead of a precomputed maxScroll and recomputes the moving bottom per frame.

New tests in cli/src/hooks/__tests__/use-scroll-management.test.tsx assert "chat scroll following", "PageUp stays in history across streaming updates, then PageDown resumes following", "a no-op auto-scroll does not swallow the next mouse scroll", "scroll to latest reaches a moving bottom and follows subsequent output", and "mouse input interrupts a scroll-to-latest animation".

70a78466da2239b118a3891b0ccced51e1ac07bc.text: The chat window no longer gets confused about when you're trying to scroll versus when the assistant is scrolling for you. If you use the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK and you scroll with your mouse wheel while the chat is pinned to the bottom, your next wheel scroll now moves the view instead of being ignored. This is a bug fix you can use today with no action needed on your part.

f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.10 adds annual billing and subscription revenue tracking. You can now choose a yearly billing plan for your subscription, and the system calculates monthly recurring revenue (MRR) consistently by treating a yearly plan as one-twelfth of its annual price. The release also updates the /byok command so you can pick low, medium, or high reasoning effort for bring-your-own-key runs, with the choice remembered in your settings and translated correctly across different AI providers. Additionally, GPT-6.1 Sol has been added to the free model picker as a temporary promotional option that is free in the US but requires a paid plan elsewhere, and a new subscription tier ranking and upgrade path helps guide plan selections.

afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.9 adds OpenAI's new GPT-6.1 Sol model to the free model picker, letting users run that flagship model at no charge in the US with a one-session-per-day cap, while users outside the US can access it through paid Freebucks plans. The GPT-6.1 Sol model is wired into the CLI and Desktop agent allowlists as both a base orchestrator and a code reviewer, so coding tasks can use it for planning and review. The release also tracks when someone who clicks a Freebuff ad comes back to use the assistant, recording how long they were away based on their next submitted prompt. Promotional copy and pricing notes now clearly state that GPT-6.1 Sol is free in the US, paid elsewhere, and capped at one session a day for every account, so the catalog and price notices agree.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.8 adds a new advertising slot for launch-focused partners. When you type words about launching, deploying, or demo-ing your work (like "deploy", "ship", "launch", "demo"), a partner ad row now appears above your input, alongside the existing pull-request ad row. The streak bonus that rewards daily use now correctly shows up in your daily Freebucks allowance instead of your wallet, fixing reports that it was missing for users east of the Pacific. Ad copy from partners is now sanitized to prevent terminal escape-sequence issues, and the release download path is locked down to trusted Freebuff/Codebuff origins over HTTPS. The version is bumped to 0.1.8 with a bugs URL added to the package metadata for easier issue reporting.

2b4fd7db6a35ecfa22bbfdcdcce6913119b55120.text: A developer who already saved their own provider key can now add a second model to the assistant's menu that uses that same saved key and endpoint, but with its own separate token limits and its own lifetime. Adding that second model does not touch the first one: if the new one fails to save, the tool automatically cleans up only the new key it tried to make, leaving the existing setup untouched, so you can keep using the model you already have.

9986cb57a5ea50e771b02b1fe7f6bc3cfbeed1fd.text: Freebuff added a set of internal tracking names and event labels for its X (formerly Twitter) advertiser acquisition campaign. This change is for the engineering team that runs Freebuff advertising, not for people using the coding assistant. The code that reads these names is not yet active, so nothing visibly changes for you today.

The row carries a promotional field sourced from the new `GPT_61_SOL_PROMOTIONAL` constant in `common/src/constants/freebuff-sol-promo.ts`, which the CLI model selector renders as a warning detail. New agent roots `base2-free-gpt-6-1-sol`, `base3-free-gpt-6-1-sol` and `code-reviewer-gpt-6-1-sol` are registered in `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`, and the READMEs add the model row while rewording the Muse Spark 1.3 fallback copy.

055e9c3cd792ca332c6838f1f47c12415c638f54.text: This release (Freebuff CLI 0.2.5) adds a way to tell users apart when they hit a usage cap for a different reason: instead of just saying 'try again later,' the assistant can now explain that account identity verification is required. It also makes the credentials file on your computer more private by tightening its permission settings so only you can read it, and it stops repeating the same login error message over and over when something goes wrong when loading your account.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.1 adds a compact terminal-environment description to its session and ad requests, and reports per-prompt input counts (typed characters, paste events, how fast you type) in its run metadata. When you start Freebuff, the CLI now probes its own ancestor processes in the background and records whether your terminal answered the startup color query, so the descriptor fills in "launcher detected" and "terminal answered color" flags on its own. The CLI ships a fresh Freebuff-specific error message for when OpenAI's provider refuses a request as a possible cybersecurity risk, telling you to try a different model instead of retrying the same one. The same terminal-environment descriptor is attached to ad auction requests, ad click recordings, and impression acknowledgements, so ad targeting and bot-filtering use one consistent view of your client. The chat composer now counts each typed character, multi-character key event, and bracketed paste, seals those counts when you submit, and attaches them to the run that prompt starts. Freebuff builds only ship the environment header on requests, so Codebuff users are unaffected by the new headers. The main effect for Freebuff users is that session and ad requests now carry a short, fixed-format summary of your terminal (size, kind of shell or editor that launched it, whether it answered the color query) and your run metadata includes how you composed that prompt, while a newly worded error message guides you to switch models when OpenAI's content filter blocks a request as a cybersecurity risk. Note: the available release evidence is incomplete on whether the new error message is actually surfaced to you in the UI or only defined for the server to match against.

The CLI also fetches landing-screen ads only when the banner can be drawn, at 18 terminal rows or more; sponsored-command checks now refuse unreadable command forms. Three other distinct changes in this release window update model configuration, revise credential-redaction depth handling, and refine sponsored Git-command checks.

The CLI changes sanitize terminal command and tool output before display, gate landing-screen ad fetching on the 18-row banner threshold, and `common/src/ads/sponsored-command-refusals.ts` refuses unverifiable sponsored commands, including commands nested beyond the parser's depth limit.

dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.summary: The diff hardens SSRF protections in the SDK's URL-fetch tooling. It adds a default fetch transport for the read_url tool that is constructed from the host-lookup and blocking policy (with comments stating it re-validates at connect time against the addresses it actually connects to), extends the address-blocking policy with extra non-globally-routable ranges that ipaddr.js classifies as 'unicast', and extracts DNS resolution plus policy enforcement into a new exported resolveAllowedAddresses helper that throws an SsrfError if any resolved address is blocked. In sdk/src/tools/ssrf.ts it adds an AddressPolicy type, exports defaultLookup and unwrapHost, and extends isBlockedAddress with EXTRA_BLOCKED_RANGES covering IPv4-compatible IPv6 (::/96), benchmarking (198.18.0.0/15), site-local IPv6 (fec0::/10) and local-use NAT64 (64:ff9b:1::/48). assertUrlAllowed gains an isBlocked option and now delegates hostname checks to resolveAllowedAddresses, with updated docs noting the pre-flight check alone does not pin the address a later connection uses. In the read_url fetch loop, assertUrlAllowed is called with the isBlocked policy at every redirect hop, and the redirect response's body is cancelled so its connection is released before following the redirect.

a4846ebf48b5d8bbe08744fb2d6f26f119d19861.text: You can now type /todo (or /todos) in the terminal to open a live, scrollable checklist panel that shows the main assistant agent's current task list, with completion counts and the ability to scroll through long lists. 7f957e9d65768a7b5bfd994df8d7eac8891bbfb2.text: Solar Pro 4, a stronger model from Upstage, is now available to pick in Freebuff again after being brought back today alongside its cheaper sibling, Solar Mini 4. dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.text: This release (0.2.9 of Freebuff) hardens how the tool reads web pages safely and tightens when ads appear on the landing screen. The URL-reading tool now checks every network address it connects to twice: once before connecting and again when the connection is actually made, so a malicious website cannot fool it by returning one safe address during the check and a private, internal address when the connection is opened. It also now blocks a broader set of non-public addresses (IPv4-compatible IPv6, benchmarking ranges, and a few other reserved ranges) and re-checks each address after a redirect, so a public link cannot redirect to an internal one. Sponsored task commands that run on your own machine got stricter too: the command-checker now refuses any command it cannot fully read, including deeply nested wrappers (more than six levels), PowerShell script files, and encoded commands that cannot be decoded, replacing them with a 'too deeply nested to check' marker rather than leaving anything unread. On the landing screen, ads are now always enabled but will not be fetched or rotated when the terminal is too small to show the ad banner (below 18 rows), which prevents serving ads that nobody can see. The published SDK package also no longer ships source maps, which previously contained the full source code of every bundled module.

03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.text: Freebuff 0.2.11 is a behind-the-scenes maintenance release that bumps the CLI version number and adds a safety check for MCP tools with required arguments. The release evidence is incomplete for broad user-facing capabilities: there is no confirmed new AI model, new shortcut, or new CLI command. The only concrete change documented is a fix for a crash or failure when a model tries to call an MCP tool that needs arguments; the update ensures the tool gets the right input it needs, which prevents the model from seeing empty inputs and calling tools incorrectly. Because the second listed change was rejected by a check, no other behavior is confirmed to have shipped. For most users this version only advances the CLI version; if you rely on MCP tools that require parameters, this build applies the parameter handling fix; otherwise there is no everyday change worth noticing.

d71a831b3a7a5b66a7a100a47a69c2c6bcc70d82.text: Freebuff 0.2.8 hardens terminal safety by sanitizing commands and tool output before display: escape sequences that could rewrite your clipboard, change your window title, or inject hidden characters are now stripped, so what appears in your terminal matches what actually ran. The shared sanitizer also collapses bare carriage returns (progress-bar redraws) the way a real terminal would, keeping diagrams and code samples aligned. These protections apply across the command display, the preview that renders as a tool runs, and every tool's captured output (files read, URLs fetched, etc.) before it reaches your screen. No new models, shortcuts, or pricing changes ship in this release. The release evidence is otherwise limited to packaging and agent-definition edits that do not change user-visible behavior, so those are not described here.

d39b73d5da6478aaa896070eedb17835d6d9c282.title: SDK locates Windows git.exe alongside bash for missing Git installs
d39b73d5da6478aaa896070eedb17835d6d9c282.summary: The SDK's `windows-bash.ts` module adds `windowsGitCandidates(env)` and `findWindowsGit(env, registryRoot?)` which search the same Git for Windows roots as bash plus GitHub Desktop's bundled `git.exe` before falling back to the registry, so a Windows machine with Git outside PATH is no longer reported as missing git. The candidates reuse `gitRoots(env)` and append GitHub Desktop app directories, sorted newest first, and `findWindowsGit` mirrors `findWindowsBash` by consulting the filesystem first and the registry only for this machine's own env

c5c0acc93f8fec48e0f7f78c536c4ed6dea74a2c.text: This Freebuff release 0.2.7 clarifies streak reset timing and keeps AI tasks running when they were about to stop mid-way. Streak clock times now say '(your time)' so you know when your next daily bonus lands in your own clock instead of guessing it meant server time (it never appears for a Pacific-midnight reset). When an agent stops with a 'Continue' card while its to-do list is still part done, it now gets nudged to keep working instead of handing you a stopped task - capped at three nudges per turn and left alone when the model finishes or explicitly ends the turn. A server-only model list that isn't in your local picker no longer breaks image inputs: image support is now read from that server row so text-only models get a description rather than a rejected request. In narrow terminals, the '(your time)' label is dropped before the whole streak status line disappears, so you still see when your next bonus lands.

44c800d2617286631654dfd4d3c7b2b0e8e4d6b4.text: This release of Freebuff CLI (0.2.6) updates the AI models shown in the model picker and adjusts how locked or paid-only rows display their plan or budget state. The default model for new users is now MiMo 2.6 Flash instead of GLM 5.3 Flash, and DeepSeek V4 Pro was removed from the catalog, replaced by GLM 5.3 Flash as the deep-reasoning pick. Locked rows that require a paid plan now consistently show a lock label and open the plans page when selected, and the picker shows the server's per-account verdict on which rows are locked rather than guessing. A new device signing step attaches an install-specific signature and catalog fetch id to session and completions requests when a model catalog is held, and unopened scheduled rows are filtered out before display. The Freebucks meter now keeps a model switch's first-tab discount reservation through the quote used for the replacement purchase, and the SDK gained a per-request header hook so hosts can sign backend completions.

8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 is a minor release that mainly refreshes the Freebuff client version and brings a few behind-the-scenes additions. The release bumps the Freebuff package version to 0.2.4 from 0.2.3, which is a packaging change that doesn't add new user features on its own. It also includes updated agent definitions and a new authentication token helper, along with expanded type definitions for Freebuff sessions to support new country-verification and pricing signals. The available release evidence does not establish any new end-user behavior, safety enhancement, or product capability beyond the version bump, so users would not notice any visible difference after installing this release.

985c872eb8d43f538ab77d933ef7c43125d100ff.text: Freebuff CLI release 0.2.3 refines how the up and down arrow keys move through your recent chat messages. When you press an arrow to cycle through past prompts, the typed content you have not edited still lets the arrows jump between those recalled messages, instead of just moving the cursor within the current line. The keyboard handler now passes an extra flag marking whether the current draft is a recalled history entry that you have not changed, and the input interceptor uses that flag to decide whether arrows should page through history or move the text cursor. Escape also now closes a new sponsor detail panel, and a new Ctrl+O shortcut instead of the display ad. The change keeps Escape's existing behaviors intact and only claims Escape to close the panel while it is open. For everyday users this means arrow-based history navigation behaves consistently when recalling a previous message, and a new Escape-to-close panel becomes available when the sponsor dock is open.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff 0.2.2 changes how your own-provider keys (BYOK) behave when they fail and makes the streaming from compatible providers more resilient. When you connect your own AI provider key, validation now names the exact environment variable that is missing or wrong, trims stray whitespace, and rejects keys that contain line breaks, so a mis-pasted key is reported instead of silently breaking a run. When a model is marked as used up for the day, the app now stops and tells you when it will be available again instead of quietly moving you to a different model. Streaming chat from OpenAI-compatible providers no longer drops the whole response when a server omits the tool-call position index, and a paste that accidentally split a URL across two lines is now rejoined instead of saving a broken endpoint. A couple of test and session-type bookkeeping updates keep the supporting machinery consistent, but the user-facing impact is in the BYOK and daily-limit handling above.

e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.0 caps reasoning effort at high for several AI models, including Muse Spark, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Gemini 3.8 Flash, based on a product decision after measuring that the highest reasoning level added only a small amount of extra thinking while significantly increasing response time. The Muse Spark default reasoning effort setting drops from the highest level to high, and the reasoning effort ladders for affected models are adjusted to stop at high instead of going higher, with the Gemini model also pinning every request to high so no other effort level can take effect. One onboarding flow change was also included in shared configuration, and one other intended change was dropped from the release because its summary was discredited, so users should rely on the source evidence for any details not described here.

e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.text: This release adds a safety feature that catches file-saving attempts which are cut off mid-generation, so an incomplete write is refused instead of overwriting a file with truncated content. When the AI's output is cut short in the middle of a tool call (for example, arguments that stop mid-word or mid-sentence), the system now detects the cut-off shape, tells the user that nothing was written, and suggests making smaller edits rather than re-sending the oversized call. For direct file writes, it blocks a write that would replace an existing file of 30 or more lines with a much shorter copy that leaves brackets unclosed where the original file had them all closed. Both refusals record a content-free telemetry event (sizes, tool and model names only, never paths or file content) to the service's log store. The net effect is that users are protected from accidentally saving a half-finished version of their file when the AI's response is truncated. Tests assert that the bracket-matching and size-ratio checks behave as described, but the evidence does not include proof of a deployed capability beyond those checks.

f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.text: This release lets you control how much reasoning a BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) run does, and it cleans up how billing intervals and monthly prices are calculated for Freebuff subscriptions. With the new /byok effort command, you can pick low, medium, or high reasoning effort for your own-provider runs, and that choice is saved in your settings and applied at the start of each run. The request is automatically translated into the right field for each provider (OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible), and if a provider refuses that field with an error, the run retries once without it instead of failing. For subscriptions, a stored billing interval is now normalized so anything not marked yearly is treated as monthly, and monthly recurring revenue (MRR) is computed per subscription by reading the list price for the tier and dividing a yearly plan by twelve. A new per-subscription MRR pricing export and an admin view of paying subscribers split by billing cadence accompany these changes. The Freebuff CLI package itself is now versioned 0.1.10.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.text: Freebuff 0.1.8 adds a second sponsor row above your coding input. The row shows an advertiser's message only while you are typing about shipping, deploying, demoing, or announcing what you built. If you are writing about a pull request or code review instead, the row shows the pull-request advertiser. The two rows swap instantly as you type, and a paused campaign stops showing within 30 minutes. The release also fixes how your daily streak bonus is shown. The streak bonus now adds to your daily Freebucks allowance instead of your wallet credit, and the terminal now says when today's bonus landed and when it will expire. On the ad-measurement side, the service now tracks an extra "invoiced CPM" value for ads billed outside the product so delivery reports can include it. One outdated notice about a tier change was removed from the landing screen, and the version number advanced from 0.1.7 to 0.1.8.

afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.9 adds GPT-6.1 Sol to the free model picker and caps it at one session per day for every account, with promotional copy making its pricing clearer in the model selector. The release introduces a post-click return label (COD-694) that measures whether a user who clicks a Freebuff ad comes back to the assistant, using the next submitted prompt as the return signal on the CLI since a terminal cannot detect focus changes. A shared UTM-tagging system now adds default campaign tags to links in sponsored tasks so advertiser visits from the assistant are properly attributed, without altering links that already carry UTM parameters or appear in code. House ad targeting was refined to withhold only campaigns measured on subscription-started conversions while still serving other house campaigns like Discord join to subscribers. The README and Chinese translation now document GPT-6.1 Sol as free in the US or paid elsewhere with the daily session limit clearly stated alongside the existing model catalog.

38cd1ed44428f573c4754d8e0cee868f2875b54e.text: This release of Freebuff (version 0.0.204) improves how the app handles crashes and unexpected exits. When Freebuff crashes, it now saves a local report and sends it to the team on your next launch, so they can investigate recurring problems. If your terminal closes or the process is killed while you have an active Freebuff session, your session is now kept alive so it can resume on your next launch instead of being ended and lost. It also fixes a bug that could cause the chat interface to freeze when showing inline ads, and isolates certain internal errors so a UI problem during a chat no longer kills your entire session.

dbc6a776fc0f8005806d797c00fe2c6caf1781c6.text: This release fixes a misleading error message that could confuse paying Codebuff users when they run out of credits. Previously, if a paid user exhausted their Codebuff account balance, the system mistakenly treated their out-of-credits message as a Freebuff provider problem and told lite-mode users it was "on us, not your account". The fix routes Codebuff's own out-of-credits alerts to the standard balance-refill flow instead of mislabeling them as service-wide issues. One change: paying users now correctly see a message pointing them to add credits, rather than being told the fault belongs to the provider. The available release evidence covers only this single bug fix, so this summary is limited to what that change establishes.

f783139ae5607e7b53e6dd5608186d133930d7bd.text: This release adds two new advertising placements to the Freebuff interface and fixes a session-management issue in the CLI. Advertisers can now buy single-advertiser 'partner' slots that appear directly in the app's UI (such as within the skill picker or above the composer bar), as a new 'partner' ad format. The session fix ensures the CLI correctly resumes an already-paid-for session hour when restarting after an unexpected stop, instead of accidentally buying a duplicate session. These changes improve how ads appear in the free assistant and how users return to their work without losing progress or paying twice.

baffcb89339ea373a63aa77202bec34e76f80444.text: This update tightens control over sponsored free runs, widens access to two previously plan-only models, and clarifies how your data is used. Sponsored tasks now start their run-clock when work actually begins instead of when you click Accept, and the CLI refuses commands that could touch your Linux environment, wipe databases, or alter your containers before any shell runs. GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro move to full access at full tier, with the picker updated to reflect that change. Tests on the SDK side now default the first-party CPM leg to off so older tests don't break, and README and policy text are synced to the narrower data-use scope that restricts evaluation to connected GitHub repos. Put plainly: sponsored runs are more predictable and safer, GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro are now available without a paid plan, and ad-related testing defaults match production without overriding it.

a23f0ae16d9c7d69458dce20ca74178bc530ffb8.text: This release improves how long conversations are shortened and rewritten when you edit or resume them. The message-trimming tool now counts only your own prompts instead of also counting internal system notes such as Stop messages or earlier summaries, and it can set the cutoff point starting from the end of the history when the host reports how many user prompts existed, so editing a recent message no longer removes most of the conversation. Separately, the summarization step that compresses old history now replaces large base64 images and other binary data with a short placeholder instead of feeding all those characters to the model, which previously caused repeated, slow summarization attempts on image-heavy threads.
