7f957e9d65768a7b5bfd994df8d7eac8891bbfb2.title: Solar Pro 4 returns to the free model picker
7f957e9d65768a7b5bfd994df8d7eac8891bbfb2.summary: Solar Pro 4 is back in the free model picker beside Solar Mini 4: `SOLAR_PRO_4_MODEL` is added to `FREEBUFF_MODELS` and to `LIMITED_FREEBUFF_MODEL_IDS`, the latter gated on `FREEBUFF_SOLAR_PRO_4_ENTITLEMENT.limitedAccess`. Its `tagline` now reads from `SOLAR_PRO_4_OFFER` instead of `SOLAR_REGULAR_OFFER`, and `premium` is read from `FREEBUFF_SOLAR_PRO_4_ENTITLEMENT.fullAccess.premium` rather than hardcoded `false`. The `supersededBy` pointer to Solar Mini 4 is removed, which would otherwise rewrite saved Pro 4 picks onto Mini 4 on every load. Both READMEs add the Solar Pro 4 row and list it among the unmetered and limited-access models.
7f957e9d65768a7b5bfd994df8d7eac8891bbfb2.evidence: In `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, `SOLAR_PRO_4_MODEL` is added to the `FREEBUFF_MODELS` array and to `LIMITED_FREEBUFF_MODEL_IDS` (gated on `FREEBUFF_SOLAR_PRO_4_ENTITLEMENT.limitedAccess`), its `tagline` switches from `SOLAR_REGULAR_OFFER` to `SOLAR_PRO_4_OFFER`, and its `supersededBy` block pointing at `FREEBUFF_SOLAR_MINI_4_MODEL_ID` is deleted.
7f957e9d65768a7b5bfd994df8d7eac8891bbfb2.unknowns: The diff does not show the body of the `common/src/constants/freebuff-solar-promo.ts` hunk or what changed in `freebuff/cli/release/README.md`, whose hunk contains only context lines.

changes.what: Solar Pro 4 is added back to `FREEBUFF_MODELS` and to `LIMITED_FREEBUFF_MODEL_IDS` behind `FREEBUFF_SOLAR_PRO_4_ENTITLEMENT.limitedAccess`, with its `supersededBy` pointer to Solar Mini 4 removed and `premium` now sourced from the entitlement.
`SOLAR_PRO_4_OFFER` is exported and replaces `SOLAR_REGULAR_OFFER` as the source of the Solar Pro 4 tagline.
The English and Chinese README model tables add the Solar Pro 4 row and include it in the unmetered and limited-access model lists.
The CLI release README is also modified, though the shown hunk contains only context lines.

verifyClaims.claim: No explicit verification coverage for: docs
No explicit verification coverage for: README.zh-CN.md

7f957e9d65768a7b5bfd994df8d7eac8891bbfb2.text: Solar Pro 4 is back as a free model choice in Freebuff, sitting right next to Solar Mini 4 in the list you pick from. If you use Freebuff's CLI, web app, desktop app, or SDK and you're on the free tier, you'll see Solar Pro 4 again as a selectable model. In everyday use, Freebuff users in supported regions now have access to both Solar Pro 4 and Solar Mini 4 at no cost, and the system will no longer automatically swap any saved preference from Solar Pro 4 back to Solar Mini 4 on startup.

9f521ec5f2e38db447cafa0549633d728a284921.text: This release brings Solar Pro 4 back to Freebuff's free model list, so you can pick Upstage's stronger flagship text model at no charge (it is unmetered at full access, like the other models that cost no session). It also adds a standing 10-Freebucks offer tied to Solar Pro 4, visible in the promo constants and the README catalog. Additionally, when a paid task runs alongside a free conversation or an ad is requested, the system can attach a pair of opaque IDs that point at the conversation's trace and its last finished run, so the service can later tell which prompt an ad or offer followed; interrupted runs are no longer skipped when advancing that pointer, and a finished-but-not-adopted run is advanced past correctly. Finally, a crash-recovery path for free sessions now records a per-process live file for your hour of access and resumes an unused, unexpired hour if the previous CLI process died, so closing a terminal or a crash no longer forces you to buy a second hour for the same session.

3dd05d3b673ee4d6db441f3ff75480154b3d4a1f.text: Freebuff version 0.0.198 changes how sponsored (advertiser-funded) coding tasks are run in the CLI. Instead of creating a separate git branch and working copy, a sponsored task now edits the files in your current folder directly, and you can undo it with a single command (/ads:undo) that reverses the changes, matching what the desktop app already does. The task runs as normal chat content in your existing conversation (with a fresh short-term memory), so queued messages wait until it finishes and you are told when it is done; the conversation also gets a brief note explaining what changed. The consent screen was simplified to show the advertiser name plus two plain-English questions, and the offer now comes through a dedicated per-turn request so a matching task appears immediately rather than after up to a minute. This only affects users who accept a sponsored task; a sponsored task that edits your real folder is recoverable by undo, and the run no one is watching no longer asks questions and decides on its own.

5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.text: Freebuff CLI v0.0.197 is a maintenance release focused on stabilizing updates, sessions, and history browsing for the free AI coding assistant CLI. Updates: when you close the CLI it now finishes the session cleanly instead of interrupting an in-progress chat to install an update (so an active conversation is never replaced mid-turn); the embedded search tool now installs through a temp file and swap so a failed write never leaves a half-installed binary behind. Sessions: Freebuff now remembers an active paid session and reconnects you to the same model and session when the app relaunches, instead of dropping you back to the model picker; the takeover prompt (when a second CLI tries to start) offers a 'Choose model' option to back out without exiting. UI: a new 'H' keyboard shortcut and a History button open your saved chats, and ended sessions now show a read-only view of the transcript with a feedback prompt hidden for messages when there's no active live chat. Pricing: the first-tab discount for a live session now correctly reads the same Desktop purchase store that the session owner is billed against, so the price you see matches your account. One change was excluded from the summaries, so its behavior is not confirmed by this release evidence.

3b7ce89c8102761014eafbe97cced66d9a22ec88.title: GPT-6.1 Sol added to the free model picker and agent registry
3b7ce89c8102761014eafbe97cced66d9a22ec88.summary: GPT-6.1 Sol enters the Freebuff free model picker as a US-or-paid-plan exclusive with OpenAI flex capacity upstream ordering ('openai/flex','openai'), a $2.50/$12.50 per-million token ceiling, medium default reasoning effort, and a promotional flag pointing the picker at the GPT_61_SOL_PROMOTIONAL notice. The model is wired into the agent registry at common/src/constants/free-agents.ts across the base2 root, base3 CLI root, reviewer, desktop session set, desktop concurrency set, web/base3 CLI agent id maps, reviewer map, and free-mode agent map tables, plus the subscription premium list in common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts. A new promotional block in cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx renders the short notice in the picker, and GPT-6.1 Sol is added to the chat window map in agents/base-chat.ts alongside a Muse Spark 1.3 fallback notice rewrite.
3b7ce89c8102761014eafbe97cced66d9a22ec88.evidence: Added new model row GPT-6.1 Sol to the picker in README.md and README.zh-CN.md; defined constants FREEBUFF_GPT_61_SOL_MODEL_ID, FREEBUFF_GPT_61_SOL_REASONING_EFFORT, FREEBUFF_GPT_61_SOL_MAX_PRICE, GPT_61_SOL_PROMOTIONAL, and gating lists FREEBUFF_US_OR_PAID_MODEL_IDS / FREEBUFF_PRO_ONLY_EVERY_SURFACE_MODEL_IDS / FREEBUFF_PLAN_METERED_CATALOG_MODEL_IDS in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts; wired the model to agents agents/base2/base2-free-gpt-6-1-sol.ts, agents/base3-free-gpt-6-1-sol.ts, agents/reviewer/code-reviewer-gpt-6-1-sol.ts; added a promotional block in freebuff-model-selector.tsx and a new file common/src/constants/freebuff-sol-promo.ts.
3b7ce89c8102761014eafbe97cced66d9a22ec88.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer that enforces the US-or-paid gating at runtime, or a committed rollout date for the GPT_61_SOL_PROMOTIONAL temporary price.

changes.what: Added GPT-6.1 Sol model row and constants, promotional notice, US-or-paid gating lists, and registered it across desktop sessions, desktop concurrency limits, web/base3 CLI agent id maps, reviewer map, and free-mode agent map tables.
Added base2 root, base3 CLI root, base3 reviewer, and chat window context entry for GPT-6.1 Sol.
Added a promotional notice block to the model selector and rewrote the Muse Spark 1.3 fallback notice text.
Documented GPT-6.1 Sol in the free model picker table.

3f2d082375aabc8445a2cf61d9a107d8c895e905.text: Freebuff updated the tracking codes it uses to measure which of its text ads bring new advertisers onto the platform, swapping in a fresh set of identifiers for the start of the signup flow and four follow-up steps. This only affects Freebuff's internal advertising analytics, not the coding assistant itself. If you are not an advertiser, you do not see or control anything here, and your coding sessions are unchanged.

6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.text: This Freebuff release updates the Chat thinker helper to use a newer AI model (GPT-6 Luna replacing GPT-5.6 Luna, with the 5.6 line now paused and redirected to a fallback), and adds the wiring for a new in-place sponsored-run mode where an advertiser-funded setup task edits your working folder directly instead of creating a branch and commit. It also introduces a dedicated per-turn endpoint (/api/v1/ads/agentic/offer) that decides whether to show a sponsored agentic card, gated by a single server flag so the old display path stops asking once a client supports the new route. The launchpad installer now keeps your paid hour when it replaces the running Freebuff binary to apply an update, so you don't get dropped back on the model picker after a restart. Error handling now recognizes DeepSeek's content-filter refusals and tells you to switch models rather than retry the same blocked request. None of these are framed as performance improvements in the evidence; they are capability and cutover changes, and in-place execution is available only to builds that declare support for it.

23f705370e838f58a16497340c19da2b6b351270.text: When several AI models end up with the same discounted price of zero Freebucks, the model list now orders them by their original (pre-discount) price instead of just their name, so a model normally priced at 2 Freebucks no longer appears above one normally priced at 15 Freebucks. This new ordering rule is shared across the CLI, web, and desktop versions of Freebuff so they stay consistent. The change is live today for anyone using Freebuff to pick which AI model to run when a first-tab discount applies.

70a78466da2239b118a3891b0ccced51e1ac07bc.text: The chat window no longer gets confused about when you're trying to scroll versus when the assistant is scrolling for you. If you use the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK and you scroll with your mouse wheel while the chat is pinned to the bottom, your next wheel scroll now moves the view instead of being ignored. This is a bug fix you can use today with no action needed on your part.

d6e5a5e06f05beba7018af9e345b704058ef54ae.text: The Freebuff team added the plumbing so the assistant can later choose which of Freebuff's own ads to show using an in-house AI model, instead of always picking from a fixed rotation. The system is built and ready, but the switch that activates it is turned off by default, so no one is being routed through the new model yet and nothing about your experience changes today. When an operator later flips that switch on, the model will run on a sticky, per-user sample (default 0% today), and any ad it cannot serve will still fall back to the regular ad path. This is internal infrastructure work for whoever operates the Freebuff service, not something you configure or notice as a user right now.

2b4fd7db6a35ecfa22bbfdcdcce6913119b55120.text: A developer who already saved their own provider key can now add a second model to the assistant's menu that uses that same saved key and endpoint, but with its own separate token limits and its own lifetime. Adding that second model does not touch the first one: if the new one fails to save, the tool automatically cleans up only the new key it tried to make, leaving the existing setup untouched, so you can keep using the model you already have.

a8c632ee26b9700e7304d1e830fd4157ce3653ce.text: The Freebuff landing screen now always attempts to load and display ads, using a setting that bypasses the usual requirement for a prior user message, since the landing screen has no conversation yet. The server tries its main ad provider first and falls back to alternatives if needed. This change applies to Freebuff users who see the landing screen on compact terminals, ensuring ads appear even on shorter terminal windows. Ads remain mandatory on the Freebuff free tier regardless of screen size. Additionally, the SDK's URL-reading tool now uses the platform's built-in fetch with per-redirect safety checks instead of a previously custom fetch method that has been removed, keeping the URL-reading path secure and simpler for developers integrating the SDK.

bcb726800e42b55458879a15244d6d2f45e61956.text: When a software update downloads to your computer but the download gets cut off (like when you close the terminal window), it now gets fully installed the next time you open the app. Previously, that update would be lost and would re-download every time you reopened the app. Your computer now checks the downloaded update to make sure nothing changed or got corrupted before installing it, and it also makes sure it doesn't install an older update if you've already gotten a newer one somewhere else. The Freebuff team added a setting so they can track which version of the installer created your app, which helps them improve the update process.

af742b4afe363b3aafc8d7c7da50b4721dc658bb.text: When this assistant fetches a web page, it now checks the site's address twice, right before connecting, so a website can no longer trick it by giving a safe address at check time and a private one (like your home network) at connection time. It also blocks a larger set of non-public addresses, including IPv4-compatible IPv6 and a few more ranges, and re-checks every redirect hop instead of just the first URL. This affects you whenever the assistant uses its URL-reading tool to view a web page; in everyday use you just see it refuse unsafe or tricking URLs instead of silently following them.

9a24ecd20f4d9e277f877907a9d6850d6382e882.text: The sponsored-run command checker now refuses to run any command line it cannot fully read before executing, instead of letting questionable commands through. It rejects command chains nested more than six layers deep, PowerShell commands delivered as encoded blobs that fail to decode, and PowerShell script files (-File) whose contents are not visible on the command line. When a credential value is hidden inside a data structure nested more than thirty-two levels deep, the redaction step replaces that unreadable subtree with a clear placeholder rather than leaving it exposed. The change is live today and applies to anyone accepting a sponsored task that runs commands on their own machine; no setup is required.

cc9b5daf7055fd8c3a1095bfdbfc788014a7708d.text: The retirement of the Kimi K3 AI model from subscription plans means that paid subscribers can no longer use this specific AI assistant model. This change affects only users who have a paid subscription plan, as the model was removed because its provider shut down and it was never available in the free model selection list (the 'picker'). Subscribers will no longer see or be able to select Kimi K3 as an option when choosing which AI model to use, which prevents confusion where a model might be listed in a plan but not actually accessible. If you are a paid subscriber, you simply won’t find Kimi K3 in your list of available AI models anymore.

10c969706881170ce54df95709887b58e32ed911.text: When you open Freebuff in a very short terminal window (below 18 rows tall), the landing screen no longer shows an ad banner there. The tool only fetches an ad for that banner spot when the window is tall enough to actually display it, so it doesn’t pay for or record impressions on an invisible ad. This only matters to Freebuff’s own free users, since paying Codebuff users never see ads anyway. Nothing else about how you use Freebuff changes.

a56263b791609357ec8bb7d3e2be4bbc9ed6a20a.text: When you ask the assistant to run a command in your terminal, its output is now cleaned up before it is shown to you: any hidden terminal commands that could have copied text to your clipboard, opened links, or redrawn parts of the screen are removed, so you only see the plain, readable result. This applies to every command the assistant runs for you, including live commands while they are still running and the history you can scroll back through afterward. If a command draws a progress bar that jumps around the line, the assistant now shows only the final line, just like a normal terminal would. You do not need to do anything to get this protection; it starts working the moment you update.

0f1fc2d8fa542f76735645866e2d510c7cd66ca6.text: MiMo 2.6 Flash is now the model that starts automatically whenever you open Freebuff, on the terminal, in the web app and on the desktop app, replacing GLM 5.3 Flash. If you already picked a different model, Freebuff keeps your choice, so you will not be switched unless you accept it. Everyone can now see MiMo 2.6 Flash in the model list, and the paid-only models that a plan unlocks are now shown even to people without a plan, grayed out with a link to buy one, so the upgrade path is visible instead of hidden. This is live today, so the next Freebuff session you start will run on MiMo 2.6 Flash unless you pick something else first.

9986cb57a5ea50e771b02b1fe7f6bc3cfbeed1fd.text: Freebuff added a set of internal tracking names and event labels for its X (formerly Twitter) advertiser acquisition campaign. This change is for the engineering team that runs Freebuff advertising, not for people using the coding assistant. The code that reads these names is not yet active, so nothing visibly changes for you today.

924ba8e19e1464297fe1eb0284cee5b0f16148cd.text: When a Freebuff user hits a spending limit that requires identity verification, the landing screen now shows an 'ID verification required' message with a link instead of the usual 'resets at midnight' daily budget text. This affects Freebuff CLI users who are blocked from starting a new session because the system needs to confirm their identity before allowing further use. You will see a clear ID-check notice with a link to verify, rather than a countdown to a budget reset, so you know the next step is verification rather than waiting.

643c65bbab6758b2f881d400a86551962aa73c67.text: The account session types now carry two new optional signals: one explaining whether re-checking your country would actually change your access (and why it would not, if that is the case), and, when country re-verification cannot help and you are in a limited region, an optional paid-plan offer built from the service's plan catalog with its headline, daily Freebucks, current versus plan daily Freebucks, the list of higher plans cheapest first, and a plans page link tagged for attribution. This affects only the Freebuff engineering team, who maintain these shared session types; no user-facing behavior changes until a client and server read and render these fields, so today you notice nothing different.

e32b322ebdcb417c7acb704627f1b9b9bc2017c9.text: The Freebuff catalog now drops any model rows that are scheduled to open in the future, so they can't be picked or used until they actually become available on a later refresh. Requests tied to the catalog now also carry a tracking id and a cryptographic signature proving they came from your specific app install, so the server can trust them. This affects anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK with the server-driven catalog enabled. You won't see anything different directly, but future-dated models will correctly wait to appear and your picks will be more securely tied to your install.

925bc3fc61b0927e0189685d5d1f0dfb0fee38c8.text: When you pull up a past message you already sent and then press Up or Down again, the arrow keys now keep walking through your message history instead of jumping the text cursor to the start or end of that message. Developers who type and edit their own new message still get the normal cursor movement behavior. This ships in the Freebuff CLI today, so the next time you recall an earlier prompt and press Up again, it shows you the prompt before that one, and so on, until you either start editing the recalled text or move the cursor yourself.

a080b0350b619eac9376a20495be7f15326080d1.text: A new spend provider named 'vercel' has been added to the list of allowed providers, allowing billing routed through Vercel AI Gateway to be recognized alongside existing providers. This is an internal configuration change for the billing side of the service. If you pay for Freebucks or use metered Freebuff sessions, you will not see any new prompts or options, but the system can now correctly attribute spend that flows through Vercel. No action is needed from you.

66f02773b360e100a133eccdb5e26ef42173913b.text: When you run out of your daily free sessions for a specific AI model you picked (for example GPT-6.1 Sol), Freebuff no longer quietly switches you to a different model and keeps going. Instead, your session stops right there, and you see a message telling you when that model becomes available again. You then get to choose to wait or pick another model yourself. This only applies to runs that hit the daily model limit, and it is live today.

8a89a68610cb8088579974edb1a01c2e6e9f6032.text: If you already have a custom provider connection set up and decide to change the base URL (for example, to fix a missing path segment), the update command now requires you to explicitly state which environment variable holds your provider key before the change goes through, and the tool confirms the URL is actually different before asking. Users updating an OpenAI-compatible endpoint to a new base URL must now provide a valid environment-variable name so the key can be sent to the new location; changing only the trailing slash or keeping the same endpoint no longer triggers that prompt, and a malformed variable name is rejected.

a65a05b3511a4ba7bf8d838348796a1a58d45705.text: The session response now includes a country verification flag indicating whether the server has confirmed the request comes from an allowed country. This is information for the Freebuff engineering team as part of shared type definitions, not a change to your experience. Because no code reads this flag yet, it is in place but does nothing for you today. Your daily use is unchanged.

28d82f9a80eb3c590275d1072338856d577e7742.text: The Freebuff CLI now tells you more when your own AI provider connection (BYOK) is checked, reporting the endpoint's HTTP status and pointing out when the model you selected isn't in the provider's published model list, showing which models are available instead. This affects only developers who add their own API key and provider URL through the /byok command, not users on the default Freebuff plan. You'll see clearer warnings right when adding or validating a connection, so a misconfigured local proxy or wrong endpoint is spotted before your first coding run instead of mid-conversation. The change is live today in the CLI and SDK validation paths.

a50d7e783cb6733fe7ac14503afb30f4c49748ba.text: The BYOK command now correctly handles pasted text that contains line breaks in the middle of words, such as URLs or model names, by joining those broken parts back together when it is clearly the right thing to do. Users of the Freebuff CLI who paste a /byok add or /byok update command that wrapped mid-word will no longer have half the URL silently dropped or get confusing extra-words errors. Instead, the command recognizes the split and either fixes it automatically or shows a clear message listing exactly what is missing or unexpected, so pasted commands work as intended.

9aede7717867ad17a5aeac24cb14ecddb12d1d68.text: When the assistant asks a model to make a tool call, the model streams the answer back in small pieces, and each piece is supposed to carry a number (an index) telling the assistant which call it belongs to. Some model providers and routing services that speak an OpenAI-style format forget to include that number, which used to make the assistant drop the whole tool call, so the task stopped mid-sentence with something like 'Writing the file.' and then nothing happened. Now, when that number is missing, the assistant figures out the right call by looking at any ID or function name attached to the piece, falling back to continuing the call it was already working on.

6fbd1ad3e5ea867246171a0c6d90aebdc63fa504.text: When you connect your own AI provider key (BYOK) and something goes wrong, the assistant now tells you exactly what the problem is in plain language. If the key is missing or invalid, it names the specific environment variable that's set wrong, instead of giving a vague error. The assistant also strips out stray whitespace from your key so harmless formatting in a config file does not cause failures. This only affects you if you use the /byok command to run your own model; regular Freebuff sessions are unchanged.

b63254fdc6b1967224a0eaea03df93dd75c5724b.text: Freebuff's engineering team is adding more detail to a compact status report that the CLI sends to Freebuff's servers so it can understand what kind of machine and network setup is asking for help. The report now indicates whether the user manually forced a different time zone, which kind of proxy (if any) is being used, whether secure certificate checking was turned off, and whether an extra certificate was added, plus the computer's built-in time zone only when it was overridden. This is internal plumbing that lets Freebuff diagnose problems like misconfigured networks or clocks without collecting private URLs or full configuration details, and it requires no action or change from Freebuff users today.

039c90769849244284480ca92f0b350f7aa0a71b.text: The assistant used to show your remaining free usage based on whichever pool of usage limits happened to come first from the server, which sometimes meant the count and the 'resets when' timer were pulled from two different limits. Now both the counter and the countdown look at the single shared usage pool that matches your premium model, so the numbers you see agree with each other. This corrects moments where a usage count or reset time appeared to come from a different allowance than the one that actually governs your premium model. If you use the Freebuff assistant on the free tier and see a usage counter on the landing screen or the session-ended banner, the figure and its reset timer now describe the same pool instead of potentially mismatched ones.

fc37ac10e299ace4c9055da809823202303a75c8.text: The assistant now treats a caller’s deadline (like a timeout you set) as a cancellation, not as an error or as the service's own five-minute idle limit. Developers using the Freebuff CLI, web or desktop app, or the programmable SDK get a clearer 'cancelled by you' message instead of a misleading 'no response for five minutes' when their own timeout fires. No action is required from users; the way you interact with the assistant stays the same, only the wording when a timeout cancels your request is more accurate today.

592b3211840b26f528305bfbea7954cdbc5ead5b.text: The assistant now keeps its discounted price reservation active in more situations, so if you are running multiple coding sessions at once in the terminal, switching or closing one session no longer cancels the price you locked in. This matters to people who use the terminal version and buy coding time with credits. In everyday use, when a session ends the system now checks whether it belongs to a multi-session terminal purchase and holds onto that reservation instead of releasing it immediately, while older single-session behavior is unchanged.

5d525143041ab63d8faf7aec68b3ef6eb11be287.text: Freebuff, the company that runs the assistant, decided to turn down the deepest thinking level on a few of its strongest paid AI models, including GPT-6.1 Sol and Gemini 3.8 Flash. This affects you only if you pay for those specific premium models: your requests now use a little less reasoning depth instead of the maximum. You will not see a speed change either way, since the difference was only about eight percent more thinking for twenty-six percent more wait time, and the company judged that trade-off was not worth it. Nothing else in your experience changes.

b6925d1398492646733a7269207331d414e7a2b9.text: The Freebuff CLI now attaches a small, non-sensitive summary of your terminal and how you typed your last prompt to both ad requests and each run it starts, so the service can tell real developer sessions apart from bot traffic and bill accordingly. This affects users of the Freebuff CLI and web/desktop sessions, not Codebuff's paid product. You will not see it anywhere in day-to-day use; the only effect is that ad requests and run metadata now carry this terminal-plus-typing summary as a compact header and a metadata field, and the one-time probe at startup quietly fills in a few fields in the background without delaying launch.

e3d7701e9223662ede68d501c3bdc686168d36cb.text: The assistant now refuses to save a file when a generated edit looks like it was cut off before finishing, instead of trying to apply it and leaving a broken file behind. This affects anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web app, desktop app, or SDK to edit code with the AI. In daily use, you will see a clear message explaining that the write was not applied when the AI's response runs out of room or drops mid-edit, rather than finding an incomplete or truncated file on disk.

41c03830a5fb0af4241a56663cfadfa6cfa24a56.text: A new command in Freebuff's own-provider mode (when you connect your own AI account) now lets you choose how much deep thinking the assistant does on each task, picking from three effort levels. When you pick a level, Freebuff asks your provider for that amount of reasoning in a way your specific provider understands, and if that provider rejects the request, Freebuff automatically retries without the extra-thinking request so your work still goes through. This affects anyone running Freebuff with their own API key on OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, or OpenAI-compatible services, and you experience it as a new option to demand more or less step-by-step analysis before the assistant answers, with no action required for existing setups to keep working.

fa7f6a239db7ed3d74758432e00ac1acdbc847f4.text: Sponsored-run procedures in the Freebuff monorepo now attach default UTM tags to links that send a developer to an advertiser's own site, while leaving the advertiser's existing UTM tags and code-block links untouched. It affects advertisers and sponsors who buy placements or run sponsored campaigns on the Freebuff platform. If you click a tagged link during a sponsored run, the advertiser's analytics can now plainly see it came from Freebuff, so untagged visits from sponsored runs should drop off. No action is needed from you; this is a backstage fix so Freebuff gets proper credit for the traffic it sends, and it only applies to advertisers' own domains.

155c66375523b6e95e5af4ec6ff6f3ef71057bf7.text: The description shown next to the GPT-6.1 Sol model in the Freebuff model list now tells you it is free to use in the United States, and that everyone else, including people with paid plans, must have a paid plan to use it at all. This only affects the wording you see in the Freebuff assistant on the web, on the desktop, and in the app. If you are in the US you can try the model without a paid plan, though you are still limited to one session per day; if you are outside the US the row now clearly says a paid plan is required before you can pick it.

d71a831b3a7a5b66a7a100a47a69c2c6bcc70d82.text: This Freebuff release hardens how terminal commands and their output are shown to you in the CLI. Previously, commands typed by the AI and the text they produced could carry hidden terminal escape sequences (like OSC 52 clipboard-copy codes or cursor moves) that could behave unexpectedly when rendered. Now, every command you see from the assistant and every captured output result is put through a sanitizer that strips these escape sequences first, so what is drawn to your screen is plain text. The release also tightens ad-request consistency by routing both the display auction and the impression pixel through the same shared user-agent logic, so ads are targeted and counted with one agreed client identity instead of two that could disagree. The Muse Spark model agent roots are clarified in their own docs, and one omitted change (for which the summary was discredited) is left out of this rollup. Net effect for users: terminal tool calls no longer render raw escape sequences that could hijack your clipboard or redraw your screen, and ad impressions are recorded against the same client identity the auction was aimed at. The release evidence does not establish new model access, pricing, speed, or reliability changes beyond the terminal-text sanitization and the ad user-agent alignment.

9f521ec5f2e38db447cafa0549633d728a284921.text: Solar Pro 4 is back in the Freebuff model picker, offered at a standing price of 10 Freebucks alongside Solar Mini 4. The release also adds crash recovery for Freebuff sessions so a CLI that crashes or closes mid-session no longer forces you to buy a second hour, resuming instead from where the dead process left off. Sponsored offer and ad requests now carry a pointer to the last finished run in your conversation instead of conversation text, letting ads be linked back to the prompt that triggered them without sharing the prompt itself. The ad trace pointer is also advanced past interrupted runs so it does not name an unfinished run that was never actually adopted.

d39b73d5da6478aaa896070eedb17835d6d9c282.text: The assistant now knows to look in more places on Windows for the Git program, including the special folder used by GitHub Desktop, when Git is not already listed in the system's program path. You do not need to do anything different. If you had previously seen a message that Git was missing even though you had installed it, the program will no longer report it as missing and will be able to start normally.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: This release sharpens up the parts of Freebuff that keep you running when you bring your own AI provider key (the /byok system), fix confusing error messages, handle flaky provider responses more gracefully, and add one extra environment detail to the diagnostic info Freebuff reports about your terminal. The most useful change is that BYOK error messages now name the exact environment variable (like OPENROUTER_API_KEY) that's missing or rejected, so you can actually see what to fix instead of a vague 'credentials failed' note - and the CLI's /byok update command now lets you point an existing connection at a new endpoint and tell it which key variable to use, instead of forcing you to delete and re-add the whole connection. The release also fixes streaming hiccups where tool calls could drop entirely if a provider's reply left out an index number, and Freebuff now correctly detects that problem and keeps the tool call stitched together. On the desktop side, the client environment descriptor now also reports your system timezone and proxy settings, which helps Freebuff's operator dashboards understand where Freebuff is running without exposing your private network details. If a model has hit its daily session cap, the CLI now stops you cleanly with a message saying when it'll open again, rather than silently switching you to a different model you didn't ask for. Some changes touched core session types and test docs, but the release evidence is incomplete on their user-visible behavior.

bb46c52bc16e41ff79cb08aa459448643ab95ddb.text: When you see an ad in the Freebuff assistant, the request that gets sent now labels who actually wrote each message: it can tell which lines you typed yourself apart from the ones the assistant generated on its own (like error summaries or step-by-step notes). This is internal wiring behind the ad display, so it changes nothing about how the assistant feels to you and you do not need to do anything. Freebuff's team made this change today so they can serve more relevant, correctly targeted ads.

73c6ceb590d8d56df307de723563cd09d01e2ea0.text: After clicking a Freebuff ad, the CLI now watches for a follow-up signal that you came back to the assistant. For terminal users, that signal is simply your next typed prompt (a second ad click also counts), and the time between the click and your first new prompt is recorded as how long you were away. This is an internal ad-quality label that helps decide which ads are worth running; it does not change any session, allowance, or quota you see.

1654e2212f8267b7b9bebccea8ec5a4992d638d8.text: The Freebuff engineering team added a safety lock on the new Meta model (Muse Spark 1.3) so that when it is reached through OpenRouter, traffic can only go to Meta's own endpoint and cannot be silently rerouted to a cheaper or different host. A price ceiling is recorded so that if anyone tries to repackage or resell the model at a different rate, the request is refused instead of billed. The change is internal configuration that the routing code does not yet read, so it has no user-visible effect today, and nothing is announced to end users or advertisers.

28ccadc6687c271cf00e473547c11ed8a096c363.text: The assistant added a clear daily limit of one session per account for the GPT-6.1 Sol model, both in the internal rules and in the written model descriptions so they match. This affects anyone who can use GPT-6.1 Sol, including people on paid plans. If you use that model, you will now see plainly that you get only one session with it each day, and a second attempt will be stopped, so you will not be surprised by a refusal.

0fce93281ac8d26b2e7a391bbcd5c36cffa5ade0.text: When the assistant tells you when a busy pricing period starts or ends, it now checks the time zone the browser or computer reports instead of trusting it blindly, and falls back to UTC (the same zone everywhere) if the device's clock setting is missing or unreadable. This fixes the model-availability and pricing labels you see in the web assistant, desktop app, CLI, and SDK, so they show a readable time and zone instead of crashing the page. You do not need to do anything; the labels now stay on screen on devices whose clock zone the browser cannot name (for example some game-console and Chrome browsers).

bb4c8ba7c39a35a6514781f05ae534d40f2db56f.text: If you keep a daily streak going, the bonus it earns no longer sits in your Freebucks wallet, it lifts your free daily allowance instead and vanishes when that day's pool resets. Who it affects: Freebuff users on the Freebucks pay-as-you-go meter (free and paid plans), especially those outside Pacific time. Everyday impact: If you used to see streak bonuses pile up in your balance and stay there, they now add to just today's allowance and disappear at your local daily reset, so your balance won't grow from streaks anymore. The screen also tells you both when today's bonus expires and when tomorrow's will arrive, so a streak bonus no longer looks 'missing' on days your allowance refills before the Pacific reset. Nothing to do yourself: it's already live, and no action is needed.

ac87c9098fc871744393073cd90171bdf837608a.text: The web-searching helper that the assistant sends off to research a topic now has a fixed budget of 15 steps, after which it is forced to stop and deliver its final answer instead of searching indefinitely. This prevents a single question from triggering hundreds or thousands of search-and-read cycles in one session. Anyone who asks the assistant to research something on the web may notice that very large or open-ended research tasks now end sooner with a complete, though shorter, summary rather than running until the assistant itself decides to stop.

0fd74f6d3862b0a725b49dee8334356c26c1a7e5.text: The per-referrer cap that limited how many web referrals a single person could bring in has been removed from the referral program's shared configuration, and the documentation now explicitly states there is no cap on how many referrals are recorded or counted for anyone. This affects the company's internal referral-program configuration used by the system that decides who gets credit for sending new sign-ups. In daily use, nothing changes for you: there was no limit on how many referred friends could earn you rewards, and there still isn't one.

5083cff73efa88122e17fdab135b5ce4db0280e0.text: The internal test scripts that automatically start a Freebuff session and wait for it to wake up now also recognize the chat-first ready screen, so a brand-new install or a freshly started session is detected as booted even before the old ASCII art banner appears. This is internal test-suite plumbing, so it does not change anything you see in the Freebuff terminal or desktop app today; automated end-to-end checks just become less flaky. No action is required from you.

58699f0e07179ec3da47ddc01f58272ff7c6f565.text: The wording of the Freebuff subscription ads has been rewritten so that they now describe extra usage in hours per day rather than extra sessions per day, and the ads now mention the name of the paid plan tier alongside the combined daily allowance of free and paid usage. These ads appear to Freebuff users as occasional prompts to upgrade, so you may see this refreshed copy instead of the previous sessions-focused messages. Because these are just text strings shown in ad slots, there is no change to how Freebuff works day-to-day or any impact on your account usage limits.

2abe8724f6320e633a07d1cb04090f2c0fd58a41.text: The CLI now detects when your draft message mentions a pull request, code review, or merging, and shows a small branded ad row from a sponsor next to those features in two places: just above the input box while you're typing, and as a row under the /review command in the slash menu. It affects only Freebuff sessions where ads are enabled (that is, free users, not paying subscribers or people using their own API keys), and only when a specific sponsor deal is active for that session. In daily use, you may see a single colored line with the sponsor's title, destination, and an "Ad" label appear above the input while you type something about a pull request, or below the /review menu item, and it refreshes no more than once every thirty minutes.

c684005190fe848d10946a348b40f9b79b671282.text: When your free session runs out and the assistant offers to keep going on its backup model, the name shown on screen now says 'DeepSeek V4.1 Flash' instead of the previous 'DeepSeek V4 Flash'. Anyone who hits that end-of-session screen in the Freebuff terminal app is the only audience affected. You will see the corrected model name on the message that appears after your session ends; no other behavior changes.

24636b016b85a8983dd35c208e1cd569e6eb2fca.text: When you edit or shorten a saved conversation, Freebuff now trims the right amount of the assistant's memory instead of cutting too much and deleting parts of your chat it should keep. It also no longer sends large screenshots or base64-encoded images to the summarization step, which previously made it extremely slow or caused it to hang and never finish summarizing your conversation. This affects anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web version, desktop app, or SDK to review or edit the history of a conversation, including when they edit an earlier message or when the assistant tries to condense a long conversation to save room.

cb1dc4f15b6aec59f80dfac74c06d1427e76ec4e.text: When the CLI crashes with a fatal error, it now writes a small crash report to disk and, on the next launch, sends that report to analytics (as 'cli.fatal_crash') so developers can see what went wrong instead of relying on screenshots. The crash report only includes basic details (error name, a short message, and the top few stack lines), is deleted once shipped or ignored if it is more than a week old, and is always opt-in to the user's crash recovery (it can keep a paid-for hour if one was active). In daily use you won't notice anything new unless a crash happens, and even then the report is best-effort and won't stop or slow down your next launch.

06bf5c3390a40a61f96676cd94fdedbb04552956.text: When a paying user of the assistant runs out of their own Codebuff credits, the message they now get explains their personal balance ran out and points them to add more credits, instead of wrongly telling them the failure was caused by a shortage in the assistant's own provider accounts. This correction applies to paying customers using the CLI in its lighter mode, and most users will only notice if they actually hit an out-of-credits situation, where the guidance is now accurate instead of misleading.

9e3fdf7603a276e2559d229d347fcaa976740d7a.text: Freebuff has added a new kind of ad slot, called a partner slot, that belongs to one advertiser. These slots are not available for ordinary self-service advertisers to buy from the console; an operator places a campaign on them by agreement. Freebuff also now labels these partner slots based on where they appear in the app, so reports show a meaningful name like 'Desktop - Skill picker' instead of a raw id. The first-party ad rail now serves these partner slots separately from regular sponsor breaks, and the daily spend limits and creative rules for breaks no longer accidentally apply to them. This is live in the shared ad-placement configuration today and affects how advertisers and the people who buy ad space on their behalf see and use these slots.

e27f00b1a1bc6baa8deb5600bf98fd70d627d1d1.text: When you copy something on Linux and it only gets placed into your terminal's clipboard through a fallback method (instead of a proper clipboard tool being installed), the message now tells you that the copy may not have actually worked and suggests installing wl-clipboard or xclip as a fix. This only happens for you if you are running on Linux and your copy relied on this terminal-only fallback, so users on macOS, Windows, or remote sessions are not affected. If everything works normally with your system's clipboard tool, nothing about the message you see changes.

a78f5290258b53013a16fefea0715f6d74f445f0.text: Your free assistant hour now automatically resumes when the app updates between the old single-session version and the new multi-session version. If an old app crashed and left you an unused free computing hour, the new app detects it on startup and continues that same hour without making you pay for a new one or pick a model again. This only affects free users on the CLI, web, or desktop app; the moment you end a session, switch models, or pick a different option, the app returns to the normal model-selection screen.

38cd1ed44428f573c4754d8e0cee868f2875b54e.text: Freebuff 0.0.204 improves reliability when the coding assistant crashes or gets interrupted, and fixes an issue that could freeze the chat during fast responses. The CLI now remembers your paid session hour if it crashes or gets killed, so the next launch resumes right where you left off instead of ending your session and making you start over. Inline ads are now handled with a single steady placeholder when hidden, which stops a React loop that could freeze the chat during rapid streaming. Crashes are now saved to a local file on shutdown and reported when the app restarts, so the team can see real crash details instead of just a terminal error. External signals like closing the terminal window or the launcher disappearing now keep your active session alive to be resumed, rather than ending it as if you had chosen to quit. A safety wrapper around the chat UI updates ensures a single failed UI update no longer kills your whole coding run and session.

38cd1ed44428f573c4754d8e0cee868f2875b54e.title: Freebuff 0.0.204 releases with fatal crash reporting
38cd1ed44428f573c4754d8e0cee868f2875b54e.summary: Freebuff 0.0.204 is published (cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-identity.ts, freebuff/cli/release/package.json) and consolidates the CLI claim-prefix as FREEBUFF_CLI_CLAIM_PREFIX in common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts. The release also ships synchronous fatal-crash capture (fatal-crash-report.ts, tracked as cli.fatal_crash), keeps an active Freebuff hour across external exits and launch update restarts (renderer-cleanup.ts, freebuff-session-store.ts), and isolates SDK event-handler throws from killing the run (sdk-event-handlers.ts). The inline-response-ads store notification that triggered 'Maximum update depth exceeded' is now gated on a frozen NO_RESPONSE_ADS singleton (use-gravity-ad.ts).
38cd1ed44428f573c4754d8e0cee868f2875b54e.evidence: freebuff/cli/release/package.json bumps version from 0.0.203 to 0.0.204 (snapshot commit 38cd1ed4). cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-identity.ts now imports FREEBUFF_CLI_CLAIM_PREFIX from @codebuff/common/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions and assigns it to CLI_MULTI_SESSION_PREFIX. common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts defines FREEBUFF_CLI_CLAIM_PREFIX = 'cli:' and adds isFreebuffCliClaim, plus release notes mention a fatal crash reporting flow, session-resume slot keeping, ad slot identity fix, and SDK event handler isolation.
38cd1ed44428f573c4754d8e0cee868f2875b54e.unknowns: The diff omits the full set of files in the release window, so the rollup of every functional change between 0.0.203 and 0.0.204 is not fully visible here. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Version bumped to 0.0.204 in the release manifest.
FREEBUFF_CLI_CLAIM_PREFIX ('cli:') is defined and isFreebuffCliClaim added; CLI_MULTI_SESSION_PREFIX now references it.
A fatal crash is persisted locally and shipped as cli.fatal_crash by the next launch.
External exits and launcher update restarts keep the active Freebuff hour for the next launch to resume.
SDK event handlers are wrapped so a UI state update cannot throw into the run.
Hidden inline ads return a frozen NO_RESPONSE_ADS singleton to stop redundant store writes.

9f521ec5f2e38db447cafa0549633d728a284921.title: Freebuff CLI 0.0.199 release bump with trace context, crash recovery
9f521ec5f2e38db447cafa0549633d728a284921.summary: The Freebuff CLI release package is bumped from 0.0.198 to 0.0.199. This window adds a shared trace-context module that attaches an `AdTraceContext` of ids to agentic-offer and ad display requests, a crash-recovery path in `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-relaunch.ts` that writes a PID-named live record under `getConfigDir()` and resumes an unexpired hour a dead local process left behind, and a new `RunOptions.traceSessionId` option on the public SDK `run()` so a host can name a conversation's trace before its first run returns.
9f521ec5f2e38db447cafa0549633d728a284921.evidence: The commit `9f521ec5` bumps the Freebuff CLI release package version from 0.0.198 to 0.0.199 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, coinciding with the release window whose analysis notes enumerate four shipping changes: trace-session and last-run id attachment on agentic-offer requests and ad display requests, a crash-recovery path that writes a PID-named live record under `getConfigDir()` and resumes an unexpired hour left by a dead local process, an explicit `adTraceContext` field advanced past unfinished runs, and a new `run()` option `traceSessionId`.
9f521ec5f2e38db447cafa0549633d728a284921.unknowns: The rollout order of the trace-context, crash-recovery, and trace-session pieces across the client and server, and whether the new constants read from any operator config visible in this diff. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

7e523f09d13937ced4f365dc7a5cf162cd2f5320.text: Freebuff tightened an earlier privacy promise: it used to say that outside reviewers could also evaluate code they label as AI-training-eligible, and now it says those reviewers may only evaluate code that is already connected to a GitHub repository inside your Freebuff project. This change only adjusts the public wording and dates in the policy and README docs, so it does not alter anything the assistant actually does for you today. If you ever connect a GitHub repository (for example through Freebuff Cloud) and a model is labeled as allowed to train on data, then that connected repository is the only code those reviewers can look at, rather than any other code you might send them.

7de825ebc35aa3637e3b6a6c6ffd99111adc6950.text: Advertised coding tasks that run on your own computer can now ask you to connect a specific third-party account, and only that account's credential is passed into the isolated task environment. This lands today for developers who run sponsored (advertiser-funded) tasks through the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK. You will see a masked prompt asking for the requested credential before such a task starts, with an option to skip, and the assistant still reads the variable name but never its value, so your own matching environment variable is scrubbed and replaced only by the one you provide for that single run.

22929c3492e000b3e7f0e7f91ddefebdd911e1c2.text: When you accept an advertiser-sponsored task in the Freebuff CLI, the assistant can now no longer run commands that break out of your project to touch the rest of your computer. Specifically, it refuses to launch into Windows Subsystem for Linux, run destructive database commands like drop, reset, or wipe, or control containers and images that might affect your own running services. You don't need to do anything differently, but if an advertiser's procedure tries one of these commands, the assistant stops and reports the refusal instead of carrying it out.

03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.11 released with deferred update adoption
03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.2.11 was published by bumping the version literal in freebuff/cli/release/package.json. The launcher now writes a staged.json manifest for deferred updates and adopts orphaned staging directories on next launch via adoptOrphanedStagedUpdates(), so a terminal-closed session no longer re-downloads the same release each time; installStagedBinary gained a keepStagingOnFailure option that preserves staging dirs on Windows file-lock failures, and the exit handler calls it with that flag set. Launch telemetry in cli/src/index.tsx now records launcherVersion from the CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_VERSION env var, which cli/release-core/launcher.js sets on spawned children to distinguish installs that can handle deferred updates.
03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.evidence: freebuff/cli/release/package.json: version field bumped from 0.2.10 to 0.2.11; cli/release-core/launcher.js: new adoptOrphanedStagedUpdates() walk reads staged.json manifests in config dir, renames orphaned staging dirs, verifies sha256 of staged files before installStagedBinary, and calls installStagedBinary with keepStagingOnFailure:true from the exit handler; cli/src/index.tsx: APP_LAUNCHED telemetry now emits launcherVersion from CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_VERSION, which cli/release-core/launcher.js sets as CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_VERSION on spawned children
03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.unknowns: The exact user-visible rollout of the new launch telemetry field is not specified in the source hunks. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.9 adds a new AI model, GPT-6.1 Sol, to the free model picker, available in the US for free and elsewhere only on paid plans, capped at one session per day per account. The release also improves how Freebuff measures ad clicks by tracking whether users return to the assistant after clicking a Freebuff ad, using the user's next submitted prompt in the terminal as the return signal, with a 30-minute watch window. Additionally, the GPT-6.1 Sol model now has updated promotional text clarifying its free-in-US and paid-elsewhere status with a daily session limit, and Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 is marked as newly available in the Desktop release.

3b7ce89c8102761014eafbe97cced66d9a22ec88.text: Freebuff added a new AI model called GPT-6.1 Sol to its free model picker and agent registry, making it available to users in the US for free and to paid subscribers elsewhere at a temporary promotional price of 100 Freebucks. If you're a developer using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK in the US, you can now select this model at no charge; if you're outside the US or on a limited tier, it appears locked unless you have a paid plan. The change also updated the model catalog, README documentation, subscription premium lists, and wired the model into the agent orchestration system so it can be used across the platform immediately.

03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.11 changes how the installer handles updates it staged but could not finish applying. When a launcher downloads a new version but the terminal is closed before it can move the new files into place, that staged update is now written to a manifest and left on disk so the very next time the CLI launches it adopts (installs) that already-downloaded update instead of downloading it again. The adoption step verifies the files match the recorded hashes and confirms the target platform before installing, and it skips or cleans up staging directories owned by still-running sessions so two launchers never install the same staged copy twice. If installation fails and the files are locked (for example by antivirus on Windows), the staged update is kept rather than deleted so a later launch can finish the job, and crash diagnostics now strip terminal-escape sequences from captured output before printing it. The release also adds test coverage that pins down how parameterized MCP tools are schema-served and argument-parsed end to end over stdio.

05b8302ce19e998ea16f2f38c400c62c94d974b7.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.10 version bump in release package
05b8302ce19e998ea16f2f38c400c62c94d974b7.summary: The version field in the Freebuff CLI release manifest at freebuff/cli/release/package.json advances from 0.2.9 to 0.2.10, marking publication of the Freebuff CLI 0.2.10 release line. This is a release-bump commit touching only the version literal; the bin, scripts, files, os, cpu, and engines fields remain unchanged.
05b8302ce19e998ea16f2f38c400c62c94d974b7.evidence: The version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json was changed from 0.2.9 to 0.2.10, with the +1/-1 stats matching the single version literal update. No other fields in the package manifest were modified in this release-bump commit, and no source code, launcher, or runtime logic changes are visible in the diff.
05b8302ce19e998ea16f2f38c400c62c94d974b7.unknowns: The specific features or fixes bundled in the 0.2.10 release are not described in this commit, only that the version literal was advanced from 0.2.9 to 0.2.10.

dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.9 with sanitized terminal output and stricter
dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.summary: The Freebuff CLI ships version 0.2.9, published from freebuff/cli/release/package.json, and now runs all model commands and captured tool output through sanitizeTerminalOutput from common/src/util/terminal-safe-text.ts before terminal rendering, closing terminal escape sequences and OSC payloads in command and output text. The landing screen ad hook is always enabled with forceStart so ads are fetched only when the banner can draw, exporting landingScreenDrawsAds and landingAdOptions from cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx and sharing the compact-height logic via shouldHideGravityAds in cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts. The sponsored-command walk now refuses lines it cannot fully read, adding git and unverifiable refusal kinds plus the SPONSORED_CREDENTIAL_TOO_DEEP sentinel for credentials nested past REDACT_MAX_DEPTH=32 in common/src/ads/sponsored-run-credentials.ts. The release also adds 4 other changes across cli, common, and sdk packages.
dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.evidence: Release commit dfec4965 bumps the Freebuff CLI version from 0.2.8 to 0.2.9 in freebuff/cli/release/package.json; the release also ships terminal-output sanitization (sanitizeTerminalOutput now applied to model commands and tool output in cli/src/components/blocks/tool-branch.tsx, cli/src/components/terminal-command-display.tsx, cli/src/components/tools/run-terminal-command.tsx, and cli/src/utils/message-block-helpers.ts), the landing-screen ad hook refactor (exports landingScreenDrawsAds and landingAdOptions from cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx, using enabled: true with forceStart), and the sponsored-command-refusals hardening in common/src/ads/sponsored-command-refusals.ts and common/src/ads/sponsored-local-execution.ts that adds git/unverifiable refusal kinds and deep-credential redaction limits.
dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.unknowns: The 4 omitted release members and their exact functional surface are not shown, so their end-user effect beyond the four changes above is not established.

changes.what: Version bumped from 0.2.9 in the Freebuff CLI release manifest.
Model commands and tool output are sanitized via sanitizeTerminalOutput before drawing in tool-branch.tsx, terminal-command-display.tsx, run-terminal-command.tsx, and message-block-helpers.ts.
The landing screen ad hook is always enabled with forceStart and the banner-height gate is centralized through landingScreenDrawsAds and landingAdOptions.
The command walk now fails closed on unverifiable lines, adding git and unverifiable refusal kinds with TOO_DEEP sentinel and new git option handling.
Nested credential values beyond REDACT_MAX_DEPTH are replaced with SPONSORED_CREDENTIAL_TOO_DEEP instead of being left unread, exported now.
Adds sanitizeTerminalOutput that collapses CRLF and runs sanitizeTerminalText over collapsed lines.

dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.9 tightens safety for sponsored coding tasks and cleans up what gets shown in the terminal. Sponsored runs now refuse commands they cannot fully inspect before running: wrapper chains nested deeper than six levels, PowerShell script files, and encoded commands that fail to decode are all blocked, and git subcommands that move history or configuration are refused when reached through wrappers. Credential redaction now replaces deeply nested arrays or objects with a placeholder instead of leaving them partially unread. The URL-reading tool now validates the address it connects to in the same step as the check, so a name that passes the security check but resolves to a private address later cannot be used to reach internal systems, and more non-routable IP ranges are refused. The terminal now strips escape sequences from commands and tool output before drawing them, so a fetched page or test script can no longer write to the clipboard or rewrite the screen. The landing screen keeps fetching ads as long as its banner can be drawn, and the hook stays enabled there even on compact terminals. Updating gives you these safety and display fixes with no new catalog entries.

05404fdc0ea423339f2f03e5694ba7e1716d0f18.text: The sponsored task run now gets its one-hour compute budget clock when the task actually starts running, instead of counting down from the moment the run was accepted and waiting in the queue. Developers who use the Freebuff terminal to run an advertiser-funded task will see the run keep its full hour to complete work even if it had to wait in line behind another task, but the run still cannot outlive the original grant it was accepted under. If a task starts very late, you get the full hour from that start time; if it starts near the old cutoff, you only get the time left until the grant expires. No action is needed from you, and the task still only costs the advertiser a single acceptance fee regardless of how long it ended up running.

Added nextResetAt to FreebuffUsageStreakSummary and expanded the current/longest field docs to note that the streak counts on the account's own days while the activity map and longest stay on Pacific dates.
Reworded the inline comment on the streak bonus status line to say the streak day is the account's own day since 2026-10-01, so normally midnight, matching the new copy logic.

45917a419db7942c34b29fba5a262d91842edfa7.title: Context pruner run tracking matched by parsed agent name, not
45917a419db7942c34b29fba5a262d91842edfa7.summary: The context-pruner agent's ledger-bypass in loopAgentSteps now matches the parsed agent name ('context-pruner') exactly instead of substring-matching the id, so agents whose id merely contains the string 'context-pruner' keep their real run tracking. This is the only source change in the commit; it is accompanied by a new regression test in packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/loop-agent-steps.test.ts. The switch replaces the prior agentTemplate.id.includes('context-pruner') check and prevents model-calling agents like 'context-pruner-test-agent' from being handed the in-process untracked run id that the web API refuses.
45917a419db7942c34b29fba5a262d91842edfa7.evidence: In packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts (loopAgentSteps), the context-pruner run-tracking skip was changed from agentTemplate.id.includes('context-pruner') to parseAgentId(agentTemplate.id).agentId === 'context-pruner'; the import of parseAgentId from @codebuff/common/util/agent-id-parsing was added alongside a new UNTRACKED_RUN_ID_PREFIX export and test 'skips run tracking for the context-pruner by name, not by substring' in packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/loop-agent-steps.test.ts

changes.what: The context-pruner ledger bypass now matches the parsed agent name exactly instead of substring-matching the agent id, preventing model-calling agents whose id contains 'context-pruner' from receiving the refused in-process run id.
An untracked-run-id prefix constant was exported for the context-pruner bypass path.
A regression test was added asserting that context-pruner and codebuff/context-pruner@1.0.0 skip run tracking as 'untracked-', while context-pruner-test-agent keeps its ledger run id.

fd8544efc05980f125eeb774c42bc4a5bc7c1bd0.title: Billboard ad format and Desktop billboard placements
fd8544efc05980f125eeb774c42bc4a5bc7c1bd0.summary: A new billboard format was added to `PLACEMENT_FORMATS` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts`, along with `isBillboardFormat` and `isFirstPartyOnlyFormat` predicates that treat billboards as first-party CPM-only inventory like partner slots. Two Desktop billboard slots, `Desktop-Billboard-Sidebar` and `Desktop-Billboard-Panel`, were registered in `PLACEMENT_SLOTS` with available: false, keeping them operator-placed until the console can upload artwork. The companion module `common/src/ads/billboard.ts` defines the shape specs, placement IDs, refresh timing, and asset validation rules that describe what artwork a creative must carry to fill each slot.
fd8544efc05980f125eeb774c42bc4a5bc7c1bd0.evidence: New file `common/src/ads/billboard.ts` (141 lines) defines billboard placement IDs, shape specs, refresh/dismiss constants, and asset validation functions. Modified `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts` adds `'billboard'` to `PLACEMENT_FORMATS`, adds `isBillboardFormat` and `isFirstPartyOnlyFormat`, adds two billboard slots (`Desktop-Billboard-Sidebar`, `Desktop-Billboard-Panel`) to `PLACEMENT_SLOTS` with available: false, and adds `BILLBOARD_PLACEMENT_IDS` plus labels.

737f5fdd98e579cadfc0e785f8e13946bf9d97f7.title: Retire MiniMax M3, GLM V52, and Ox Alpha from Freebuff
737f5fdd98e579cadfc0e785f8e13946bf9d97f7.summary: common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts adds FREEBUFF_RETIRED_MODEL_IDS (containing FREEBUFF_MINIMAX_M3_MODEL_ID, FREEBUFF_GLM_V52_MODEL_ID, and FREEBUFF_OX_ALPHA_MODEL_ID) plus isFreebuffRetiredModelId and freebuffRetiredModelMessage so retired models get a clear message instead of an unknown-model error. The README files now list Space Bunny Alpha among the limited-access models everywhere the other Freebuff-served models are enumerated. New tests in common/src/constants/__tests__/freebuff-retired-models.test.ts assert the retired ids, the message text, and that Space Bunny Alpha remains in the limited catalog because admission already allowed it.
737f5fdd98e579cadfc0e785f8e13946bf9d97f7.evidence: common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts adds FREEBUFF_RETIRED_MODEL_IDS, isFreebuffRetiredModelId, and freebuffRetiredModelMessage; the new test file common/src/constants/__tests__/freebuff-retired-models.test.ts imports them and asserts retired ids, the message copy, and limited-tier membership. README.md and README.zh-CN.md add Space Bunny Alpha to the limited-access model lists, and freebuff/cli/release/README.md updates the limited-mode lists to include Space Bunny Alpha.

Adds Space Bunny Alpha to the limited-access model lists in the free-access section.
Adds Space Bunny Alpha to the limited-access model lists in the free-access section.
