f9d8ab812096fdcfcf2e35cee46dff6ce2ce18ee.title: GLM 5.3 Flash deal-ending notice removed after Sep 30 deal closed
f9d8ab812096fdcfcf2e35cee46dff6ce2ce18ee.summary: The `dealEndingSoon` block was deleted from the `GLM_V53_FLASH_MODEL` const in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, clearing the "Deal ends Sep 30 · 15/hr after" warning from the GLM 5.3 Flash picker row. The explanatory comment beside the removed field now states the Sep 30 deal notice came off on 2026-10-01 because the deal ended and the price moved (15, then a temporary 25 peak through the catalog). This is a data-only edit to the model catalog constant with no new reader in the diff.
f9d8ab812096fdcfcf2e35cee46dff6ce2ce18ee.evidence: In common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts, the GLM_V53_FLASH_MODEL const had its `dealEndingSoon` field (a { tooltip, short } object) removed; the adjacent comment now records that the Sep 30 deal notice came off on 2026-10-01 because the deal ended and the price moved to 15/hr with a temporary 25 peak.
f9d8ab812096fdcfcf2e35cee46dff6ce2ce18ee.unknowns: The consumer that previously rendered `dealEndingSoon` on the picker row is not visible in this diff, so the observable UI effect of the removal is not confirmed here.

5a7029d37117e9437e43a5260de124977ec3ee66.title: Remove tagline field from plan upsell offer type
5a7029d37117e9437e43a5260de124977ec3ee66.summary: The plan upsell offer type in common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts drops its optional `tagline` field, leaving only the headline, plans list, and plans URL. The example headline text is also updated from 'Unlock up to 350 Freebucks a day with Freebuff Pro' to 'Get up to 350 Freebucks a day with Pro'.
5a7029d37117e9437e43a5260de124977ec3ee66.evidence: The diff in common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts removes the `tagline` field from the FreebuffPlanUpsell type and changes the example headline comment from 'Unlock up to 350 Freebucks a day with Freebuff Pro' to 'Get up to 350 Freebucks a day with Pro'.
5a7029d37117e9437e43a5260de124977ec3ee66.unknowns: The diff does not show whether any consumer of the type was updated to remove references to the removed `tagline` field.

d9cf8afbfddbd4d46eb4b2af8b606d98b3d6cf1e.text: When a database error is so large that recording every detail would be wasteful and slow down logging, the system now keeps the most important parts and drops the bulky ones. Engineers who investigate problems still get the error type, a trimmed stack trace, and the root cause from Postgres, but the giant SQL statement and its long list of input values are replaced with short summaries. This is internal reliability work for the Freebuff engineering team, and you as a user do not notice it at all.

1e49cb763a73d9381f5724a9f34264c0a7fb95df.text: When you run an agent you downloaded from someone else's public profile, Freebuff now blocks it from automatically connecting to outside tools or running hidden helper programs unless that creator has been explicitly approved to run code on your machine. This affects anyone who runs shared or community-built agents through the Freebuff CLI, desktop app, or web assistant. In daily use, an agent from an unapproved publisher either loads normally (if it only uses prompts and pre-set tools) or stops with a clear message telling the creator's name to add it to a trusted list before anything runs.

c838c9d5a1601b11eefa74984610ab6ab49980e7.text: The streak bonus meter that shows how close you are to your next daily Freebucks reward now uses your own account's reset time instead of always using Pacific time. Freebuff CLI, web, and desktop users on the Freebucks meter will now see times that match their own timezone, like 'midnight' when they're at home, or a labeled clock time if they're working from a different timezone. Days that are more than a day out now also show the weekday so you know exactly when the next reward becomes available.

45917a419db7942c34b29fba5a262d91842edfa7.text: The assistant now correctly identifies which helper programs are meant to be skipped during internal bookkeeping, by checking the program's true name instead of just hunting for a substring. This only matters to the people who build and maintain the assistant's internals, so everyday use is not affected. It prevents a false match from breaking an unrelated program that merely happened to share part of its name.

737f5fdd98e579cadfc0e785f8e13946bf9d97f7.text: Three older AI models are being permanently removed from Freebuff's list of options, and anyone still trying to use them will now see a clear message telling them to update, instead of just getting an error that the model doesn't exist. Who it affects: Freebuff users (on the free tier or in limited regions) who may have been picking these retired models, especially anyone on an older version of the app that still lists them. Everyday impact: You won't see those three models anymore, but Freebuff now explains the change and points you to update your installation, so picking them again just tells you what to do instead of failing silently.

fd8544efc05980f125eeb774c42bc4a5bc7c1bd0.text: Freebuff's ad system now recognizes a new kind of large image ad called a 'billboard' that can appear as a floating card over Desktop's project sidebar and right-hand Ad panel. Two specific billboard slots were registered, but they are marked as unavailable and must be set up manually by Freebuff's operators until the ad-upload tool supports the required artwork. The change defines the exact image sizes, aspect-ratio tolerance, and content rules each billboard needs, plus the timing for how often a new billboard ad loads and how long it stays visible. This prepares the foundation for image ads, but has no visible effect on your coding session or ad experience today.

5a7029d37117e9437e43a5260de124977ec3ee66.text: The promotional message shown to users who have hit their free-tier limit lost a short descriptive line, leaving only the main headline and plan list. The main text was also reworded from 'Unlock up to 350 Freebucks a day with Freebuff Pro' to 'Get up to 350 Freebucks a day with Pro'. This only affects the Freebuff engineering team, since it edits a shared internal data shape that both the app and server read. You will not notice any change in daily use beyond the slightly shorter heading, and no action is required on your part.

f9d8ab812096fdcfcf2e35cee46dff6ce2ce18ee.text: A temporary discount badge that read 'Deal ends Sep 30' was removed from the GLM 5.3 Flash option in the model list, because that discount period closed on September 30 and the regular price took effect on October 1. It affects only the internal catalog that Freebuff's engineering team maintains, not any live pricing logic. Freebuff users will not notice anything change beyond the disappearance of the now-expired 'deal ends' label.

d71a831b3a7a5b66a7a100a47a69c2c6bcc70d82.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.8 release: terminal sanitization and ad code trimmed
d71a831b3a7a5b66a7a100a47a69c2c6bcc70d82.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.2.8 is released as a version bump in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` from 0.2.7 to 0.2.8, bundling several changes across the CLI, common, agents, and SDK packages. The CLI now routes captured terminal command output and tool results through `sanitizeTerminalOutput` from `@codebuff/common/util/terminal-safe-text` in `tool-branch.tsx`, `terminal-command-display.tsx`, `run-terminal-command.tsx`, and `message-block-helpers.ts`, stripping OSC sequences and collapsing carriage-return progress redraws. The release also drops several ad- and cost-tracking modules from `common/` (sponsored conformance, verification, Supabase experiment, CF worker signals, spend providers, disposable-email, db-health-alerts, subscription costs, levels, cost-mode), along with the `freebuff/SPEC.md` file and a landing-screen ad asset. The Muse Spark 1.3 contributor agent (`agents/base3-free-muse-spark-1-3.ts`) is repointed to the single-loop harness via `createBase3CliRoot` and the shared `FREEBUFF_MUSE_SPARK_13_CONTRIBUTOR_MODEL_ID`.
d71a831b3a7a5b66a7a100a47a69c2c6bcc70d82.evidence: Version field in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumped from `0.2.7` to `0.2.8`; multiple files modified across agents, cli, common, sdk, and packages; 8+ files removed including `assets/ads/freebuff-pro-after-hours.md`, `common/src/ads/sponsored-proposal-conformance.ts`, `common/src/ads/sponsored-verification.ts`, `common/src/ads/sponsored-verifier.ts`, `common/src/ads/supabase-format-cpc-experiment.ts`, `common/src/ads/supabase-format-experiment.ts`, `common/src/ads/supabase-setup-invitation.ts`, `common/src/constants/cf-worker-signals.ts`, `common/src/constants/freebuff-cost-mode.ts`, `common/src/constants/freebuff-levels.ts`, `common/src/constants/spend-providers.ts`, `common/src/types/subscription-costs.ts`, `common/src/util/db-health-alerts.ts`, `common/src/util/disposable-email.ts`, and `freebuff/SPEC.md`.
d71a831b3a7a5b66a7a100a47a69c2c6bcc70d82.unknowns: The rollout status of the removed ad and cost modules and whether any runtime behavior depended on them is not established.

changes.what: Terminal tool output, command display, and tool-branch previews now pass through `sanitizeTerminalOutput` to strip escape sequences before rendering.
Removed ad-verification, Supabase experiment, cost-mode, spend-provider, disposable-email, db-health, subscription-cost, levels, and CF worker-signals modules.
Muse Spark 1.3 contributor agent definition repointed to the single-loop harness using the shared model id.
Deleted the after-hours pro ad creative markdown asset.
Release package version bumped from 0.2.7 to 0.2.8.
Removed the Freebuff product specification document.

29214deac7fa874ca7abacea8095c1c429cce7d5.text: When your coding session stops working half-way through (for example, you close the window or it hits an error), the system now correctly points its internal tracking to the last complete task instead of the broken one, so the next request is matched to the right spot. This is an internal fix that only affects the Freebuff advertising team's records, not what you see or type in your chat. You do not need to do anything differently, and nothing about your sessions or your credit balance has changed.

d1ee8151d300fcd429df7b9d499ac123b50f7f85.text: When you send a message to the assistant in Freebuff's terminal version, the tool can now tuck two invisible reference tags into its request for a sponsored task suggestion. These tags are just IDs that point back to your current conversation and its most recent completed step, so the suggestion engine can match the offer to the exact chat that asked for it, without ever copying the content of what you wrote. The change only affects the behind-the-scenes wiring between the terminal app and Freebuff's ad service, and only the Freebuff engineering team can see or rely on it; you do not toggle anything or see a new menu, so daily use stays the same. It is live today as part of the CLI's offer-request path.

ab6bf9cb6c21a1501dd4f76f4be2cfffcee2207b.text: Freebuff now ties your first-tab discount to the person actually running the session, so the discount is read from the same purchase account that's paying the bill instead of an old single-session store that misreported prices for ordinary CLI use. This is live today for users of the Freebuff CLI when their session is active and the attempt ID matches, while legacy trial sessions still use the old store. In daily use, the price quote shown for models now matches what you're actually billed against, so you won't see a discounted price that doesn't line up with your account.

aeff04d65f0eddb4376babe7867103beb26d71d1.text: Sponsored tasks now run directly in your current folder instead of creating a separate branch, so the assistant edits your files in place and you keep or undo those changes with a single command. This affects Freebuff CLI users who accept sponsored task offers in their terminal, and they will notice the task changes their files directly with no branch or commit created. The new '/ads:undo' command replaces older worktree-based commands, and it works from both the command line and the on-screen undo button above the text input.

3082a3c005c13b211ad385cb606335d1d30d2e28.text: Freebuff now waits until you close your session before installing an automatic background update, so a download that finishes mid-work will never interrupt, restart, or replace the running assistant. The update that was downloaded in the background is held until the moment you exit, then it is installed only if no other window has already installed something newer, and if installation fails it leaves the version you were using untouched and preserves your original exit status. No action is required from you.

8fdaf5925043bd28c7bae1bb29beaf1fb5b8d7f2.text: When you're using the Freebuff terminal coding assistant and you're between chats or viewing an old conversation, you can now press a dedicated History button (shown as 'H · History' on screen) to browse past conversations without disrupting whatever might be running. A separate read-only mode lets you scroll through a saved chat transcript cleanly, with a 'Choose model' option if you want to start fresh, and message footers hide the feedback prompt while reading. The free-session landing screen now reserves space for this History button so the chat history list stays usable on smaller terminals, and the read-only view clears any leftover live-chat actions first so you can't accidentally submit or trigger commands on an old transcript.

45b6c98d656423c8d284fa69499eb6258f4186cb.text: When the Freebuff CLI starts up, it unpacks a built-in file-search tool into a temporary folder first, and only moves it to its final location once the copy is fully written and made runnable, so the tool never appears half-finished or unusable due to a crashed or concurrent launch. This matters most when Freebuff is installed somewhere your computer treats as protected, since the app will now silently place a working copy in your personal cache folder instead of failing, and it keys each copy by its exact contents so future updates always replace stale versions with the correct one. You won't see a settings toggle or notice any delay, but if a future upgrade of Freebuff previously got stuck reusing an old or broken search tool, that specific glitch is what this prevents.

93f5e6d99c94f55caa8bc4c067196475a1f732d5.text: When you press Esc to stop the assistant or your free session ends and you type again right away, the conversation history used to get wiped, forcing you to start over. Now the app keeps track of your session in a smarter way so that aborting or timing out preserves your chat instead of clearing it. This affects Freebuff CLI, web, and desktop users on the free tier whenever a session is interrupted or expires. In daily use, you will notice your conversation stays intact after interrupting or after a session times out, so you can pick up where you left off without losing context.

3d5300b6644c823970cb9588f6fde93ff3e39f2b.text: When the Freebuff app automatically installs an update in the background, the launcher stops the old version and starts the new one with a signal that previously caused the paid session to be released, which dropped the user back onto the model picker with the full price displayed. The CLI now treats that specific signal as an update handoff, keeps the active paid session on hold, and the relaunched binary resumes exactly where it left off instead of restarting on the model picker. No action is required from you, and the session you paid for is preserved across the update.

29e85c6f3045cc88e2a00a1a446ea8d0897eb47e.text: The assistant's shared error-reference list now includes a matching rule and message for a DeepSeek content safety refusal, so any Freebuff surface that reads this catalog can recognize the specific response and tell you to switch models instead of retrying the same blocked request. It affects Freebuff users who hit this refusal on DeepSeek, guiding them to a different model (for example, GLM 5.3 Flash or MiMo) since the whole conversation gets resent and will be refused again on DeepSeek. For surfaces that already wire this catalog into their error handling, you would see the helpful switch-models message in place of a generic failure; until each surface connects to the new constants, the behavior is in place but does nothing yet.

b729016fa17b4c24fcf4e4ffcfa8c66bf0ff19d5.text: A new version flag lets a Freebuff client run a sponsored task directly in your current working folder instead of creating a separate copy with its own branch and pull request. The offer request and the accept step now both carry an in-place execution version, so only clients that explicitly declare this capability run that way, while older requests behave exactly as before. This is a developer-facing capability landing now. Who it affects: Freebuff engineering maintainers and the in-place client builds that opt in. Everyday impact: If you are on a build that uses this version, an accepted sponsored offer can edit your working copy in place with no branch, and the proposal card shows actions to review and undo those changes instead of opening a pull request.

43740b75c7546ca72d3a9d0fa2b91df7a65a739f.text: The reason code used when a user's country doesn't qualify for a paid assistance feature had its description updated. Previously it was described as 'outside Tier 1 geo, where agentic is not funded', but now it documents that Tier 2 countries are actually served at $1, so the code now only applies to completely unrecognized locations. This is purely an internal documentation update to keep dashboards accurate; it does not change who is eligible today or affect any user's experience.

4dd7beb1aa58644b4655c0165f8a8225bdd3dfb7.text: Free mode users who hit a pacing limit will no longer see a separate notice about the session being slowed, and app makers who built on the SDK can no longer hook into that slowed-state warning to show their own labels or renewal prompts. The assistant still pauses and resumes under load, but any custom messaging or renewal offers that apps registered through this listener are no longer available. If you are an app developer calling this listener, remove those calls so your integration keeps compiling.

e427a2138e275b587c5370965028159356eea64b.text: The shared policy information file updated its "last updated" and "privacy policy last updated" date fields to October 1, 2026, replacing the previous September 25, 2026 entry. This is internal metadata consumed only by the Freebuff engineering team; it does not change any user-facing policy text or promises. As a result, there is nothing you notice in your daily use, and no action is required on your part.

d71a831b3a7a5b66a7a100a47a69c2c6bcc70d82.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.8 ships a terminal-sanitization safety pass and some ad-related cleanup. The headline change is that output from terminal commands (both the commands the agent types and what those commands print back) now has terminal escape sequences stripped before it is displayed, so a repository's test output or a fetched page can no longer inject OSC-52 clipboard writes, window-title changes, or cursor moves into your terminal. Alongside that, the ad-request builder now sends the shared browser-like user agent to ad providers on every call site rather than letting different callers use different identities, and the post-click attribution user agent is unified with the auction's so an impression records the same client that won the bid. The release also trims a now-deleted after-hours subscription promotional asset and relaxes the Freebuff catalog to drop rows whose scheduled open time is still in the future, so timed model launches appear only once they are actually eligible. Together these land as a tighter, safer terminal experience where command output cannot hijack your clipboard or terminal state, and ad measurement sees a single consistent client identity. The remaining diffs are comment-only or packaging-version bumps and establish no additional user-visible behavior.

2a28f46750d4224e3bc70e2dc9cf8b1c4c73ee49.text: The internal record of when Freebuff's Privacy Policy was last revised was corrected to show October 1, 2026. This bookkeeping value lives in shared core files and is used to keep policy notices consistent across Freebuff's apps and website. It does not change what data is collected or how it is used, and you won't notice anything different when using Freebuff. The policy text itself and your data-use options stay exactly the same.

5e1579a5cab63056ed76b338490991bc981e05b7.text: The assistant's error-checking for typed model names now correctly ignores messages that are really about what a model cannot do, rather than the name being wrong. This affects only Freebuff maintainers, the engineering team that builds the Freebuff assistant. You do not need to do anything; the change makes the assistant less likely to incorrectly tell you a model name is misspelled when the real problem is the model refusing a request, so error messages about your own-key provider connections stay accurate.

68940f7cca1e973aca042a9ad72cca6db7c4f044.text: The documentation comment for the campaign review setting was updated so that when an advertiser or reviewer wants to manually check each ad before it goes live, it now points to the correct admin page at '/web/admin/ads/advertisers-legacy'. This change only affects Freebuff employees or operators who manage advertiser campaigns on the admin dashboard; regular users who use Freebuff to code are not impacted and will not notice any difference in how the product works. No action is required, and there is no visible change to your experience using Freebuff.

05b8302ce19e998ea16f2f38c400c62c94d974b7.text: The Freebuff CLI publishing manifest had its version label advanced from 0.2.9 to 0.2.10, recording that a new release line has been cut. Who it affects: Internal release engineering only. Everyday impact: None for users. This is a packaging label change with no code, so updating to it does not alter anything you see or do in the assistant. You can stay on the previous version until your next install, since the label itself carries no new behavior.

f99efcb213cfbb833ecbcf8cff4fde1be33781e8.text: The wording shown to the assistant during a sponsored run was tightened so the procedure it was given to follow is stated as the only thing it should do, and the user's recent messages are labeled as read-only background for context, never as additional tasks. This affects anyone running a sponsored task through the Freebuff CLI today. In daily use you will not notice anything different; this does not add a feature or change a setting, it only adjusts how the assistant is told to behave during these specific ad-sponsored runs.

c5c0acc93f8fec48e0f7f78c536c4ed6dea74a2c.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.7 release and streak line compact fallback
c5c0acc93f8fec48e0f7f78c536c4ed6dea74a2c.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.2.7 is published (version 0.2.6 to 0.2.7 in freebuff/cli/release/package.json), bundling a streak-line width fix in the shared Freebuff streak utilities. The CLI layout helper getFreebuffStreakBonusStatusForLayout now renders the streak bonus status in two passes: first with the parenthetical clock label, and falling back to the unlabelled compact form when the labelled row is too wide for the terminal, so a narrow terminal keeps the status line instead of hiding it. The lower-level shared getters gain a compact flag and a labelReaderClock option that drop the (your time) suffix on clock times for surfaces too narrow to fit it, while midnight stays bare.
c5c0acc93f8fec48e0f7f78c536c4ed6dea74a2c.evidence: Diff in cli/src/utils/freebuff-streak-line.ts, common/src/util/freebuff-streak-line.ts, and freebuff/cli/release/package.json; commit c5c0acc9 is the Freebuff CLI 0.2.7 release-bump, and the source hunks add a compact fallback plus the labelReaderClock/compact logic in getFreebuffStreakBonusStatusForLayout, formatFreebuffStreakResetTime, and getFreebuffStreakBonusStatus.

c5c0acc93f8fec48e0f7f78c536c4ed6dea74a2c.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.7 tightens two areas of everyday behavior. First, when an AI assistant running a task finishes by showing "continue with the next step" suggestions while still having unchecked items on its own to-do list, the assistant is nudged back to work once (or up to three times) instead of stopping and making you type "continue", unless it already marked the task done or declined with no progress. Second, the streak-bonus status line shown under a 7+ day streak now fits narrow terminals by dropping the "(your time)" label and showing just the clock time, while still labeling odd hours clearly for readers outside Pacific time (for example a Dubai user on a 17-day streak now sees "after 11:00 AM (your time)"). A server-catalog-only model that is text-only now correctly stays text-only instead of receiving images and failing, and the package version is bumped to 0.2.7.

44c800d2617286631654dfd4d3c7b2b0e8e4d6b4.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.6 rolls out a new default AI model and updates the model catalog. The new default model is MiMo 2.6 Flash, which replaces GLM 5.3 Flash as the recommended starting choice for new users. The model picker interface was updated to show MiMo 2.6 Flash first, and the Freebuff catalog now handles models that are scheduled to launch in the future by hiding them until they are ready. A new device-signing system was added so that catalog-based requests from supported clients are authenticated with a per-installation signature, improving security for model selection. Additional changes refined how paid-plan rows appear in the limited-access catalog and fixed how purchase discounts are applied when switching models, ensuring the discount transfers correctly during a model switch. Some of these changes only take effect when the server supports them, so the available release evidence for end-user impact is incomplete.

055e9c3cd792ca332c6838f1f47c12415c638f54.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.5 release with credentials hardening and ID
055e9c3cd792ca332c6838f1f47c12415c638f54.summary: The Freebuff CLI 0.2.5 release bundles two functional changes on top of the 0.2.4 base: cli/src/utils/auth.ts now tightens the credentials file mode to CREDENTIALS_FILE_MODE (chmod after each write and on read, skipped on win32) and deduplicates credentials parse/read error logs via logCredentialsFailureOnce with loggedCredentialsFailures bounded by MAX_LOGGED_CREDENTIALS_FAILURES=20, addressing the per-render re-read in getUserCredentials. cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx now renders an identity-verification block for session.status==='spend_limited' && session.verificationRequired, backed by the new verificationRequired?: true field on that admission variant in common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts. The version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json was bumped from 0.2.4 to 0.2.5.

055e9c3cd792ca332c6838f1f47c12415c638f54.text: This 0.2.5 release hardens credentials, adds identity verification gating, and refines the free model picker. It clamps the credentials file to owner-only read/write to keep stored login tokens private, and collapses repeated credentials-read errors into a single log line per distinct failure so a mismatched pre-0.2.4 install can no longer spam local logs. The landing screen now shows an explicit ID verification required warning with the account hub link when the server flags an account, separate from the daily budget cap. Free model picker entries gained an icon field with size guidance and per-model notes, and the desktop client can surface a premium slot taken admission. Users with capped free trials see a limited offer countdown to zero, and the waitlist and sponsored proposal statuses now carry a server-sent message. The evidence shows these behaviors but is incomplete about any deployed capability behind flags, so only the above user-facing changes are confirmed.

8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 release
8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.summary: Freebuff CLI release 0.2.4 increments the version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.2.3 to 0.2.4, bundling the keychain-backed auth token storage from member 6fc184b and the server-driven catalog model directory from member a080b035. The auth change adds cli/src/utils/auth-token-store.ts with a SecretStore abstraction and stores the bearer token in the OS keychain via Bun.secrets instead of credentials.json, while retaining the file token as a fallback on keychain failure, and is wired into cli/src/index.tsx via the new loadStoredAuthToken() call before any credential reads. The catalog change introduces a new FreebuffModelCatalog wire type in common/src/types/freebuff-model-catalog.ts and a client-side catalog store (cli/src/state/freebuff-catalog-store.ts) plus a use-freebuff-catalog hook (cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-model-catalog.ts) that fetches and caches the server model catalog keyed by catalog handle rather than compiled model id.

8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.text: Release 0.2.4 of the Freebuff CLI ships a new server-driven model catalog along with stronger login token storage. You should know about the model catalog first: the list of AI models you can pick from is now downloaded fresh from Freebuff's servers at startup, so new, re-priced, or rotated models reach you without waiting for a CLI update, and your saved pick follows a stable internal key that maps to whichever model it currently points to. Second, your login token moved out of a readable text file and into your operating system's secure keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service) when available, with the file still used as a fallback so you will not get signed out on machines where the keychain is locked or unavailable. Third, country-verification hints that tell the app whether verifying your location could improve your access now arrive alongside a paid-plan upsell, so limited-access users see the real cost instead of a generic prompt. These changes affect every Freebuff CLI user, with the catalog requiring the server-side protocol to be present and the token protection applying to Freebuff accounts only (the Codebuff paid CLI still uses the shared credentials file). Where the evidence does not establish a behavior, such as a fully rolled-out UI for the upsell, the release notes are incomplete on that point.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.1 adds the ability to send information about your terminal environment and your typing behavior (like how many characters or pastes your prompt had) along with every ad request and session run, so the system can better understand and filter usage. This release also adds a new error message for when content is flagged due to possible cybersecurity risk by the AI provider, telling users to try a different model. For everyday users on Freebuff, ad requests now carry more detailed environment headers (like whether you're on a shell, terminal, or SSH), and the system records one-time details when it starts up to help identify bot-like traffic. The change is only active on Freebuff; paid Codebuff runs are unaffected.

e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.title: Freebuff CLI 0.1.11 with cut-off file edit guard
e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.summary: Release 0.1.11 packages the truncated-write guard from commit e3d7701e. The agent runtime now refuses two shapes of a file edit cut off mid-generation: `parseRawToolCall` recognizes an incomplete JSON prefix in tool arguments and reports an explicit error instead of inviting a re-issue, while `processFileBlock` refuses a `write_file` that would replace an existing file of 30+ lines with a copy under 60% of its size that leaves brackets open where the current file balances them. Both refusals emit the new `FILE_WRITE_GUARD_EVENT` to Axiom via the updated allowlist in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`.
e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.evidence: The commit is a release-bump of `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, changing the version from `0.1.10` to `0.1.11`. The release member source evidence for this window (commit e3d7701e) shows a new `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/truncated-write-guard.ts` module, changes to `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts` (adding the truncated?: true field to `ToolCallError` and an `isTruncatedJsonPrefix()` check in `parseRawToolCall`), changes to `packages/agent-runtime/src/process-file-block.ts` (using `detectTruncatedRewrite()` to refuse a `write_file` under 60% of an existing 30+ line file that leaves brackets open), and the addition of `FILE_WRITE_GUARD_EVENT` to the allowlist in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`.
e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.unknowns: The diff for this commit only shows the package.json version bump; the behavioral source hunks come from the release member evidence for commit e3d7701e.

e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.text: This release adds a safety guard that stops file edits from being applied when an AI response gets cut off mid-generation. The runtime now detects two failure patterns: tool-call arguments that stop mid-JSON before closing brackets or strings, and write_file operations that would replace an existing file with a much shorter copy ending in unclosed brackets. When either situation occurs, the runtime refuses the write and tells the model nothing was written. Both refusals log a content-free event to Axiom with sizes, tool, and model names only. The change includes tests and a documentation section describing the guard.

f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.title: Freebuff CLI 0.1.10 with BYOK reasoning effort controls
f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.summary: Freebuff CLI release 0.1.10 adds support for configuring reasoning effort on BYOK runs. The new `/byok effort` command allows selecting `low`, `medium`, or `high` reasoning effort, which is saved as `byokReasoningEffort` in `settings.json` and translated per provider dialect in `byokRequestTransform`. If a provider returns an HTTP 400 or 422 error rejecting the effort field, `byokReasoningRetryBody` retries the request once without it. Additionally, `freebuffSubscriptionMrrUsd` is introduced in `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts` to calculate monthly recurring revenue across subscription billing intervals.

Translates BYOK reasoning effort per provider dialect and retries requests once without it on HTTP 400 or 422 rejections.

f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.10 adds a new way for you to control how much thinking a model does when you run it with your own API key (BYOK). You can now type a new command, /byok effort, and pick low, medium, or high reasoning effort for your own-key runs; that choice is saved in your settings and applied each time you start a run. The app translates your pick into the right format for each provider you connect to (OpenRouter, Anthropic, or OpenAI-compatible services), and if a provider does not accept that setting, the run automatically retries without it so your task still completes. The release also bumps the Freebuff package version to 0.1.10 for the npm-published CLI. Evidence from this release is limited; the available release evidence is incomplete regarding other bundled capabilities beyond the BYOK reasoning effort controls.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.8 fixes a bug where streak bonuses were reported as missing for users east of the Pacific timezone. 38cd1ed44428f573c4754d8e0cee868f2875b54e.text: Freebuff 0.0.204 fixes a crash that could shut down your coding session and adds better crash reporting so future crashes are easier to diagnose. When the chat failed during fast AI streaming (the 'Maximum update depth exceeded' error), a UI problem inside an ad display hook could unexpectedly end your entire session along with your Freebuff hour; inline ads now stay stable during heavy streaming so this no longer interrupts your work. Previously, if the CLI crashed, you only saw an error in the terminal; now it writes a small report locally and the next time you launch, that crash info is sent to telemetry (counted for every version so reliability can be tracked), but only if your Freebuff hour was at stake. The version number moves from 0.0.203 to 0.0.204; everything else in the release package (README, binary list, support for Intel and Apple Silicon Macs and Windows/Linux) is unchanged.

a23f0ae16d9c7d69458dce20ca74178bc530ffb8.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.203 fixes two problems that affected long conversations when they get shortened before being sent to an AI model. First, when the system compresses an old conversation to save space, model-compaction now names large binary data (like screenshots or base64-encoded images inside tool results) instead of copying all those characters into the shortening request, which previously caused extremely long calls that blocked the conversation. Second, the SDK's truncation logic now counts only the messages you actually wrote when deciding where to cut history during an edit, instead of also counting system-generated messages like Stop notifications or previous summaries that moved the cut too early and deleted more conversation than intended. The shortening logic can also count from the end of the thread using the new totalUserTurns parameter, so edits to messages in very long, already-summarized conversations no longer answer null and clear everything. Users who stop long sessions often and then edit earlier messages will find their conversation is preserved as expected instead of being lost.

baffcb89339ea373a63aa77202bec34e76f80444.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.200 ships with several safety and access updates for sponsored runs and model access. Sponsored (advertiser-funded) runs now start their time window when the task actually begins rather than when you click Accept, and the assistant is told that the approved procedure is the only goal of the turn, reducing confusion from extra instructions. These sponsored runs are now blocked from entering Windows Subsystem for Linux, running destructive database commands (like dropping tables), or managing containers (like starting Docker), and can declare specific credentials (like an API key) that are injected safely into their environment and redacted from any output. Two models, GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro, are moved out of a US-or-paid-only restriction into full access for most users, while remaining plan-only for accounts on a limited tier. The clipboard copy feature now gives clearer guidance when a copy only reached the terminal over SSH, and the data-use policy narrows code evaluation to connected GitHub repositories only. Tests for the advertising system default a first-party CPM setting to off to match older test assumptions. Overall, this release tightens what advertiser-run tasks can touch on your machine, opens up two popular models more widely, and clarifies how data and copied text behave.

9f521ec5f2e38db447cafa0549633d728a284921.text: This Freebuff CLI release focuses on two main areas: better ad tracking and recovery from crashes. First, the assistant can now securely link ad requests to your conversation (by run id only, never the actual conversation text) so sponsored tasks are better tracked without compromising your privacy. Second, if the CLI crashes or your terminal closes unexpectedly, the app now saves its session state to a local file and automatically resumes your hour-long free session the next time you start, instead of charging you for a new one. Additionally, Solar Pro 4 is back as a selectable AI model for tasks. The release also cleans up ad trace pointers when runs are interrupted, so ads are no longer associated with failed or abandoned work. Users benefit from not losing their progress on a crash and having clearer ad attribution to their actual conversations.

Freebuff 0.0.198 replaces the old worktree-based recovery commands /ads:pull-request and /ads:remove-worktree with one /ads:undo that shares one implementation with the dock Undo button via handleProposalUndo. 0cb910451c1b774876b017cf60f059ed6e9f2e82.text: Freebuff is now at version 0.2.12, which is mainly a packaging release. The changes here are mostly about how the software is built and tracked: the CLI's version label was bumped to 0.2.12, the README and license notices were updated, and the project moved to a new monorepo path so the installed package is now called 'freebuff' instead of 'codebuff'. Some shared code was cleaned up (an unused helper was removed and a couple of type files were added or changed), and the local build scripts that package the CLI were adjusted. For most users this update is just a new version number to install - the day-to-day features, the ads, and the AI models you use are unchanged by this release.

a4846ebf48b5d8bbe08744fb2d6f26f119d19861.text: A new /todo command opens a live checklist panel (TodoPanel) inside the chat window that shows the main AI agent's current task list as it works. The panel reads the latest checklist from the conversation, shows how many items are done, scrolls on its own when there are many items, and can be closed with the Escape key - the same way the review and queue panels behave. This is available now to anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web, or desktop app, and the checklist updates in place as the agent checks off each step.

6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.196 ships a new AI model line and smoother session handling when the app updates itself. The free chat thinker now uses GPT-6 Luna instead of GPT-5.6 Luna, with the old model moved to the withdrawn list so existing picks fall back gracefully. When the launcher updates the app in the background, the currently paid session is preserved instead of being released, so the relaunched binary can resume rather than dropping you back to the model picker. A new DeepSeek content filter recognizer gives a clearer message guiding users to switch models instead of retrying, and the agentic-sponsored-run offer machinery gains an in-place execution mode that runs edits directly in the user's current conversation without creating branches or pull requests. These changes affect free-tier CLI and Desktop users, plus the sponsored-run surfaces and SDK callers, with the in-place mode only taking effect when an updated client declares support.

5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.text: This Freebuff CLI update (0.0.197) ships four notable improvements: updates now wait until you close your session before installing, so a running session is never interrupted by a new version; the embedded ripgrep search tool now installs through a safer temporary-then-rename process with a fallback cache when the normal location is not writable; the chat history viewer now works while a Freebuff session is not active (for browsing past transcripts read-only without composing or running), and the 'H' key plus a new 'H · History' shortcut open it on the landing and superseded screens; and pricing for the first-tab discount is now read from the same Desktop purchase store used for an active session, fixing misreported prices for ordinary CLI claims. Read-only chat browsing also hides feedback prompts during browsing. One other change was dropped from the summary due to a discredited description, and an accompanying launcher test harness exercises the deferred install flow with an install-on-exit check that prevents downgrading or overwriting after another invocation already installed.

A zone is dropped when the runtime resolved Etc/Unknown or nothing, when the zone is UTC but TZ is set to a non-UTC value, when the process is on a remote host signaled by SSH_CONNECTION, SSH_CLIENT, SSH_TTY, CODESPACES, REMOTE_CONTAINERS, GITPOD_WORKSPACE_ID, or container, or when ICU reports a fixed-offset Etc/GMT±N on a win32 platform. 0cb910451c1b774876b017cf60f059ed6e9f2e82.text: The Freebuff 0.2.12 release is a minor packaging and catalog stability release. The only clearly-evidenced user-visible change is a model catalog update: Space Bunny Alpha is now offered to limited-access accounts alongside the existing free models, and the catalog marks DeepSeek V4 Pro as retired with a clear upgrade nudge (run npm install -g freebuff@latest). Several entries are scope-only or data/config changes (ads serving, event IDs, logging fields, tests, gitignore) and do not establish a new user behavior. The release note itself is categorized as packaging. Available release evidence shows only that limited-access users now see Space Bunny Alpha in their model picker and that old clients naming retired models get a guidance message to update. No other new capability or safety protection is demonstrated by the provided source hunks.

547e2f0af84c148d1eb8107513f9ba88fe3589d7.text: The Freebuff terminal chat now lets you switch AI models and adjust how deeply the model thinks, all without leaving your conversation. You type /model to open a model picker right inside the chat view, or press Tab on a model to cycle its reasoning depth. A persistent footer shows your current model, its thinking level, and how to pull up older chats or help, so you no longer need a separate screen just to change settings. This applies only to Freebuff (free tier) users; the session admission flow that decides when and how a model actually starts has moved its confirmation step into this same in-chat interface.

8ea9ab3e1f7758075f6ed807a54065e1ba89894a.text: A behind-the-scenes fix that stitches each message together with the account it belongs to, so two different people running at the same time never get each other's logs mixed up. This only affects Freebuff's internal engineering team, not anything you see or do. Nothing changes for you today; the assistant still works the same in your terminal.

f6c9bf23ecd733d05db82bdabd99521388488a73.text: The assistant now checks whether the clock on the computer it runs on is genuinely the user's own, and only reports that clock to the Freebuff account when it trusts it to be, otherwise it sends nothing. This affects Freebuff's free users, whose daily Freebucks reset window is anchored to their device's timezone. You will not see anything change in the app today, but you will no longer be silently treated as being in UTC (which could shift your Freebucks reset) when your device reports UTC only because it is a remote server, a cloud dev container, or a Windows machine that lost its named timezone, so your reset time now stays pinned to your real location.

0cb910451c1b774876b017cf60f059ed6e9f2e82.text: Freebuff 0.2.12 is a smaller release that mostly refines existing behavior rather than adding big new features. The clearest user-facing change is that a user's Freebucks daily bonus and streak reset now follow the user's own timezone (the account's daily allowance reset, normally the user's own midnight since 2026-10-01), instead of always resetting at Pacific midnight, so a streak bonus no longer appears to vanish for users far from Pacific time. The release also adds handling for retired models (MiniMax M3, GLM 5.2, OX Alpha, now explicitly refused instead of running on `base2-free`), brings Space Bunny Alpha into the limited-access picker (it was already admitted at limited access but missing from the CLI and Desktop pickers), and adds a new "billboard" image ad placement format with defined artwork shapes for Desktop. Behind the scenes it wires up a precomputed-score ad experiment (a sticky 50/50 per-user test that only activates when ad creatives publish their scored snapshots), adds a new X advertiser acquisition event mapping, and includes various log/event field updates plus test coverage guards to keep free-mode root agents pinned to approved prompt openings.

0cb910451c1b774876b017cf60f059ed6e9f2e82.text: Freebuff 0.2.12 ships a timezone fix for Freebucks streaks, new Billboard ad placements for Freebuff Desktop, a new Space Bunny Alpha model in the free picker, plus several backend updates to logging, model retirement, and the agent publisher trust system. The streak bonus is now tied to your own daily reset time instead of Pacific time, so travelers and remote-desktop users see their streak day roll over at their local midnight rather than a fixed server clock. Freebuff Desktop gains full-bleed image ad slots (sidebar and right-panel billboards) that run on the first-party CPM ad leg only. The free model list now includes Space Bunny Alpha (a limited-preview model), while older models like MiniMax M3, GLM 5.2, and Ox Alpha are formally retired and blocked from running. On security, the SDK now refuses to run agents from untrusted publishers that contain executable code or MCP servers, and the CLI lands on /todo slash command support. Additional backend changes tighten BigQuery schema lookups, error logging size limits, version comparison for Windows Git installs, and update the X (Twitter) advertiser event identifiers.

70a78466da2239b118a3891b0ccced51e1ac07bc.title: CLI scroll guard scopes the programmatic flag to each write
70a78466da2239b118a3891b0ccced51e1ac07bc.summary: The chat scrollbox now routes every programmatic `scrollTop` write through a new `setScrollTop` callback that sets `programmaticScrollRef.current` to true only around the assignment and resets it in a finally block. This fixes a race where OpenTUI emits scroll changes synchronously and emits nothing for a no-op assignment, which could let the programmatic flag stay set long enough to swallow the user's next wheel event when already at the bottom. The messages-change effect and each animation frame now call `setScrollTop`, and the scroll-change handler only short-circuits when `!programmaticScrollRef.current`.
70a78466da2239b118a3891b0ccced51e1ac07bc.evidence: In cli/src/hooks/use-scroll-management.ts, the `setScrollTop` callback wraps `scrollbox.scrollTop = top` in a try/finally that clears `programmaticScrollRef.current`; `animateScrollTo` and the messages-effect now call `setScrollTop` instead of setting the flag and assigning scrollTop directly, and the scroll-change handler now short-circuits only when `!programmaticScrollRef.current`.

70a78466da2239b118a3891b0ccced51e1ac07bc.text: The assistant now keeps track of whether the chat window was scrolled by the program itself, so it can tell the difference between its own scrolling and your next mouse wheel or keyboard scroll. This fixes a bug where, when you were already at the bottom of the chat and new content arrived, your next attempt to scroll up with the mouse wheel or PageUp could be ignored, leaving you stuck at the bottom instead of letting you browse the conversation history. It is live today for anyone using the Freebuff CLI chat interface.

0cb910451c1b774876b017cf60f059ed6e9f2e82.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.12 brings a clearer streak reward system, fixes for agent trust handling, safer logging, and a few behind-the-scenes additions for ads and model retirement. The streak rewards now align with each user's own daily reset time instead of always Pacific time, fixing confusion for users in other timezones. Earned daily Freebucks bonuses now expire exactly when that day's allowance resets, so the bonus status shown matches what actually happens. New security checks validate publisher and agent names before downloading remote agents, blocking path-traversal style tricks that could load an untrusted agent under another publisher's name. Log entries now clip oversized error details like large SQL statements, so important error causes are no longer cut off before reaching the diagnostic logs. A new set of retired AI models is recognized by the app, so very old CLI versions get a clear upgrade message instead of a confusing unknown-model error. The first-party ad scoring system gained a new experiment field, and billboard-style image ad slots were added for the desktop app with shape and size validation.

0cb910451c1b774876b017cf60f059ed6e9f2e82.text: Freebuff 0.2.12 (2026-10-02) rolls up timezone-aware Freebucks handling and new ad placement tracking. The Freebucks daily-allowance clock now keys off the account's own timezone instead of always Pacific, so users outside Pacific see streak resets and bonuses land on their local midnight, with the CLI omitting a misleading UTC header for remote/SSH sessions and Windows fixed-offset zones. Concrete highlights: (1) Ad serving now tracks a per-user split between shared and dedicated Redis state (`ad_redis_store` field) and logs a new precomputed-ad-score experiment arm so ad delivery can be measured independently of the first-party model routing. (2) New Desktop billboard placements (sidebar and right-panel image slots) ship with defined aspect-ratio shapes and upload validation, gated behind `available: false` so they are operator-placed only for now. (3) Log payloads now cap long SQL query strings and parameter lists, so oversized database errors still surface the real cause instead of getting cut off in telemetry. Everyday impact: Freebucks allowance days and streak-day rollovers align to each account's reported timezone, affecting when the daily Freebucks limit refreshes and when a streak bonus is paid or expires (older/unreported accounts stay on Pacific). The README model catalog adds Space Bunny Alpha to both the full and limited pickers and notes GPT-6.1 Sol is one promotion-priced session per day. Available release evidence is incomplete for the claimed BYOK SDK changes and the omitted second commit, so its user-visible effect is not documented here.

Each saved model owns its key, so rotation or removal of one cannot break siblings; environment-backed sources keep their `env:` reference verbatim rather than copying a key value. A new test asserts that a failed save cleans up its copied key and leaves the source usable.

0cb910451c1b774876b017cf60f059ed6e9f2e82.text: Freebuff version 0.2.12 is a maintenance and refinement release rather than one that introduces new user-facing features. The evidence shows improvements focused on correctness and edge-case handling for existing systems, with no new capabilities named in the supported member changes. Two concrete changes stand out. First, the assistant now better determines which timezone to use when reporting daily bonus resets for the Freebucks streak meter, avoiding confusion for users running Freebuff remotely (such as over SSH or inside Codespaces), and gracefully falling back to omitting the header when the local timezone cannot be reliably determined rather than guessing incorrectly. Second, the agent runtime and SDK now recognize an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server declared by a remote agent template as executable content that requires the publisher to be trusted before running, closing a gap where MCP servers attached to an untrusted publisher's agent could have been launched without the existing trust check. Everyday impact is limited to users in specific situations. The timezone correction matters to developers using Freebuff from a remote host or container whose system clock is set to UTC by default, where the streak bonus status could previously have appeared to reset at an unexpected time. The added MCP trust check only affects users who download and run third-party agents from the agent registry that ship MCP server connections, requiring those publishers to be explicitly trusted before their agents start any local or remote tools. The remaining supported changes are internal: test coverage refinements, log payload size limits to prevent oversized error reports from being cut off in telemetry, retired model handling, and internal placement/ad-experiment tracking fields. No new model, picker entry, or headline feature is established by the release evidence. The single most useful concrete effect for a typical user is that the streak bonus reset time now reports correctly when Freebuff is run from a remote host, since that is the only change touching user-visible behavior described by supported source evidence.

0cb910451c1b774876b017cf60f059ed6e9f2e82.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.12 (released October 2, 2026) is a stability and correctness release for the free AI coding assistant. It does not add new model choices to the main picker, but it fixes several behind-the-scenes behaviors that shape how Freebuff tracks your usage time, serves ads, and guards against untrusted code. The streak/rewards system now keys your daily allowance off your own home midnight (since October 1) rather than Pacific time, so travelers and remote users see a reset time that matches their own clock, and the CLI surfaces a clearer message about when the next daily +15 Freebucks bonus arrives. Error and log handling got tighter: oversized database or error payloads are trimmed before they reach operational logs, large bulk-insert messages no longer truncate the underlying failure, and the ad-serving telemetry gained new fields that let the ads team measure a precomputed pre-ranked ad experiment and geo-tier routing without exposing raw user ids or IPs. The agent registry now treats MCP servers as executable content (not just inline code), so downloading an agent that wires up its own MCP tools is refused unless its publisher is explicitly trusted. Finally, several drift guards and test setups were tightened so a misregistered agent prompt, a malformed published agent id, or a leftover test environment variable can no longer silently change behavior in production.

bcb726800e42b55458879a15244d6d2f45e61956.title: Deferred self-updates are staged, adopted, and tracked by launcher
bcb726800e42b55458879a15244d6d2f45e61956.summary: The release launcher now writes a staged.json manifest into the per-pid staging directory when a deferred self-update is staged (cli/release-core/launcher.js, writeStagedManifest), and each launch runs adoptOrphanedStagedUpdates() to install an update a previous launcher downloaded but never finished installing on its own exit. installStagedBinary gained a keepStagingOnFailure flag so an aborted exit-time install leaves the directory in place for the next launch to adopt, and stagedFilesMatch() re-verifies each file's sha256 plus an allowlist of names before adoption. The CLI binary now exposes which npm wrapper started it as CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_VERSION, read through getCliEnv() in cli/src/utils/env.ts, declared in cli/src/types/env.ts, and sent as launcherVersion on the APP_LAUNCHED analytics event in cli/src/index.tsx.

bcb726800e42b55458879a15244d6d2f45e61956.text: The release launcher now writes a manifest file into the per-download directory when it stages a deferred self-update, and on each launch it checks for updates that a previous launcher downloaded but never got to install on its own exit. This lets a session that was closed mid-update finish installing the staged binary on the next launch, including re-verifying each file's checksum. The CLI also now reports which npm wrapper started it via the CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_VERSION environment variable on the APP_LAUNCHED analytics event. This affects Freebuff CLI users and is live today: closing a terminal window mid-update no longer means re-downloading the same release on every later launch.

03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.11 fixes a problem where closing the terminal window during a background update left the downloaded new version staged but never installed, forcing every later launch to re-download it. The launcher now records a manifest of the staged files and, when you open the app again, adopts a staged update that a previous launch left behind, installing it at the right time. It also re-checks the staged files match before installing and cleans up directories left by launchers that no longer exist. The release also adds a test fixture and end-to-end test covering parameterized MCP tools with required arguments, so tools with required inputs are now verified to receive those arguments correctly.

03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.11 deferred self-update adoption and launcher version
03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.summary: The Freebuff CLI release manifest at freebuff/cli/release/package.json was incremented to 0.2.11, publishing the deferred self-update work that now lets a new launch adopt a staged update a previous launcher downloaded but could not install before the terminal was closed. installStagedBinary in cli/release-core/launcher.js now accepts keepStagingOnFailure, writes a staged.json manifest with per-file sha256 hashes, and the new adoptOrphanedStagedUpdates run at startup claims orphaned <tempDownloadDirName>-<pid> directories and re-verifies their hashes before moving files; on exit the launcher also writes the staged manifest so the next launch adopts the update instead of re-downloading it. A new CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_VERSION env var is emitted into spawned processes and tracked in the APP_LAUNCHED event, letting launch telemetry distinguish install paths that can adopt deferred updates from ones that cannot.
03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.evidence: freebuff/cli/release/package.json version bumped from 0.2.10 to 0.2.11; the release window's source evidence is the deferred self-update staging work in cli/release-core/launcher.js (commit bcb726800e42b55458879a15244d6d2f45e61956) which adds staged-update adoption on launch plus a CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_VERSION env var, and parameterized MCP tool e2e test fixtures in packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/mcp-parameterized-tools-e2e.test.ts (commit 93ee44807e99bfec9d8d467bb31df95a13c9e795).

03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.11 improves how the assistant updates itself when running as a downloaded app. The launcher now safely adopts an already-downloaded update left behind by a previous session instead of re-downloading the same version every time, and it records the download wrapper version so telemetry can tell which installs support deferred updates. A staged update manifest with file checksums lets a later launch verify and install an update a dead launcher never finished, while keeping the staging directory when installation fails on Windows due to antivirus or file locks. Crash reports now strip terminal-control characters before replaying captured output so the report cannot accidentally re-enter alternate screen mode. New tests verify parameterized MCP tools serve complete schemas and arguments end-to-end. Together, these changes mean self-updating downloads are reused instead of repeated, and crash diagnostics stay readable.

af742b4afe363b3aafc8d7c7da50b4721dc658bb.title: Read url tool pins connections to validated addresses to close DNS
af742b4afe363b3aafc8d7c7da50b4721dc658bb.summary: The read url tool now fetches through `pinnedFetch`, a new transport in `sdk/src/tools/pinned-fetch.ts` whose `net.connect` `lookup` validates addresses via `resolveAllowedAddresses` and connects only to those it just checked. The `read_url` call in `sdk/src/run.ts` now passes only `url` and `max_chars` through to `readUrl`, so SSRF transport options stay the host's, never the tool call's. The default transport uses `pinnedFetch` except under Bun with a proxy configured, where `globalThis.fetch` is used so the proxy keeps resolving names, and additional non-routable ranges (`::a.b.c.d`, `198.18.0.0/15`, `fec0::/10`, `64:ff9b:1::/48`) are now refused.

The `read_url` tool in `sdk/src/run.ts` was changed to pass only `url` and `max_chars` to `readUrl`, and `sdk/src/env.ts` adds `isHttpProxyConfiguredFromEnv` to let `pinnedFetch` defer to Bun's `fetch` when a proxy is configured.

af742b4afe363b3aafc8d7c7da50b4721dc658bb.text: The assistant's web-reading tool now checks twice before it connects to a website. First it looks up the site's address and makes sure it isn't pointing to a private or internal location, and then it connects only to the address it just approved, so a site can't trick the check and sneak the assistant onto an internal network. This protects you whenever the assistant fetches a link, and it also closes off the extra non-routable address ranges that could previously slip through. If you use the assistant through the SDK and you rely on an HTTP proxy while running under Bun, your existing proxy setup keeps working unchanged.

9a24ecd20f4d9e277f877907a9d6850d6382e882.title: Sponsored command walk refuses unreadable lines and git history moves
9a24ecd20f4d9e277f877907a9d6850d6382e882.summary: The sponsored command walk in common/src/ads/sponsored-command-refusals.ts now fails closed on lines it cannot finish reading: wrappers nested past MAX_DEPTH=6, an -EncodedCommand that will not decode, and a -File script whose contents are off the command line all return an 'unverifiable' refusal instead of null, and two new refusal kinds 'git' and 'unverifiable' were added to SponsoredCommandRefusalKind with matching refusal sentences. A Judge type carrying a refused-git set is threaded through analyzeCommandLine, analyzeSegment, and analyzeRest, and the new sponsoredRefusedGitInvocation export re-runs the same walk on Linux to find the first refused git subcommand reached through wrappers like bash -c or cmd /c. common/src/ads/sponsored-local-execution.ts imports GIT_VALUE_OPTIONS and sponsoredRefusedGitInvocation and switches sponsoredGitSubcommands to a GIT_EXECUTABLE regex that matches git.exe and spelled-out paths, so sponsoredRefusedGitSubcommand asks both the flat scan and the walk, then re-exports sponsoredGitRefusal. common/src/ads/sponsored-run-credentials.ts replaces the silent depth guard in redactSponsoredCredentialDeep with REDACT_MAX_DEPTH=32 and a SPONSORED_CREDENTIAL_TOO_DEEP placeholder, so deeply nested values are reported rather than leaked.
9a24ecd20f4d9e277f877907a9d6850d6382e882.evidence: In common/src/ads/sponsored-command-refusals.ts, the kind set expands from 'wsl'|'database'|'container' to add 'git' and 'unverifiable', with MAX_DEPTH=6, a Judge type threaded through analyzeCommandLine/analyzeSegment/analyzeRest/analyzeRest, new exports GIT_VALUE_OPTIONS, sponsoredRefusedGitInvocation, SPONSORED_CREDENTIAL_TOO_DEEP, and refusal sentences for git/unverifiable branches; the walk now refuses lines it cannot finish (wrappers deeper than MAX_DEPTH, undecodable -EncodedCommand, -File script files) rather than waving them through. In common/src/ads/sponsored-local-execution.ts, the old flat /git$/ scan is replaced by a new GIT_EXECUTABLE regex (matching git.exe and spelled-out paths) plus the shared GIT_VALUE_OPTIONS set and a call to sponsoredRefusedGitInvocation, and sponsoredGitRefusal is now re-exported from this module. In common/src/ads/sponsored-run-credentials.ts, redactSponsoredCredentialDeep gains REDACT_MAX_DEPTH=32 and SPONSORED_CREDENTIAL_TOO_DEEP, replacing deep-unreadable values wholesale instead of returning them silently.

9a24ecd20f4d9e277f877907a9d6850d6382e882.text: When you ask the assistant to run commands during a sponsored task, it now double-checks git commands more thoroughly and refuses any command it can't fully read through, rather than letting unreadable commands slip through. This affects only the engineering teams who maintain Freebuff's sponsored task system, since it changes safety checks in the code. You won't notice this change in your daily use.

dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.9 ships with two main changes: safer terminal output and tighter control over ads on the landing screen. First, any text that comes back from a command or web page and would normally be drawn in your terminal (the command itself, its stdout/stderr, or tool results) is now stripped of escape sequences before you see it, so a crafted script or fetched page can no longer hijack the terminal (for example, silently rewriting your clipboard with OSC 52 or retitling the window). Second, on the landing screen the CLI no longer fetches an ad when the terminal is too short (below 18 rows) to actually draw the banner, so Freebuff stops serving banner ads it cannot display. The landing screen otherwise keeps ads always-on with forceStart so they load before you type, and the server tries Gravity first, then falls back to ZeroClick and Carbon. In the SDK the read_url tool now pins every network connection to only the address it has just validated at connect time, and validates each redirect hop again, closing the DNS-rebinding gap where a hostname could pass the safety check with one answer and connect with a different (private) answer. The SDK also no longer ships source maps, and a runtime app-URL override is now only honored for codebuff.com/freebuff.com hosts over https or loopback unless CODEBUFF_ALLOW_CUSTOM_APP_URL=1 is set. For users, the visible effects are: terminal output shown in the app can no longer run control-sequence tricks against you, the Freebuff landing screen stops loading banner ads on terminals under 18 rows, the read_url tool resists DNS-rebinding style fetches, and the published SDK package is smaller and no longer embeds full source. The release evidence for the landing-ads gate, terminal stripping, and read_url safety is backed by dedicated tests; the version bump in the release manifest is packaging only.

a8c632ee26b9700e7304d1e830fd4157ce3653ce.text: The Freebuff engineering team removed a special, more-secure way the SDK used to load web pages when an advertiser-funded task needed to read a URL, and let it go back to loading pages the normal way instead. They also cleaned up two helpers that decided whether to show ads on the landing screen and whether to hide them on small terminals, inlining that logic directly where it is used. Finally, they simplified the sponsored-command safety check by dropping a separate nested-git-wrapper parser so the same gate now judges git subcommands in one place, and moved the git subcommand refusal text into the local-execution module where it is read.

6931512368f9e246683b095dd2bf8ff43a811af8.title: BYOK lock recovery unlinks stale PID lock files
6931512368f9e246683b095dd2bf8ff43a811af8.summary: A new `recoverByokLock` function in `sdk/src/impl/byok-lock.ts` checks whether the PID recorded in `connections.lock` belongs to a dead process and, if so, unlinks the lock file so the current writer can proceed. The `withLock` method in `sdk/src/byok.ts` now publishes an already-complete PID atomically via a temporary candidate file and `fs.link`, calling `recoverByokLock(lock)` on EEXIST instead of waiting for the previous 5000ms timeout with no recovery. A loopback TCP listener keyed by the observed PID acts as a short-lived mutex so competing reapers never unlink a successor's lock, and the owner is re-read under that mutex before unlinking.
6931512368f9e246683b095dd2bf8ff43a811af8.evidence: New file `sdk/src/impl/byok-lock.ts` exports `recoverByokLock`, which the `withLock` method in `sdk/src/byok.ts` now calls when `fs.link` returns EEXIST to decide whether a stale PID lock file at `connections.lock` can be unlinked.
6931512368f9e246683b095dd2bf8ff43a811af8.unknowns: Whether any downstream consumer of the SDK's BYOK metadata store other than the CLI relies on the previous non-recovering lock behavior, and how the loopback-mutex fallback behaves on Windows where TCP loopback semantics differ.

6931512368f9e246683b095dd2bf8ff43a811af8.text: When a process that was saving your BYOK provider connections crashes, it can leave behind a stale lock file that falsely makes the configuration think it's still in use. The recovery now checks whether the recorded process is actually dead and, if so, removes the leftover lock so the writer can proceed without waiting for the timeout. This is an internal change to the SDK's file-based metadata store used by the Freebuff CLI's BYOK feature, affecting only the local locking behavior behind the /byok commands. You will notice that if a Freebuff process holding the connection settings lock crashes, the next writer recovers the lock on its own instead of requiring you to manually delete connections.lock from the configuration directory.

10c969706881170ce54df95709887b58e32ed911.title: Landing screen ad fetch is gated by banner height floor
10c969706881170ce54df95709887b58e32ed911.summary: The Freebuff landing screen now derives its ad-hook options from `landingAdOptions`, which sets `enabled` to `terminalHeight >= LANDING_AD_MIN_HEIGHT` (18), so the ad banner is dropped and no ad is fetched on terminals shorter than 18 rows. The previous hardcoded enabled: true call is replaced by this height-gated path, and `useGravityAd` now calls the extracted `shouldHideGravityAds` helper to apply the same compact-height rule. The landing-screen comment notes that a fetched-but-undrawable ad would be served and never acknowledged, counting against the user in the ad-signal detector.
10c969706881170ce54df95709887b58e32ed911.evidence: In `cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx` the diff adds `LANDING_AD_MIN_HEIGHT = 18`, exports `landingScreenDrawsAds` (returns `terminalHeight >= LANDING_AD_MIN_HEIGHT`) and `landingAdOptions` (sets `enabled` from that check), and replaces the previous hardcoded useGravityAd({ enabled: true, ... }) call with `useGravityAd(landingAdOptions({ terminalHeight, placementIds }))`. In `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts` the inline `shouldHideAds` expression is replaced by a call to a new exported `shouldHideGravityAds` helper that computes `!enabled || (terminalHeight <= 17 && !isFreeMode)`.

10c969706881170ce54df95709887b58e32ed911.text: The Freebuff landing screen now stops trying to fetch and show a sponsored text ad on terminals that have fewer than 18 rows of space (roughly less than 18 lines tall). Instead of always attempting to load an ad and then being unable to draw it, the landing screen only turns on the ad slot when there is enough room to actually display the banner, and the shared ad-loading helper that other screens use now applies the same height check. This prevents an ad from being counted as shown when it never appears on screen, which previously could have affected how the user's ad-viewing behavior is measured. This change is live today for Freebuff users on any terminal window shorter than 18 rows.

c5c0acc93f8fec48e0f7f78c536c4ed6dea74a2c.text: Freebuff 0.2.7 ships a couple of small, practical changes. The streak status line now labels clock times as '(your time)' so a reset hour shown in your local clock is not mistaken for server time, and it falls back to a shorter unlabelled form when the terminal is too narrow to fit it. The agent runtime now checks the agent's to-do list when a turn ends on follow-up suggestions, and if the list is still part done it sends a nudge message instead of stopping, so an interrupted task resumes without you having to type 'continue' (up to a small per-prompt limit). A new model-image support lookup also consults a server-side catalog row when the compiled model list does not know a model, so a text-only model no longer receives image input and gets refused by its upstream.

79da3da895e8c3a3baa19b0b58d7d8fdd6e5682d.text: When you pick a model that only Freebuff's own server catalog knows about (not one baked into the app), the assistant now correctly asks that catalog whether the model can see images, instead of guessing. Previously, text-only models that the app didn't already know about were told the model could accept images, so the assistant sent picture data anyway and the model rejected the whole message, which broke multi-step image threads 104 times in the first half hour. This only affects you when you're using a model that isn't in the locally bundled model list. There's nothing you need to do, and you should no longer see image-based prompts fail on supported surfaces.

dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.9 release with SDK and ad hardening
dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.summary: The Freebuff CLI release manifest was bumped from 0.2.8 to 0.2.9, bundling a terminal-output sanitization pass, landing-screen ad gating by an 18-row banner floor, and a re-enabled sponsored-command git refusal walk. Gated the landing-screen ad banner behind an 18-row terminal floor and routed the ad hook through landingAdOptions so no auction runs where nothing can be drawn.
Sanitized model commands and captured tool output before terminal rendering via sanitizeTerminalOutput in the tool-block and terminal-command components.

dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.text: The Freebuff CLI 0.2.9 release strengthens security and stabilizes ad behavior in the terminal, with the changes centered on the read_url tool, the landing-screen ad banner, and command safety for sponsored runs. Security hardening for read_url: The `read_url` tool now connects only to an address it has just validated, so a hostname can no longer pass the safety check with one answer and then connect to a private address with a different answer (DNS rebinding). Every redirect hop is re-checked, and more non-routable address ranges are refused. Under Bun with a proxy configured, the proxy-friendly global fetch is still used, so that case keeps working. read_url now passes only the `url` and `max_chars` parameters forward, blocking callers from overriding the host's transport or safety options. Landing screen ads behave correctly: On terminals shorter than 18 rows, the landing screen no longer fetches an ad it cannot draw; the ad fetch is now gated by the actual banner height floor, so a served-but-invisible slot no longer counts against your render ratio. Terminal output is cleaned before display: Captured command output and tool results are sanitized of terminal escape sequences (clipboard writes, window titles, cursor moves) before they are rendered, so text from a fetched page or a repo's test script cannot hijack the terminal. Sponsored-run command safety: The safety check now refuses command lines it cannot fully read (deeply nested wrappers, unreadable -EncodedCommand and -File forms) instead of letting them through, and it now refuses git history- and configuration-moving subcommands like commit, push, checkout, and reset during an in-place sponsored run; it also refuses entering WSL, touching databases, and starting or pushing containers. Users who run Freebuff in the terminal get a slightly safer read_url tool against DNS tricks and see cleaner, non-manipulable output from commands and tool results. Sponsored-run participants benefit from refusals that now stop unreadable and git-history-moving commands before they execute. One visible side effect for Freebuff users on very short terminal windows is that the landing ad banner may be dropped entirely to give the model picker more room.
