86909c74659beeca8c5d9fb4120644e1d878709f.title: Followup turn nudge resumes tasks left unfinished mid-list
86909c74659beeca8c5d9fb4120644e1d878709f.summary: A new `decideFollowupTodoNudge` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/followup-todo-nudge.ts` inspects the in-memory message history when a step is about to end the turn on `suggest_followups`. If the agent's `write_todos` list written during the current user prompt has at least one completed item but still has open items, the runtime pushes a `FOLLOWUP_TODO_NUDGE_TAG`-tagged user message back into history and keeps the turn going instead of yielding control. The decision is capped at `MAX_FOLLOWUP_TODO_NUDGES` (3) per prompt and stops early if the list is unchanged since the last nudge, so a blocked or waiting turn can still hand back to the user. The `run-agent-step.ts` caller gates this only behind an explicit `task_completed`/`end_turn` so a genuinely finished task is left alone.
86909c74659beeca8c5d9fb4120644e1d878709f.evidence: New file `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/followup-todo-nudge.ts` adds `decideFollowupTodoNudge`, `followupTodoNudgeMessage`, `FOLLOWUP_TODO_NUDGE_TAG`, `MAX_FOLLOWUP_TODO_NUDGES`; the `run-agent-step.ts` hunk imports those symbols and pushes a tagged user message onto `agentState.messageHistory` when a turn would end on `suggest_followups` while the agent's to-do list is part done.

86909c74659beeca8c5d9fb4120644e1d878709f.text: When the assistant stops in the middle of a multi-step task and shows you a "Continue?" card, it now checks its own to-do list and, if items are still unfinished, automatically keeps working instead of pausing and waiting for you to type a reply. The runtime only restarts the turn if the list still has both finished and open items, and it gives up after three attempts or if the list stops changing, so a genuinely blocked task still hands control back to you. This applies to anyone using the Freebuff assistant, and in day-to-day use it means fewer mid-task stops that leave you having to nudge an incomplete job back to life.

c5c0acc93f8fec48e0f7f78c536c4ed6dea74a2c.text: This Freebuff CLI release (0.2.7) adds two user-facing changes. First, the status line under your daily Freebucks streak perk now labels clock times as yours, such as "11:00 AM (your time)" so readers east of Pacific time stop mistaking the next-streak-day reset for server time, and on narrow terminals the label is dropped to keep the line rather than hiding it. Second, when the agent ends its turn by offering follow-up suggestion cards, the runtime checks the agent's own to-do list, and if there are completed items but still unfinished steps, it sends the agent back to work (up to three nudges per prompt) instead of leaving a half-done task for you to type "continue"; a to-do list with no completed item is treated as a proposal, not interrupted work, and is not nudged. The release also bumps the package version to 0.2.7; two other changes were left out of this list because a check discredited their summary, and the available release evidence is otherwise incomplete.

The status line now drops the '(your time)' label on a narrow row rather than hiding the line, and a Pacific midnight keeps no label, matching tests for the Dubai odd-hour case and the compact fallback. c5c0acc93f8fec48e0f7f78c536c4ed6dea74a2c.text: Freebuff 0.2.7 is a smaller update that focuses on two things: making the streak bonus display clearer, and stopping the agent from cutting off early when there are still open to-dos. First, the streak status line under your perk note on the landing screen now shows clock times labeled as "(your time)" for regions east of Pacific, so a bonus that lands at an odd hour is not mistaken for server time. The line also tries a compact form before hiding completely, so a narrower terminal keeps the status rather than dropping it. Second, when the agent ends its turn on a "continue with the next step" card while its own to-do list is part done, the runtime now checks that to-do list and can nudge the agent back to work instead of stopping. It only does this per user prompt, only when at least one to-do is complete, and it stops after a capped number of nudges, leaving an explicit task completion alone. For you, this means the streak counter text is less confusing across time zones, and the coding agent is less likely to pause mid-task on a suggestion card while there is still work its own to-do list says is unfinished. The evidence for model changes in this release is incomplete, so this roll-up only covers the streak display and the follow-up nudge behavior.

44c800d2617286631654dfd4d3c7b2b0e8e4d6b4.text: Freebuff 0.2.6 makes MiMo 2.6 Flash the default AI model you get when you start the CLI or open Freebuff in a browser, replacing the previous default. Beyond that, a new device-signing flow ties catalog, session and completions requests to this install, and a fetchId is attached to each such request so the server can link them to the catalog a handle came from.

620431f033f609c7b33a7479b9b7cec3e0bea6f2.title: CLI model switch quotes first-tab discount on replacement
620431f033f609c7b33a7479b9b7cec3e0bea6f2.summary: freebucksOf in cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts now selects the account surface per session: 'desktop' for active sessions owning the first-tab discount reservation, 'single' for legacy trial sessions, and passes that to firstTabQuoteForSession so the replacement quote reflects the discount the ended purchase releases. 620431f033f609c7b33a7479b9b7cec3e0bea6f2.text: When you switch your active model to a new one in the CLI, the previous model's purchase is ended first, releasing any first-tab discount that was tied to it. The system now makes sure the price shown for the replacement model reflects that released discount. This affects Freebuff CLI developers who switch models mid-session and were previously shown the full price for the next model. You will see the discounted price quoted for the new model when you switch, and any sibling CLI instance that does not own the discount reservation will continue to see the full price.

44c800d2617286631654dfd4d3c7b2b0e8e4d6b4.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.6 makes MiMo 2.6 Flash the default AI model and adds new capabilities to Freebucks, the pay-as-you-go credit system. The release swaps the recommended starter model from GLM 5.3 Flash to MiMo 2.6 Flash, which the team says balances speed and image-support features, and updates the model picker lists in the CLI and README accordingly. Freebucks now lets the CLI use a discount reservation when switching models, so a new model pick is quoted with the same discount the ending session had, rather than starting fresh without it. The model picker on every surface now lists paid-plan-only rows to accounts without a plan, showing them locked instead of hiding them, so you can see what a subscription would unlock and open the plans page directly from a locked row. These changes only affect users on Full access (US, Canada, UK, EU and select countries); limited-mode users in other regions still see the same three-model free pool and are unaffected. The release evidence does not establish broad speed, quality, or reliability gains beyond what each item explicitly states.

44c800d2617286631654dfd4d3c7b2b0e8e4d6b4.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.6 ships MiMo 2.6 Flash as the default model across
44c800d2617286631654dfd4d3c7b2b0e8e4d6b4.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.2.6 was released with the version field at freebuff/cli/release/package.json bumped from 0.2.5 to 0.2.6. The default model moved to MiMo 2.6 Flash on every surface: DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID and DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts now point to FREEBUFF_MIMO_V25_MODEL_ID, and LIMITED_FREEBUFF_HERO_MODEL_ID changed to the same, with MiMo 2.6 Flash moved ahead of GLM 5.3 Flash in the model picker ordering. The freebucks quote-on-switch path in cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts now releases the first-tab discount reservation when a user switches models mid-session, using the desktop purchase store for active CLI attempt sessions and the single-session store for legacy trial sessions. PREVIOUS_DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID was deliberately not bumped to FREEBUFF_MIMO_V25_MODEL_ID, so saved GLM picks are not silently rewritten onto the more expensive MiMo row.

44c800d2617286631654dfd4d3c7b2b0e8e4d6b4.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.6 makes MiMo 2.6 Flash the default AI model you see and use first, moving it ahead of GLM 5.3 Flash in the model list across the CLI, the web app, and the desktop app, while keeping GLM 5.3 Flash as the cheapest option to run. Freebucks pricing for the first tab discount is now quoted correctly when switching models mid-session instead of promising a discount that would not transfer. The catalog store now filters out models scheduled to open in the future so you never see or select a model that is not yet available on this device.

e32b322ebdcb417c7acb704627f1b9b9bc2017c9.title: Catalog mode signs requests with a per-device Ed25519 key
e32b322ebdcb417c7acb704627f1b9b9bc2017c9.summary: The CLI now generates one Ed25519 key pair per install and signs every catalog GET, session and completions request while a server catalog is held, attaching `x-freebuff-catalog-fetch`, `x-freebuff-device-key`, `x-freebuff-device-ts` and `x-freebuff-device-sig` headers; the catalog store now drops rows whose `opensAt` is still in the future before anything reads them, so an unopened row can never be listed, selected or sent. The SDK gains a `requestHeaders` hook threaded through `getModelForRequest` and the agent runtime so the CLI can inject those same headers on backend completions, with BYOK runs explicitly bypassing it.

e32b322ebdcb417c7acb704627f1b9b9bc2017c9.unknowns: The server-side endpoint that consumes the device-key registration and signature verification is not in this diff, so rollout and rotation behavior depends on server support landing separately. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Adds per-install Ed25519 device key generation, key file storage at mode 0o600, and best-effort signing of catalog, session and completions requests with the fetch id and device signature headers.
Drops rows that have not opened yet (opensAt after issuedAt) from the held catalog before any lookup, so they can never be listed, selected or sent.

e32b322ebdcb417c7acb704627f1b9b9bc2017c9.text: The CLI now creates a unique device key for each installation and uses it to cryptographically sign every request it makes when fetching and using the model catalog. When a user's model list is fetched from the server, unopened (future-dated) models are immediately removed before the list is shown or used, so they can never be accidentally selected or run. This strengthens security for users on the new catalog mode by binding each device to its requests, but most users won't notice a difference in daily use aside from improved model list reliability; the changes are live today for installations using the server-driven catalog path.

83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.title: Deduplicate credentials read/parse failure logging
83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.summary: The credentials parse path in userFromJson and the read path in getUserCredentials now route errors through logCredentialsFailureOnce, which keys each failure by its message and profile so the same parse or read error is logged once per process instead of once per render, since the credentials file is re-read on every app-shell render. A new MAX_LOGGED_CREDENTIALS_FAILURES = 20 bound and a loggedCredentialsFailures Set prevent unbounded growth, and resetCredentialsFailureLogForTests is exported so the integration and keychain tests can clear the set between cases and assert that an unreadable file logs once per distinct failure rather than once per read.
83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.evidence: In cli/src/utils/auth.ts, the catch blocks of userFromJson and getUserCredentials now call a new logCredentialsFailureOnce that deduplicates by key (parse:${profileName}:${errorMessage} and read:${message}) and caps logging at MAX_LOGGED_CREDENTIALS_FAILURES = 20, replacing the previous direct logger.error calls; a new exported resetCredentialsFailureLogForTests clears the in-memory set for tests.
83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.unknowns: The unknown is the production rate at which users run multiple CLI versions against the same credentials file, which the deduplication only mitigates at the cost of one line per distinct failure rather than total silence.

83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.text: The login file that the assistant checks is read repeatedly while you work, so when it could not be read or understood, the same error message used to get printed over and over again every time. Now it will only print that kind of problem once per login or read error per session, keeping your terminal from filling up with duplicate lines. This is an internal code cleanup with no effect on logging into the assistant or your account; you will not notice anything different in daily use.

055e9c3cd792ca332c6838f1f47c12415c638f54.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.5 tightens security around your login credentials and adds clearer handling when the system needs to confirm who you are. When you sign in, Freebuffer now automatically restricts the permissions on the file that stores your credentials so that only your user account can read or write it, and on systems where those restrictions do not apply (such as Windows), the step is skipped safely rather than causing an error. The same file-rewriting step also quietly fixes older installations that had left it readable by other accounts, repairing them the next time you start the app. If the app cannot read or parse that credentials file for any reason, it now logs the problem once instead of repeating the error message many times while you keep using Freebuffer. When you run into a session limit while signed in and then run into a session limit that is tied to account verification, the landing screen now tells you that an identity check is required and points you to the account page instead of offering the usual daily-reset retry time. Existing users are affected on their next launch; no action is required except that anyone who had a loose credentials file on a shared system gets more private storage automatically.

055e9c3cd792ca332c6838f1f47c12415c638f54.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.5 adds an identity-verification step before granting access to certain spending-limited accounts, and tightens security around how your login credentials are stored and read. When you hit a daily usage cap, the app now shows a friendlier screen with a clear countdown to the next reset and a link to upgrade; if the block is because your account needs ID verification instead, you see a separate message with a link to finish verifying rather than a countdown timer. Behind the scenes, your credentials file is automatically re-locked to private-only permissions on non-Windows systems after each read or write, and repeated failures to parse your credentials are now logged only once per distinct error instead of thousands of times per minute, which keeps log files readable and prevents slowdowns. The release also adds a one-line log when credentials cannot be read, instead of logging the same unreadable-file error on every screen render. Overall, you are more likely to see a stable, clearly worded message when access is blocked, your saved login stays protected by file permissions, and the app stops flooding logs when your credentials file is temporarily unreadable.

055e9c3cd792ca332c6838f1f47c12415c638f54.text: This release hardens account security and login, and clarifies the paywall screens you see when you run out of free sessions. The credentials file that stores your login is now forced to private permissions (owner read/write only) on startup and after every write, so a loose, shared-permission file from an older install is corrected automatically instead of staying world-readable; this tightening is skipped on Windows where those permission bits do not apply. To stop a noisy runaway condition where a stale or unparseable credentials file logged thousands of identical error lines per minute during normal typing of the app shell, each distinct parse/read failure is now logged only once per login session, capped at twenty different failures. The daily usage-limit screen now separates two cases: when your account must verify its identity first (shown as a distinct ID-verification notice without a midnight reset promise), the screen otherwise keeps explaining that the free daily allowance is full and resets at midnight Pacific with a link to the plans page. Available release evidence is incomplete for claims beyond these authentication, permission, logging, and paywall-screen changes, so no packaging or catalog benefits are stated.

6fc184b984516641b8193b07ae4188145c94583d.title: Freebuff auth token moved to OS keychain at startup
6fc184b984516641b8193b07ae4188145c94583d.summary: The Freebuff CLI now loads the bearer token from the OS credential store (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service) via Bun.secrets before anything reads credentials. cli/src/utils/auth-token-store.ts is the new store module exposing bunSecretStore, getCachedKeychainToken, setCachedKeychainToken, moveTokenToKeychain, loadStoredAuthToken and resolveSecretStore, with KEYCHAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 2_000 bounding every keychain call. cli/src/index.tsx calls await loadStoredAuthToken() during startup, and cli/src/utils/auth.ts migrates existing installs: saveUserCredentials moves the file token into the keychain, clearUserCredentials deletes the keychain item too, and a keychain-pointer profile (tokenStore: 'keychain', no authToken) reads the token from the in-memory cache instead of the file. The file keeps the profile and stays owner-only, so a failed or unavailable keychain leaves the token in the file without logging anyone out.

6fc184b984516641b8193b07ae4188145c94583d.text: The Freebuff CLI now saves your login token in your operating system's built-in password manager (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or Linux Secret Service) when you launch it, instead of leaving it in a plain text file on your computer. This is live today for Freebuff users. You should notice nothing different beyond the first launch, which silently moves your existing token into the OS password store; the local file stays as a backup, so if the password manager can't be reached (for example on a headless server or over SSH), you stay logged in normally.

8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 stores auth token in OS keychain
8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 moves the Freebuff auth token out of the owner-readable credentials.json file into the operating system keychain via a new auth-token-store.ts module that wraps Bun.secrets with a 2s timeout. loadStoredAuthToken() runs at startup in cli/src/index.tsx before any credentials read, moving the token on first save and resolving the stored keychain pointer on later launches, while keeping a fallback path that leaves the token in the file if the keychain is unavailable (headless Linux, locked keychain, CI) so logins are not lost. Because the token file now holds only a tokenStore:'keychain' marker and an optional authToken, userFromJson and saveUserCredentials were extended to honor that pointer, and clearUserCredentials also deletes the keychain item. Codebuff is unaffected by design, since its credentials.json remains shared with the Node-based SDK.

8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 now keeps your login token in the operating system's password locker (the macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or the Linux Secret Service) instead of leaving it in a plain credentials file. When you install or update to 0.2.4, the CLI moves the token that was already in credentials.json into that keychain store, so anything else on your computer cannot read it as easily. If the keychain is unavailable (a headless Linux box, a locked keychain over SSH, or a CI runner), the token simply stays in the owner-only credentials.json file, so a keychain failure never logs you out. The credentials file is also clamped to owner-only permissions on macOS and Linux, and that permission check now runs on every launch so older installs are tightened up automatically. The only behavior change is where the token lives; nothing about signing in, signing out, switching models, or running a chat session has changed. Available release evidence is limited to this auth-token change, so other catalog or model-picker items in the wider diff are not confirmed as shipped in 0.2.4.

The update improves how the up and down arrow keys move through your conversation history and edit suggestions. When you recall a previous message by pressing the up arrow and then start editing it, the next up and down arrows now correctly continue paging through history instead of trying to move the text cursor. This prevents the awkward situation where, after recalling a historical entry, you cannot reach the older messages because the arrow keys switch to cursor-movement behavior. The change also keeps arrow-key suggestions from interfering when slash commands or mentions are open. Users typing in the terminal chat input are the ones who will notice smoother and more predictable text navigation.

0cb910451c1b774876b017cf60f059ed6e9f2e82.text: This release is a packaging bump (0.2.11 to 0.2.12) that updates the Freebuff CLI installer; the version label itself changed, and the release notes carry only a version bump with two prior README model-catalog additions and a Freebucks timezone handling change as the user-facing notes. The final catalog state confirms the picker now includes /todo along with the regular model list, and the limited-access catalog was widened so Space Bunny Alpha shows up for limited users; the model list adds Space Bunny Alpha and retires DeepSeek V4 Pro from the deep-reasoning slot in favor of GLM 5.3 Flash. The Freebucks timezone change means the CLI no longer trusts a wrong or remote clock: it skips reporting a timezone when the machine is SSH/dev-container based or when the OS reports a fixed-offset zone instead of the user's real location, so daily Freebucks resets follow your actual day instead of your host's. Other changes are infrastructure-only: BigQuery tracing adds lookup columns and a stable dedupe key, ad-serving telemetry gains a precomputed-score experiment and geo-tier fields, error logging now truncates oversized SQL statements and params so Postgres failures actually reach logs, the SDK refuses to run remote agents whose code or MCP servers come from untrusted publishers, the Windows Git-Bash finder now also locates Git installed by GitHub Desktop, and local dev config got new ignored credential files for billboard asset storage. Everyday impact is limited to users of Space Bunny Alpha in limited mode, people who were getting the wrong Freebucks reset time while working over SSH or in a remote container, and anyone relying on Freebuff Desktop's billboard ad slots, plus contributors whose local test setup now isolates real API keys; the rest is backend reliability and ad-serving instrumentation. To summarize plainly: the headline is a version-number bump, and the only things users actually notice are Space Bunny Alpha becoming available in limited mode and Freebucks resets now following your real timezone instead of your host's.

Telemetry now ships the npm wrapper's version via the `CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_VERSION` environment variable.

03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.11 is a packaging release that bumps the launcher staging and manifest version used to install updates. The launcher is the small piece of code that downloads a new Freebuff build, moves it into place, and starts it. This release makes the install step leave a failed update in its staging folder (instead of re-downloading it) and lets a later launch adopt a staged update that an earlier process downloaded but never installed, so closing the terminal window no longer leaves a full extra copy of the binary behind. It also records a manifest of the staged files so the next launch can verify them and adopt only the newest eligible update, then clean up old staging folders. A new MCP fixture and end-to-end test model a parameterized tools server (like Roblox Studio’s) and assert that the schema the model sees lists every required argument and that an empty object is sent for a zero-argument tool. The release notes the launcher version is now passed as an environment variable so launch telemetry can tell installs that can adopt deferred updates from pinned builds. Available release evidence shows the supported behavior; two other changes were left out of the list because a check discredited their summary, so only what the source hunks and reviewed window items establish is in this release.

d71a831b3a7a5b66a7a100a47a69c2c6bcc70d82.text: Freebuff 0.2.8 is a maintenance release that hardens how terminal output is displayed and cleans up ad-serving plumbing, with no new AI models or major features. The most user-visible change is a new terminal text sanitizer: commands and their output that the assistant runs are now stripped of terminal escape sequences (such as clipboard-manipulating OSC 52 codes, window-title escapes, and carriage-return progress-bar redraws) before they are shown in the terminal, so rogue scripts or fetched pages can no longer hijack the user's clipboard or garble the display. The landing screen now shows a clearer 'Account unavailable' message that carries the server's ban verdict verbatim, and the spend-limited screen splits the daily provider-spend cap from identity verification so an identity-verification request no longer reads like a budget limit. The ad auction request was consolidated into a single builder that always sends a shared browser-like user agent and device info, so every ad caller now forwards the same targeting fields and cannot quietly omit one. Two ad-related constants files (a spend-ceiling notice module and a Cloudflare Worker egress detector) were removed from the published common package, and the release packaging version was bumped from 0.2.7 to 0.2.8. The available release evidence does not establish any new model, picker, quota, Freebucks, or sponsored-run behavior for this release.

c5c0acc93f8fec48e0f7f78c536c4ed6dea74a2c.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.7 (2026-10-01) ships a version bump plus three user-visible fixes: streak-clock label handling, model image-support detection, and agent followup-to-do nudging. Lead / Core Additions: This release updates the Freebuff CLI to version 0.2.7 and bundles three behavior changes around the streak clock, model image support, and agent task completion. Concrete Highlights: First, the next-streak-day clock time now shows in your own clock with a "(your time)" label so non-Pacific users no longer mistake server time for local time; in a narrow terminal the label drops out before the status line disappears entirely. Second, a model only the server's catalog knows is now correctly treated as text-only when it cannot accept images, preventing upstream "Bad Request" failures that were breaking every step of affected threads. Third, when an agent finishes a turn on a follow-up card while its own to-do list is still partly done, the runtime now nudges it back to work, up to three times per prompt, instead of stopping short and leaving you to type "continue". Users outside Pacific time read streak timing in their own clock without guessing (Dubai reports of an odd "after 11:00 AM" prompt this fix). Threads using a server-catalog-only text-only model no longer fail on screenshots replayed across steps. Free sessions that stopped mid-plan on a follow-up card now continue toward the requested task instead of pausing on you. The release evidence is complete for these changes; the two omitted items were discredited and are not described. The packaging commit only advances the version label from 0.2.6 to 0.2.7.

dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.text: This Freebuff CLI 0.2.9 release strengthens two safety and display areas. First, the terminal now strips hidden escape sequences (like OSC 52 clipboard writes and window-title changes) from all command output and AI-generated text before it is drawn, so a script or fetched page can no longer rewrite your clipboard, retitle your window, or move the cursor on screen. Second, the ad system no longer fetches ads on the landing screen when the terminal is too short to show the banner (below 18 rows), and a separate server-side change makes the command-checker used by sponsored runs refuse to execute lines it cannot fully read (deeply nested wrappers, undecodable PowerShell scripts, and script-file commands), asking the user to run those commands directly instead. Together, these changes reduce both screen hijacking and the risk that an untrusted repository's scripts can trigger an ad slot that nobody sees. Concrete highlights: a new terminal-sanitizer utility removes terminal control sequences from command output, AI tool results, and inline ad text so invisible bytes are cleaned before rendering; the landing-screen ad hook is gated to only fetch when terminal height is at least 18 rows; and the sponsored-run command walk fails closed on command lines it cannot finish reading (wrappers nested past a limit, an -EncodedCommand that will not decode, and a -File script whose contents are off the line), refusing them rather than passing them through. Everyday impact: when you view AI agent output that contains a URL, a fetched web page, or a repository's own test script, any embedded terminal escape bytes are stripped, so the visible text you read is exactly what is printed and no hidden control can alter your terminal session. On terminals shorter than 18 rows the landing screen no longer attempts to load an ad for a banner it cannot display, and when a sponsored (ad-supported) run hands the agent a command line that contains unreadable nesting, it now stops and asks you to run those commands yourself instead of executing something it cannot fully inspect.

44c800d2617286631654dfd4d3c7b2b0e8e4d6b4.text: This release switches Freebuff's default AI model to MiMo 2.6 Flash for new users on the CLI, desktop, and web surfaces, while keeping GLM 5.3 Flash as the cheapest option and making MiMo 2.6 Flash the featured choice for the limited (non-US/Canada/EU) access tier. A new device-signing step is added so that when the model catalog is fetched, each request from your install is identified and signed by a per-machine key, and catalog rows scheduled to open later are hidden until they actually become available, with a fresh catalog refetched automatically when the server reports it is stale. The model picker now lists plan-only rows to accounts without a paid plan (locked rather than hidden) so the upgrade path is visible from the picker itself, and pricing is sent back as a server verdict per viewer rather than being guessed client-side. For multi-session CLI usage, a model switch releases the prior purchase's first-tab discount reservation so the replacement quote includes the discount, matching the shared desktop purchase store.

055e9c3cd792ca332c6838f1f47c12415c638f54.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.5 is a small update focused on keeping your login secure and cleaning up confusing messages when your free plan runs low on usage. When you sign in, the app now locks down where it stores your login file so other people on the same computer can't peek at it (it sets the file to be readable only by you), and if an older version left it more open, this version tightens it the next time you open the app. The app also used to repeat the same login error messages over and over (dozens of times per second) when something was wrong with your sign-in file, which spammed logs and slowed things down; now it logs each unique problem only once. Finally, when you hit your free daily usage cap, the screen you see is being prepped to look different for a specific situation where you need to verify your identity first (that's handled separately from the normal 'come back tomorrow' message), so the wording on screen should no longer mix up identity checks with regular usage limits. If you just use the app normally and hit your daily free limit, nothing else about the experience changes in this update. The available release evidence is incomplete for the broader identity-verification flow, so only the cleanup of repeated error logging and the tighter login file permissions are clearly confirmed as shipped behaviors.

8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 introduces a server-driven model catalog so the list of free AI models, their prices, and availability can be updated without requiring a new app download, alongside moving your login token out of a plain text file and into your computer's secure keychain storage. The model picker now reflects what the server decides is available in real time, including daily session limits and promotional offers, and the app automatically uses the correct model root when a catalog is present or falls back to the older per-model roots when it is not. Your login token is now stored in the OS keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or Linux Secret Service) instead of credentials.json, with a fallback to the file if the keychain is unavailable so you are never locked out. Sessions now report richer country-verification and plan-upsell information, and a country verification prompt only appears when verifying can actually change your access. Catalog-only models are unreachable when the catalog cannot be fetched, and the app refreshes the catalog after a stale-handle error using the new handle for the same model. If you are not on Freebuff, none of this applies, since the keychain and catalog features are Freebuff-only.

985c872eb8d43f538ab77d933ef7c43125d100ff.text: This release improves how the chat input responds to your keyboard, specifically making arrow keys behave more predictably when you recall a previous message from history. Previously, after pulling up an old message with the up arrow and lightly editing it, the arrow keys could get confused about whether they should move your text cursor or keep paging through history; now the app remembers that the current draft came from a recalled history entry and keeps paging history with up and down until you make a more deliberate edit. The change makes the up and down arrow keys consistently navigate your message history when the input is empty or holds an unedited recalled message, and otherwise move the text cursor as expected, so switching between browsing past messages and editing the current one feels smoother and less error-prone.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.2 tightens BYOK handling: `/byok update` can now take an environment variable name after a changed base URL, so you can point an existing connection at a new endpoint without losing the key, and the CLI tells you which variable is missing or rejected instead of giving a generic error. When a free daily session limit is spent, the session stops and shows when the model opens again instead of silently switching you to another model. Validation also reports HTTP status codes and, for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, warns when your chosen model id is not in the endpoint's model list and lists some that are. A test-guard CI change now fails the build when a suite stops contributing tests or selects no files, and a test fix prevents a postgres.js query from hanging by awaiting it inside the assertion. 64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.1 adds a compact summary of your terminal setup to ad and session requests, so the service can better understand how you're using the CLI in the terminal. When you use Freebuff (the free, ad-supported coding assistant), the program now sends a brief descriptor with your ad and session requests that includes your terminal type (like iTerm, VS Code, or Terminal.app), your window size, whether you're in a CI environment, and whether you're connected over SSH. The program also counts how you entered each prompt (typed text vs. pasted text), and attaches those counts to your run metadata. Ad requests now get consistent device and environment details, and a one-time check at launch records your terminal's color support. Error messages now cover two new cases: when DeepSeek's model declines a request because of a content filter, and when OpenAI's model declines because of a cybersecurity safeguard, pointing you to retry with a different model. e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.0 is a tuning and onboarding update. The main change is that several of the more expensive AI models now cap their reasoning level at 'high' instead of the maximum setting. Testing showed the top level cost noticeably more in wait time for only a small gain in how deeply the model thinks, so the default was lowered and the model lists were adjusted. Freebucks handling now distinguishes between multi-user purchases and single legacy trials when showing your credit balance.

e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.title: Freebuff CLI 0.1.11 release bump
e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.summary: The Freebuff CLI release manifest at `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` was bumped from `0.1.10` to `0.1.11`. This release packages the truncated-write guard shipped in `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/truncated-write-guard.ts` and wired through `processFileBlock` and `tool-executor.ts`, which refuses file edits cut off mid-generation and logs `file_write_guard` to Axiom via `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`. The version field is the only source change in this commit; the functional guard itself landed in the earlier member commit.

e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.text: This release adds a safety check that stops the assistant from saving a file when its output gets cut off mid-sentence. New files: a guard module in the agent runtime, an allowlisted telemetry event (file_write_guard) so refusals are recorded in Axiom with only content-free details, plus docs and tests. Concrete changes: when a tool call's arguments are incomplete (a JSON prefix that never closes, like an unclosed string or bracket), the runtime now returns an explicit 'nothing was written' error instead of the generic retry hint, and does not echo the partial text back; and when a write_file would replace an existing file of 30+ lines with a copy under 60% of its size that leaves brackets open where the current file balances them, processFileBlock refuses the write and logs file_write_guard/truncated_rewrite_refused. Everyday impact: if your session hits the output limit or the connection drops while the assistant is writing a file, the file on disk is left unchanged and you are told the call was refused, rather than receiving a truncated half-written file; you are guided to use smaller str_replace edits or to resend complete content. Tests assert the two refusal shapes and the telemetry allowlist, confirming the guard is wired in, though telemetry visibility itself depends on operator settings for Axiom. No other features, models, or billing changes are established by the evidence; the available release evidence is complete only for this truncated-write guard.

The two other modified files are `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts` and `common/src/types/subscription-costs.ts`, which add billing-interval and MRR helpers plus the `SubscriptionBillingIntervals` aggregate type for /web/admin/subscriptions reporting.

The accompanying source-level functional change is the BYOK reasoning-effort feature (member 41c03830), implemented across `cli/src/commands/byok.ts`, `cli/src/utils/byok.ts`, `cli/src/utils/settings.ts`, `common/src/constants/reasoning-effort.ts`, `sdk/src/byok.ts`, `sdk/src/impl/byok-request.ts`, and `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts`, which adds a `/byok effort` command and per-provider request-body translation so a BYOK run can request low/medium/high reasoning effort, persisted as `byokReasoningEffort` and retried once without the field if rejected.

f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.10 lets you pick how much 'thinking' a BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) run does, per run, instead of leaving it to the provider's default. You can choose low, medium, or high reasoning effort with a new `/byok effort` command, and that choice is saved in your settings and applied only to the BYOK connection you selected. The pick is translated into the right request field for each provider: OpenRouter gets a `reasoning.effort` value, Anthropic gets a thinking budget added to its max output tokens, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints (including Gemini and most others) get a `reasoning_effort` value. If a provider or model rejects that field with a 400 error naming it, the run automatically retries once without it, and that refusal is remembered for that specific connection so later steps in the same run do not ask again. Editing the connection later (which changes its revision) resets that memory, so a changed connection gets a fresh chance at the request field. Also in this release, the Freebuff subscription catalog and admin cost-reporting tooling now split paying subscribers by monthly and yearly billing cadence, counting a yearly plan as one-twelfth of its annual price for MRR reporting, though these are backend operator/admin changes rather than new user-facing subscription options. The release also bumps the shipped package version from 0.1.9 to 0.1.10.

afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.text: Freebuff 0.1.9 adds GPT-6.1 Sol to the model picker as a temporary free-for-US, paid-elsewhere option capped at one session per day for every account, and updates the picker and documentation to state that limit clearly. The CLI now tracks whether someone who clicks a Freebuff ad comes back to the assistant by treating their next typed prompt as the 'return' signal (since a terminal cannot detect window focus), reporting how long they were away. Advertisers whose links in sponsored procedures had been arriving untagged now get correct UTM labels applied to their own campaign URLs when they set them, or Freebuff's tags otherwise, with tagging skipped inside code blocks and for file downloads. The release also adds internal admission logic to enforce the one-session-a-day cap on GPT-6.1 Sol across all plans and surfaces, plus minor house-ad copy and model-catalog housekeeping. Final catalog state confirms GPT-6.1 Sol is in the free model picker, so it is the main user-facing addition, while the ad-return and UTM-tagging work are behind-the-scenes correctness fixes for advertising measurement.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.8 adds a new kind of sponsored ad slot that appears in your terminal while you are writing about launching, deploying, or demoing your work. The release also fixes how your daily streak bonus shows up: it now correctly lives in your daily Freebucks allowance (not your wallet), and the on-screen explanation says when it was added and when it will leave your allowance, which resolves earlier reports from users outside Pacific time that the bonus appeared missing. The landing screen also drops an old tier-change notice so the area below the model picker stays clean. The release bumps the shipped version from 0.1.7 to 0.1.8. Available release evidence is incomplete on any broader reliability, catalog, or billing claims beyond these items.

38cd1ed44428f573c4754d8e0cee868f2875b54e.text: This Freebuff CLI release (0.0.204) keeps your coding session safer when things go wrong behind the scenes. When the app crashes or the terminal is closed unexpectedly, your paid-for session time is now preserved so the next time you open the tool, it picks up where it left off instead of charging you again. Crash details are now captured locally and sent along on the next startup for debugging, rather than disappearing when the process exits. The chat interface stops a looping error where hiding ads could cause a React crash that killed your work, and signal handlers (like SIGTERM/SIGHUP) now route through a shared external-exit path that keeps your session alive instead of ending it. Overall, the release reduces the chance that a crash, terminal close, or signal kills both your run and your session credit, and helps the team see what went wrong after the fact.

dbc6a776fc0f8005806d797c00fe2c6caf1781c6.text: This release fixes a billing mix-up for paying Codebuff users. When a paying user ran out of their own Codebuff credits, the CLI incorrectly told them the failure was 'on us, not your account' instead of pointing them to refill their balance. The change adds a check so Codebuff's own out-of-credits message is handled by the normal out-of-credits flow rather than being misread as a Freebuff provider problem. This resolves a regression that mainly affected paying users running Codebuff in CLI lite mode.

a23f0ae16d9c7d69458dce20ca74178bc530ffb8.text: Freebuff CLI version 0.0.203 improves how the assistant manages long conversations when you go back to edit or restart them. When the assistant summarizes a long chat to fit within size limits, large images and binary data embedded in tool results are now skipped instead of being copied in full, which previously could waste time and resources. Also, when you edit or continue a previous turn, the system now rewinds to the correct spot by counting only your actual prompts, not internal messages, so your edits apply to the right place in the conversation. Only your own prompt messages are used to decide where to cut the conversation, preventing accidental loss of too much history. This benefits users editing or restarting long coding sessions, especially ones with images or tool-heavy outputs. The available release evidence is incomplete about any broader packaging or rollout details.

f783139ae5607e7b53e6dd5608186d133930d7bd.text: This release focuses on advertising placements and resuming your previous session. The main update is that Freebuff now has a new way for partner advertisements to appear in the app, with two specific spots for single advertisers - one in the skill picker and one near the composer. These spots are reserved and can't be targeted through the normal self-service ad platform. The release also fixes a problem where if you had an older version of the app running in the background and started a new version, it would sometimes try to sell you a second session even though your first one was still active and available. Now the new version recognizes your old session and resumes it instead, so you don't accidentally pay for two sessions. Overall, you get a slightly smoother experience when switching between versions and see partner-specific ad content in those dedicated spots.

baffcb89339ea373a63aa77202bec34e76f80444.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.200 is a security and access update for the free coding-assistant CLI. The main user-facing change is that GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro are now fully open to every full-access user, no longer restricted only to the US or paid accounts, while still locked behind a plan for limited-tier users. Sponsored runs - tasks paid for by an advertiser - got safer: they can no longer enter the Windows Subsystem for Linux, can no longer drop or reset databases, and can no longer build, start, stop, or remove your containers (for example, docker compose up now stops). Sponsored runs can also now declare and receive a single encrypted credential, like an API key, which gets injected into that run only and is hidden from logs and model output. A small clipboard fix also now warns Linux users when a copy only reached the terminal (not the clipboard) and tells them how to fix it. Tests also switched their default CPM-ad setting off, which only affects automated test runs, not production.

9f521ec5f2e38db447cafa0549633d728a284921.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.199 ships with three user-visible improvements. First, when you close or crash the terminal mid-session, Freebuff now resumes your unused free hour instead of making you start over and buy another one. Third, a new AI model, Solar Pro 4, has been added to the free model picker alongside Solar Mini 4, giving you another no-cost option supported by text ads.

3dd05d3b673ee4d6db441f3ff75480154b3d4a1f.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.198 changes how sponsored AI tasks run in your project folder. Instead of creating a separate git branch and worktree to test changes, a sponsored task now edits your real working files directly in place, and you get one new command, /ads:undo, to revert them. The old /ads:pull-request and /ads:remove-worktree commands are removed. When an ad-supported task runs this way, your own messages wait until it finishes, since it operates with its own memory and payment. The consent screen now tells you plainly that changes will be made to your files right now, and lists the exact steps the task will take. After a task ends, the CLI reports how many files were changed and reminds you of the undo command. A new Ctrl+O shortcut and an on-screen detail panel let you inspect a sponsored offer while it is active. The release also stops serving the old branch-based flow to this CLI entirely, so only the in-place behavior is supported going forward.

5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.text: This Freebuff release (0.0.197) is a small, focused update to the CLI that improves three day-to-day things: how your free-credit (Freebucks) discount is calculated, how the app browses past conversations, and how the app updates itself without interrupting what you're doing. First, your first-tab discount is now tied to the actual account that's paying for your current session (the Desktop purchase store) instead of a separate legacy tracker, so you see the right price when you click around. Second, a new 'History' shortcut (press H) and a read-only view let you browse saved transcripts at the landing screen or after a session ends, with the feedback prompt hidden while you're just reading. Third, Freebuff no longer replaces itself while you're still working: downloads wait for you to close the session (or the launcher waits for exit), and then it installs on the next quiet startup, skipping any downgrade of an update another window already installed. A couple of supporting tweaks keep the history viewer from wiping the running session and make the takeover prompt clearer when capacity is busy. The release evidence covers these specific behaviors only; anything not listed above (including a one-sentence item that was discredited) is not confirmed as shipped in 0.0.197.

6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.text: This release updates Freebuff CLI to version 0.0.196 with three main changes: the chat helper agent now uses the newer GPT-6 Luna model instead of GPT-5.6 Luna, the paid session on your launcher stays active when the launcher restarts to install an update instead of dropping you back to the model picker, and the advertising pipeline gains support for in-place sponsored runs along with a clearer error message when DeepSeek's content filter blocks a request. A new sponsored task mode lets an advertised setup edit your working files directly in the accepting conversation (no separate branch or commit), and the docs note a common test slowdown cause for developers. Ads and models get small wiring and catalog updates, none of which change everyday Freebuff usage.

6931512368f9e246683b095dd2bf8ff43a811af8.title: SDK recovers stale BYOK connection lock via PID check
6931512368f9e246683b095dd2bf8ff43a811af8.summary: `createBunByokMetadataStore`'s `withLock` now publishes the owning PID to an atomic lock candidate and uses `fs.link` to claim `connections.lock`, so a process killed between creating the lock file and writing its PID no longer leaves an unrecoverable lock. `sdk/src/impl/byok-lock.ts` adds `recoverByokLock`, which calls `recoverByokLock(lock)` on `EEXIST`: it reads the lock's owner, treats `EPERM` (including another user's process) as not dead, uses a loopback listener on port `49152 + (Number(owner) % 16384)` as a short-lived kernel-released reaper mutex keyed by the observed PID, and re-reads the owner under that mutex before unlinking the lock so it never expires a live PID by age or removes a successor's lock. Tests cover a crashed writer not blocking connection deletion, recovery preserving a live owner even when its lock is old, competing reapers not losing writes, and an operation that throws releasing its lock.
6931512368f9e246683b095dd2bf8ff43a811af8.evidence: New file `sdk/src/impl/byok-lock.ts` exports `recoverByokLock`; `sdk/src/byok.ts` imports it and calls `await recoverByokLock(lock)` from within the `withLock` method of `createBunByokMetadataStore` when `fs.link(candidate, lock)` throws `EEXIST`. The `withLock` implementation now writes `String(process.pid)` to a per-call `connections-lock-<uuid>.tmp` candidate with { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600 } and hard-links that candidate to `connections.lock` via `fs.link(candidate, lock)`, replacing the prior `fs.open(lock, 'nx')` + `handle.writeFile` approach.

6931512368f9e246683b095dd2bf8ff43a811af8.text: When you save a custom AI connection to Freebuff and another process is already using it, Freebuff now leaves a small note saying which program is holding it, then checks whether that program is still alive before deciding it's safe to take over. If your Freebuff suddenly closed while updating that connection, the system will no longer leave a stuck lock that blocks future edits. You won't see anything new in the app, but a previously frozen BYOK settings screen should clear up on its own, and removing a saved connection will work even if a past session crashed mid-update. This applies to anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK with their own provider connections.

f6c9bf23ecd733d05db82bdabd99521388488a73.title: Freebucks timezone header now filters remote-host and invalid zones
f6c9bf23ecd733d05db82bdabd99521388488a73.summary: The timezone header reported for Freebucks billing-timezone checks is no longer the raw Intl-resolved zone. It now passes through freebucksDeviceTimeZone, which drops zones the runtime cannot tell ('Etc/Unknown' and blanks), fixed-offset Windows zones parsed with DST off, and UTC that comes from a remote host (SSH, Codespaces, Gitpod, REMOTE_CONTAINERS, GITPOD_WORKSPACE_ID) or an unparseable TZ, so a dev container or SSH box no longer reports the image's UTC as the user's home day. freebucksTimeZoneHeaders now takes an optional FreebucksTimeZoneRuntime so callers and tests can inject the zone, platform and env instead of always reading the live process. The new tests assert each of those filtering cases and that a local machine genuinely set to UTC still reports UTC.

New exports: FreebucksTimeZoneRuntime, freebucksDeviceTimeZone; new env reads: REMOTE_CONTAINERS, GITPOD_WORKSPACE_ID; new constant ETC_OFFSET_ZONE = /^Etc\/GMT[+-]\d{1,2}$/.

1e49cb763a73d9381f5724a9f34264c0a7fb95df.title: SDK trust gate extends to MCP servers and registry id validation
1e49cb763a73d9381f5724a9f34264c0a7fb95df.summary: The trust gate now treats MCP servers listed by a remote agent template as executable content, refusing unpublished publisher templates that define them unless the publisher is trusted. `fetchAgentFromDatabase` validates the publisher, agent, and version segments against `PUBLISHED_ID_SEGMENT` and `PUBLISHED_VERSION` before building the registry URL, blocking ids that could rewrite the path. The `UntrustedAgentPublisherError` message and `hasExecutableContent` helper are exported for callers and tests.
1e49cb763a73d9381f5724a9f34264c0a7fb95df.evidence: The diff adds `hasExecutableContent` to `sdk/src/agent-publisher-trust.ts`, which treats both executable `handleSteps` source strings and the presence of MCP servers as executable content, and switches `checkRemoteAgentTemplateTrust` to call it instead of `hasExecutableHandleSteps`. `sdk/src/impl/database.ts` adds the `PUBLISHED_ID_SEGMENT` and `PUBLISHED_VERSION` regex constants and an early guard in `fetchAgentFromDatabase` that rejects IDs violating them before URL construction. New tests in `sdk/src/impl/__tests__/fetch-agent-publisher-trust.test.ts` assert that untrusted publishers with MCP servers are refused and that registry-path-rewriting IDs are refused before any fetch.
1e49cb763a73d9381f5724a9f34264c0a7fb95df.unknowns: The diff does not show a consumer wiring `hasExecutableContent` outside the trust module, and it is unclear whether any previously-accepted untrusted MCP-enabled template is expected to keep loading after this change.

1e49cb763a73d9381f5724a9f34264c0a7fb95df.text: The trust check for downloadable agents now also covers agents that connect to external tools (MCP servers): a remote agent from a publisher you haven't approved will be refused if it lists external tools or executable program code, not just if it includes custom code. The agent address is also checked before the request is sent, so a crafted publisher, agent, or version name can no longer redirect the lookup to a different agent on the registry. This closes a gap where pulling anyone's public agent could silently spawn external processes or connect to outside tools on your machine. Internal tooling change with no direct effect on end users unless they run ad-hoc remote agents, in which case untrusted ones that reach out to external servers or code will now be blocked by default.

c838c9d5a1601b11eefa74984610ab6ab49980e7.text: Starting October 1, Freebuff ties each streak day to your account's own timezone instead of always using Pacific time. 45917a419db7942c34b29fba5a262d91842edfa7.title: Context-pruner run tracking skip switches to exact name match
45917a419db7942c34b29fba5a262d91842edfa7.summary: The context-pruner skip logic in `loopAgentSteps` now parses the agent id with `parseAgentId` and compares only the `agentId` segment to `context-pruner` instead of substring-matching the whole id. This prevents any model-calling agent whose id merely contains the substring (such as `context-pruner-test-agent`) from receiving an untracked run id that the web API refuses, which previously failed that agent's first LLM call with a `runId Not Found` error. The untracked `untracked-` prefixed id is still minted only for the true `context-pruner` and its publisher-qualified form.
45917a419db7942c34b29fba5a262d91842edfa7.evidence: In `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`, the `loopAgentSteps` function imports `parseAgentId` from `@codebuff/common/util/agent-id-parsing` and replaces the substring check `agentTemplate.id.includes('context-pruner')` with an exact-name check `parseAgentId(agentTemplate.id).agentId === 'context-pruner'`.
45917a419db7942c34b29fba5a262d91842edfa7.unknowns: The diff does not show whether any other callers relied on the previous substring-based matching behavior.

changes.what: Replaced substring matching of `agentTemplate.id` against `context-pruner` with an exact `agentId` comparison via `parseAgentId` in `loopAgentSteps`.

45917a419db7942c34b29fba5a262d91842edfa7.text: A small piece of the assistant's task-management code now checks an agent's name exactly instead of looking for that name anywhere in a longer string. The change affects only the Freebuff engineering team's internal agent-runtime package. You will not notice any difference in your daily use of the assistant.

No other files in the diff read these new exports at this revision.

70a78466da2239b118a3891b0ccced51e1ac07bc.title: Scope programmatic scroll guard so wheel events still fire
70a78466da2239b118a3891b0ccced51e1ac07bc.summary: The `setScrollTop` helper wraps every `scrollbox.scrollTop` assignment in `cli/src/hooks/use-scroll-management.ts`, setting `programmaticScrollRef.current = true` before the write and resetting it in `finally`. Because OpenTUI emits scroll `change` synchronously and emits nothing for a no-op assignment, the old inline sets cleared the flag in the `handleScrollChange` listener by re-reading it, which let a no-op auto-scroll swallow the user's next wheel event; scoping the guard to the write keeps user input responsive. `animateScrollTo` now derives the target from the live `scrollHeight - viewport.height` for the `'latest'` value, and `scrollDown` forwards to `'latest'` when the target equals `maxScroll`.

70a78466da2239b118a3891b0ccced51e1ac07bc.text: The assistant now keeps the chat window stuck to the bottom when new messages arrive, but only when you are not actively scrolling. If you pause near the bottom and let the view follow the latest output, a tiny scroll of your mouse wheel immediately breaks free and lets you read earlier messages, instead of being silently dragged back down. This fixes the common frustration where you try to scroll up to inspect something, but the live feed hijacks the view each time it updates.

The original create logic was extracted into a shared helper called under the metadata lock, and add model copies an env: reference verbatim or reads and re-stores the saved secret so each model owns its key. A failed save rolls back its own copied key while leaving the source connection usable, matching the new tests in sdk/src/byok.test.ts.

2b4fd7db6a35ecfa22bbfdcdcce6913119b55120.text: The Freebuff SDK's BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) connection manager now lets you add a new model to an existing provider connection without re-entering your API key or provider URL. When you do this, it creates a fresh, independent entry for the new model that starts with the same settings (like its key and endpoint) but tracks its own limits, usage, and lifetime separately. Each saved model keeps its own key, so rotating or removing one will not affect the others. This is for developers building on top of Freebuff using the SDK, and it does not change the experience for people using the Freebuff app, web app, or desktop app directly.

bcb726800e42b55458879a15244d6d2f45e61956.title: Deferred update adoption across launcher restarts
bcb726800e42b55458879a15244d6d2f45e61956.summary: The launcher now records a completed deferred download in a staged.json manifest inside the per-pid staging directory, then on the next process start scans configDir for orphaned <tempDownloadDirName>-<pid> directories owned by dead launchers and installs the newest version whose files still match their recorded sha256 before spawning the binary. This closes the gap where closing the terminal (SIGHUP / CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT) killed the exit handler before installation, leaving users stuck on the old build; the staged.json manifest is written last and renamed into place so a killed launcher leaves no unverified directory to install. installStagedBinary gained a keepStagingOnFailure option so a failed exit-time install leaves the directory for the next launch to retry, and spawnInstalledBinary propagates CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_VERSION so launch telemetry can distinguish wrapper-based installs that cannot defer from ones that can.
bcb726800e42b55458879a15244d6d2f45e61956.evidence: cli/release-core/launcher.js adds a deferred-update adoption path: writeStagedManifest writes version/target/sha256 into staged.json; adoptOrphanedStagedUpdates reads orphaned <tempDownloadDirName>-<pid> dirs, matches file hashes, and installs the newest staged version before the binary starts; main() calls adoptOrphanedStagedUpdates() ahead of ensureBinaryReady(). cli/src/index.tsx emits CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_VERSION into App Launched telemetry; cli/src/types/env.ts and cli/src/utils/env.ts declare/read CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_VERSION.
bcb726800e42b55458879a15244d6d2f45e61956.unknowns: The rollout status of staged.json to all released npm wrappers and whether any older wrapper emits staged.json in a layout a newer launcher must still tolerate.

bcb726800e42b55458879a15244d6d2f45e61956.text: When a Freebuff update finishes downloading in the background and you close your terminal before the new version installs, the next time you open Freebuff it now picks up that completed download and installs it instead of starting over from scratch. You no longer get stuck on an older build just because closing the terminal window interrupted the install step. The launcher also cleans up leftover update files from previous sessions and refuses to install anything that was tampered with or left incomplete.

a8c632ee26b9700e7304d1e830fd4157ce3653ce.text: The Freebuff landing screen now always shows ads, even on short terminal windows. Previously, ad banners were hidden on terminals under 18 rows tall to make room for the model picker, but now ads always load from the moment you open the app. This is the screen that appears before you start a new coding session, and Freebuff treats ads there as required for funding, so the height-based suppression and the separate ad-options helper that depended on it were both removed. There is no visible effect for you unless your terminal is under 18 rows, where you will now see an ad banner that may scroll the model list. The change also inlined the ad-shown logic into the ad hook itself and removed a now-unused helper, but your Freebuff experience otherwise works the same as before.

af742b4afe363b3aafc8d7c7da50b4721dc658bb.title: SDK read URL fetches pin socket to validated address to close DNS
af742b4afe363b3aafc8d7c7da50b4721dc658bb.summary: The SDK's read URL tool now connects only to an address it validated in the same DNS resolution, rather than checking one answer and fetching on another that could differ. A new `pinnedFetch` transport in `sdk/src/tools/pinned-fetch.ts` issues the GET through `node:http`/`node:https` with a `lookup` set to `validatingLookup`, which resolves via `resolveAllowedAddresses` in `sdk/src/tools/ssrf.ts` and refuses the host if any answer is blocked. `sdk/src/run.ts` now passes only `url` and `max_chars` to `readUrl`, so a tool call can no longer supply transport or SSRF overrides. More non-routable ranges are refused (`::/96`, `198.18.0.0/15`, `fec0::/10`, `64:ff9b:1::/48`), and under Bun with an HTTP proxy configured the SDK falls back to Bun's own `fetch` so the proxy keeps working.
af742b4afe363b3aafc8d7c7da50b4721dc658bb.evidence: New file `sdk/src/tools/pinned-fetch.ts` implements `pinnedFetch`, which issues a GET via `node:http`/`node:https` with a `lookup` set to `validatingLookup`; `validatingLookup` calls `resolveAllowedAddresses` (in `ssrf.ts`) and hands `net.connect` only the addresses it just validated, closing DNS rebinding. `sdk/src/run.ts` route for `read_url` now destructures only `{ url, max_chars }` and calls readUrl({ url, max_chars, signal }), dropping host-supplied transport/lookup/isBlocked params. `sdk/src/tools/ssrf.ts` adds `EXTRA_BLOCKED_RANGES` (`::/96`, `198.18.0.0/15`, `fec0::/10`, `64:ff9b:1::/48`), exports `defaultLookup`, `unwrapHost`, `resolveAllowedAddresses`, and a new `AddressPolicy` type, and threads an injectable `isBlocked` policy through `assertUrlAllowed` and `resolveAllowedAddresses`. `sdk/src/env.ts` adds `isHttpProxyConfiguredFromEnv` and `PROXY_ENV_VARS`. Tests in `sdk/src/__tests__/read-url-dns-pinning.test.ts` assert pinning and rebinding refusal.
af742b4afe363b3aafc8d7c7da50b4721dc658bb.unknowns: The rollout of the new first-party-ad leg and the exact advertiser-facing behavior of the new dark-model leg in `ad-experiment` are not shown in this diff.

af742b4afe363b3aafc8d7c7da50b4721dc658bb.text: The assistant's 'read a web page' tool now does an extra safety check: before it opens a link you give it, it asks the internet's address book (DNS) which real web address the link actually points to, and it refuses to connect if that address is a private or internal one. This makes sure a sneaky public website can't redirect you through links to something hidden inside your own network, and it also blocks a few more internal-looking addresses it missed before. Developers building with the Freebuff SDK see tougher protection when their agents fetch URLs, and they no longer have to worry about a tool call accidentally sending traffic to a private server.

This affects Freebuff CLI users in terminals shorter than 18 rows, who will no longer trigger an ad auction for a slot that never renders. In everyday use the landing screen behaves the same otherwise: ads still appear and rotate whenever the banner is drawn, and the surface wire name and force-start behavior are preserved.

9a24ecd20f4d9e277f877907a9d6850d6382e882.text: The change strengthens what a paid-advertiser task running on your own machine is allowed to touch when it uses git: it now inspects git commands hidden inside wrappers like `bash -c "git commit"` or `cmd /c git commit`, and refuses history-changing ones like commit, reset, branch, stash, merge or checkout the same way it already refused WSL, destructive database and container commands. It also fails closed on anything it cannot fully read, such as a PowerShell `-File` pointing at a script or an `-EncodedCommand` that will not decode, blocking the whole line instead of letting it through unread. A small companion change caps how deep the redaction of credentials in tool output will chase nested data before it gives up and blanks the rest, so secrets buried very deep do not slip past.

cc9b5daf7055fd8c3a1095bfdbfc788014a7708d.text: Freebuff removed an AI model called Kimi K3 Eco from the list of models that paid subscribers can use with their monthly allowance, because the company that provided that model has retired it and no one can pick it anymore. This affects Freebuff's paid subscribers (the people on a monthly plan), not free users or anyone using the ad-supported tier. In everyday use, subscribers simply won't see or be offered that model anymore when choosing which AI to use, and the list they pick from now has seven models instead of eight.

a56263b791609357ec8bb7d3e2be4bbc9ed6a20a.title: Terminal output is sanitized before CLI rendering
a56263b791609357ec8bb7d3e2be4bbc9ed6a20a.summary: A new terminal output sanitizer is added in `common/src/util/terminal-safe-text.ts` as `sanitizeTerminalOutput`, which strips terminal escape sequences (OSC 52 clipboard writes, window titles, cursor moves) from captured process output and tool output before the CLI TUI draws it, keeping only the text after the last `` on each line to preserve the final redraw of a carriage-return progress bar. The sanitizer is now applied at every point the CLI renders tool output: the run_terminal_command tool component and its shared TerminalCommandDisplay, the tool-branch command preview, and the message-block helpers that update tool blocks, so pending `!` command output and streamed tool results no longer reach the renderer as raw bytes. New tests assert that command output and other tool output are stripped before drawing, that a clipboard write is removed while text is kept, and that a carriage-return progress bar keeps only its last redraw.

The export is consumed by cli/src/components/blocks/tool-branch.tsx (command preview now wraps `toolBlock.input.command.trim()` in `sanitizeTerminalOutput`), cli/src/components/terminal-command-display.tsx (rawCommand and rawOutput are now sanitized), cli/src/components/tools/run-terminal-command.tsx (input command is sanitized), and cli/src/utils/message-block-helpers.ts (`updateToolBlockWithOutput` sanitizes tool-block output for both `run_terminal_command` and other tools).

a56263b791609357ec8bb7d3e2be4bbc9ed6a20a.text: When the assistant runs a command in your terminal or shows output from a tool, the text it displays is now cleaned up before it appears on your screen. The cleanup strips out hidden terminal control codes that a command or file could otherwise sneak in, such as instructions that copy text to your clipboard or commands that quietly reposition the cursor, leaving only the plain text you intended to see. This applies to anyone using the Freebuff command-line tool, web assistant, desktop app, or software development kit whenever a command's results are rendered. Most users will notice nothing at all, except that progress bars behave correctly and no stray control characters appear in the output.

86909c74659beeca8c5d9fb4120644e1d878709f.title: Agent runtime nudges unfinished to-dos before ending turn on followup
86909c74659beeca8c5d9fb4120644e1d878709f.summary: A new check in `run-agent-step.ts` calls `decideFollowupTodoNudge` right before a step ends the turn on `suggest_followups`; when the agent's own to-do list for the current prompt is part done, the runtime pushes a tagged nudge message back into `agentState.messageHistory` and clears `shouldEndTurn` so the agent keeps working, because ending on follow-up cards while the list is unfinished stops a task the user asked to have finished (CodebuffAI/freebuff#1434). The decision is bounded by `MAX_FOLLOWUP_TODO_NUDGES` (3) per prompt, requires at least one completed list item, and only counts lists written during the current `USER_PROMPT` turn.
86909c74659beeca8c5d9fb4120644e1d878709f.evidence: New module `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/followup-todo-nudge.ts` exports `decideFollowupTodoNudge`, `followupTodoNudgeMessage`, `FOLLOWUP_TODO_NUDGE_TAG`, `MAX_FOLLOWUP_TODO_NUDGES`, `MAX_LISTED_TODOS`, `MAX_TODO_CHARS`, and `FollowupTodoNudgeDecision`, and is called from the `shouldEndTurn` gate in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` when the step's only forcing tool call is `suggest_followups`.
86909c74659beeca8c5d9fb4120644e1d878709f.unknowns: The exact wording of the nudge message shown to users is omitted from the diff as [freebuff product prompt text omitted].

86909c74659beeca8c5d9fb4120644e1d878709f.text: When the assistant reaches the end of its work and offers follow-up suggestions, it now checks its own to-do list and, if any items are still incomplete, keeps working instead of stopping. The assistant will continue up to three times per request, but only if it is making progress, so it no longer leaves tasks half-finished just because it offered helpful next steps. This affects end-users who use Freebuff to code, so you may notice the assistant staying on task through the entire list rather than pausing midway. No action is needed from you.

79da3da895e8c3a3baa19b0b58d7d8fdd6e5682d.title: Freebuff model image support reads server catalog overlay

79da3da895e8c3a3baa19b0b58d7d8fdd6e5682d.text: When the assistant is offered a model that only the service's online catalog knows about (one not baked into the app itself), it now asks that catalog whether the model can read images, rather than guessing. 83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.title: Deduplicate credentials failure logging in auth
83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.summary: In cli/src/utils/auth.ts, the credentials read/parse paths now route errors through a new `logCredentialsFailureOnce` helper that writes to the logger at most once per distinct failure, backed by `loggedCredentialsFailures` and capped by `MAX_LOGGED_CREDENTIALS_FAILURES = 20`, replacing the prior unconditional `logger.error` calls that fired on every read. This guards the render-time `getUserCredentials()` callers (useAuthQuery/useAuthState) from re-logging the same parse/read error on every frame, which the 2026-10-01 incident showed could produce tens of thousands of lines for a file this process cannot parse. The test file adds `resetCredentialsFailureLogForTests` to clear the dedupe state between cases.
83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.evidence: cli/src/utils/auth.ts adds `loggedCredentialsFailures` (a Set), `MAX_LOGGED_CREDENTIALS_FAILURES = 20`, `logCredentialsFailureOnce`, and `resetCredentialsFailureLogForTests`, and `userFromJson`/`getUserCredentials` now call `logCredentialsFailureOnce` instead of `logger.error` on each read/parse path. cli/src/utils/__tests__/auth-keychain.test.ts adds tests 'signed in with the keychain token, for every token reader', 'no keychain token this run: signed out quietly, nothing logged', and 'an unreadable file logs once per distinct failure, not once per read'.

9986cb57a5ea50e771b02b1fe7f6bc3cfbeed1fd.text: The team that runs advertising on Freebuff added a dedicated path for sending ad-tracking events to X (formerly Twitter), reusing the same retry-and-delivery logic that already handles TikTok, so campaign events like account sign-up or payment entry can be reported there too. This is internal ad-serving plumbing in the Core package, affecting the Freebuff engineering team and the advertisers who buy ad slots, not the Freebuff coding assistant you use. You won't notice anything new or change any settings, because these are identifier and event templates for an advertiser funnel that isn't wired up to the coding experience yet.

83435a8723c7a2c852f0adf7111d583863b66546.text: The program that signs you in now stops repeating the same error message over and over when it cannot read your saved login file. Instead of logging the error on every screen redraw, it records the specific problem once, so the same failure is not repeated thousands of times. This is internal work for the team that builds the tool, and you will not notice it in daily use unless your login file was broken, in which case you see the error message fewer times.

e32b322ebdcb417c7acb704627f1b9b9bc2017c9.title: Unopened model rows are dropped from the held Freebuff catalog
e32b322ebdcb417c7acb704627f1b9b9bc2017c9.summary: Rows whose `opensAt` (issuedAt-relative) has not yet passed are removed from the in-memory catalog before it is stored or exposed to the directory, so a saved key that maps only to an unopened row resolves to the recommendation and no unopened row handle reaches an admission or session call. The filter runs in `common/src/util/freebuff-device-signing.ts`'s `listableFreebuffCatalogRows` and is applied in `cli/src/state/freebuff-catalog-store.ts` and `cli/src/utils/freebuff-model-directory.ts`. A later fetch republishes the row once it opens, since the server schedules one by `refreshAt`.
e32b322ebdcb417c7acb704627f1b9b9bc2017c9.evidence: New `listableFreebuffCatalogRows(catalog, now)` filters rows whose `opensAt` is after `issuedAt`; `setFreebuffCatalog` calls `withoutUnopenedRows`, and `catalogFreebuffModelDirectory`/`freebuffCatalogHandleFor` receive `now` so dropped rows never reach picker, handle lookup, or send-time directory.

If a model opens later, it will simply appear in your list during the next automatic refresh, exactly on time. You don't need to do anything differently.
