6fc184b984516641b8193b07ae4188145c94583d.title: Freebuff auth token moved to OS keychain via Bun.secrets
6fc184b984516641b8193b07ae4188145c94583d.summary: On startup, `loadStoredAuthToken()` now runs before any credential read in `cli/src/index.tsx`, resolving a `SecretStore` from the new `auth-token-store.ts` and either reading a cached keychain token or promoting a file token into `Bun.secrets` (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or the Linux Secret Service). The profile stays in `credentials.json` with `tokenStore: 'keychain'` and no `authToken`, so a failed or unavailable keychain (headless Linux, locked keychain over SSH, CI, old Bun runtime) leaves the token in the owner-only 0600 file and never logs the user out. Reads stay synchronous via a cached token, and `moveTokenToKeychain` only rewrites the file after it confirms the store round-trips the value.
6fc184b984516641b8193b07ae4188145c94583d.evidence: New file `cli/src/utils/auth-token-store.ts` defines a `SecretStore` interface and `bunSecretStore` over `Bun.secrets` with a `KEYCHAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 2_000` bound; `cli/src/utils/auth.ts` imports `getCachedKeychainToken`, `resolveSecretStore`, `setCachedKeychainToken` and adds `moveTokenToKeychain`, `loadStoredAuthToken`, plus `tokenStore: 'keychain'` in `storedUserSchema`; `cli/src/index.tsx` now calls `await loadStoredAuthToken()` before `parseArgs()` and reads credentials. Added tests in `cli/src/utils/__tests__/auth-keychain.test.ts` cover keychain moves, startup migration, sign-out fallback, and non-throwing reads.

This change is internal to the shared types module and no code in the diff actually reads or displays these fields yet, so you notice nothing today. 925bc3fc61b0927e0189685d5d1f0dfb0fee38c8.title: Chat input keeps Up/Down paging history from a recalled entry
925bc3fc61b0927e0189685d5d1f0dfb0fee38c8.summary: The CLI chat input now treats a recalled (but unedited) history entry as a history draft for Up/Down navigation in `resolveChatKeyboardAction` and `shouldInterceptChatInputKey`. This stops Up from recalling only the newest prompt and then resolving to `none` on subsequent presses, while left/right still edit the text of a recalled entry.
925bc3fc61b0927e0189685d5d1f0dfb0fee38c8.evidence: In `cli/src/utils/keyboard-actions.ts`, the `ChatKeyboardState` type gains a `lastEditDueToNav: boolean` field, `createDefaultChatKeyboardState` initializes it to `false`, and `resolveChatKeyboardAction` introduces an `inHistoryDraft` check (`inputValue.length === 0 || lastEditDueToNav`) for the Up/Down history branches (Priority 10 and 10.5) and adds `!(state.lastEditDueToNav && (isUp || isDown))` to the Priority 7.5 non-empty-draft arrow guard. `cli/src/hooks/use-chat-keyboard.ts` now passes `lastEditDueToNav: draft.lastEditDueToNav` into `resolveChatKeyboardAction`. `cli/src/utils/chat-input-key-intercept.ts` adds the same `inHistoryDraft` check (`state.inputLength === 0 || state.lastEditDueToNav`) to the Up/Down history intercept branches.

925bc3fc61b0927e0189685d5d1f0dfb0fee38c8.text: When you press the Up arrow while typing a new message, the assistant now lets you keep paging back through older messages you've sent, even if you just recalled one and haven't edited it yet. This only applies to you if you use the assistant's chat, desktop, or command-line versions. You no longer hit a wall where pressing Up once shows the newest old message and then stops: each additional Up press loads an earlier message, and Down brings you back toward your current prompt, letting you browse your recent messages smoothly.

a080b0350b619eac9376a20495be7f15326080d1.title: Add server model catalog to override compiled Freebuff picker
a080b0350b619eac9376a20495be7f15326080d1.summary: A new Freebuff model catalog subsystem fetches a server-side model directory over a versioned HTTP protocol (x-freebuff-catalog-protocol 1) from /api/v1/freebuff/models, with a zustand store that swaps between the compiled directory and a catalog-built one. The catalog rows override the compiled per-model policy for session price, effort ladder, tier access, daily session limits, and context windows, while every method returns undefined for no override so non-catalog models keep compiled behavior. The CLI session and chat-admission flows now gate their model lookups through getFreebuffModelDirectory(), and send/refresh paths retry once on a freebuff_catalog_stale refusal after refreshing the catalog. Catalog-selected rows also drive a dedicated base3 root agent (base3-free-catalog) built at runtime from the catalog row so new models need no release.
a080b0350b619eac9376a20495be7f15326080d1.evidence: New files cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-model-catalog.ts, cli/src/state/freebuff-catalog-store.ts, cli/src/utils/freebuff-model-catalog.ts, cli/src/utils/freebuff-model-directory.ts, cli/src/utils/freebuff-catalog-agent.ts, and common types/constants (freebuff-model-catalog.ts, freebuff-model-policy-overlay.ts) introduce a server-fetched model catalog that overrides the compiled per-model picker; modified components (freebuff-model-selector.tsx, freebuff-chat-header.tsx, session-ended-banner.tsx, status-bar.tsx, freebuff-referral-banner.tsx, use-freebuff-chat-admission.ts, use-freebuff-session.ts, use-send-message.ts, settings.ts, local-agent-registry.ts, freebuff-agent-selection.ts, agents/base3.ts) replace direct freebuff-models lookups with the new FreebuffModelDirectory abstraction.

8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 introduces server-driven model selection and keychain-based login storage for the Freebuff tier. The CLI now fetches its list of available AI models from Freebuff servers instead of relying only on models compiled into the app, and the login token used for Freebuff sessions is now stored in the operating system's secure keychain rather than a plaintext file. Freebuff sessions gained support for a country-verification offer flow that can present a paid-plan upsell when access is limited by region, and the daily session limit for the GPT-6.1 Sol promotion is now enforceable through a server-provided policy overlay that can override compiled limits. Freebuff CLI users get the model picker reading the server catalog directly when their account has it, while the auth token moves into the macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or Linux secret service (falling back to the file if the keychain is unavailable so logins are not lost). On a limited-access region, users who cannot unlock full access with country verification are instead shown a paid-plan offer with server-provided prices and daily Freebucks numbers. The server catalog also lets a single catalog root agent run every model row so new or re-priced models appear without a CLI release. For most users the main effect is that the Freebuff model picker and session admission now reflect server-provided pricing, availability and session limits in real time.

a080b0350b619eac9376a20495be7f15326080d1.text: This change adds a new system so the app's team of helper models (the list you pick from when you start coding) is now loaded from the internet each time you open the app, instead of being permanently baked into the app itself. It affects the free version of the coding assistant, Freebuff, that people use on the terminal or web. With this change, new models and price changes can appear in your model picker without needing to download a new version of the app first.

1a2b5e9ba875ca41db6cdce6ca13fb93796527b0.title: Uuidv7 generator for append-heavy primary keys
1a2b5e9ba875ca41db6cdce6ca13fb93796527b0.summary: Adds `uuidv7` in `common/src/util/uuidv7.ts`, producing RFC 9562 version-7 UUIDs whose first 48 bits hold a Unix-millisecond timestamp, version 7 and variant 10xx bits enforced over the random bytes, returned as a standard hyphenated UUID string. The JSDoc explains it targets append-heavy primary keys such as `agent_run` (COD-751), where v4's random placement dirties random btree pages and re-writes whole WAL pages after checkpoints, whereas v7's time ordering appends to rightmost pages. Tests assert well-formedness, timestamp encoding in the high 48 bits, version/variant bit stability under zero and all-ones random sources, monotonic string sorting across consecutive milliseconds, uniqueness of 10000 ids minted in the same millisecond, and compatibility with the zod `.uuid()` and `z.uuid()` validators the run and step schemas use.
1a2b5e9ba875ca41db6cdce6ca13fb93796527b0.evidence: New file `common/src/util/uuidv7.ts` exports `uuidv7(now = Date.now(), random = crypto.getRandomValues)`, encoding a 48-bit Unix-millisecond timestamp in the first 48 bits, setting version 7 and variant 10xx bits, with accompanying tests in `common/src/util/__tests__/uuidv7.test.ts`; the JSDoc references (`agent_run`, COD-751) ties the motivation to append-heavy primary keys.
1a2b5e9ba875ca41db6cdce6ca13fb93796527b0.unknowns: The diff does not show where `uuidv7` is consumed or any rollout across `agent_run`/COD-751 beyond the JSDoc reference.

1a2b5e9ba875ca41db6cdce6ca13fb93796527b0.text: The engineering team added a small helper that creates ID labels which are ordered by when they were made, instead of in random order. This keeps the database from getting slower when many records are written every second, especially the tables that track each assistant run. It is purely internal tooling for the codebase's shared utilities, so you will not see anything new in the app. Nothing in this change affects how you use the assistant today.

8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 with keychain auth and server model catalog
8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.summary: The Freebuff CLI release manifest at freebuff/cli/release/package.json moves from 0.2.3 to 0.2.4. This window ships the Freebuff auth token to the OS credential store: a new auth-token-store.ts in cli/src/utils keeps the bearer token in macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or the Secret Service via Bun.secrets, with loadStoredAuthToken() called once at startup in cli/src/index.tsx before anything reads credentials, and moveTokenToKeychain() migrating the file token on a verified successful write while leaving it in the owner-only file on headless Linux, locked keychains and CI so a failed keychain never logs anyone out. The landing screen, chat header, chat footer, status bar, session-ended banner and chat admission now resolve models through the in-memory server catalog directory (cli/src/state/freebuff-catalog-store.ts) instead of getFreebuffModel, so a catalog-aware session runs on a row's handle rather than a compiled model id; a new useFreebuffModelCatalog hook starts the fetch in cli/src/app.tsx ahead of useFreebuffSession, and a runtime-built base3 root in cli/src/utils/freebuff-catalog-agent.ts carries the row's handle as its model while agents/base3.ts accepts compaction and modelLabel options so the opaque handle is never told to the model. Sponsored grants still run on their plain model id, because the catalog root admits handles only, so cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts routes catalog mode through getFreebuffCliAgentIdForModel(grant.modelId). A new common/src/types/freebuff-model-catalog.ts defines the x-freebuff-catalog-protocol wire contract and a legacy-digest migration that maps a pre-catalog saved pick onto its row without the catalog naming the old id; pricing and effort ladders defer to a server-only policy overlay in common/src/constants/freebuff-model-policy-overlay.ts that the web API registers and every client compiles to undefined so pre-catalog behavior is unchanged.

8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 makes the command-line AI coding helper remember you securely and keeps the list of AI models it offers up-to-date from Freebuff's servers. Your login token is now stored in your operating system's password keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or Linux Secret Service) instead of a plain file, so other programs on your computer cannot read it and a leaked dotfiles repository will not expose it; if the keychain is unavailable, you simply stay signed in using the file as before. The model picker now pulls its list of available AI models from your Freebuff account in real time, so new, re-priced, or rotated models appear without needing a new CLI download, and a model with a promotional daily cap (like the GPT-6.1 Sol one-session-a-day preview) is now enforced at the moment you start a chat. A new 'base3' orchestrator root runs catalog models using the server-supplied handle so each model needs no new agent definition, while the CLI still falls back to its built-in model list when it cannot reach the server. The auth token file is also clamped to owner-only permissions on launch and after every save, healing existing installs that were left world-readable, and a country-verification check can now block the 'verify country' prompt when a region cannot change your access, offering a paid-plan upsell instead.

The `sameEndpoint` helper normalizes both the supplied and existing base URLs via `normalizeByokBaseUrl` to tell whether the endpoint actually changes, and only then prompts for the variable name. When the user supplies a valid variable, `byokStore.update` writes `credentialRef` as `env:${environmentVariable}` in the connection patch.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.2 ships with clearer error messages for custom (BYOK) connections, better handling of streaming responses from compatible model providers, and a stop-on-limit policy that prevents you from being silently switched away from a model you ran out of daily uses on. When a provider rejects your key or a model is not found, the messages now name the specific environment variable (such as OPENROUTER_API_KEY, not the key value itself) and the HTTP status, so you can fix the problem without exposing secrets. OpenAI-compatible model streams that omit a tool-call index are no longer dropped, which previously could end a turn with no tool action and just text like "Writing the file." When you hit your daily session limit on a model, the client stops that model and shows when it becomes available again rather than falling back to another model behind your back. The SDK now trims stray whitespace from stored credentials and rejects keys that contain line breaks, and it reports which variable is missing when a saved connection cannot read its key.

8a89a68610cb8088579974edb1a01c2e6e9f6032.text: The update command for your own-provider connections can now take the name of an environment variable as an extra argument. When you point a connection at a new URL, the tool no longer refuses the change just because the stored key was meant for the old endpoint instead of demanding you set it up again from scratch. It compares the old and new URLs to decide whether the address really changed, and only then asks for the variable name holding your provider key. The change is for people using the CLI with their own provider keys; if you only ever move a model between the same endpoint or fix a trailing slash, you notice nothing and no extra steps are required.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.2 release with streaming, BYOK and daily-limit fixes
2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.summary: This release-bump commit (2cde35ae) ships the Freebuff CLI release manifest at 0.2.2 via freebuff/cli/release/package.json (0.2.1 -> 0.2.2) and defines a new FREEBUFF_INSTALL_ID_HEADER = 'x-freebuff-install-id' constant in common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts for a Desktop install id; the constant itself has no visible reader in this diff. The wider 0.2.2 window includes six functional changes: OpenAI-compatible streaming now infers missing tool-call indexes, BYOK validation/error messaging names the missing or rejected environment variable, a spent daily model limit now stops the run instead of falling back to another model, the CLI environment descriptor gains proxy/TLS fields, and testing docs warn against handing bare postgres.js queries to expect rejects. This commit itself only carries the version bump and the header constant addition.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.2 improves reliability around AI model connections, daily usage limits, and streaming responses. Concrete Highlights: 1. BYOK diagnostics now name the missing environment variable instead of a generic error: When your custom AI provider rejects a login or a key is unreadable, the CLI now explains exactly which environment variable is unset in the current Freebuff process (for example, OPENROUTER_API_KEY), rather than a vague connection failure. A 401 error now names the variable the key came from and points to that variable's value. Keys with surrounding whitespace from a.env file are trimmed, and keys with embedded line breaks are rejected. 2. Daily limit hits stop the run instead of silently switching models: When a model has reached its daily session limit (such as promoted GPT-6.1 Sol sessions), the CLI now stops the run and tells you when the model opens again, rather than quietly moving you to a fallback model and quoting you a different price. 3. OpenAI-compatible streams no longer drop whole chunks when tool-call data is missing an index: Streaming responses from OpenAI-compatible servers and proxies now handle tool-call deltas that omit the index field by inferring the correct call slot, so a single malformed chunk no longer ends the turn with a silently dropped tool call. These changes apply to you when using BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) connections to OpenAI-compatible providers, when a model's daily session limit is reached, or when a provider streams tool-call data without an index. The daily-limit fix affects any model governed by FREEBUFF_DAILY_SESSION_LIMITS, including the GPT-6.1 Sol promotion. BYOK users starting a run from an exported environment variable will see clearer errors naming the variable to check.

2ac20ca0400a11a6e7af5824c096bea34824b6b2.summary: A new section in `docs/testing.md` records that handing a bare postgres.js query to `expect(...).rejects` under bun 1.3.14 hangs forever, because the query is lazy and only runs when `.then()` is called, which `.rejects` does not do. This hung `region-verifier-runs.integration.test.ts` and the `test-integration-packages/internal` job on every PR until #4595. The prose directs authors to await the query inside a function and assert on its thrown error, citing the test's own `rejects` helper as an example.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: This Freebuff 0.2.2 release improves streaming connections to AI providers, makes Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) credential diagnostics clearer, and fixes how daily model usage limits are enforced. The CLI now handles streaming responses from OpenAI-compatible services that leave out tool call position markers, so those responses no longer fail. BYOK setup now tells you exactly which environment variable is missing or invalid instead of giving a generic error, and it warns you when a configured model is not listed by the provider's endpoint. When a model hits its daily usage limit, the CLI now stops the run and tells you when it resets, rather than silently switching to a different model you did not choose.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.2 ships a set of refinements to the command-line coding assistant and its Desktop companion rather than a new headline feature. The release hardens the bring-your-own-key (/byok) flow: when you add or update a custom provider connection, the CLI now tells you which named environment variable is missing or rejected, shows whether your model is in the endpoint's published model list (with the first 20 ids), and explains connection problems in plain terms like 'connection refused' or 'answered with a web page instead of a model list'. It also fixes /byok behavior when a long command was pasted and got split by line wraps, and stops the CLI from silently re-admitting you onto a fallback model when your daily session cap for a specific model is spent - instead it shows how many hours remain until that model opens up again. Alongside that, OpenAI-compatible streaming endpoints that forget to include a tool-call sequence number are now handled gracefully instead of dropping the whole chunk, and a documentation change records the repo's test-count guardrails so missing test files can no longer hide behind a green CI check. Together these changes mainly help people wiring up custom AI providers by hand and anyone who has bumped into silent fallbacks or confusing BYOK error messages.

In `cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts`, the `model_unavailable` branch of `useFreebuffSession` now treats `next.dailyLimitReached` as a stop condition, so the CLI lands on the picker and shows `next.availableHours` instead of silently re-admitting on the fallback model. The change is motivated by a 2026-09-30 case where a user quoted Sol's price and was silently switched to MiMo. One other area is affected alongside this gate.

66f02773b360e100a133eccdb5e26ef42173913b.text: I'll analyze the provided technical summary and diff to extract the key points for a plain-English explanation. The change involves the assistant stopping when a requested AI model has reached its daily usage limit, rather than automatically switching to a different model. Specifically, when you request a specific model that has hit its daily usage cap (like GPT-6.1 Sol during a promotion), the system now informs you that this exact model is unavailable and tells you when it will be available again, instead of silently switching you to another model (like MiMo). This affects Freebuff users - people using the free tier of the Codebuff AI coding assistant.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.2 ships with clearer BYOK (bring-your-own-key) error messages and improved model-session handling, plus a fix for OpenAI-compatible streaming that previously dropped tool calls when servers omitted an index field. Key changes: • BYOK connection errors now name the missing or rejected environment variable (for example, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) and show the HTTP status, instead of a generic message; the CLI also trims stray whitespace from pasted URLs and no longer silently drops extra pasted arguments. • When you point a BYOK connection at a new base URL, the CLI now asks you to confirm the environment variable to send to that endpoint, preventing accidental credential reuse. • OpenAI-compatible chat streams that arrive without a tool-call index no longer break the whole response; they are now associated with an existing or new tool call automatically. • A spent daily model limit (such as a capped promotion) stops the run instead of silently switching you to a different model. The CLI and Desktop client now also report a few more environment facts to the service (timezone override, proxy settings, TLS/ca-certificate flags) in a privacy-safe summary form. The available release evidence is incomplete on broader capabilities; this roll-up covers only what the listed source hunks establish.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: This Freebuff 0.2.2 release improves how the CLI handles BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) connections and fixes streaming issues with OpenAI-compatible providers. When you run /byok commands, error messages now clearly name which environment variable is missing or rejected instead of giving generic warnings, and the /byok update command can accept a new key variable when changing endpoints. Streamed tool-call chunks from OpenAI-compatible providers that omit an index field are now handled gracefully instead of failing entirely. Additionally, session admission responses now include a daily limit flag so users hitting a model's daily quota are stopped outright rather than silently switched to a different model. The client environment descriptor now reports proxy and TLS settings and system timezone info to the server for better diagnostics. A release bump and install id header constant round out the changes.

e18dda65668489eb93037a42814cb509485d5dd8.title: Default agentic CPC set to 300 cents in agentic pool
e18dda65668489eb93037a42814cb509485d5dd8.summary: `common/src/ads/agentic-pool.ts` introduces `DEFAULT_AGENTIC_CPC_CENTS` set to 300 cents as the starting price for new agentic campaigns, and rebases the existing `AGENTIC_TIER2_ACCEPT_PRICE_CENTS` ceiling onto that new constant. The field joins the existing Desktop purchase and session-count metadata, so every admission state carries the same verification flag without per-variant changes.

Sent on GET.'

a65a05b3511a4ba7bf8d838348796a1a58d45705.text: The session admission response now includes an optional boolean field that reflects your current country verification status on GET requests, riding alongside existing Desktop purchase and session-count metadata on every admission state. This affects the Freebuff engineering team and internal maintainers, since the file is the shared wire-level type definition used by both server and CLI to stay in sync. For everyday use there is no visible effect or action required by you yet. The field is marked as not granting full access and is only sent on GET, so it does nothing until server-side or client-side code begins populating or consuming it.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: This release improves bring-your-own-key (BYOK) credential setup and streaming from OpenAI-compatible providers. BYOK validation now names the specific environment variable that is missing or rejected, rejects keys containing line breaks, and trims surrounding whitespace so valid keys aren't rejected. When a server omits a tool-call index in a streamed response chunk, the assistant now infers the missing index from existing or new calls instead of dropping the whole chunk. The OpenAI-compatible chat streaming layer also tolerates these missing indexes while still honoring ones that are explicitly provided. Additionally, a new session-admission flag lets the server tell a user their chosen model's daily limit is spent rather than silently moving them to a different model, and the CLI surfaces which environment variable a saved key comes from on a connection check. Note: the release evidence is incomplete for one category of changes because a check discredited its summary, so only the behaviors demonstrated by the source hunks above are established here.

07d3adb8588e54e5d2b6e6b87a71eb71ec93bcfa.title: Add optional completion check, deadline reminders, and background
07d3adb8588e54e5d2b6e6b87a71eb71ec93bcfa.summary: The default base3 agent enables completionCheck, which offers one verification pass after edits using available tools before ending the turn, gated by a remaining step budget and an optional deadline. Packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts implements the gate with a completionCheckpoint that survives transient transport failures, and adds urgency-tiered deadline reminders as time budget expires. The SDK now supports BACKGROUND terminal commands with a new releaseBackgroundTerminalCommands export and persistent log files, and model-provider.ts adds sanitizeByokTransportError plus retry-after propagation for BYOK transport errors. Deadline awareness is threaded through RunOptions.deadlineAt in sdk/src/run.ts, with 11 files changed across agents, shared core types, agent runtime, and SDK.

The diff covers 11 files across agents, common/types, agent-runtime, and sdk with +1077/-53.

07d3adb8588e54e5d2b6e6b87a71eb71ec93bcfa.text: The assistant now spends one last look at its own work before wrapping up, like double-checking that it saved the right files and ran the tests it said it would. The development team built this into the agent runtime and made the default coding assistant turn it on, so every coding session that edits files gets this extra verification step before the turn ends. The change also lets the runtime warn the assistant when a hosted time limit is about to run out, and it adds support for long-running terminal commands that keep running after the session ends, along with safer handling of provider connection errors in the toolkit.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.2 improves how your own AI API key connections are set up and reported. When you add or update a BYOK (bring-your-own-key) connection, error messages now name the specific environment variable that is unset or rejected, instead of a vague credential warning, and they avoid printing any key text. Validation of an OpenAI-compatible endpoint now reports the HTTP status code, flags when the configured model is missing from the endpoint's model list (and lists what is available), and suggests a fix such as appending /v1 to the base URL. A paste that was split across lines (for example a base URL wrapped mid-word) is now rejoined before the command is rejected, so fewer connections fail to save. Chat streaming from OpenAI-compatible servers is also more tolerant: tool-call chunks that arrive without an index are matched to the right call instead of dropping the turn. These changes only affect users who configure their own provider connections; Freebuff's free and paid model access is unchanged.

a50d7e783cb6733fe7ac14503afb30f4c49748ba.title: /byok rejoins paste-split line breaks and rejects extra args
a50d7e783cb6733fe7ac14503afb30f4c49748ba.summary: The `/byok` command in `cli/src/commands/byok.ts` now re-parses input with `joinSplitPaste` when a pasted command contains bare line breaks that split an argument mid-word: if the only consistent reading is that those breaks were splits, the joined command runs; otherwise the command is reported with its extra words rather than silently dropping them. `maxPositionalArguments` enforces each subcommand's argument ceiling (list/off/help allow 0, effort allows 1, add allows 4 or 5 depending on provider, update allows 3) so trailing words like a dropped `/v1` suffix are no longer saved silently. Missing arguments now yield an incomplete-command message naming each placeholder, and unknown provider types are reported by name instead of proceeding to usage.
a50d7e783cb6733fe7ac14503afb30f4c49748ba.evidence: In `cli/src/commands/byok.ts`, `handleByokCommand` was refactored to use a new `parseByokCommand` helper, and `maxPositionalArguments` plus `joinSplitPaste` (driven by the `BARE_LINE_BREAK` regex) were added so pasted mid-word line breaks are rejoined when that is the only consistent reading, while over-argument commands now report `Unexpected extra argument(s)` instead of dropping words silently.
a50d7e783cb6733fe7ac14503afb30f4c49748ba.unknowns: The diff does not show which terminal emulators or paste methods trigger the bare line break path in production A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

a50d7e783cb6733fe7ac14503afb30f4c49748ba.text: When you paste a slash-command for bringing your own provider key into the chat, the assistant now correctly rejoins parts that got split by a line break in the middle of a word (like a URL or model name) and refuses to silently drop any extra words you pasted. Developers using that slash-command will see it run as typed when a pasted line break replaced a space, and when something looks wrong it names the missing piece or the extra words instead of guessing. No action is needed from anyone; this only changes how pasted commands are handled.

8adc16eebfb6f3bf1b9d496d63549ccc9f23fb86.text: The Freebuff system now tracks when a paid subscription was paused due to a failed renewal payment (a new optional field was added to the shared session data). For everyday users, there is no visible change today: the field is in place but nothing in the system reads it yet, so it does not alter how subscriptions, payments, or the Freebuff experience work. Until a developer wires up logic to use this field, a failed-payment plan will not be surfaced differently to you.

6fbd1ad3e5ea867246171a0c6d90aebdc63fa504.title: BYOK credential errors name the env variable instead of masking
6fbd1ad3e5ea867246171a0c6d90aebdc63fa504.summary: BYOK connection load failures now surface a typed `ByokCredentialError` carrying the store's own message, which names the environment variable (e.g. `OMNIROUTE_API_KEY`) when it is unset or rejected, instead of the generic "Unable to load the selected BYOK connection". The CLI's run-start catch calls the new `byokLoadFailureMessage` to render that message, and model-provider.ts passes `byokCredentialVariable(byok)` into `getByokProviderErrorMessage` so a 401 to an environment-keyed connection names the variable rather than the key. CRLF trimming of loaded keys is now centralized in `getSecret`, which throws `ByokCredentialError` for empty or line-broken values.
6fbd1ad3e5ea867246171a0c6d90aebdc63fa504.evidence: New `byokLoadFailureMessage` in cli/src/utils/byok.ts formats ByokCredentialError with its own message; use-send-message.ts route catch calls it for BYOK connection load failures. New `ByokCredentialError`, `byokCredentialVariable`, `missingEnvironmentCredentialMessage`, `rejectedByokCredentialMessage` in sdk/src/byok.ts replace generic strings in getSecret with typed credential errors naming the env variable. model-provider.ts passes `credentialVariable: byokCredentialVariable(byok)` into getByokProviderErrorMessage for 401 responses.

This change affects Freebuff users who configure their own API keys through environment variables. You will now see specific guidance like which variable name is missing, making it easier to fix configuration issues without guessing.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.2 focuses on the connection between the CLI and AI providers you bring yourself (BYOK), plus how streamed responses are handled. The release changes how the /byok update command accepts arguments, letting you also change which environment variable holds your API key when you edit a connection's base URL. It improves how streaming responses from OpenAI-compatible providers are parsed, so tool calls embedded in a streamed answer no longer break the whole response if they omit an index field. It also refines the validation messages shown when a provider endpoint can't be reached or returns an unexpected answer, and adds finer-grained signals so the CLI can tell the difference between a model that is temporarily out of daily capacity versus one that is fully unavailable.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.title: Freebuff 0.2.2 with install id header and BYOK endpoint confirmation
2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.2.2 is released, alongside a new `FREEBUFF_INSTALL_ID_HEADER` constant (`x-freebuff-install-id`) defined in `freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts` for a Desktop install id that persists across sign-ins but is not a credential. The `/byok` command now rejoins mid-word paste line breaks and requires an environment variable to be named when updating a connection to a base URL that points at a different endpoint than the current one. OpenAI-compatible streaming no longer drops a tool-call delta whole when the provider omits `index`, inferring the slot instead via `inferToolCallIndex`. This release window also contains a daily session limit stop in the freebuff admission type, proxy and timezone fields in the client environment descriptor, and a premium reset that reads the resolved quota row.

The release manifest in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumps `version` from `0.2.1` to `0.2.2`. Member hunks for this window also add `inferToolCallIndex` in `packages/llm-providers/src/openai-compatible/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts, model-id rejection + credential error helpers in sdk/src/byok.ts` and `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts`, `/byok paste-split and endpoint-confirmation logic in cli/src/commands/byok.ts`, a `dailyLimitReached admission field in common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts, client env proxy/timezone fields in cli/src/utils/client-environment.ts` and `cli/src/types/env.ts, premium reset quota in cli/src/utils/freebuff-premium-reset.ts, and a docs test note in docs/testing.md`.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff 0.2.2 adds a couple of user-visible improvements around bringing your own AI provider key and confirming it works. When you add or update a Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) connection in the terminal, the command now validates the endpoint directly and tells you whether the model is listed by the provider, showing the actual HTTP status and available model names when a model is missing rather than just saying the save failed. If an endpoint is unreachable, it now says so in plain terms (for example, 'connection refused' or 'did not answer within 10 seconds') and, for OpenAI-style base URLs, suggests appending '/v1'. A daily session limit is now treated as a hard stop that explains when the model opens again instead of silently moving you to a different model. The release also tightens paste handling so a long command broken across lines is no longer mis-saved with a truncated URL. The available release evidence is incomplete for the full set of changes, but the main user-facing gains are clearer BYOK setup and validation feedback, plus a safer daily-limit behavior.

9aede7717867ad17a5aeac24cb14ecddb12d1d68.title: Open AI-compatible chunk schema makes tool call index optional, added
9aede7717867ad17a5aeac24cb14ecddb12d1d68.summary: The streamed tool-call delta handler in the OpenAI-compatible chat language model now falls back to `inferToolCallIndex(toolCalls, toolCallDelta)` when a delta omits `index`, instead of assigning it directly. The chunk schema's `index` field switched from `z.number()` to `z.number().nullish()`, so deltas from servers and proxies that omit the index no longer fail parsing and drop the call. The new `inferToolCallIndex` export resolves the slot by `id` when present, otherwise continues the last unfinished call of the same function or opens a new slot.
9aede7717867ad17a5aeac24cb14ecddb12d1d68.evidence: In packages/llm-providers/src/openai-compatible/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts, the chunk schema changed from `index: z.number()` to `index: z.number().nullish()`, the delta handling changed from const index = toolCallDelta.index to `const index = toolCallDelta.index ?? inferToolCallIndex(toolCalls, toolCallDelta), and a new exported function inferToolCallIndex` was added to infer the slot of a streamed tool-call delta that carries no index.

9aede7717867ad17a5aeac24cb14ecddb12d1d68.text: The assistant used to lose track of what to do next whenever an external service forgot to label a small piece of a streamed reply. Now it can keep the conversation on track by matching the unlabeled pieces to the right step based on context instead of giving up. This only affects the engineering team that maintains the assistant's connection to external services. You, as a user, will not notice anything different because the change prevents silent failures behind the scenes rather than adding anything new.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff 0.2.2 adds a BYOK connection-confirmation flow and an install identifier header for client sessions. When adding a Bring-Your-Own-Key connection, the CLI now validates the chosen endpoint against a normalized URL and asks you to reconfirm the key variable before switching a connection to a different endpoint, so a pasted base URL with a stray line break no longer silently drops the path. The validation report now prints the provider's HTTP status and, for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, lists the models the server actually offers when your chosen model is not among them, instead of only saying the endpoint is reachable. A per-run send error now names the specific credential problem (for example, which environment variable is unset in this process) rather than a generic client-creation failure. The release also hardens CI test counting, classifies provider error bodies by status code, and reports daily session-limit refusals as a stop rather than a silent fallback to another model.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.2 release with Desktop install-id header constant
2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.summary: This is the release-bump commit for Freebuff CLI 0.2.2, which only touched `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` (version 0.2.1 to 0.2.2) and `common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts`. In the constants file a new header `FREEBUFF_INSTALL_ID_HEADER` (value `x-freebuff-install-id`) is defined alongside a comment that it is a random id Freebuff Desktop mints once per install and keeps across sign-ins and that it is not a credential; no reader of the constant appears in this commit, so by itself it changes no runtime behavior yet. Five earlier members (BYOK endpoint check, OpenAI error pattern, client env descriptor, etc.) and three later members are described in the surrounding same-day sequence but are not part of this commit's source hunks. The release notes list a 0.2.2 window with an SDK model-provider change and eight other members, but those summaries are discredited evidence, so the changes they describe are not attributed here.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: This release (Freebuff CLI 0.2.2) rolls out several user-facing fixes and improvements mostly centered on connecting your own AI provider keys and on clearer session limits. You can now update a BYOK connection to point at a new API base URL and explicitly name the environment variable holding your key when doing so, which prevents accidentally sending your key to the wrong endpoint. The `/byok` command also handles pasted commands better, warning you about extra arguments instead of silently dropping parts of a long URL, and it can tell you which models an OpenAI-compatible endpoint actually lists when your configured model is missing. On the session side, daily model limits are now treated as a hard stop (you are told it's used up for today) instead of quietly switching you to a different model, and Freebuff Desktop now carries a country-verification flag and more precise premium slot handling. The Desktop client environment header also gained extra signals (timezone override, proxy location, TLS behavior, extra CA certs) to support diagnostics, and the SDK model-provider layer now inspects the name of the key variable behind a BYOK request in 401 errors. The release evidence is otherwise incomplete for a full picture: many members are scoped-only or source-only updates, and several files are truncated, so some claimed behaviors should be treated as unverified until confirmed by runtime. In short, the most useful concrete effect is that BYOK setup is more forgiving of pasted commands and safer when you move a key between endpoints, while daily model limits now stop you outright instead of redirecting you to another model.

b63254fdc6b1967224a0eaea03df93dd75c5724b.title: Client environment descriptor reports proxy, TLS, CA, and timezone
b63254fdc6b1967224a0eaea03df93dd75c5724b.summary: The `x-freebuff-env` descriptor built in `cli/src/utils/client-environment.ts` now includes `tzo` (TZ override presence), `px` (proxy bucket via `proxyBucketOf`), `tls` (NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED disabled), and `ca` (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS present) fields, plus a `stz` field carrying the OS IANA zone only when `TZ` overrides it. `cli/src/utils/env.ts` now returns `ALL_PROXY`, the `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY` pairs, `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED`, and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` from `getCliEnv()` so the descriptor can read them. `bucketProxy` reduces a proxy URL to where it points (loopback vs remote) rather than sending the raw value, and `zoneFromZoneinfo` extracts an IANA zone from a `/etc/localtime` link or `/etc/timezone`.
b63254fdc6b1967224a0eaea03df93dd75c5724b.evidence: cli/src/utils/env.ts adds `TZ`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `https_proxy`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `http_proxy`, `ALL_PROXY`, `all_proxy`, `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED`, and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to `getCliEnv()`, and cli/src/utils/client-environment.ts uses those values in `proxyBucketOf` and `formatClientEnvironment` to add `tzo`, `px`, `tls`, `ca` fields plus an optional `stz` field gated on a TZ override, with new exports `ProxyBucket`, `bucketProxy`, `zoneFromZoneinfo`, `ReadSystemTimeZone`, and `readSystemTimeZone`.
b63254fdc6b1967224a0eaea03df93dd75c5724b.unknowns: The notes do not identify a new reader that consumes the added descriptor fields or whether the server-side catalog of expected fields was updated to parse them.

b63254fdc6b1967224a0eaea03df93dd75c5724b.text: The assistant now sends a brief, privacy-safe summary of your terminal's proxy, timezone, and security settings alongside its session and ad requests, so Freebuff can detect misconfigured or risky setups like an intercepting proxy, a forced timezone, or disabled certificate checks. The proxy value is reduced to a rough bucket (none, on this machine, or remote) rather than the raw URL, and the only full value shared is the system's own timezone name, and only when your custom timezone override hides the real one. This is an internal telemetry change for operators who run Freebuff's service and infrastructure, not a new feature or setting for end users. There is no visible change in the assistant's behavior or what you see in the terminal.

5e1579a5cab63056ed76b338490991bc981e05b7.title: SDK matches quoted BYOK model IDs in rejections
5e1579a5cab63056ed76b338490991bc981e05b7.summary: The `BYOK_MODEL_REJECTION_PATTERNS` array in `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts` gains a regex that matches model IDs quoted with backticks, single quotes, or double quotes. The `getByokProviderErrorMessage` function now truncates the model name to `MAX_MODEL_ID_IN_MESSAGE` characters and returns a message advising users to verify the exact model ID. The change improves recognition of BYOK provider rejection responses that embed quoted model names.
5e1579a5cab63056ed76b338490991bc981e05b7.evidence: In `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts`, the `BYOK_MODEL_REJECTION_PATTERNS` regex array adds a new pattern matching model IDs wrapped in backticks, single quotes, or double quotes with escaped characters, and the `getByokProviderErrorMessage` function returns a descriptive message using `MAX_MODEL_ID_IN_MESSAGE` (120) to truncate the model name, all within the same file.
5e1579a5cab63056ed76b338490991bc981e05b7.unknowns: The rollout timing of this error-matching change across the SDK and CLI is not visible in the diff. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

5e1579a5cab63056ed76b338490991bc981e05b7.text: The assistant's built-in helper that reads error messages from AI providers now recognizes cases where a provider says a model name is wrong, even when that name is wrapped in quotes or special markers. Previously some valid error messages were missed because the model ID in the error text was quoted, which let the pattern fail to match. This affects the developer tools (the SDK) that build apps and scripts on top of the assistant, not the assistant experience itself. If you're not building with the SDK, you won't notice this change and have no action to take.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff Desktop 0.2.2 ships with a new install-id header that the desktop app sends on its requests, plus updates to the BYOK (bring-your-own-key) connection flow. When you set up a custom provider key, the app can now tell you whether the endpoint is reachable, whether that specific model is listed by the provider, and it can suggest a fix (like adding /v1 to the URL) when something looks wrong. It also now asks you to reconfirm your key's environment variable name if you change the endpoint to a different one, since a new endpoint means a new key might be needed. Behind the scenes, the desktop client also shares a bit more about your terminal environment (like proxy settings and timezone overrides) with the service to help with diagnostics, but only presence flags and fixed bucket names, not raw values.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.2 release with daily-limit stop and install-id header
2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.2.2 release bumps the manifest at freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.2.1 to 0.2.2, and ships three prior members that landed in this window. A spent GPT-6.1 Sol daily session limit is now a hard stop rather than a silent fallback to another model, via a new `dailyLimitReached` field on model_unavailable admission responses read in use-freebuff-session.ts. CLI update: freebuff-premium-reset now takes a single resolved quota row instead of the whole rate-limits map. A random install id header constant is defined but has no reader in the diff yet. Three other release members (BYOK endpoint validation, client environment descriptor, docs testing) are left out of this summary because their prose was discredited and no source evidence was supplied for them.
2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.evidence: Current commit 2cde35ae bumps the release manifest at freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.2.1 to 0.2.2 (release-bump, +5/-1). Member 2f6a1d4e adds FREEBUFF_INSTALL_ID_HEADER = 'x-freebuff-install-id' as a new export in common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts but the diff shows no reader of it yet. Member 039c9076 rewrites getFreebuffPremiumResetAt in cli/src/utils/freebuff-premium-reset.ts to take a single `quota` param instead of `rateLimitsByModel`. Member 2ac20ca0 adds the dailyLimitReached boolean to the model_unavailable branch of the FreebuffSessionAdmissionResponse in common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts and wires useFreebuffSession in cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts to treat it as a stop, never a fallback.
2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.unknowns: The release member text for the BYOK, client-environment, and testing changes was discredited and no source evidence was supplied, so their mechanisms and audience are not described here.

changes.what: Release manifest version bumped from 0.2.1 to 0.2.2 in the Freebuff CLI package.
use-freebuff-session now treats a spent daily session limit as a stop instead of a fallback to another model.
getFreebuffPremiumResetAt now accepts a single resolved quota row instead of the rate-limits map.
FREEBUFF_INSTALL_ID_HEADER constant defined but has no reader in the diff yet.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.2 adds a clear stop when you reach a model's daily session limit and improves how your own provider key connects and is validated. When a model's daily session limit is spent, the app now stops the session and tells you the model is used up instead of silently switching you to a different model, so you are not quoted one price and charged for another. The /byok command for connecting your own API key now better handles pasted URLs that split across lines, requires the credential variable name when you change the base URL to a new endpoint, reads the provider's model list to warn you if your chosen model id is not listed, and gives specific error messages when a key is unset, rejected, or unreachable. A new client environment descriptor sent with requests now reports proxy settings, TLS certificate overrides, timezone overrides, and the system timezone, so connection issues are easier to diagnose. The release also fixes a test-harness hang where a lazy database query could stall a job, and updates documentation about how CI guards against tests silently disappearing.

039c90769849244284480ca92f0b350f7aa0a71b.title: Resolve shared quota pool by majority vote across clients
039c90769849244284480ca92f0b350f7aa0a71b.summary: The landing-screen session counter, the session-ended banner, and the model-selector premium header each previously read Object.values(...)[0] from rateLimitsByModel, which picked whichever pool the server happened to serialize first. A new getFreebuffSharedPoolQuota export in common/src/util/freebuff-session-pools.ts resolves the pool by majority vote over a section's rows and skips subscription-backed rows so a private allowance never labels another model's quota; the landing counter and banner now call it with isFreebuffPremiumModelId, and getFreebuffPremiumResetAt in cli/src/utils/freebuff-premium-reset.ts now accepts the resolved quota row instead of the whole map.
039c90769849244284480ca92f0b350f7aa0a71b.evidence: Commit 039c9076 modifies cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx and cli/src/components/session-ended-banner.tsx to replace Object.values(rateLimitsByModel)[0] with getFreebuffSharedPoolQuota(rateLimitsByModel, isFreebuffPremiumModelId); adds the getFreebuffSharedPoolQuota export to common/src/util/freebuff-session-pools.ts, which resolves a section's header pool by majority vote and excludes subscription-backed rows; edits cli/src/utils/freebuff-premium-reset.ts so getFreebuffPremiumResetAt takes a single FreebuffSessionRateLimit instead of the whole map.
039c90769849244284480ca92f0b350f7aa0a71b.unknowns: The diff does not show the rollout schedule for the subscription-backed row behavior or whether older servers without pool labels still serialize in the expected order.

changes.what: Adds getFreebuffSharedPoolQuota which resolves a section's header pool by majority vote and excludes subscription-backed rows, and updates getFreebuffSectionQuotas to compute counts over non-subscription candidates.

Replaces Object.values(rateLimitsByModel)[0] for sessionRateLimit with getFreebuffSharedPoolQuota(rateLimitsByModel, isFreebuffPremiumModelId) so the landing counter reflects the premium pool, and passes the resolved quota to getFreebuffPremiumResetAt.

Replaces the first-entry premiumQuota selector with getFreebuffSharedPoolQuota(getRateLimitsByModel(s.session), isFreebuffPremiumModelId) so the banner reports the same pool the landing counter shows.
Changes getFreebuffPremiumResetAt to accept a quota?: FreebuffSessionRateLimit parameter instead of rateLimitsByModel?: FreebuffSessionRateLimitByModel, reading quota?.resetAt directly.
Passes the resolved sharedRateLimit to getFreebuffPremiumResetAt instead of rateLimitsByModel.

039c90769849244284480ca92f0b350f7aa0a71b.text: When several models share one daily usage pool, the assistant used to pick whichever number the server listed first to show the countdown and used-so-far count, which could label the wrong pool and show a stale or incorrect limit beside the model you actually used. The change makes the landing counter, the post-session banner, and the model picker all agree on a single pool by majority vote over the rows shown, while giving any per-model ceiling or subscriber allowance its own separate chip instead of letting it speak for the group. This affects anyone using the free CLI, web, desktop, or SDK session surfaces when their account has more than one quota pool in the same section.

fc37ac10e299ace4c9055da809823202303a75c8.title: Caller abort signal now short-circuits idle timeout error text
fc37ac10e299ace4c9055da809823202303a75c8.summary: The agent runtime and SDK now distinguish a caller-initiated abort from a server-side idle timeout. loopAgentSteps and runOnce check `signal.aborted` before classifying an error, so a caller deadline (AbortSignal.timeout, which rejects with a TimeoutError) no longer surfaces as Freebuff's five-minute fetch idle timeout message. The two new tests in cli/src/hooks and sdk/src/__tests__ pin this behavior: a caller deadline reports 'Run cancelled by user' and a silent upstream plus caller deadline resolves at the deadline as a cancellation.
fc37ac10e299ace4c9055da809823202303a75c8.evidence: In packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts, loopAgentSteps's catch block now guards on `isAbortError(error) || signal.aborted` and comments explain the 20-second caller deadline via AbortSignal.timeout rejected as a TimeoutError that isFetchIdleTimeoutError matches. In sdk/src/run.ts, runOnce's callMainPrompt catch now branches on `signal?.aborted` to build the abort error before falling through to the idle-timeout/transient checks.
fc37ac10e299ace4c9055da809823202303a75c8.unknowns: Whether the same signal-aborted branch is reflected in other callers of the agent runtime or in the Freebuff web/desktop surfaces, which this commit's files do not show.

changes.what: loopAgentSteps catch block now treats `signal.aborted` as a user cancellation, suppressing the idle-timeout message for caller deadlines.
runOnce catch now checks `signal?.aborted` to build the abort error before falling through to idle-timeout and transient error selection.
Added assertion verifying the held session is ended with its instance id before switching models.
Added test asserting a caller deadline reports as a cancellation rather than the five-minute idle timeout.
Added test asserting run() with a caller deadline and silent upstream resolves at the deadline as a cancellation.

fc37ac10e299ace4c9055da809823202303a75c8.text: When you choose to stop a task yourself, such as by hitting a cancel button or a timer you set expiring, the assistant now correctly reports that it was your action that ended the run. Previously, a timeout you set could be mistaken for the system idly waiting five minutes and then stopping on its own, which produced a confusing message. The fix checks whether you initiated the stop before deciding what explanation to show. This affects anyone using the Freebuff assistant through the terminal, web, or desktop app, or embedding it via the SDK: you simply see the cancellation reason that matches what actually happened, with no change needed on your end.

b6925d1398492646733a7269207331d414e7a2b9.title: Add terminal client environment and input profile telemetry to CLI
b6925d1398492646733a7269207331d414e7a2b9.summary: New modules collect a compact v1 client environment descriptor (ancestor process buckets, terminal program, size, color reply) and per-prompt input profile counts (typed chars, keypresses, paste events, compose time), emitted as the x-freebuff-env header on session and ad requests and as codebuff_metadata fields on chat runs. The composer now reports each typed keystroke and bracketed paste via new onTypedText and onPaste wrappers, sealing the profile per submitted prompt keyed by its trimmed text. startClientEnvironmentProbe runs on CLI startup to fill ancestor process kinds asynchronously, and noteTerminalColorReply records the OSC color-query reply; neither blocks startup. Both descriptors are Freebuff-only, gated by IS_FREEBUFF, and send counts or fixed bucket names only, never raw prompt text, paths, or process names.
b6925d1398492646733a7269207331d414e7a2b9.evidence: Three new files added: cli/src/utils/client-environment.ts (exports getClientEnvironmentDescriptor, clientEnvironmentHeaders, startClientEnvironmentProbe, lookupProcessAncestry, formatClientEnvironment), cli/src/utils/input-profile.ts (InputProfileCounter, recordTypedInput, recordPaste, withPasteCount, sealInputProfile, takeInputProfile), common/src/constants/freebuff-client-descriptor.ts (FREEBUFF_CLIENT_ENV_HEADER, FREEBUFF_INPUT_PROFILE_METADATA_KEY, bucket types). Diff hunks in cli/src/chat.tsx, cli/src/components/multiline-input.tsx, cli/src/components/chat-input-bar.tsx, cli/src/utils/use-send-message.ts, cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-identity.ts, cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts, cli/src/ads/ad-request.ts, cli/src/ads/partner-ads.ts, cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts, cli/src/index.tsx wire these together.
b6925d1398492646733a7269207331d414e7a2b9.unknowns: The server-side consumers of the x-freebuff-env header and the freebuff_input_profile metadata key are not visible in the diff, so their use for targeting, filtering, or billing is not established by these changes alone.

changes.what: Adds startClientEnvironmentProbe to launch async ancestor process lookup, noteTerminalColorReply to record the OSC color reply, and clientEnvironmentHeaders to emit the x-freebuff-env descriptor on IS_FREEBUFF requests.

Adds InputProfileCounter tracking typed chars, keypresses, multi-char events, pasted chars, paste events, compose milliseconds, and peak typed chars per second, with sealInputProfile binding a snapshot to a submitted prompt and takeInputProfile consuming it for metadata.

Defines the x-freebuff-env header constant, metadata keys for client environment and input profile, the v1 descriptor version, and TerminalProgramBucket and ProcessKindBucket literal types used by the bucketing functions.
Calls sealInputProfile(inputValue) in handleSubmit and wraps createPasteHandler with withPasteCount so bracketed pastes are counted before the paste handler runs.
Threads onTypedText={recordTypedInput} through to MultilineInput and invokes onTypedText?.(textToInsert) in handleCharacterInput so every typed key event is recorded.
Calls clientDescriptorMetadata(content) inside extraCodebuffMetadata for Freebuff non-BYOK runs and spreads clientEnvironmentHeaders() into ad auction, impression, click, and session request headers.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.text: This Freebuff CLI update adds two small but useful improvements you can notice day to day. First, the CLI now reports which model is being used when you send a prompt, so error messages clearly tell you the request was declined and which provider rejected it; this helps you switch to another model instead of seeing a confusing message. Second, the ad system on the sponsored review route now sends an audience signal (the same browser-like identifier it already uses on web), so the same targeting rules apply whether you are reading an ad in chat or on the docked web view, with no visible change to you unless you happen to qualify for a different ad fill. The release evidence is otherwise limited to packaging, so beyond these two changes the available release notes do not establish additional new capabilities.

b6925d1398492646733a7269207331d414e7a2b9.text: The Freebuff terminal assistant now quietly counts how you type and which terminal program you use, so the engineers can better understand usage patterns. It tracks things like how many characters you type versus paste, which terminal you are running (like iTerm or VS Code), and whether the terminal supports color, all without recording what you actually type or any private file names. Right now these new measurements are only collected and stored internally, they do not change anything you see or do in your coding session.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.1 release with client environment header
64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.2.1 is released from freebuff/cli/release/package.json, bumping the package version from 0.2.0 to 0.2.1. The session-admission request in cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts now spreads clientEnvironmentHeaders(), which adds the x-freebuff-env header built by the new cli/src/utils/client-environment.ts module as a compact v1 terminal-environment descriptor. On the run path, cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-identity.ts attaches freebuff_client_env and, for composer-submitted prompts, freebuff_input_profile metadata populated by cli/src/utils/input-profile.ts so the server can see terminal kind and per-prompt typing/paste counts without raw text.
64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.evidence: Commit 64e8d89a bumps the Freebuff CLI release manifest at freebuff/cli/release/package.json from version 0.2.0 to 0.2.1 (release-bump commit, +3/-1), published as Freebuff CLI release 0.2.1. A second release member (b6925d1398492646733a7269207331d414e7a2b9) modifies cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts to add clientEnvironmentHeaders() to the session-admission headers, with the descriptor built in a new cli/src/utils/client-environment.ts module and emitted as the x-freebuff-env header. cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-identity.ts adds clientDescriptorMetadata() which attaches the x-freebuff-env value and the per-prompt input profile under the freebuff_client_env and freebuff_input_profile codebuff_metadata keys on run creation, and cli/src/utils/input-profile.ts (new) counts typed/pasted characters, keypress events and compose time per submitted prompt via recordTypedInput, withPasteCount and sealInputProfile.
64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.unknowns: The server-side handler that consumes x-freebuff-env, freebuff_client_env and freebuff_input_profile is not present in the diff, so the feature's observable effect depends on a server rollout not shown here.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.1 ships a new client-environment descriptor header, an x-freebuff-env header attached to ad and session requests, which summarizes the terminal you are running in using only presence flags, terminal size, fixed terminal-program and ancestor-process buckets, and whether the terminal answered the startup color query. The release also adds per-prompt input profiling, counting how your chat message was composed (characters typed by key, multi-character key events, bracketed pastes, paste events, first-input-to-submit time, and peak typed characters per second) without sending the prompt text itself, and forwards those counts in run metadata. Error handling gains a new pattern and message for OpenAI’s cybersecurity safeguard refusal (GPT-6.1 Sol on 2026-09-30), telling you the content was flagged and that retrying the same model will be refused again. Affected users see: advertisers get a consistent terminal-context signal for ad requests, Freebuff servers get an anonymized terminal summary for session and ad calls (Freebuff builds only), and conversations refused by the cybersecurity filter now show a specific, actionable message pointing at another model. The available release evidence is incomplete on broader reliability, billing, or model-catalog changes beyond these three mechanisms.

1d624b2aaf25302cafde35530631657767e4a5d3.title: OpenAI cybersecurity safeguard error pattern and message added
1d624b2aaf25302cafde35530631657767e4a5d3.summary: A new pair of constants is exported from common/src/constants/freebuff-errors.ts to recognize OpenAI's 403 cybersecurity safeguard, matching the literal substring /flagged for possible cybersecurity risk/i, and to carry a user-facing message that tells users the request was flagged and they should try rephrasing or another model. The addition follows the same shape as the existing DeepSeek content filter recognizer, but the diff only introduces the constants and their documentation; no matching reader in cli/, sdk/, or common/src/util is present in this revision, so nothing yet consumes them.
1d624b2aaf25302cafde35530631657767e4a5d3.evidence: common/src/constants/freebuff-errors.ts adds two new exports, FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CYBER_RISK_ERROR_PATTERN (/flagged for possible cybersecurity risk/i) and FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CYBER_RISK_MESSAGE ("[freebuff product prompt text omitted]"), alongside a comment stating the pattern matches OpenAI's 403 cybersecurity safeguard seen on GPT-6.1 Sol (2026-09-30).
1d624b2aaf25302cafde35530631657767e4a5d3.unknowns: The commit introduces the error pattern and message constants but does not include the matching or recovery code that reads them, so their consumer and the surface that will use them are not visible in this diff.

1d624b2aaf25302cafde35530631657767e4a5d3.text: Engineers added two new pieces of shared wording that the app can recognize and display when a model from OpenAI refuses a request because its cybersecurity filter thinks the input looks risky. These pieces of wording sit in the app’s central error definitions and include both a way to detect OpenAI’s refusal text and a message explaining that the request was flagged and the user should try rephrasing or pick a different model. No part of the app currently reads or uses these new pieces yet, so you will not see any change right now. This is internal work only for the Freebuff engineering team, and nothing behaves differently until a later change puts the new wording into the app’s error-handling flow.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.1 adds a new way for the app to describe what kind of terminal and typing setup you are using. When you use Freebuff, your computer sends a short, privacy-safe summary of your terminal program and how you typed your question (keystrokes vs paste), so the ad system can target and count things more accurately. The app still works the same, but this extra detail helps the service show ads and handle your session in a more accurate way across requests.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.1 release bump
64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.summary: The `version` in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` is bumped from 0.2.0 to 0.2.1. This release window also contains two adjacent members: a CLI change that attaches the `x-freebuff-env` client-descriptor header to ad auction and impression requests and sends per-prompt input counts via `clientDescriptorMetadata`, and a common-side addition of `FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CYBER_RISK_ERROR_PATTERN` and `FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CYBER_RISK_MESSAGE` for OpenAI's 403 cybersecurity-safeguard refusal. The release-bump commit itself modifies only the version field.
64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.evidence: The Freebuff CLI release manifest at `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumps the `version` field from 0.2.0 to 0.2.1 in this release-bump commit (+3/-1), and the release-member source evidence shows adjacent members `b6925d13` (CLI ad-request update adding `x-freebuff-env` headers and input-profile metadata) and `1d624b2a` (common freebuff-errors adding `FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CYBER_RISK_ERROR_PATTERN` and `FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CYBER_RISK_MESSAGE`).
64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.unknowns: Whether the 0.2.1 release is actually published and whether the two adjacent members are included in this release window are not shown by the release-bump commit alone.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.1 ships two user-facing additions built for Freebuff (the free, ad-supported tier): a compact terminal-environment descriptor and a per-prompt typing-paste profile, both attached to ad requests and session/run metadata. Ad requests now carry an x-freebuff-env header and codebuff_metadata carrying a v1;in=...;out=...;tp=...;sz=...;osc=... style string that summarizes terminal/TTY/CI/SSH status, detected terminal program, process ancestry, and whether the terminal answered the startup color query, so ad targeting and bot filtering use the same client facts the server already sees on session calls. Chat input is now counted: typed characters, keypresses, multi-character keypresses, pasted characters, paste events, time-to-first-input, and peak characters-per-second are sealed when you submit a prompt and forwarded in codebuff_metadata as freebuff_input_profile (freebuff-only), while pastes are counted through a wrapped paste handler and the profile resets on each submit. Finally, a rejected 'cybersecurity risk' error message for Freebuff runs is replaced with product prompt text (per the shared freebuff-errors constant), so OpenAI 403 content-flag responses are now described with in-product wording instead of echoing the provider's text. The available release evidence is incomplete regarding any performance, reliability, or quality gains; this roll-up reflects only what the source hunks establish.

0f5eda6e9e294d729f7798c7bf3d9263eeed44bc.title: WSL commands allowed instead of refused in sponsored runs
0f5eda6e9e294d729f7798c7bf3d9263eeed44bc.summary: The sponsored-run command walk no longer refuses WSL entry as a class. In `common/src/ads/sponsored-command-refusals.ts`, the `wsl` refusal kind, the `WSL_COMMANDS` set, the `WSL_SHARE` regex, and the `isWindowsWslBash` helper were removed, and a `wslCommand` helper now unwraps the WSL options (-d, --distribution, -u, --user, --cd, -e, --exec, --shell-type) and returns the inner command line so it is inspected by the existing database, container, git and unverifiable rules. `cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts` and `common/src/ads/sponsored-local-execution.ts` updated one comment each to drop the WSL mention. The net effect is that entering WSL is permitted, while destructive database, container lifecycle, and history-moving git subcommands reached through WSL are still refused by the same walk.

0f5eda6e9e294d729f7798c7bf3d9263eeed44bc.text: The change lets a sponsored task run commands through the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) instead of refusing them outright. Previously, launching WSL from a sponsored run was blocked as a whole class; now the assistant unwraps the WSL layer and inspects whatever command comes after it, still refusing destructive database and container commands if those are hidden underneath. This affects developers who use the Freebuff CLI to run advertiser-sponsored tasks in place, letting their procedures reach their Linux toolchains through WSL.

The legacy single-session fallback still calls firstTabQuoteForSession but now always passes the 'single' surface, releasing the discount reservation for ended single-session purchases.

592b3211840b26f528305bfbea7954cdbc5ead5b.text: When you have an active Freebucks purchase in the CLI, the assistant now keeps that purchase's discount and time reservation in place instead of routing it through a different discount path meant for first-time buyers. This only applies to CLI-based Freebucks purchases linked to the current session; older single-session purchases still release their discount when they end. If you are using the CLI and start or switch a paid session, you will now keep the discount you originally bought for that session rather than seeing a quoted replacement price applied through the standard first-tab discount. The change does not affect free-tier usage or anyone buying Freebucks through the web or desktop apps.

51b40e3b7df6b180ed089d2204f6bb3a91f93c4f.summary: The `role`, `intended_use`, and subscriptions questions in `FREEBUFF_ONBOARDING_QUESTIONS` now carry `shuffleOptions: true`, so their chips render in a random order per form mount, matching the behavior already shared by the `referral_source` question. The shared form logic in `common/src/constants/freebuff-onboarding-form.ts` shuffles every flagged question via a seeded Fisher - Yates, pins the `other` option last, and leaves the kind: 'scale' proficiency question in its fixed ordered ramp. A new test, "shuffles every choice question while preserving the proficiency scale", asserts that every choice question is shuffled while the proficiency scale keeps its order.

51b40e3b7df6b180ed089d2204f6bb3a91f93c4f.text: When you sign up for Freebuff and get asked a few quick questions about who you are, what you want to build, and which coding tools you already use, the answer choices now appear in a different, random order each time, instead of always in the same list. This only affects the new signup form and only the questions without a natural order; the sliding 'how much do you code' scale still goes from left to right as usual. You, as someone filling out the form, just see the options shuffled, so you might spot 'Founder' before 'Developer' on one day versus another, with no action needed on your part. The shuffle is in place behind the scenes; it does not change what Freebuff can or cannot do for you.

e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.text: Freebuff 0.2.0 caps how much deep reasoning certain AI models will do before they start to slow down, lowering the maximum reasoning depth for Muse Spark and GPT-6.1 Sol and locking Gemini 3.8 Flash at a fixed middle setting. The reasoning limits come from measurements showing the highest setting gave only a small gains in thinking quality for a much bigger cost in waiting time, so the service now keeps responses snappier. The onboarding survey also shuffles its answer options and adds new subscription choices like Lovable, Replit, Cursor, and Codex, while the Freebucks credit system stops promising that a discount from one purchase will transfer to a different model. Affected users are people choosing AI models from the picker, anyone buying or using Freebucks credits, and new signups going through the setup questions, and the available evidence does not establish broader safety or reliability changes to the CLI itself.

e3d7701e9223662ede68d501c3bdc686168d36cb.title: Agent runtime refuses cut-off file writes and tool calls
e3d7701e9223662ede68d501c3bdc686168d36cb.summary: The agent runtime now refuses two shapes of a file edit that was cut off mid-generation, per packages/agent-runtime/src/util/truncated-write-guard.ts. In process-file-block.ts a write_file that would replace a 30+ line file with under 60% of its size and leave brackets open where the original balances them is rejected via detectTruncatedRewrite and logged as axiomEvent file_write_guard with metric truncated_rewrite_refused. In tool-executor.ts parseRawToolCall now returns a ToolCallError carrying a new truncated:true flag when isTruncatedJsonPrefix recognises incomplete JSON arguments, answering with truncatedToolCallMessage that names the cause (output token limit or dropped connection) and never echoes the partial input. common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts adds the matching file_write_guard event constant and a FILE_WRITE_GUARD_FIELDS allowlist of content-free metadata (sizes, tool and model names, runId) so the refusal is observable on the Axiom stream.
