e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.text: This release adds a safety feature that stops the assistant from saving a file when its response gets cut off mid-generation: if a write attempt looks like a partial, incomplete copy of an existing file, nothing is written and the file on disk stays unchanged. It also changes how the assistant reports cut-off tool calls to you, showing a clear "nothing was written" message instead of asking you to re-send the same oversized call. Behind the scenes, new operational logs record these refused writes so the team can monitor when they happen. The result is that you no longer risk having a half-finished or truncated file overwrite your work when the model hits an output limit.

e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.text: Freebuff 0.2.0 ships a quieter default reasoning level for the Muse Spark model, plus small fixes to how Freebucks balances and the onboarding flow reads. The Muse Spark 1.2 and 1.3 Contributor rows now cap their reasoning effort at 'high' instead of 'xhigh', a product-side change meant to trade a bit of reasoning depth for lower latency on those models. The Freebucks balance logic was updated so multi-session CLI purchases keep their reserved discount and hour in place, while legacy single-session end states still release their discount reservation, and the balance check now relies on a server quote rather than promising a discount will transfer to another model. Onboarding questions now consistently shuffle their options and the role question gained shuffling too, so the form no longer always shows the same fixed order. The release evidence is incomplete for the '3 other changes left out of this list because a check discredited its summary', so I can not describe those.

5d525143041ab63d8faf7aec68b3ef6eb11be287.text: The assistant's reasoning depth controls for three premium models were adjusted. Freebuff developers who select these paid models in the app will see them think less deeply than before. Specifically, Muse Spark now caps its reasoning effort at 'high' instead of the previous maximum, GPT-6.1 Sol also caps at 'high' with a hard limit, and GPT-6 Luna removes its top 'max' setting. This likely means slightly faster responses with potentially less thorough analysis for these specific paid models, while all other model settings remain unchanged.

e3d7701e9223662ede68d501c3bdc686168d36cb.text: The AI coding assistant now refuses to apply a file edit that appears to have been cut off mid-generation instead of writing a broken, half-finished version of your file to disk. This matters when a response hits the output token limit or the connection drops while the assistant is writing a large file, which previously left your file with an incomplete fragment like code ending in `ui.horizontal_wrapped(ui` instead of a complete program. The change protects developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK who rely on the assistant editing their files, so you will now get a clear error telling you nothing was written and suggesting smaller, targeted edits via str_replace rather than silently corrupting your file with a truncated copy.

e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.11 ships a new safety guard that stops the assistant from applying file edits that were cut off mid-generation. When a response runs out of output room or drops its connection in the middle of a file write, the old behavior could leave a half-written file on disk; this release refuses that write instead and explains what happened, so the file on disk is left unchanged and you are pointed toward making smaller edits. The refusal is logged with only content-free details (sizes, tool and model names) and never echoes the partial content back to the model, which avoids the model mistaking the head of the file for the file itself. This change applies to write_file, str_replace, apply_patch, propose_write_file, propose_str_replace, and create_plan, and is enforced both when a tool call's arguments are incomplete JSON and when a completed write_file would replace an existing file with a suspiciously short, bracket-left-open copy of itself. Users writing or rewriting files through the agent loop get a clearer error and protection against truncated writes overwriting their files; the rest of the release is a packaging version bump only.

41c03830a5fb0af4241a56663cfadfa6cfa24a56.title: BYOK reasoning effort command and request body support

The SDK request transform now writes the effort into the outgoing completion body using a dialect per provider, with an Anthropic thinking budget added on top of the `max_tokens` output cap (`ANTHROPIC_ANSWER_TOKENS`), and retries a once-stripped body when a provider returns 400 or 422 referencing the reasoning field. A 400 or 422 mentioning reasoning_effort, thinking, or budget_tokens is retried without it and remembered per connection revision. This spans the CLI, shared reasoning-effort constants, and the BYOK SDK packages across 7 files.

The SDK applies that effort to BYOK request bodies in `sdk/src/impl/byok-request.ts` (byokRequestTransform, applyReasoningEffort, byokReasoningRetryBody, byokReasoningDialect, BYOK_ANTHROPIC_THINKING_BUDGETS, ANTHROPIC_ANSWER_TOKENS) and the model provider in `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts` retries with a stripped body on 400/422 rejections.

fa7f6a239db7ed3d74758432e00ac1acdbc847f4.title: UTM tagging for sponsored procedure links at save time
fa7f6a239db7ed3d74758432e00ac1acdbc847f4.summary: A new module tags advertiser-domain URLs inside agentic procedures when they are saved, so visits from sponsored runs carry Freebuff attribution. `tagSponsoredProcedureLinks` appends ordered UTM pairs only to untagged links on an advertiser's own domains and skips code spans, command lines, API hosts, file URLs and links that already carry any `utm_*` parameter. The added `SUPABASE_PINNED_PROCEDURE_SHA256S` set pins the catalog procedure hashes that must stay byte-identical so the save-time rewriter cannot disturb stored procedure text.

Hunk in `common/src/ads/supabase-format-experiment.ts` adds `SUPABASE_PINNED_PROCEDURE_SHA256S`, a set that re-includes `SUPABASE_FORMAT_AUTH_PROCEDURE.procedureSha256` and is documented to be unchanged by the UTM writer.

fa7f6a239db7ed3d74758432e00ac1acdbc847f4.text: When a sponsored run shows a developer a help article or product page on an advertiser's own website, Freebuff now quietly adds the advertiser's tracking tags to that link as it is saved, so the advertiser can see the visit came from Freebuff even though the agent opened the page directly rather than through a redirect. The tagging only touches plain links the developer would open in prose, skips links inside code, installation commands, API hosts, download files, and any link that already carries tracking tags, and it borrows the advertiser's own campaign tags when they set them on their landing page.

41c03830a5fb0af4241a56663cfadfa6cfa24a56.text: A new option was added so you can tell the assistant how deeply it should think before answering, but only when you are running the assistant through your own AI service key. You pick a level (low, medium, or high) with a chat command, and that choice is remembered for future runs that use your key. The chosen level is translated into the right format for whichever service you connected to, and if a service does not accept that setting, the request is automatically retried without it. This applies to you only if you run the assistant using your own provider account key.

f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.text: This Freebuff CLI 0.1.10 release adds the ability for users who bring their own AI provider key (BYOK) to choose how much 'reasoning effort' a model puts in. A new `/byok effort` command lets you pick low, medium, or high reasoning for models you run with your own API key. The chosen effort is only applied to the start of a run, and only for tools that a model supports, so picking an unsupported option falls back without breaking the run. If a provider rejects the chosen reasoning level, the system automatically retries without it and remembers that preference so it does not keep trying. The CLI version is bumped to 0.1.10 and a new subscription billing helper is added for internal cost reporting. For developers, if you are not using your own provider key, nothing changes here.

afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.9 adds GPT-6.1 Sol as a new free model option and a post-click return label (COD-694) to measure whether ad clickers come back to the assistant. Concrete highlights: GPT-6.1 Sol is now available, free in the US and a paid plan elsewhere, with one session a day for every account; the picker, README, and admission debit all agree on that daily limit so a second session is rejected cleanly. Ad click return tracking now records when a user returns after clicking an ad, measuring click-to-next-prompt latency as the signal since a terminal cannot detect focus, with a 30-minute watch window and matching wire contract. Untagged links in a sponsored procedure are now auto-tagged with the advertiser's own UTM parameters if present, otherwise with Freebuff's defaults, applied once at save time so the executed and reviewed text stay byte-identical. Everyday impact: any Freebuff user in the US (or anyone on a paid plan) can now pick GPT-6.1 Sol in the model picker, but each account gets exactly one session per day on it regardless of plan, a cap enforced before you reach a refusal. Advertisers gain a consistent signal of whether ad clicks bring users back to the assistant, improving ad attribution without changing which ads you see. Links the assistant hands you while following a sponsored task now carry proper tracking tags so ad clicks can be attributed correctly. The final catalog at this release confirms GPT-6.1 Sol is in the free model picker, matching the documented daily-session cap; the available release evidence is otherwise incomplete on timing of availability and regional rollout details.

afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.9 ships GPT-6.1 Sol in the free model picker, a new OpenAI flagship model offered at a temporary promotional price (free in the US, paid-plan-required elsewhere) with a hard limit of one session per day for every account, and it is announced with a New badge on the Desktop and Web pickers. The house ad copy was updated so that subscribers are now served only house campaigns measured on subscription_started (the Discord join, Freebucks top-up and model launch campaigns still reach subscribers), and the change applies to both Web and Freebuff Web surfaces. GPT-6 Luna is a full-access model and Space Bunny Alpha is beta, both now available for selection. The ad-serving system gained click-through tracking: when you click an ad it watches for your next prompt (or another ad click) to confirm you came back, and it sends that return signal after the click itself is recorded. The promotion label for GPT-6.1 Sol now states the one-session-a-day daily cap up front so nobody hits the limit for the first time as a refusal. The README model table now lists GPT-6.1 Sol with its daily session cap noted in the Best for description instead of the previous generic promotional-price text.

bb46c52bc16e41ff79cb08aa459448643ab95ddb.text: The ad-auction request now records whether the most recent message was typed by the developer (labeled USER_PROMPT) or injected automatically by the runtime (labeled STEP_PROMPT or TOOL_CALL_ERROR), and only these three labels are forwarded to the auction server. This affects only Freebuff's internal ad-targeting pipeline; Freebuff users do not see any change in their chat experience. In daily use nothing looks different, because the change only helps the ad server tell the developer's own prompt apart from the system's automatic messages.

73c6ceb590d8d56df307de723563cd09d01e2ea0.text: The Freebuff CLI now records whether you come back to the assistant after clicking an ad. It starts a 30-minute timer when you click an ad, and treats your next typed prompt as proof you returned, measuring how long you were away. This signal feeds the ad-targeting pipeline and is applied by an evaluation lab, not the client itself. The feature is internal measurement for ad performance, not an ad displayed to you.

28ccadc6687c271cf00e473547c11ed8a096c363.text: A special discounted price was added for OpenAI's newest GPT-6.1 Sol model, and every Freebuff account is now limited to using it for only one paid hour per day (called a session), even if you have a paid plan. The model picker and pricing notice now clearly tell you this limit before you try to use it, so you won't be surprised by an unexpected refusal. You'll see a note about the "one session a day" cap next to GPT-6.1 Sol when you open the model list or read the pricing details, and when you select the model, Freebuff tracks how long that session lasts and will let you know if you've reached your daily limit. This change applies to all developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK, and it does not affect your regular daily usage allowance for other models.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.text: Freebuff 0.1.8 adds a new ad slot for launch-related content. When you type about launching, deploying, shipping, or demoing your work in the composer, a partner ad row appears above your input (alongside the existing pull-request ad slot). The two slots never appear together, and neither shows while a menu, review screen, or takeover is open. The streak bonus also became easier to understand: it now goes into your daily allowance and expires with that allowance, rather than sitting in your wallet, and the landing screen no longer shows an old tier-change notice. Telemetry for the ad-serving fatigue layer was expanded, and the Muse Spark model can now fall back to an OpenRouter lane with a price ceiling. The package version is bumped to 0.1.8.

25fab627e738eaf5ca5c596187c62fc2e12c5649.text: A new line item was added to the place where Freebuff's ad system tracks the total results for each ad slot (in the shared placements constant module). This new value records money earned from certain billboard-style ads that are billed separately through an insertion order, meaning the amount is not counted in the normal spend totals used for rate calculations. The change affects whoever is running ads on Freebuff's ad rail, since that is who the placements console and its numbers belong to. For an advertiser, the console now adds those separately invoiced ad earnings to what is shown as spend and result pricing, so their reported numbers reflect that extra income without altering the per-impression costs already calculated from the regular totals.

51e08c800533ae4206e4e740eade9b700d2b7d9f.text: The short marketing text that appears in Freebuff's subscription ads has been rewritten, swapping a few lines of copy for slightly different wording while keeping the same overall message. This only affects the fallback safety-net ad shown to Freebuff's free users when no paid campaign is running; paying subscribers still see nothing here, and the ad-serving rules and frequency caps are unchanged. The developer notes that, because this file lives in a shared package, the web frontend may need a separate deploy to actually show the new text, but no user action is required.

afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.title: Freebuff CLI 0.1.9 release with GPT-6.1 Sol and ad click return
afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.summary: The Freebuff CLI ships as version 0.1.9, adding GPT-6.1 Sol (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`) to the free model picker with a temporary promotional price, one session per day across every account and a "New" picker badge. GPT-6.1 Sol is paid only on the Pro-only surface and slot-bound on Desktop, with model entries added to the base2/base3 agent maps, subscription premium list, reviewer map, and `FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_SLOT_BOUND_MODEL_IDS` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts` and `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`. The release also adds post-click return tracking via new `common/src/ads/click-return.ts` and `cli/src/ads/click-return.ts` modules wired into the CLI prompt path and ad click recording, plus a `newBadge` field on `FreebuffModelOption` and forwarding of runtime source tags on ad auction messages.
afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.evidence: Release commit bumps `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` from `0.1.8` to `0.1.9`; the window also adds GPT-6.1 Sol to the free model picker in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` with a promotional field and a new `newBadge` on the Muse Spark 1.3 row, and pins a one-session-per-day limit via `FREEBUFF_DAILY_SESSION_LIMITS` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-sol-promo.ts`; CLI ad click handling gains a post-click return watcher in `cli/src/ads/click-return.ts` wired through `cli/src/commands/router.ts` and `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts`, and ad request messages forward runtime source tags (`USER_PROMPT`/`STEP_PROMPT`/`TOOL_CALL_ERROR`) from `cli/src/ads/ad-request.ts`; README model table rows for GPT-6.1 Sol updated in `README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`, and `freebuff/cli/release/README.md`.
afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.unknowns: The full set of behavioral consumers for the new click-return endpoint and whether the `newBadge`/promotional rendering shipped on Desktop and Web in this release is not fully shown by the partial diff.

afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.text: Freebuff 0.1.9 adds a new promotional AI model called GPT-6.1 Sol to the picker. GPT-6.1 Sol is free in the US and needs a paid plan elsewhere, and every account, paid or not, gets one session per day with it. GPT-6.1 Sol is now paired with its own dedicated code reviewer agent and its own orchestrator, and it has been added to the model catalog, desktop concurrency limits, subscription premium lists, and reviewer mappings. The release also adds UTM link-tagging to sponsored task output so clicks on advertiser links in a run are correctly credited to Freebuff. For ad clicks, the CLI now tracks when you come back after opening an ad link by watching for your next prompt, an upper bound on how long you were away. The house ad campaign changes so that subscribers are still shown non-subscription house campaigns (like Discord join), not just the subscription one. A pinned-procedure hash guard is added to keep UTM tagging from changing the bytes that readiness checks hash, and GPT-6.1 Sol has its promotion text updated to clearly state the one-session-a-day limit so you never hit the limit as a surprise refusal.

No runtime enforcement code is shown in the diff, so the constants are defined in place but not yet read by any consumer.
1654e2212f8267b7b9bebccea8ec5a4992d638d8.evidence: Added two new exported constants in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`: MUSE_SPARK_OPENROUTER_UPSTREAM_ORDER = ['meta'] as const, and MUSE_SPARK_OPENROUTER_MAX_PRICE = { prompt: 0.15, completion: 0.3 } as const, accompanied by a JSDoc block describing the OpenRouter lane for Muse Spark Contributor requests.

1654e2212f8267b7b9bebccea8ec5a4992d638d8.text: Freebuff engineers added two new configuration entries for Muse Spark's backup route through OpenRouter, pinning it to the 'meta' upstream and capping its price at $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.30 per million output tokens; this keeps picks flowing through Meta's account on OpenRouter at the same rate as the direct key, which Meta blocked for policy reasons on September 28, 2026, routing traffic to a fallback model instead. The configuration only applies to the internal routing logic that directs traffic through OpenRouter, so it primarily affects the Freebuff engineering team and how the system handles model selection behind the scenes.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.8 adds a new launch-intent partner ad slot that appears in the composer row when you type launch-related words like ship, deploy, announce, demo, video, deck, slides, pitch, landing, producthunt, or changelog. A new mentionsLaunchKeyword helper detects these whole words in your prompt to trigger the CLI-Partner-Composer-Launch placement, complementing the existing PR-intent ad slot. The release also fixes the streak bonus display so the daily Freebucks reward and its expiration are shown in your local time zone, correcting confusion where users east of Pacific thought their bonus was missing. Additionally, the tier change notice constant was removed from the landing screen, and the package version was bumped to 0.1.8. The available release evidence is incomplete regarding broader model updates or performance gains.

bb4c8ba7c39a35a6514781f05ae534d40f2db56f.title: Streak bonus status now tracks allowance expiration and dual resets
bb4c8ba7c39a35a6514781f05ae534d40f2db56f.summary: The streak response gains `bonusExpiresAt`: when today's Freebucks streak bonus leaves the daily allowance (its own reset, not the streak day's Pacific reset), as an ISO instant that is null once passed. `getFreebuffStreakBonusStatus` now emits the expiration alongside the next streak-day reset in the reader's local clock, rendering one reset for Pacific readers and both for non-Pacific ones. The Freebucks window also carries `streakBonus`, the 15-per-day portion of `limit`, so the allowance can label what the streak added. Two test files cover granted, expired, credited, and older-server branches.
bb4c8ba7c39a35a6514781f05ae534d40f2db56f.evidence: Commit [bb4c8ba7] modifies four files: cli/src/utils/freebuff-streak-line.ts, common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts, common/src/types/freebuff-streak.ts, and common/src/util/freebuff-streak-line.ts, plus their two test files. The diff adds a `bonusExpiresAt` field to FreebuffStreakResponse, threads it through getFreebuffStreakBonusStatusForLayout -> getFreebuffStreakBonusStatus -> formatFreebuffStreakResetTime for dual-reset copy, and adds a `streakBonus` field to FreebuffFreebucksWindow. New tests assert granted/expired/credited bonus copy and Pacific-reader single-reset wording.
bb4c8ba7c39a35a6514781f05ae534d40f2db56f.unknowns: The diff does not show which server versions emit `bonusExpiresAt`; behavior for accounts off the Freebucks meter (null `freebucksDailyBonus`) is preserved but the rollout audience for the new window field is not named. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Adds `bonusExpiresAt?: string | null` to FreebuffStreakResponse, documenting when today's granted bonus leaves the daily allowance (null once passed, absent on older servers).

Reworks getFreebuffStreakBonusStatus to read `bonusExpiresAt` and render dual-reset copy (today's allowance reset plus next streak-day reset in the reader's clock), plus a granted-but-expired branch; updates getFreebuffStreakPerk wording to '+N to your daily allowance with each day's first message'.
Threads `bonusExpiresAt` from the incoming FreebuffStreakResponse into getFreebuffStreakBonusStatus within getFreebuffStreakBonusStatusForLayout.
Adds optional `streakBonus?: number` to FreebuffFreebucksWindow, documenting it as the 15-per-day portion of `limit` that expires with the pool at `resetAt`.

bb4c8ba7c39a35a6514781f05ae534d40f2db56f.text: Freebuff now tracks when your daily Freebucks bonus from a streak of 7+ days runs out, and tells you that in your own timezone along with when your next streak day starts. Developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK see a clearer daily status line that distinguishes a bonus that has already reset from one that is still active. You only see this if your daily allowance is in the new rollout audience; accounts already off the Freebucks meter are unaffected, and older servers that don't send the new fields fall back to the previous wording.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.text: This Freebuff CLI update adds a new launch-intent partner ad slot that appears as a single colored line above your message box when you type words like 'deploy', 'ship', 'launch', or 'demo' -- the same kind of targeted ad already shown for pull-request mentions, now extended to cover launching and showing off what you built. The streak bonus display was made more precise: on the Freebucks meter, the daily bonus is now described as added to your daily allowance (rather than the wallet) and shown with its expiration time in your local clock, so streak bonuses that land on someone's yesterday in distant time zones no longer read as missing. Model availability notices on the landing screen were simplified by removing the old tier-change constant for full-access users, leaving that space blank instead of showing an outdated release-note line. The advertiser placement accounting gained an optional invoiced-CPM value field (COD-677) so externally billed CPM impressions can be reported alongside product delivery figures without letting them rewrite past spend totals. The published version label in the release package.json advances from 0.1.7 to 0.1.8.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.title: Freebuff CLI 0.1.8 adds launch-intent partner ad slot
f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.summary: The CLI release bumps the package version from 0.1.7 to 0.1.8 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`. The composer partner row above the input now also checks `mentionsLaunchKeyword` against the draft and, when it matches and nothing else owns the space, auctions the new `CLI-Partner-Composer-Launch` placement instead of the PR-only slot, with `cli/src/chat.tsx` keying `PartnerAdLine` by `composerPartnerPlacementId` so a switch between slots does not keep drawing the stale fill. The matching registry entries and labels were added in `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts`, and the whole-word matcher `mentionsLaunchKeyword` with its `LAUNCH_INTENT_KEYWORDS` set landed in `common/src/ads/partner-triggers.ts`, sharing the same `mentionsAnyWord` tokenizer as the PR trigger so the two slots stay mutually exclusive per draft.
f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.evidence: The release manifest at `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` advances the version from 0.1.7 to 0.1.8, and `cli/src/ads/partner-ads.ts` adds a `composerLaunch` key set to `CLI-Partner-Composer-Launch`, with `cli/src/chat.tsx` importing `mentionsLaunchKeyword` from `common/src/ads/partner-triggers.ts` to gate that slot, and `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts` registers the new `Desktop-Partner-Composer-Launch` and `CLI-Partner-Composer-Launch` partner slots in `PLACEMENT_SLOTS` and `PLACEMENT_FORMAT_LABELS`.

Added a `composerLaunch` placement id and routed the composer partner row through a `composerPartnerPlacementId` selector that prefers the PR slot on PR intent and falls back to the launch slot on launch intent.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.8 adds a new partner ad slot that appears when you are writing a message about launching, deploying, or showing off what you built, alongside the existing pull-request ad slot. The streak bonus display now correctly tells you when today's bonus is added to your daily allowance and when it expires, fixing confusion for users in time zones east of Pacific. A notice that used to show on the landing screen for full-access accounts was removed because the daily pool is already shown in the model header and picker rows. The ad-placement metric system gained a new optional field for invoiced CPM impressions that are billed outside the product, and the fatigue-ranking layer started recording its own set of telemetry fields so ad delivery dashboards can see how fatigue scoring agrees with the main ranker. Finally, the publisher manifest was bumped to 0.1.8.

acceptedPr.title: fix(common): honor DeepSeek Beijing weekend boundaries
acceptedPr.author: c8dhjp4tyv-bit
acceptedPr.body:
> Recreated on the rewritten `main` after #1096 was auto-closed during repository maintenance. This carries the final change set from the old branch onto the new history.

Fixes #1090

## Summary

- Export and directly test the Beijing weekend predicate at the Friday/Sunday UTC boundary.
- Apply DeepSeek's weekend off-peak rule only from its effective instant, 2026-08-22T16:00:00Z.
- Keep historical pricing and expensive-window checks from retroactively treating pre-change weekends as off-peak.

## Why

The existing weekend tests used instants where UTC and Beijing were already on the same weekend day, so removing the `+8` hour conversion left the suite green. The new boundary cases pin Friday 16:00Z and Sunday 16:00Z, where the calendars diverge.

## Verification

Prior validation before the history rewrite:

- `bun test common/src/__tests__/freebuff-peak-hours.test.ts` — 26 passed
- `bun run --cwd common typecheck` — passed
- Prettier check and `git diff --check` — passed

The full `common` test command cannot pass in this public checkout because several existing tests reference private/web files absent from the mirror; the changed test file passes independently.

0fce93281ac8d26b2e7a391bbcd5c36cffa5ade0.title: Peak window time zone resolver falls back to UTC on unsupported zones
0fce93281ac8d26b2e7a391bbcd5c36cffa5ade0.summary: The weekend/peak-window resolver in `common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts` now exports `isSupportedTimeZone`, which probes a zone by constructing `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone })`, and `resolveWindowTimeZone` uses it so a zone the runtime cannot format resolves to `FALLBACK_WINDOW_TIME_ZONE` ('UTC') instead of throwing. This stops the Cloud model-picker page from crashing in browsers whose `Intl` cannot name a reported time zone, pinning Friday 16:00Z and Sunday 16:00Z boundary behavior.
0fce93281ac8d26b2e7a391bbcd5c36cffa5ade0.evidence: In `common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts`, a new exported `isSupportedTimeZone(timeZone: string)` function was added that constructs `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone })` and returns false on throw; `resolveWindowTimeZone` was rewritten to use it so an unsupported zone returns `FALLBACK_WINDOW_TIME_ZONE` ('UTC') instead of throwing. New tests assert fallback-to-UTC, rejection of guarded names, and passthrough of supported zones.
0fce93281ac8d26b2e7a391bbcd5c36cffa5ade0.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer reads `isSupportedTimeZone` outside this file or when the fix rolls out to end-user browsers.

0fce93281ac8d26b2e7a391bbcd5c36cffa5ade0.text: The code that decides which AI model you can use for free now checks whether your device's clock can name its own time zone before trying to display one. If it cannot, the message falls back to UTC instead of crashing. This only affects the screen that shows model prices and availability; everyday coding sessions are unchanged, and no action is needed from you.

3e7db03d51d7fadf954a6daaee87949e67782596.summary: The testing.md docs now spell out that a server should call server.listen(0) (or server.httpServer.listen(0) for Vite) and read back the port it actually got, and that each run needs its own cacheDir for the deps optimizer so two overlapping runs don't share node_modules/.vite. A child that exits before listening should also report its stderr and exit status, rather than printing a bare 'Vite exited before listening:' prefix with nothing after it.
3e7db03d51d7fadf954a6daaee87949e67782596.evidence: docs/testing.md: the commit adds a new section under item 1 'Three things to check before blaming the machine' elaborating that servers should listen on port 0 and read back the port they got, plus per-run cacheDir for the Vite deps optimizer, and that a child's stderr should be carried when reporting a child's death (the diff expands the Vite-related guidance by 13 lines and adjusts surrounding wording).

a99e5b771f53b678fcaf6ac889cc57487dd22a62.title: Pin freebuff-desktop flake hunts to the package's Bun version
a99e5b771f53b678fcaf6ac889cc57487dd22a62.summary: The flake-hunt guide now instructs running `freebuff-desktop` hunts on the Bun pinned in `freebuff-desktop/.bun-version` rather than the toolchain `bun` on PATH. A 2026-09-26 run that failed `mcp-consent-bridge.test.ts` only on the toolchain's Bun 1.3.14 - because its `node:http` does not emit `close` on a response whose client hung up - was captured as a deterministic version difference rather than a flake. `flake-hunt.ts` itself now aborts a desktop hunt when the `bun` it would spawn is not the pin and tells users how to satisfy it.
a99e5b771f53b678fcaf6ac889cc57487dd22a62.evidence: docs/testing.md - adds a paragraph documenting that freebuff-desktop is fuzzed on the Bun version pinned in `freebuff-desktop/.bun-version`, noting a 2026-09-26 failure of `mcp-consent-bridge.test.ts` on the toolchain Bun 1.3.14 traced to `node:http` not emitting `close` on a hung-up response, and that `flake-hunt.ts` now refuses a desktop hunt when the runnable `bun` is not the pin, plus `bunx bun@<pin>` as the workaround and `--any-bun` to opt out.
a99e5b771f53b678fcaf6ac889cc57487dd22a62.unknowns: Whether the `--any-bun` flag already existed or was introduced by the same change is not shown in the diff.

ac87c9098fc871744393073cd90171bdf837608a.title: Researcher-web capped at 15 steps with forced answer
ac87c9098fc871744393073cd90171bdf837608a.summary: The web researcher agent gains a handleSteps generator that runs at most MAX_RESEARCH_STEPS = 15 steps, then injects a forced answer instruction and yields one final 'STEP' instead of relying on the runtime's 200-step default. This caps runaway research after the 2026-09-26 incident where five messages spawned 1,519 researcher calls, and matches the behavior asserted by the new tests 'researcher-web step budget', 'a researcher that never answers is told to, then stopped', and 'survives serialization, as the runtime runs it'. The base-chat instructionsPrompt diff hunk shown here is whitespace-only and introduces no behavioral change to CONTEXT_WINDOWS. docs/testing.md adds guidance about polling the end of backgrounded work, the backgroundSettled() helper, and a budgets.ts guard that fails import on inverted wait deadlines. One concrete detail: a forced add_message of role 'user' carrying the stepPrompt content is yielded exactly once after the 15-step loop, before the final 'STEP'.
ac87c9098fc871744393073cd90171bdf837608a.evidence: agents/researcher/researcher-web.ts: a new handleSteps generator defines MAX_RESEARCH_STEPS = 15 and, after the loop, yields an add_message tool call followed by a final 'STEP'; the preceding diff hunk also added stepPrompt and a comment recounting the 2026-09-26 runaway of 1,519 researcher calls per message. agents/base-chat.ts: the only hunk shown in the diff is a no-op whitespace/comment block in instructionsPrompt (no CONTEXT_WINDOWS lines changed are part of this commit's diff hunk header). docs/testing.md: a new section documents a flaky engines.test.ts wait-on-marker-vanish test, the backgroundSettled() escape hatch, and the budgets.ts helper that rejects inverted deadlines.
ac87c9098fc871744393073cd90171bdf837608a.unknowns: The commit summary mentions Docs changes across 3 files, but the only base-chat hunk present in the provided diff is a whitespace/no-op block, so it is unclear whether other reviewers expected base-chat edits to ship in this same commit. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Added a handleSteps generator that limits the web researcher to MAX_RESEARCH_STEPS = 15, then yields a forced add_message answer and one final STEP to stop runaway search.
The visible diff hunk only touches instructionsPrompt whitespace with no CONTEXT_WINDOWS or logic change.
Documented the engines.test.ts mid-work polling flake, the backgroundSettled() await path, and the budgets.ts import-time guard against inverted wait deadlines.

ac87c9098fc871744393073cd90171bdf837608a.text: The Freebuff engineering team added a hard stop to the web-researching helper that the chat assistant can send off to look things up online. That helper now runs through at most 15 search-and-read passes before the system itself tells it to write its answer and finishes, instead of letting it keep looping (in one recent case five chats set off 1,519 research calls in an hour). This is internal reliability work, documented in the testing guide, so the chat assistant still works the same way for you, just with runaway researchers prevented from spinning out of control.

5083cff73efa88122e17fdab135b5ce4db0280e0.title: Chat-ready boot signal and multi-pattern wait in e2e utils

cb1dc4f15b6aec59f80dfac74c06d1427e76ec4e.title: CLI ships previous-launcher fatal crash telemetry on next launch
cb1dc4f15b6aec59f80dfac74c06d1427e76ec4e.summary: A new fatal-crash-report module writes a bounded crash report (error name, first 300 chars of message, first 20 stack frames, version/platform/uptime, and whether a Freebuff hour was held) synchronously to last-fatal-crash.json as the process exits, and the next launch reads and ships it as a cli.fatal_crash analytics event before the session begins. The report is dropped if older than 7 days or corrupt, recording and reading never throw, and a report is consumed exactly once. Concurrently, useGravityAd now returns a frozen NO_RESPONSE_ADS singleton via visibleResponseAds so hidden inline ads no longer re-trigger chat's layout effect each render, and SDK event handlers are wrapped in isolateUiHandler so a throwing UI update is logged and the agent run continues instead of becoming an unhandled fatal rejection. SIGPIPE is now explicitly ignored and excluded from CLI_RENDERER_EXIT_SIGNALS so a broken-pipe write no longer tears down the renderer and risks an exit-141 death, and external exits (terminal closed, killed, launcher gone) keep an active Freebuff hour for resume via the new keepSlotForResume path instead of ending it.

cb1dc4f15b6aec59f80dfac74c06d1427e76ec4e.text: When the assistant app crashes, it now saves a small note about the crash locally as it shuts down, and the next time you open the app it reads that note and sends a quiet crash report. A broken-pipe write (like output redirected to a closed command) no longer kills the app with a confusing exit-code-141, hidden inline ads no longer cause the chat to re-render in a loop, and if the app is closed by an outside signal while a free session is running, that free time is kept for the next launch instead of being ended early. 24636b016b85a8983dd35c208e1cd569e6eb2fca.summary: The agent runtime now names media and long base64 payloads instead of serializing their bytes into the compaction request, so a screenshot-heavy thread compacts in one pass instead of restarting across many large summarizer calls. The SDK's truncateRunStateAtUserTurn gains an optional totalUserTurns parameter that, when supplied, places the rewind boundary from the end of messageHistory rather than counting user turns from the start, which previously miscounted Stop notes and compaction summaries as user turns. Two other behavior surfaces in this commit are the parseCompactionSummary double-decoding fix and the mechanical fallback logging path.

24636b016b85a8983dd35c208e1cd569e6eb2fca.text: The AI assistant no longer wastes time re-summarizing entire chat histories when those histories contain large screenshots or image files. Previously, every screenshot a tool returned (like a picture of code or a webpage) was crammed into the text the assistant tried to summarize, turning one quick summary into dozens of slow rounds. Now those images are skipped and named instead, so a session full of screenshots compacts in a single step. This speeds up and stabilizes the assistant's memory-trimming for anyone editing earlier parts of a long conversation, since the part that picks where to rewind now counts from the end of the chat instead of getting confused by internal notes and saved summaries.

a23f0ae16d9c7d69458dce20ca74178bc530ffb8.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.203 adds binary elision and user-turn-bounded truncation to long conversations. The release introduces two main behaviors: when the assistant condenses a long chat into a shorter summary, large base64 blobs such as screenshots are now named and omitted instead of being copied into the summary request, which avoids very large summarization calls. The second change makes editing or undoing a message in a long thread keep the right number of past user turns by counting only the user prompts the runtime records, and by placing the cut relative to the end of the history when the host reports total user turns. As a result, stopping a run and then editing a message no longer throws away most of the conversation, and image heavy threads summarize without repeatedly streaming huge base64 payloads. These changes apply to users editing or undoing across compacted conversations and to Desktop sessions that carry screenshots in their history. The release evidence is incomplete regarding any other user facing behavior, so no further features or safety gains are described here.

a23f0ae16d9c7d69458dce20ca74178bc530ffb8.title: Freebuff CLI 0.0.203 ships binary-eliding compaction and end-counted
a23f0ae16d9c7d69458dce20ca74178bc530ffb8.summary: The version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json moves from 0.0.202 to 0.0.203. In packages/agent-runtime/src/model-compaction.ts, a new elideBinaryStrings replacer and omittedBinary helper name base64 data URLs and long unbroken base64 runs (data URL type omitted from this summary request) instead of writing their bytes into the model-compaction summarizer request, while media parts now emit [mediaType omitted from this summary request] rather than JSON.stringify; only strings at least 4096 characters long are considered for elision. In sdk/src/compact-run-state.ts, truncateRunStateAtUserTurn now treats only messages tagged USER_PROMPT as user turns (so Stop notes, instructions prompts, and compaction summaries are no longer counted) and accepts an optional totalUserTurns argument so the cut is placed totalUserTurns - keepUserTurns prompts back from the end instead of returning null on already-compacted threads. These changes exist because screenshot- and base64-heavy threads previously serialized millions of base64 tokens into dozens of sequential ~800k-token summarizer calls that stalled and restarted on Stop, and because counting every role:'user' message placed the rewind cut a whole turn too early on threads where forgetting costs the most.

dbc6a776fc0f8005806d797c00fe2c6caf1781c6.text: This is a small packaging update that bumps the Freebuff CLI version to 0.0.202 and improves how the tool handles a specific kind of error message. The main fix makes sure that when you see a message about running out of Codebuff credits (the paid credits, not the free ones), the tool correctly sends you to the usual out-of-credits flow instead of mistakenly telling you it's a problem on Freebuff's side. This only affects users who have run low on their paid Codebuff balance, and the release evidence is limited to this single behavior correction.

a23f0ae16d9c7d69458dce20ca74178bc530ffb8.text: Freebuff CLI version 0.0.203 improves how long conversations are summarized and edited. When a thread grows too long, the assistant compresses earlier parts into a shorter summary so it can keep working without losing track of the conversation. This release changes that compression so it skips over large blocks of binary data (like screenshots packed inside tool results) instead of copying them into the summary, which previously caused extremely slow summaries and left sessions stuck. It also fixes a bug where editing a message in an old conversation could make the assistant act as if the chat had just started, by keeping the conversation's start and end points aligned when cutting or rewinding history. Users with long, image-heavy, or frequently-edited conversations are the ones this release is meant to help.

f783139ae5607e7b53e6dd5608186d133930d7bd.text: This Freebuff CLI release adds a new kind of ad slot called a 'partner' placement to the Freebuff interfaces. Rather than appearing like Freebuff's own ad cards, a partner slot is branded chrome from a single advertiser, such as a row in the skill picker or a pill above the composer, and it is marked as not available for self-serve advertisers to target, keeping it exclusive to one deal. The two new partner slots are named Desktop-Partner-Skill-Picker and Desktop-Partner-Composer-PR, and they display with friendly surface-based labels like 'Desktop - Skill picker' and 'Desktop - Composer (PR intent)' in breakdown views. The partner placement is treated as explicitly separate from sponsor breaks, so adding this new format does not accidentally make it behave like an interrupting sponsor break with hero image and tight copy limits. Freebuff also ships session-resume behavior for older local CLI processes that predate the multi-session protocol: if an old launcher left a live hour behind, the new binary can probe that local instance, confirm this account holds it, and resume it without buying a second hour, while still falling back to a fresh claim when the prior process has ended. Only the partner placement changes are described in the release evidence, so that is the confirmed user-facing addition in this release.

06bf5c3390a40a61f96676cd94fdedbb04552956.text: When you run out of your own Codebuff credits (the paid version), the message you see no longer gets mistakenly treated as a problem on Freebuff's provider side. The change affects paying Codebuff users on the CLI, web, or desktop app who receive a 402 response pointing to their balance page. You now see the normal out-of-credits message directing you to add credits, instead of copy that suggests it's a Freebuff-side provider outage.

a78f5290258b53013a16fefea0715f6d74f445f0.text: When the Freebuff assistant restarts while a free coding session is still running in the background, it now checks whether that session belongs to your account and, if so, resumes it instead of asking you to start a new one or pick another model. This helps people using the free version of the assistant, specifically when an older version was replaced by a newer one during an automatic update. In everyday use, your active free session continues uninterrupted after a restart without needing a new session or model selection.

f783139ae5607e7b53e6dd5608186d133930d7bd.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.201 adds the ability to resume a paid AI model session that was left running by an older version of the app (0.0.196 and earlier), so upgrading no longer forces you to start a new session and lose the time you already paid for. The app now checks whether a previous, still-active session belongs to this account before offering to take it over, and if that older session is no longer running, it quietly starts a fresh one instead. The advertising system gains a new optional placement type called a partner slot, which is reserved for a single sponsor (like a branded row in the skill picker), and these slots are marked unavailable for self-service advertisers. A legacy single-session hour held by a dead process from an old binary can now be detected and resumed on the same expiry time without triggering a new paid claim, with a fallback to a fresh pick if the probe finds nothing alive.

Two new exclusive partner ad slots were explicitly registered into the system, each pinned to one advertiser only and kept out of the self-service picker, so only a pre-arranged deal can occupy them. This affects advertisers and sponsors who buy or manage ad placement campaigns in the placements rail, not Freebuff developers, CLI users, or subscribers. There is no visible effect or action for Freebuff users: this is a behind-the-scenes refactor of the internal placement catalog, so your coding sessions, steering variables, and CLI behavior are unchanged.

baffcb89339ea373a63aa77202bec34e76f80444.text: This Freebuff release tightens how sponsored (advertiser-funded) runs start, what commands they are allowed to run, and how the credentials they need are declared and protected, plus a couple of policy and model-access changes. - Sponsored run timing and framing: A sponsored compute grant's time window now begins when the in-place turn actually takes the grant, not when you accept the proposal, with the deadline taken as the lesser of the grant expiry and the grant-accept plus one-hour window. The in-place prompt now states the reviewed procedure is the only goal of the turn, marks the user's recent messages as read-only background for fitting the procedure to the project, and tells the run not to resume interrupted user requests. - Command refusals for sponsored runs: New, centralized rules refuse three classes of shell commands during a sponsored run: WSL launchers that reach your own Linux environment, destructive database commands such as drop/reset/wipe/force-seed, and container lifecycle commands that could affect your running services. Each refusal is answered as a plain sentence the model can act on before any shell is reached. - Per-run credentials: A reviewed procedure can now declare a single account credential it needs (for example, an API key), the user supplies it in a masked field, and the value is injected into the run's environment after the existing sponsored scrub, redacted from anything the model reads, and restricted to safe names that cannot overwrite PATH, HOME, or steering variables. - Model access: GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro are open to full-access accounts, dropping the US-or-paid exemption that previously gated them; they remain plan-only for limited-tier accounts. Everyday impact: If you accept a sponsored task, the run starts its clock when it actually begins and is told the procedure is its sole purpose and must not resume your interrupted requests. The same run cannot reach into WSL, drop or reset your databases, or start and stop your containers, and any credential the advertiser asks for is limited to safe names and never shown to the model. Full-access users can now pick GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro without buying a plan, while limited-tier users still see them locked to a plan.

baffcb89339ea373a63aa77202bec34e76f80444.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.200 ships a batch of safety and access changes for sponsored tasks and model availability. Sponsored runs now start their time window when the run actually begins instead of at Accept, and their in-place task prompt makes clear that the approved procedure is the only goal, so the model treats it as the task rather than a possible distraction. The two newest premium models, GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro, are now fully available to general full-access accounts (still plan-only for limited-tier accounts), and the picker locking logic was rerouted to rely on the server's per-view verdict instead of a hardcoded US-or-paid gate. Sponsored runs now refuse shell commands that could escape the project sandbox: WSL launchers, destructive database commands (drop, reset, wipe, force-seed, and risky scripts like db:reset), and container lifecycle commands (docker compose up, push, etc.), answering each with a plain sentence the model can act on. A reviewed procedure can now declare one or two named account credentials it needs, which are collected from the user in a masked field, injected only into that run's environment, and redacted from anything the model reads, with strict rules preventing anything like PATH or NODE_OPTIONS from being declared. The data-use notice was narrowed so restricted partners may now evaluate only connected Cloud repositories (no longer other code used with training-eligible models), and the test harness defaults the first-party CPM ad leg to off to match tests written before that feature was enabled. Clipboard handling now warns Linux users when a copy only reached the terminal via OSC 52 and no native clipboard tool exists, telling them how to fix it. Together, these changes mainly tighten what sponsored ad-funded runs can do to a repository and its environment, and they widen access to two premium models while keeping the existing limits for lower access tiers.

baffcb89339ea373a63aa77202bec34e76f80444.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.200 tightens how sponsored tasks run and what models are available. Sponsored tasks now start their clock when the task actually runs (not when you click Accept), the in-place task prompt is rewritten so the approved procedure is the only goal, and the CLI now refuses dangerous commands before they reach your shell: anything that enters Windows Subsystem for Linux, drops or resets a database, or builds, starts, stops, or pushes containers. Two premium models, GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro, are now open to more accounts but still reserved for limited-tier users only on a plan, and the READMEs now list both as full access. The data-use text in the README and the built-in data-use notice now say restricted partners may evaluate only connected Cloud repositories, and the policy metadata records September 25, 2026 as the date the evaluation scope was narrowed to those repositories. The test harness also defaults the first-party CPM ad billing leg to off for tests, matching its production-on setting. Together these changes mainly add safer boundaries for sponsored runs, clearer wording about what is evaluated, and a couple of formerly gated models becoming generally available.

7de825ebc35aa3637e3b6a6c6ffd99111adc6950.text: A sponsored task can now ask for a specific account credential the advertiser needs, and that credential is passed to the task inside a locked-down sandbox without letting it read the user's other secrets. This is for the Freebuff engineering team, who maintain the local-run boundary and how credentials are declared, injected, and redacted in the SDK and shared ads code. Nothing you would notice changes in your daily use today. Because the code that reads these credential declarations and hands them to the task is not present in this change, the feature is in place but not yet wired into a working flow.

The picker drops the US-or-paid exemption that gated `GPT-6 Luna` and `MiMo 2.6 Pro`, and the SDK test harness defaults `FREEBUFF_FIRST_PARTY_CPM_LEG` to `off`.

baffcb89339ea373a63aa77202bec34e76f80444.text: Release 0.0.200 ships the sponsored compute feature as credential-backed runs: when an advertised task needs your account for a service it uses, the CLI now asks you for that credential after you accept, holds it only for that one run, injects it only into that run's commands, and redacts every secret spelling from everything the AI sees. The sponsored run window now starts when the in-place turn begins rather than at Accept, so the clock you actually get is tied to the work, not the consent. Sponsored runs also now hard-stop three classes of commands that reach beyond your project: anything entering your Windows Subsystem for Linux, destructive database actions like drop/reset/wipe/force-seed, and container lifecycles that could touch your own running services. GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro moved from US-or-paid-only to full access for full-access accounts, while staying plan-locked for limited-tier accounts. The CLI's clipboard handling now warns Linux users when a copy only reached the terminal (OSC 52) rather than the system clipboard, and the data-use text in the READMEs was narrowed to say restricted partners may evaluate connected GitHub repositories only, not non-repository code. Everyday impact is for users who run Freebuff-sponsored tasks on desktop: they may now connect a single required account credential securely for those runs, those runs are blocked from touching their WSL home, production databases, or container services, the time window for the run begins when it actually starts working, and GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro are now in the full-access model picker for eligible accounts.

Full-access users in supported regions can now use GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro directly without a paid plan. baffcb89339ea373a63aa77202bec34e76f80444.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.200 ships two user-facing model changes and two safety upgrades for ad-sponsored coding tasks. GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro are now fully open to full-access accounts - they no longer require a paid US plan - while remaining plan-only for limited-tier accounts. Sponsored (ad-funded) coding runs now start their 60-minute compute window when the run actually begins rather than when you click Accept, so the timed allowance matches real work. The prompt framing for those runs was tightened so the approved procedure is stated as the only goal, which cuts down the agent weighing it as a distraction. Finally, a new command-refusal layer blocks WSL, destructive database commands, and container lifecycle commands inside a sponsored run, and a credential-handling system lets a reviewed procedure declare a single app key that the CLI collects (masked), injects only into that run's environment, and redacts from everything the model can read - with base64 and quoted-argument variants stripped too, not just the raw key.

22929c3492e000b3e7f0e7f91ddefebdd911e1c2.text: A new filter was added to sponsored runs that blocks three classes of shell commands before they run: anything that enters the Windows Subsystem for Linux (including its distribution launchers and share paths like \\wsl$ and \\wsl.localhost), destructive database operations (drops, resets, wipes, rollbacks, force-seeds across many tools and ORMs), and container lifecycle commands (build, start, stop, remove, push, unless read-only). This affects people running sponsored tasks locally on the Freebuff CLI, where the task executes against the user's own working copy.

baffcb89339ea373a63aa77202bec34e76f80444.text: Freebuff release 0.0.200 opens two AI models - GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro - to full access for users on the free tier, while adding new safety protections for advertising-sponsored coding tasks. Two models are now generally available and no longer gated by country or paid status for full-access users, though they remain locked for limited-tier accounts. Sponsored runs - coding tasks funded by advertisers - now let users securely connect third-party accounts (such as an API key) in a masked field, with the value injected only into the specific command that needs it and redacted everywhere else. The CLI also refuses entire categories of risky commands inside those sponsored tasks, including any attempt to enter Windows Subsystem for Linux, drop or reset databases, and build or start containers, returning a clear reason instead of running them. When copying text on Linux via terminal escape sequences (because native clipboard tools are missing), the CLI now appends a hint telling you to install wl-clipboard or xclip if the paste comes back empty. Ads billing for sponsored tasks now has a fixed cap of $1, and the CPM ad feature defaults to off in tests. This is primarily a packaging release that bumps the version to 0.0.200.

2417e0d7bac65d892540e314b04044b73f853200.title: Resume crashed CLI hour from live PID record
2417e0d7bac65d892540e314b04044b73f853200.summary: The CLI now writes a per-process live record (`freebuff-live-<pid>.json`) when it holds an active multi-session hour via `recordLiveFreebuffSession`, and forgets it on release or when a slot ends via `forgetLiveFreebuffSession`. On startup, `useFreebuffSession` falls back from the launcher update handoff to `consumeCrashedFreebuffSession`, which scans those records for one owned by a dead PID on the same account, resumes the newest unexpired hour by an atomic rename, and deletes expired records for gone owners. The record is single-use via the rename, so a resumed hour is not re-resumed by a concurrent launch, and an update handoff additionally calls `forgetCrashRecordsFor` to retire the dead parent record of the same instance.

An ad request's `traceContext` and `askAgenticOffer` both read that field directly, joining served ads to the prompt that came after the interrupted run rather than naming the interrupted run itself.

9f521ec5f2e38db447cafa0549633d728a284921.text: Freebuff 0.0.199 brings two user-visible additions. First, the model picker gained Solar Pro 4, an unmetered AI model from Upstage with a 524K context that works everywhere Freebuff runs; it joins Solar Mini 4 (also newly available to limited-access users) and shows up in both the CLI and Web/Cloud interfaces, at a cost of 10 Freebucks per unit. Second, sponsored ad offers now carry a trace session and run ID so a served ad can be linked back to the conversation that prompted it without sending conversation text. Crash recovery for free sessions was also improved: if a terminal closes or the process crashes while you hold an hour-long free session, a later launch on the same account can resume that unexpired hour instead of buying a second one. The ad-trace wiring and crash-resume behavior apply to free-tier Freebuff users and the sponsored-offer flow, while the model addition affects all users who can pick Solar Pro 4.

baffcb89339ea373a63aa77202bec34e76f80444.text: This release adds two new safety features for Freebuff's sponsored task runs. First, the CLI can now refuse to run certain dangerous shell commands during a sponsored task: entering Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL), running destructive database commands (like dropping or resetting a database), or building, starting, stopping, and pushing containers and images. These refusals happen before the command reaches a shell, and cover wrappers and scripts that could invoke those actions. Second, the system gains support for user-connected account credentials during a sponsored run: an advertiser-reviewed procedure can declare which credential it needs (like an API key set via `requires-credential:`), the Desktop client asks the user for it in a masked field, the value is held in memory for that one run, injected only as the declared environment variable into the run's terminal commands, and redacted from anything the model reads. The model is told the variable exists, never its value. A new test fixture sets the CPM advertising leg to off by default during testing, and the data-use notice in the public README and FAQ is narrowed so restricted partners may only evaluate connected Cloud repositories (not separately uploaded files or connected repositories broadly).

2417e0d7bac65d892540e314b04044b73f853200.text: When the Freebuff CLI crashes or the terminal closes unexpectedly, it now leaves a small file recording the paid session hour it was using, and the next time you start Freebuff it recovers that same unused hour instead of immediately buying a new one. If you end the session on purpose, or if the recorded hour has already expired, that file is deleted so nothing lingers for a later launch to resume. You keep the time you already paid for through a crash, and you will not be charged for a fresh hour unless you genuinely need one.

e028156be3855dcdfc37d7cfaf5bd8467a826c41.text: The AI coding assistant Freebuff changed how two popular models, GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro, can be used by developers. These models used to only be available in the United States or to people with a paid subscription, but now they are open to every developer using the full version of Freebuff at no extra cost, though they still draw from a shared pool of compute time. The change means that if you use Freebuff as a free-tier user outside the US, you will still need a paid plan to use these models, but if you are in a supported country or have a plan, you can now pick them without extra steps. The model picker in the CLI and desktop app now shows them as "Full access" for full-access users, and locked for limited users until they upgrade.

29214deac7fa874ca7abacea8095c1c429cce7d5.text: The assistant now keeps a separate, simple bookmark that points to the most recent completed task (including tasks that were interrupted but never finished), instead of always reading it from the current active task. When a task ends on its own without you confirming it, the bookmark jumps ahead past that task. This helps make sure the next ad or suggestion is connected to the right prompt that came after the interrupted task, rather than mistakenly attaching to the interrupted task itself. This is internal behavior that makes ad tracking and suggestions more accurate, and you will not notice it directly while using the assistant.

baffcb89339ea373a63aa77202bec34e76f80444.text: What shipped in Freebuff 0.0.200 is a set of safety rules and clearer clipboard behavior, with a small privacy wording tweak in the README. Sponsored (advertiser-funded) runs in the CLI now refuse a few dangerous commands outright: anything that enters the Windows Subsystem for Linux, database commands that drop/reset/wipe data (like prisma migrate reset, docker with certain flags, django flush, rails db:drop, redis-cli flushall, and similar), and container lifecycle commands (docker build/start/stop/remove/push, docker compose up, etc.). Users can now connect an account credential to a sponsored run via a reviewed procedure that declares what it needs (e.g. requires-credential: env=SIEVE_API_KEY), and the credential is held in memory for that one run only, injected only as the declared variable, and redacted from anything the model reads (it is masked as a redacted placeholder in tool output). The redaction also covers the value written in URL-encoded and base64/base64url forms, so keys embedded in Authorization headers or curl -v output are scrubbed too, including fragments left by truncation. For clipboard, the CLI no longer claims a copy succeeded when it only reached the terminal via OSC 52 on Linux; instead it tells you the copy is unverified and how to fix it (install wl-clipboard or xclip), and on platforms that block OSC 52 it shows Shift+drag guidance even when the caller suppresses routine messages. The README and a generated data-use block narrow the 'restricted partners may evaluate' sentence to connected Cloud repositories only (dropping the broader 'eligible codebases' phrasing), reflecting an update to the September 2 2026 privacy policy effective date of September 25 2026. What these mean day-to-day: if you run or author a sponsored task, those shell commands will be refused with a clear reason before they run and you can pass one secret per run that the model cannot exfiltrate; if you copy on a Linux terminal without a clipboard tool, you will be told your copy is unverified and how to install the fix; the rest updates wording about who can review your code and when your data may be used for AI training.

9f521ec5f2e38db447cafa0549633d728a284921.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.199 keeps your free usage hour if the app crashes. This release ships crash-resume records plus Solar Pro 4. Lead / Core Additions: The CLI now remembers the hour you prepaid when the previous Freebuff run was interrupted, so a crash no longer makes you lose time you already paid for. A new AI model, Solar Pro 4, joins the free model picker. Concrete Highlights: 1) Crash recovery: if the Freebuff CLI or terminal stops unexpectedly (such as a crash or a closed terminal), the next time you open Freebuff it can resume the same usage hour instead of starting a new one and wasting the remaining time. 2) Model update: Solar Pro 4 is now available in the regular picker for free users, listed alongside Solar Mini 4, and it is unmetered at full access so it does not count against your daily session limit. 3) Safer ad attribution: the assistant now passes only opaque pointer ids to ad requests tied to your conversation, not conversation text, so ads can be joined to the right run without leaking what you wrote. Free Freebuff users can no longer lose a paid hour because a crash left a dead process holding their slot, as long as they relaunch within the hour and the dead process is gone. Users in supported regions see Solar Pro 4 as a new unmetered option in the model picker, while users in limited regions gain Solar Pro 4 as an additional free model choice. The release evidence is incomplete on any broader stability or speed claims beyond the crash-resume behavior described.

d1ee8151d300fcd429df7b9d499ac123b50f7f85.text: The CLI now sends two anonymous tracking IDs along with each ad request, linking that request to the specific agent conversation that prompted it and the last finished step in that conversation, so the ad platform can follow along with what's happening in the chat. These IDs contain no actual conversation text, only opaque identifiers, and the system validates them before sending and ignores them if malformed. This affects developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK who encounter sponsored proposals during their coding sessions. In daily use, you won't see any visible change, since this is internal bookkeeping that improves how sponsored task offers are correlated with your active coding conversation.

The two Solar models share the same underlying lane and are both unmetered at full access, with Solar Pro 4 priced at 10 Freebucks when not in limited mode. Crash recovery for free sessions was rewritten: instead of buying a second paid hour when a terminal closes mid-session, the CLI now records the active session by process id and resumes that same hour only when the previous process is gone and the hour has not expired, with an atomic claim so two terminals cannot both resume it. Ad tracing was also tightened so that a run interrupted on purpose no longer leaves the conversation pointing at the wrong prompt when the next ad request is assembled, by advancing the trace pointer past any run that finished without being adopted. Available release evidence is incomplete for broader reliability claims; the catalog state at this version is limited to Solar Pro 4 joining the picker, Solar Mini 4 remaining in it, and the session relaunch and ad trace behavior above.

3082a3c005c13b211ad385cb606335d1d30d2e28.title: Freebuff CLI defers self-updates until session exit
3082a3c005c13b211ad385cb606335d1d30d2e28.summary: The Freebuff launcher wrapper now opts into deferred self-updates via the new `deferUpdatesUntilExit: true` config, so downloaded updates stage to a per-process temp dir and only install when the running session exits. checkForUpdates stores the staged binary on the running child in a WeakMap and installPendingUpdate commits it from attachExitHandler, never downgrading an install by a concurrent invocation or re-running an unfinished download. The wrapper still keeps the process and its binary/WASM untouched until exit, and a checksum failure still never interrupts the process.

ab6bf9cb6c21a1501dd4f76f4be2cfffcee2207b.text: When you are using the Freebuff assistant in a paid session, the prices shown for each AI model now come from the same discount store used by the desktop app, rather than the older single-session store. If there is no active session, or you are on a legacy trial, the prices continue to come from the old store as before. As a result, anyone running the latest paid sessions will see first-tab discounted prices (for example $0 per hour) honored in the CLI when the session is live, while sibling or expired sessions fall back to full metered prices, and trial users see no change.

5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.text: Freebuff 0.0.197 ships the first freebucks purchase flow tied to the CLI's own storefront, plus a read-only chat transcript viewer and a launcher that can defer updates until the Freebuff session is closed. The headline change is that the CLI now reads its Freebucks pricing and the user's balance directly off the live session response, so when you open the model picker, the cost shown matches what you'd be charged right now rather than a hardcoded number, and the picker can gate admission on your actual Freebucks balance so the BYOK fallback only appears when you genuinely cannot afford any model. The launcher no longer interrupts an in-progress Freebuff session to install an update: it downloads the new version in the background, keeps your hour running until you exit, and then installs the update when the CLI closes, falling back to the user cache directory with a sha256-keyed path if the usual write location is locked down. Finally, a new History shortcut (press H) opens your chat history on both the landing and superseded screens, and a read-only chat surface lets you scroll through a saved transcript (with M to choose a model) without the composer, feedback prompts, or run hooks active, so you cannot accidentally submit work while browsing. These changes apply to Freebuff CLI users: anyone who opens the CLI now gets an admission-gated model picker backed by their real Freebucks balance, and anyone whose session is full or has ended can browse transcripts read-only. The evidence does not establish changes to model availability, benchmark scores, or billing rates beyond the purchase-bound pricing already noted, so those claims are left out.

3082a3c005c13b211ad385cb606335d1d30d2e28.text: The Freebuff launcher now waits until you close the app before installing a downloaded update, instead of interrupting your work to swap in a new version mid-session. This change affects people using the Freebuff app on desktop, in the terminal, on the web, or through the SDK. You will not notice updates happening while you are working and they now appear silently between sessions rather than pausing what you are doing.

5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.title: Freebuff CLI 0.0.197 release
5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.0.197 publishes alongside deferred launcher self-updates (`deferUpdatesUntilExit: true` in cli/release-core/launcher.js keeps the CLI alive after a staged download and installs it on exit), a read-only chat surface for browsing saved transcripts (new `ReadOnlyChat` and `HistoryShortcut` components wired into app routing), and CLI multi-session identity for purchase continuity (new `freebuff-session-identity.ts` and takeover-prompt handling). The release bump itself touches only freebuff/cli/release/package.json, while these behaviors were authored in the commits surrounding the release window.
5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.evidence: The release commit 5f5be812 modifies only freebuff/cli/release/package.json, bumping the version from 0.0.196 to 0.0.197; surrounding release-window source evidence (ab6bf9cb freebucks routing, 3082a3c0 deferred launcher updates, 8fdaf592 history/readonly chat, 93f5e6d9 session identity and takeover prompts) documents the behaviors shipped under that version.
5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.unknowns: The exact rollout timing of the multi-session identity and takeover-prompt flows across Freebuff desktop and web surfaces is not visible in this commit. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.text: This release of the Freebuff CLI makes three main improvements: it lets users safely browse past conversations and read saved transcripts in a read-only view (without a text box or model admission), and it updates the CLI launcher so that software updates download quietly in the background and install when the program exits rather than interrupting an in-progress coding session. First, a new history shortcut labeled 'H · History' is now shown on the landing and superseded screens, pressing 'h' opens the chat history, and selecting a past conversation opens a read-only chat screen where the message footer hides the feedback prompt and the composer is removed. Second, the CLI launcher now supports deferred updates: when a new version is downloaded during a session, the running program is not interrupted or replaced until the user exits, at which point the new version installs for the next launch, with safeguards so a second launcher cannot overwrite a staged binary and so the original exit code is preserved. These changes affect Freebuff CLI users: anyone can now browse conversation history with 'h' from the main screens and read old transcripts safely, and everyone benefits from non-disruptive background updates that no longer kill a coding session mid-turn when a newer CLI version is released.
