acceptedPr.title: fix(core): preserve session state on abort and error / session expiration (replaces #1055)
acceptedPr.author: Utkarsh-X
acceptedPr.body:
Fixes #1054
Reopens #1055 (rebased onto the new main history following @victorxheng's note).

### What this fixes
When a user interrupts a run with <kbd>Esc</kbd> or when a session expires, sending a follow-up message immediately was reading a stale/null in-memory `previousRunStateRef`. This caused the SDK to construct a fresh empty session state (`messageHistory = []`), wiping conversation context.

### What's included (addressing the #1055 review feedback)
1. **Regression tests (`send-message.test.ts`)**: Added 3 dedicated tests verifying:
   - User abort (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) preserves turn history + tool calls in `createRunConfig.previousRun`.
   - Session expiration / gate errors preserve history on `"continue"`.
   - Mid-run chat switches (`runChatIsCurrent === false`) never leak state into other chats.
2. **DRY state sync (`use-send-message.ts`)**: Consolidated the assignment into a simple 5-line `syncRunState` closure used uniformly across abort, completion, and error handlers.
3. **Clean scope**: Reverted the previous prompt text tweaks so this PR is strictly isolated to the session state bug (3 files total).
4. **Re-render safety**: Checked store subscriptions — zero React components subscribe to `state.runState`, so updating it alongside `streamStatus = 'idle'` causes no visual layout flash.

I intentionally kept this as minimal and safe as possible to solve the demonstrated bug without bloating the change surface or touching unrelated client/storage APIs. That said, if you'd prefer any tweaks or want me to look into anything further here, just let me know and I'm happy to research and adjust!

### Verification
- **Test Suites (202 / 202 passed across touched areas)**:
  - `bun test cli/src/hooks/helpers/__tests__/send-message.test.ts` (49 passed, including the 3 new regression tests)
  - `bun test sdk/src/__tests__/run-cancellation.test.ts` (16 passed)
  - `bun test cli/src/utils/__tests__/run-state-storage.test.ts` (37 passed)
  - `bun test packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/compact-history.test.ts` (31 passed)
  - `bun test agents/__tests__/context-pruner.test.ts` (69 passed)
- **Builds**:
  - `bun run build:sdk` (ESM, CJS, and TypeScript declarations bundled with 0 errors)
  - `bun run build:freebuff` (Native executable built with exit code 0)

93f5e6d99c94f55caa8bc4c067196475a1f732d5.title: Freebuff CLI adds multi-session claim identity and launcher relaunch
93f5e6d99c94f55caa8bc4c067196475a1f732d5.summary: The CLI now issues a private per-process claim id (prefixed 'cli:') via newFreebuffCliInstanceId and tags GETs with the heartbeat and multi-session headers so a CLI polls only its own seat, while limited-offer models keep the legacy single-session path. callFreebuffSession gains multiSession/takeoverInstanceId opts and routes DELETE attempts through /attempt when an attempt id is present. The session store gains pendingAdmission plus launcher-scoped saveFreebuffSessionForRelaunch/consumeFreebuffSessionRelaunch so an update restart reclaims its exact purchased slot, and restart releases the exact prior attempt before rotating identity.
93f5e6d99c94f55caa8bc4c067196475a1f732d5.evidence: Two new modules were added: cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-identity.ts (exporting newFreebuffCliInstanceId, freebuffCliAttemptId, freebuffSessionMetadata, and CLI_MULTI_SESSION_PREFIX = 'cli:') and cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-relaunch.ts (exporting saveFreebuffSessionForRelaunch and consumeFreebuffSessionRelaunch). The session lifecycle hook use-freebuff-session.ts imports these and now passes multiSession, takeoverInstanceId, instanceId, claimId, attemptedModel, and claimRetired through callFreebuffSession and restart, while freebuff-session-store.ts added pendingAdmission state and rewired releaseSlot/keepSlotForRelaunch around the launcher-scoped handoff.
93f5e6d99c94f55caa8bc4c067196475a1f732d5.unknowns: The server-side handling of the new multi-session, purchase-continuity, and attempt headers is not present in this diff. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: New module defining the CLI multi-session instance id prefix and helpers to mint, detect, and metadata-tag a per-process claim id.
New module persisting and consuming a launcher-scoped session handoff keyed to CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_PID so an update restart resumes its own purchase.
Imports the identity and relaunch helpers, tracks claimId/attemptedModel/claimRetired, and threads multiSession and takeoverInstanceId through callFreebuffSession and restart.
Adds pendingAdmission state and rewrites keepSlotForRelaunch/releaseSlot to consult the identity helpers and honor the launcher-scoped handoff.
Adds multiSession/takeoverInstanceId opts to callFreebuffSession and emits the multi-session, purchase-continuity, heartbeat, and attempt headers.
Imports freebuffSessionMetadata and spreads it into extraCodebuffMetadata instead of the raw instance id.

93f5e6d99c94f55caa8bc4c067196475a1f732d5.text: When Freebuff updates itself while you're working, it now remembers the paid session you were using so the new version resumes right where you left off, instead of dropping you back to the model picker with the full price showing and losing your progress. If you're using a free limited-time model trial, the existing single-instance behavior stays the same, while regular free-session users get a private multi-session claim that ensures your CLI only polls and controls its own session seat. You should notice that restarting or updating the CLI after a crash or interrupted run no longer wipes your in-progress conversation context, and if another instance takes over your session, you'll see a clearer 'session already in use' message with a 'Choose model' option instead of a hard exit.

aeff04d65f0eddb4376babe7867103beb26d71d1.title: Sponsored task dock holds the ad slot while a proposal runs
aeff04d65f0eddb4376babe7867103beb26d71d1.summary: A sponsored proposal accepted in the chat now renders in the dock above the composer instead of the transcript, replacing the display ad for as long as it holds the slot, and the ad rail pauses while it does so. The SponsoredProposalBlock gains a `run` prop carrying phase, changedFiles and undone so the card can show delivered changes and an Undo action inline. The chat runtime now starts the proposal turn when its run is queued, and keyboard Ctrl+O (PROPOSAL_DOCK_CHORD) and the new onToggleSponsoredDock handler open the card when it is docked. Consent opens the review and never accepts, and a refusal or a throw hands the card back rather than leaving it busy.
aeff04d65f0eddb4376babe7867103beb26d71d1.evidence: cli/src/chat.tsx (dockProposal memo, <SponsoredProposalBlock> rendering replacing <SingleAdBanner>, onToggleSponsoredDock handler, sponsoredDockActive in ChatKeyboardState) and cli/src/components/blocks/sponsored-proposal-block.tsx (accepts a `run` prop of type SponsoredDockRun, renders delivered/undone states and an Undo button).
aeff04d65f0eddb4376babe7867103beb26d71d1.unknowns: The server-side agentic offer flow that decides whether to surface a proposal is not visible in this diff, nor is the rollout of the in-place execution path to advertisers.

changes.what: The sponsored proposal now renders in the dock above the composer in place of the inline display ad while it holds the slot, with the ad rail paused via slotPaused: dockProposal !== null and a new Ctrl+O chord and onToggleSponsoredDock keyboard handler.
A new sponsored-run-store tracks the active run snapshot and exposes sponsoredTurnHoldsQueue so the chat runtime holds the user queue and starts the turn when a proposal's run is queued.

The proposal card gains a run prop, delivered/undone inline rendering, an Undo button, a v-toggles-procedure control, and consent that opens the review without accepting; /ads:undo now routes through the same callback as the dock Undo.

Sponsored runs no longer use a separate git worktree; in-place execution edits the working copy directly, tracked by a new sponsored-receipts ledger, with undo restoring files from recorded before/after snapshots.
Credential detection in capabilities and sandbox profiles now includes .envrc, and a new sponsored-secret-scan surfaces credential files to redact on macOS for sponsored runs.
In-place sponsored execution gained version 1 and a helper to flag workspace-targeted rows, and the conformance waivers for CLI now describe in-place delivery rather than a separate thread.

3dd05d3b673ee4d6db441f3ff75480154b3d4a1f.text: This Freebuff CLI release, version 0.0.198, ships a new way for the in-terminal AI helper to be sponsored by advertisers without needing a separate isolated checkout. Instead of creating a temporary git worktree to run an advertiser-funded task, an accepted sponsored task now runs directly inside the folder you already have open, so its changes appear right in your project. A consent screen tells you which advertiser is proposing the edits and explains that the changes happen in place and can be undone, and after the run finishes you are told what files were changed plus a command to revert them. The proposal card that shows up in-line now lives only in the dock above the composer (it no longer renders twice in the chat transcript), and a Ctrl+O shortcut opens the sponsor dock while a sponsored task is active. When the terminal is closed mid-task, the CLI now attempts to report the run's terminal state so the sponsor knows it stopped, and keeps the working copy edits visible so you know what to expect. An ad-hoc campaign toggle and a fresh test environment variable were added for the local agentic-ads harness, and the CLI now sends the same device identity information (OS, timezone, locale) and user-agent string to the ad routes whether the task comes from a display ad or a per-turn offer, so targeting and pairing stay consistent between the two flows.

aeff04d65f0eddb4376babe7867103beb26d71d1.text: Sponsored task cards now dock above the chat input: when an advertiser-sponsored coding task is accepted or running, its card replaces the rotating ad banner in that one slot until the task finishes, then the ad returns. The card gains a real Open setup button and an Undo control, plus a Ctrl+O shortcut to open its details, and it now shows live task progress, delivered files, and an inline undo so users can review and revert changes directly from the dock.

3dd05d3b673ee4d6db441f3ff75480154b3d4a1f.title: Freebuff CLI 0.0.198 release
3dd05d3b673ee4d6db441f3ff75480154b3d4a1f.summary: The Freebuff CLI package manifest in freebuff/cli/release/package.json bumps the version to 0.0.198 from 0.0.197. This is a release-bump packaging commit with no behavioral source changes in its own diff.
3dd05d3b673ee4d6db441f3ff75480154b3d4a1f.evidence: freebuff/cli/release/package.json: version field changed from "0.0.197" to "0.0.198"; analysis notes confirm Freebuff CLI release 0.0.198 published (release-bump commit nature).
3dd05d3b673ee4d6db441f3ff75480154b3d4a1f.unknowns: The specific source changes shipped in this release window are documented in earlier same-day commits, not in this packaging bump commit's diff.

3dd05d3b673ee4d6db441f3ff75480154b3d4a1f.text: Version 0.0.198 of the Freebuff CLI ships the in-place sponsored-task flow for Freebuff users: an advertised coding task now runs directly inside your current project folder, streamed into your conversation through a dedicated system row, instead of being isolated in a separate temporary checkout. Accepting an offered task opens a consent screen that shows the advertiser's exact reviewed procedure (no branch is created and nothing is pushed) and, once approved, the work proceeds with a clear notice that `/ads:undo` can put your files back; your own queued messages wait until the sponsored turn finishes. The CLI now asks the agentic offer route per turn on its own request so an eligible task can appear on the turn that earned it rather than after a delay. Two safety improvements back this flow: a one-sentence in-place consent warning makes clear that files will be edited in place, and the CLI reports its own device facts (OS, timezone, locale) and product identity to the ad routes so an offered capability is matched to what this machine can actually contain. Users on Windows are not served this flow (native Windows containment is unsupported), and Codebuff users keep the prior behavior of only writing a project marker when no GitHub remote can key the project.

8fdaf5925043bd28c7bae1bb29beaf1fb5b8d7f2.title: Add read-only chat history browsing and superseded session screen
8fdaf5925043bd28c7bae1bb29beaf1fb5b8d7f2.summary: A new `ReadOnlyChat` component renders a saved transcript with no composer, run callbacks or admission, reached via an `H` keyboard shortcut added in `HistoryShortcut`; `AuthedSurfaceRoutes` now returns `<ReadOnlyChat>` for admitted-but-not-active Freebuff sessions and `<FreebuffSupersededScreen>` on a 409 superseded response, so browsing history never tears down a running session and a rotated instance id gets a dedicated terminal screen instead of falling back to the pre-chat landing. The `MessageBlockContext` gains a `readOnly` flag set true by `ReadOnlyChat`, which `MessageFooter` consults to suppress its feedback button while reading. Plus four other small wiring changes across the landing screen, superseded screen, and store.

45b6c98d656423c8d284fa69499eb6258f4186cb.title: Ripgrep extraction writes atomically and caches by content hash
45b6c98d656423c8d284fa69499eb6258f4186cb.summary: A new `extractRipgrep` export in `cli/src/native/ripgrep-extraction.ts` writes the embedded ripgrep binary to a `.rg-` temp dir then renames it into place, so only complete executables are published, including across concurrent launches. `cli/src/native/ripgrep.ts` now calls `extractRipgrep` instead of `Bun.write` plus a `spawnSync` chmod, and falls back to a cache keyed by the SHA of the bytes only when the install dir yields EACCES, EPERM, or EROFS. Other failures like disk full are rethrown unchanged.
45b6c98d656423c8d284fa69499eb6258f4186cb.evidence: New file `cli/src/native/ripgrep-extraction.ts` exports `extractRipgrep`, which writes to a `.rg-` temp dir then renames, and falls back to a SHA content-addressed cache dir only for EACCES/EPERM/EROFS. Modified file `cli/src/native/ripgrep.ts` replaces `Bun.write` plus `spawnSync(['chmod', '+x', outPath])` with a call to `extractRipgrep`. New tests in `cli/src/native/ripgrep-extraction.test.ts` assert 'prefers the installation directory without creating a cache', 'propagates a failed cache write without leaving a partial binary', and '${code}: falls back only for access failures'.

8fdaf5925043bd28c7bae1bb29beaf1fb5b8d7f2.text: You can now browse past conversations in read-only mode without kicking anyone off a running chat. Pressing H opens your chat history at any time, and when you return to the main chat the previous session keeps running. The chat list also handles being claimed by another instance correctly, showing a clear message instead of pretending to start up normally. Message footers in saved chats hide the feedback and submit buttons so browsing never triggers new work.

5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.197 introduces deferred self-updates that wait until you exit the app before installing, so updates no longer interrupt active coding sessions. Pricing for Freebucks (the pay-as-you-go compute credits) is now fetched dynamically from the server rather than being hardcoded, meaning price changes reach your installed CLI automatically on its next poll. A new read-only history view lets you browse past conversations with keyboard navigation (H for history, arrow keys, page up/down) without needing an active AI session, and this view remains accessible even when free sessions are full or unavailable. The update system now properly handles scenarios where sessions stay open between turns, keeping processes alive until you explicitly exit rather than forcing restarts. Additionally, the launcher now uses PID-scoped temporary directories during downloads to prevent conflicts between concurrent update attempts.

45b6c98d656423c8d284fa69499eb6258f4186cb.text: The Freebuff app now saves its built-in search tool to your computer in a safer way: it writes the file completely to a temporary spot first, then moves it into place, so a crash or a second program starting at the same time can never leave you with a half-written, unusable tool. If the main folder cannot be written to, it instead saves a copy in a personal cache and remembers it by the file's contents, so upgrades always get the newest version instead of reusing an old one. This is internal maintenance that reduces startup failures of the search feature, and you will not need to do anything differently.

5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.title: Freebuff CLI 0.0.197 release with deferred updates and pricing fix
5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.summary: The release bumps freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.0.196 to 0.0.197 and ships a deferred self-update path in cli/release-core/launcher.js via `deferUpdatesUntilExit: true`, which stages downloaded updates to a per-process temp dir and only installs them when the running session exits. It also routes Freebucks price lookups in cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts to the Desktop purchase store for ordinary CLI claims (identified by `freebuffCliAttemptId`) while legacy trial sessions keep the single-session store. A new `installPendingUpdate` call in the launcher's exit handler installs the staged binary on session exit when the installed version is still older than the staged one.
5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.evidence: Version bump in freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.0.196 to 0.0.197, alongside source members ab6bf9cb6 (freebucks CLI pricing routing), 3082a3c00 (launcher deferred self-update), 8fdaf5925, 93f5e6d99, 93f5e6d99, and partial member diffs.
5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.unknowns: The commit message states 5 other changes were left out because a check discredited their summaries, so the full release-window behavior is not fully visible.

5f5be8125dc4c7507742022f3c12b60db0471670.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.197 adds support for deferred software updates that install only after you close your session, plus changes to how the CLI is identified as a multi-session purchase so your paid hour survives an update restart. When a new version is available, the launcher now downloads it in the background and waits until you exit before installing it, so updates no longer interrupt a running coding session on Windows or macOS. The paid-session accounting was also fixed so the CLI reports itself with a multi-session identity, which keeps your active paid Freebuff hour and shows your own model choice instead of a stale price on the next launch. In the landing screen, a new history shortcut button and a read-only chat view were added so you can browse past chats before starting a new session. The takeover and superseded screens were updated to offer a clearer choice to go back and select another model instead of being forced to exit.

3d5300b6644c823970cb9588f6fde93ff3e39f2b.title: CLI keeps Freebuff session slot on launcher update restart
3d5300b6644c823970cb9588f6fde93ff3e39f2b.summary: The Freebuff CLI now recognises a SIGTERM that is the npm launcher replacing the binary with a staged update via a new isLauncherUpdateTermination helper in cli/src/utils/launcher-update-restart.ts, which checks that the launcher pid is an integer greater than zero, that the process parent pid equals the launcher pid, and that the launcher process is still running. When that condition holds in the SIGTERM handler in cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts, the CLI calls keepSlotForRelaunch from the session store in cli/src/state/freebuff-session-store.ts so releaseSlot becomes a no-op on every exit path, preserving the held Freebuff session for the relaunched binary. The change targets the median ~16s window after a Freebuff user picks a model and pays for its hour.
3d5300b6644c823970cb9588f6fde93ff3e39f2b.evidence: Commit 3d5300b6 adds new file cli/src/utils/launcher-update-restart.ts exporting isLauncherUpdateTermination, and modifies cli/src/state/freebuff-session-store.ts to add keepSlotForRelaunch/slotKeptForRelaunch and a no-op early return in releaseSlot, plus cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts to call keepSlotForRelaunch on a launcher update SIGTERM.
3d5300b6644c823970cb9588f6fde93ff3e39f2b.unknowns: The rollout of the launcher update mechanism that triggers isLauncherUpdateTermination is not visible in this commit.

6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.196 keeps your already-paid session running when the launcher updates the app underneath you. Previously, a launcher-driven update would end your session and drop you back on the model picker with the full price showing, even though the hour you paid for was still reusable server-side. Now the running binary recognizes it is being replaced by an update (a SIGTERM whose parent is the live launcher), and instead of releasing your slot it keeps it, so the relaunched binary takes it over silently and you never see the picker. This covers both the clean exit path and the renderer teardown cleanup, and later release attempts become no-ops once the slot is kept. The release also swaps the chat thinker child agent to GPT-6 Luna (with GPT-5.6 Luna retired and coerced to a fallback for installed clients) and updates the model catalog wording around Gemini 3.8 Flash pricing.

3d5300b6644c823970cb9588f6fde93ff3e39f2b.text: When the Freebuff assistant updates itself in the background, it is restarting the program that is currently running your coding session. This change teaches that background update process to hold onto your paid session slot instead of ending it, so the freshly restarted program finds your work still waiting for it. If you are using Freebuff in the terminal and an update happens while you are mid-session, you will no longer be bumped back to the model picker after the restart. This only applies to Freebuff CLI users; it has no effect on paid Codebuff sessions or the web and desktop apps.

29e85c6f3045cc88e2a00a1a446ea8d0897eb47e.text: Freebuff added two new pieces of shared text that describe when the DeepSeek model refuses a request because its safety filter thinks the content is risky, and what you should do about it (switch to a different model). Nothing actually shows this text yet, so you won't notice any difference right now, it is just stored in the system for future use.

6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.title: Freebuff CLI 0.0.196 with in-place sponsored runs and session
6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.0.196 bundles several functional changes: the CLI now keeps a Freebuff session slot when the npm launcher restarts for an update, so a relaunched binary resumes the hour the user just bought instead of dropping them on the model picker (cli/src/state/freebuff-session-store.ts, cli/src/utils/launcher-update-restart.ts, cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts). It also ships the in-place sponsored execution contract (`SPONSORED_IN_PLACE_VERSION = 1` in common/src/ads/sponsored-in-place.ts), the agentic offer route wire contract with its geo-tier docstring fix, the DeepSeek content filter error pattern and message, dropped free-mode slowed-session SSE notice handling, and supporting sandbox read/write path rules for in-place runs.

Release evidence includes source hunks for members: 3d5300b6 (CLI update: freebuff-session-store, keeps session slot on launcher update restart), 29e85c6f (Shared/Core update: freebuff-errors, adds DeepSeek content filter error pattern and message), d5eaa528 (Docs update: testing), b729016f (CLI update: .gitignore), d1ee8151 (Sponsored in-place execution version 1 lands, adds SPONSORED_IN_PLACE_VERSION = 1 constant and in-place execution support), 43740b75 (Agentic offer geo tier reason docstring updated for Tier 2 coverage), 4dd7beb1 (Drop free mode session slowed notice and SDK listener).

6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.text: This release lets sponsored AI tasks edit your files directly in the place where you're working instead of always spinning up a separate branch and pull request. A new in-place execution contract (version 1) lets the client declare it can run a sponsored task right in your current conversation, and two new read/write policies keep secret-bearing files like.env and id_rsa safe during that in-place run. Behind the scenes, one dedicated endpoint now answers whether an agentic offer is available per user turn, rather than deciding it inside the main ad display request, and updated Desktop clients drive both the old and new paths through a single switch. The chat thinker child agent for freebuff.com/chat is now wired to GPT-6 Luna, while GPT-5.6 Luna is withdrawn and recognized-only so existing clients fall back gracefully instead of being refused. A paid session you just bought no longer gets dropped on the model picker when the launcher relaunches the binary after an update: the CLI now recognizes the launcher's update restart signal and preserves your session for the relaunch. The old 'session slowed' notice path and its SDK listener were removed, and a few supporting files, fixtures, and gitignore entries were added or updated to match.

43740b75c7546ca72d3a9d0fa2b91df7a65a739f.text: A code note describing when the assistant declines to offer a paid AI session was rewritten to clarify that it now only applies when the user's country cannot be matched to a supported price tier, since the lower tier is now served at $1. The change only updates the explanatory text, leaving the underlying list of reasons unchanged. It affects the Freebuff engineering team's internal documentation and dashboards, not the way the assistant behaves for you. You will not notice anything different in your coding sessions.

4dd7beb1aa58644b4655c0165f8a8225bdd3dfb7.text: Free-mode sessions that were once deliberately slowed down to spread out usage no longer notify the SDK or the apps built on it. The developers removed the plumbing that used to send a 'free-mode session slowed' message when a free-tier turn was being paced, including the listener the SDK used to listen for that notice and the per-model pacing targets it pointed at. For you as someone using the free tier, this means the assistant will no longer explicitly signal that a free session is being rate-limited for pacing; the pacing path it relied on is gone. There is no replacement notice described here, so the exact way a slowed free turn is shown in the apps now is not spelled out by this change.

6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.text: This release adds support for running sponsored coding tasks directly in your own files instead of a throwaway copy, plus a new AI model (GPT-6 Luna) replacing an older one. Sponsored setup runs can now edit your working folder in place (no branch or pull request), with new refusal rules that block reads/writes of secret and environment files and refuse history-changing git commands. The chat thinker agent now uses GPT-6 Luna while GPT-5.6 Luna is withdrawn but still recognized by installed clients. A new dedicated endpoint moves agentic card decisions out of the main ad request, with a single kill switch controlling whether such offers appear. When the launcher replaces the running Freebuff binary with an update, the paid session hour is now kept and resumed by the relaunched binary rather than dropped back to the model picker.

The version bump is the only packaging change in this commit; the rest is the accumulated source for the 0.0.196 window.

6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.196 ships with a new way for sponsored tasks to make edits directly in the user's own working files instead of creating a separate branch. A new on-request endpoint asks the agentic ad pool its own question once per turn, so agentic cards are discovered before the rest of the ad display chain runs. The chat thinker child now writes in the GPT-6 Luna model (its GPT-5.6 Luna predecessor is withdrawn but still recognized so older clients fall back instead of being refused). For sponsored in-place runs, the model is blocked from touching git history, configuration or credential files, and reads of the user's real repository are also refused while writes are limited to the working copy. The launcher can now recognize its own update restart and hold a paid session slot for the relaunched binary so the user does not lose the hour they just paid for. When DeepSeek's provider content filter rejects a request, the client tells you to switch models rather than silently retrying on the same one. A failed test expectation that pretty-prints a mounted React node can blow up test time, so new matchers avoid passing DOM nodes to matchers inside retrying checks.

b729016fa17b4c24fcf4e4ffcfa8c66bf0ff19d5.title: Add in-place sponsored run contract and read policy
b729016fa17b4c24fcf4e4ffcfa8c66bf0ff19d5.summary: A new in-place execution contract lets a sponsored run deliver changes into the user's working copy rather than a worktree. The offer and accept requests now carry an in-place version marker, the read path gains a dedicated `evaluateSponsoredReadPath` check, and git write subcommands are refused in-place via a shared refusals list.

Adds inPlaceExecutionVersion to the offer request schema and permits empty repoFullName with optional workspaceId

b729016fa17b4c24fcf4e4ffcfa8c66bf0ff19d5.text: A new in-place sponsored run lets advertisers' automated code changes go directly into your open files instead of a separate testing copy, with new read and write safety rules. The CLI now needs to declare support for this in-place style when it offers and accepts a sponsored task, and it refuses to run git commands that change history (like commits or branches) during such a run. Developers using the CLI, web app, desktop app, or SDK who take a sponsored task see changes land in their current working copy, with the changes kept to the open editor files and sensitive config files protected. Nothing changes for developers who do not opt into an in-place sponsored task.

6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.text: Freebuff 0.0.196 swaps the default thinking AI model from GPT-5.6 Luna to GPT-6 Luna (with 5.6 moved to a paused list so old pickups redirect to a fallback) and adds a new dedicated endpoint for per-turn sponsored task offers, so agentic ads are decided on their own request instead of inside the normal ad display call. Other changes tighten session handling during automatic CLI updates (so a running paid hour can be handed off to the relaunched binary instead of dropping you on the model picker), refuse to read or write secret-bearing files during in-place sponsored runs (`.env`, `id_rsa`, `.npmrc`, and git history commands like commit/push/checkout are blocked), and improve test timing notes so flaky long-running tests are easier to spot. The GPT-6 Luna swap and the new agentic offer routing are the main user-visible changes; session handoff during updates, the in-place read/write protections, and the test-doc notes are supporting reliability and safety details. Available release evidence is incomplete for broader packaging claims, so this summary covers only what the listed commits establish.

6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.text: This Freebuff CLI 0.0.196 release ships four main improvements. First, the chat thinker helper now uses the newer GPT-6 Luna model instead of GPT-5.6 Luna, and the old 5.6 model has been retired so released clients that still ask for it get gently redirected to a fallback rather than refused. Second, the session store and launcher restart logic were updated so that when the CLI is upgraded in the background and a SIGTERM arrives while the process's parent is still the live launcher, the running session is kept for the relaunched binary instead of being ended on exit, which lets you keep your paid hour and avoid being dropped back at the model picker. Third, a new agentic offer route wire contract and an agentic pool wire contract were added for Desktop ad delivery, moving agentic card decisions out of the display request into a dedicated per-user-turn endpoint gated by a single FREEBUFF_AGENTIC_ADS switch, with a closed set of reasons for when nothing is offered and deliberately non-strict response objects so the server can add fields without a version bump. Fourth, the in-place sponsored execution path was defined, letting an accepting client run an accepted sponsored offer as a turn in the accepting conversation, editing the user's working copy with no worktree or commit, with new read/write path policies that refuse credential files and git history-changing subcommands, a new 'delivered' terminal proposal state and actions to review and undo the changes, and a test cleanup note documenting why a failed DOM-node matcher can be slow.

390017bdbd85338995a252697238066940519f2a.text: A faster, experimental way to run code tasks has been added behind the scenes: the assistant can now split a coding job into several parallel sub-tasks that work at the same time, then stitch the results together itself. This fast mode is wired up to the catalog and the desktop client scheduling tables, but it is turned off in the user interface for now, so you will not see it in any model picker. 3afeef582d36c7d102fa9a948438e9b9ec72b4a5.title: Add ad adoption watcher tracking package installs after ad clicks
3afeef582d36c7d102fa9a948438e9b9ec72b4a5.summary: A new ad adoption watcher in cli/src/ads/ad-adoption.ts watches ad clicks and inspects subsequent agent commands to detect when a user installs a vendor package from an ad, emitting a postClick.packageInstalled engagement record. The watcher is bounded by ADOPTION_MAX_WATCHES and AD_MS_CAP, parsing only the first COMMAND_SCAN_CHARS of a command for up to MAX_PACKAGES_PER_COMMAND package names matched against the four package managers via parseInstalledPackages and vendorsInstalledBy. This snapshot also extends the ad client context with new system, app, locale, work and typing fact sources, adds engagement fields for idle time, reentries, keystrokes and turn failures, and wires terminal keystrokes and tool-call errors into the engagement and adoption pipelines.

3afeef582d36c7d102fa9a948438e9b9ec72b4a5.text: When you click on a Freebuff ad for a developer tool (like Supabase, Stripe, or Vercel), the CLI now quietly watches what you type next. If you install that vendor's package (for example `npm install supabase`), it sends a simple signal saying an install happened. Freebuff tracks whether the assistant installed a package after clicking an ad, but only the first install is reported and no actual commands, package names, or terminal output are sent away. This is for Freebuff users who click ads while coding in the terminal, helping Freebuff understand if ads lead to actual tool adoption. You won't see anything different happen in your terminal, though.

bff551a315b23d079d428c40bd9e30c93aa4257c.text: This release adds a second wave of in-assistant ad context that lets the ad system better understand what you are doing while you work, so it can surface more relevant sponsored content. The CLI now records when you are actively typing in the prompt box (only noting that you pressed a key and whether it was a deletion, not which key), when you have messages waiting in the queue, which tool the assistant called last, and whether a turn failed and how. After you click on a sponsored ad that promotes a developer tool, the assistant can watch your next install commands and report whether you installed the advertised package, sending only a yes/no plus a duration rather than the command text. Ads also get richer facts about your machine, such as screen size, OS version, CPU, memory, disk space, install age and runtime, plus your terminal dimensions and locale, all bucketed so no precise fingerprint can be derived. An ad-auction fetch and API round-trip timing are now measured, as are failures and idle time, and the whole client-context build guards each fact so a single broken source cannot take down an ad request. If the release evidence is incomplete, that is all the supported changes that can be described; no other capabilities are established by this release.

930cc4ed6f5dab71280f1516fa39ff9b5f47f5b5.title: CLI ad engagement adds checkpoint and late-click merge records
930cc4ed6f5dab71280f1516fa39ff9b5f47f5b5.summary: The CLI ad engagement registry gains checkpoints and late-click merge handling in `cli/src/ads/ad-engagement.ts`: a live impression now emits a checkpoint via `checkpoint()` (the record so far, no exit) when a transcript card leaves the viewport after being seen, or after `ENGAGEMENT_CHECKPOINT_MS` of exposure, whichever comes first, and a redraw of an already-flushed impression gets a click-only tracker that sends only `{ impUrl, click }` plus `postClick` so a late click still reaches the original record without overwriting the first click's features (the count grows instead). The `PartnerAdRow` component in `cli/src/components/partner-ad-line.tsx` is newly wired through `useAdEngagement` with placement: 'pinned', so partner rows now participate in that same registry alongside `AdCard`, and `cli/src/utils/exit-cleanly.ts` calls `flushAdEngagementOnExit()` from the shared exit path so any record that survived on a transcript card is sent as `window_close` on quit. A new `AdEngagementPoster` in `use-ad-engagement.ts` sequences per-impression POSTs with the later write winning on the server merge, and `ENGAGEMENT_CHECKPOINT_MS = 120_000` plus `MAX_CLICK_MEMO = 256` are the two new constants that gate the checkpoint timer and the clicked-impression memo.
930cc4ed6f5dab71280f1516fa39ff9b5f47f5b5.evidence: In `cli/src/ads/ad-engagement.ts`, `createEngagementRegistry.create` builds a click-only tracker via `createEngagementTracker({ clickOnly: { priorClick: clicks.get(impUrl) } })` when `mount` lands on an Impression already in finished, and the click-only `flush` path emits a `{ v, impUrl, click }` merge record through `sendLateClick`; `ENGAGEMENT_CHECKPOINT_MS = 120_000` and `MAX_CLICK_MEMO = 256` bound the checkpoint timer and the clicked-impression memo respectively; in `cli/src/components/partner-ad-line.tsx` the new `PartnerAdRow` component calls `useAdEngagement(ad.impUrl, { placement: 'pinned', truncated: layoutTruncated([ [ad.title, getPartnerLineLayout(ad, width).title], ]) }) and wires onClick`/`onHover into that tracker; in cli/src/utils/exit-cleanly.ts`, `createExitCliCleanly` pushes `Promise.resolve().then(deps.flushAdEngagement) into the exit cleanup list and the singleton supplies flushAdEngagement: () => flushAdEngagementOnExit() which calls live?.closeAll('window_close') followed by poster.settle()`.
930cc4ed6f5dab71280f1516fa39ff9b5f47f5b5.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side consumer of the checkpoint or click-only merge records, nor the rollout of the engagement POST endpoint changes.

930cc4ed6f5dab71280f1516fa39ff9b5f47f5b5.text: When you see a partner ad row in the CLI, like the one above the input or inside the /review menu, the assistant now records whether you scrolled it out of view before the ad finished and whether you clicked it after its first report already went out. You will not notice a new UI, but partner ad impressions and clicks are now tracked more accurately, including when the session ends.

65d7148584be4215bcb3154eea4884e851cd5602.title: Ad engagement records out and adoption release on checkpoint
65d7148584be4215bcb3154eea4884e851cd5602.summary: The engagement tracker now tracks a `recordOut` flag, marking it once the first record of any kind (a checkpoint, a late click, or a final flush) leaves for the impression, via a new `onRecordOut` callback threaded through `createEngagementTracker` and `createEngagementRegistry` and wired to `mainRecordSent` in the registry wiring. The adoption watcher's `status` check now releases a held `postClick` merge when the impression is recorded (a checkpoint has gone out), not only when it is `flushed`, so a `packageInstalled` adoption after a checkpoint sends at once. On CLI exit, `flushAdEngagement` is kicked off before the renderer unmounts the ad cards (so `closeAll` runs against `window_close`, not `unmount`) and its transport is awaited by the bounded remote cleanup. Tests assert checkpoint-once behavior, recorded status until flush, adoption-after-checkpoint sending, and that a throwing or unmounted ad flush never blocks exit.
65d7148584be4215bcb3154eea4884e851cd5602.evidence: In `cli/src/ads/ad-engagement.ts`, `createEngagementTracker` gains a `markRecordOut()` helper that sets `recordOut` and calls `onRecordOut` once from `sendCheckpoint`, `sendLateClick`, and `flush`; `EngagementTracker` exposes a new `recordOut` getter; `EngagementRegistryEnv` and `createEngagementTracker` options gain `onRecordOut`; and `createEngagementRegistry` threads `onRecordOut` from `status`. In `cli/src/ads/use-ad-engagement.ts`, `adEngagementRegistry` wires `onRecordOut` to `adoption?.mainRecordSent`. In `cli/src/utils/exit-cleanly.ts`, `flushAdEngagement` is started before the renderer teardown (`cleanupLocal`) and awaited within the bounded remote cleanup. In `cli/src/ads/ad-adoption.ts`, the `status` doc and `trySend` now treat recorded as a release state alongside `flushed`.
65d7148584be4215bcb3154eea4884e851cd5602.unknowns: The diff does not show whether `onRecordOut` consumers beyond the adoption watcher are registered, or how the `status` API is exposed to the hook or CLI surface.

65d7148584be4215bcb3154eea4884e851cd5602.text: When you click on an ad inside the Freebuff coding assistant and later install the advertised software, the assistant now reports that adoption to its server as soon as the first record about that ad has been saved, instead of waiting until you close the program. The change also reorders the exit steps so ad records are flushed before the on-screen ad cards are removed, and it makes that exit flushing never block or hang the program. This is internal reliability work for the ad-tracking plumbing (the audience is the Freebuff engineering team), and it does not change what ads you see, what you can install, or how your coding sessions work.

1b07c60e9fea2ac11adbaba285f8408efadaedd3.text: The testing system that compares two AI coding helpers against each other has gotten stricter and more resilient. When an AI is being graded on a coding task, the grader now breaks the AI's work into smaller pieces and prioritizes the most relevant parts first, so large changes don't overwhelm it. If the grading AI fails to respond once, the system now automatically retries instead of giving up. The grading prompt can also be resumed if a long run gets interrupted, letting it skip tasks that already finished. This is an internal quality-control tool for the Freebuff team to measure how their AI assistants perform, so everyday users won't notice anything different, but it means their test results will be more reliable and complete.

If you use the CLI normally, you might notice that the wallet consent flow during admission has been removed, and the model list ordering is now driven purely by the catalog discount prices.

701e755d067753d205fc4fe643bdeb60de1c3fe5.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Fast ships to the Freebuff model picker

135fb9e944505a0db8519b898a6f21a19b85a864.text: The team added a new on-off switch that keeps a faster DeepSeek model out of the model list shown on the web and in new app releases, while still letting the model run behind the scenes for people who already have full access. 4aa8cddb02b048cb52ea5c724c2f5146e834745e.title: Add picker sections file with model placement map
4aa8cddb02b048cb52ea5c724c2f5146e834745e.summary: A new module `common/src/util/freebuff-picker-sections.ts` defines the hosted model picker's three sections (Unlimited, Optimized, Powerful) with labels and tooltips, and a frozen placement map that pins each known model id to a section, order, and optional `more`/recommended flags. The exported `freebuffPickerPlacement` function resolves a row to its first placed id, otherwise infers the section from the fallback's `premium`/`locked`/`price` flags and tucks unknown rows under More. c3d72c61d37fd4193573c8facd2b9bdf892ad472.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.15 ships BYOK local connection-state safety in SDK
c3d72c61d37fd4193573c8facd2b9bdf892ad472.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.2.15 (package.json version bumped from 0.2.14 to 0.2.15) packages an SDK change that makes local BYOK connection failures safe to display. The new `ByokConnectionStateError` class in `sdk/src/byok.ts` now replaces the generic throws inside `parseConnections`, the `lookup` helper, the metadata `get` reader, and the `withLock` loop, so corrupt metadata, duplicate connections, a credential reference belonging to another connection, a removed or stale-revision connection, and a persistent lock each carry a fixed, SDK-authored message that names at most an environment-variable name and never a key value. In `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts`, `getModelForRequest` now imports `ByokConnectionStateError` and, in the BYOK `fetch` wrapper, checks the revision via `byok.assertCurrent?.()` and throws the state error's own message when present, while any other thrown error (custom resolvers and filesystem failures) is folded into the generic 'Could not verify the saved BYOK connection. Reselect the provider and retry...' message so credentials or paths cannot leak into provider dispatch.

c3d72c61d37fd4193573c8facd2b9bdf892ad472.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.15 makes your saved BYOK (bring-your-own-key) connections safer and clearer to manage, and gives Solar Pro 4 a temporary free promotion. When a saved custom-model connection can no longer be used locally (for example, it was changed, removed, or its shared settings file is corrupt or locked by another Freebuff process), the app now reports one of a fixed set of plain-language messages instead of falling back to a generic prompt, and it never sends you to talk to your provider when the problem lives on your computer. The one message shown depends on what actually broke: a changed connection asks you to pick the new revision, a removed one suggests picking another provider, a corrupt or unreadable file tells you to restore the settings, and a locked store tells you to close other Freebuff processes before retrying. If the failure mode is something the SDK does not recognize (anything that might carry private details like file paths or keys), it is masked behind a generic message telling you to reselect the provider, quit, and restart. Solar Pro 4 is now free to use as a temporary promotion, appears in the top "Unlimited" section of the model picker, and is clearly labeled as promotional so the price change is visible, not hidden.

f16c22ffd26f219ed99d694bce4fff84efeb4751.title: SDK stops retrying final refusals using status and error code
f16c22ffd26f219ed99d694bce4fff84efeb4751.summary: The BYOK model-provider retry path in the SDK now treats two refusals as final and non-retryable: the existing per-turn spend breaker (429 with the FREEBUFF_TURN_SPEND_LIMIT_ERROR_CODE error code) and a new session-superseded refusal (409 with the session_superseded error code). The old throwIfTurnSpendCapped check only matched 429 and only the spend-breaker error code, so clients retrying a capped turn saw the identical failure again; the new FINAL_REFUSALS table matches on both status and error code, then reads the body message when present or falls back to FREEBUFF_TURN_SPEND_LIMIT_MESSAGE and the session-end notice string. stream-interruption.ts classification of recovery paths is unchanged in mechanism, and the body-parsing branch that returns early on non-JSON bodies now feeds the same final-refusal predicate.
f16c22ffd26f219ed99d694bce4fff84efeb4751.evidence: sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts: the function throwIfTurnSpendCapped was renamed to throwIfFinalRefusal and now consults a FINAL_REFUSALS table that matches both status and error code; the table includes the existing 429/FREEBUFF_TURN_SPEND_LIMIT_ERROR_CODE spend breaker and a new 409/session_superseded gate sourced from FREEBUFF_GATE_CODES.session_superseded in @codebuff/common/types/freebuff-session.
f16c22ffd26f219ed99d694bce4fff84efeb4751.unknowns: Whether FREEBUFF_GATE_CODES.session_superseded.status resolves to 409 and whether any other gate codes are wired into FINAL_REFUSALS are implied by the import and table usage but not asserted in the file list. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

f16c22ffd26f219ed99d694bce4fff84efeb4751.text: The SDK now stops retrying two kinds of requests it can never recover from: when you hit your per-turn spending limit, and when your session has been replaced by another session. Previously, the system kept retrying the spending-limit refusal (an HTTP 429 tied to a specific spend-breaker error code) even though the exact same refusal would come back each time, giving the misleading impression of an ordinary rate limit. It now also recognizes 409 refusals marked with a session-superseded error code as final, so a replaced session ends cleanly instead of looping.

b1813969c4abf069b5c793cf86bdd0303d76234a.title: Terminal command broker adds temp-directory probing and empty-result
b1813969c4abf069b5c793cf86bdd0303d76234a.summary: The Windows one-shot command broker in cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts now exports probeTempDirectory, writeProtocolResponse and parseProtocol, and writes the protocol response with wx so a partial write on a full disk is removed rather than handed to JSON.parse. When the result file is empty or cut off, parseProtocol throws the INCOMPLETE_RESPONSE_MESSAGE ('terminal command broker returned an invalid response: the result file was empty or cut off') instead of a raw JSON parse error, and on a completion failure where the result was lost, createTerminalCommandBroker invokes the injected probeTempDir to append recovery guidance without surfacing a restart hint.
b1813969c4abf069b5c793cf86bdd0303d76234a.evidence: commit b1813969 modifies cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts, adding exports probeTempDirectory, writeProtocolResponse, parseProtocol, the INCOMPLETE_RESPONSE_MESSAGE constant, and the brokerFailure(tempDirectoryProblem) path; tests in cli/src/utils/__tests__/terminal-command-broker.test.ts assert the new empty/cut-off and full-temp-directory behaviors using fixtures/terminal-command-broker-empty-response.ts

b1813969c4abf069b5c793cf86bdd0303d76234a.text: When the CLI runs a command in the background on Windows, it writes the result to a temporary file instead of using direct pipes. If that temp file ends up empty or cut off because the temp directory is full, the CLI now detects it explicitly and tells you the temp directory is the problem, instead of surfacing a cryptic JSON parse error. It also probes the temp directory only when a command result is lost and appends recovery guidance suggesting you free up space or set a different temp folder, without asking you to restart. You keep the restart suggestion only when the temp directory is healthy and the result was lost for another reason. You do not need to do anything; this is a behind-the-scenes reliability fix for commands run through the Freebuff CLI on Windows.

3aecc760b7f2eb5b3f737c9b534697cd05b317a0.title: CLI loads OpenTUI renderer from config dir fallback and cleans temp
3aecc760b7f2eb5b3f737c9b534697cd05b317a0.summary: The CLI now calls `ensureRenderLibrary` before creating the OpenTUI renderer, so a temp directory that is full, read-only, or mounted noexec falls back to a content-addressed copy of the renderer installed in the CLI's own config directory (`native/` under `getConfigDir()`). If that fallback load also fails, the new `RenderLibraryLoadError` (thrown by `describeRenderLibraryFailure` after a `probeTempDirectory` check) names the offending temp directory and prints actionable remediation instead of the raw OpenTUI error. A deferred `sweepLeakedRenderLibraryCopies` pass deletes stale byte-identical copies Bun left in `bunExtractionTempDir()` (preferring `BUN_TMPDIR` over `TMPDIR`), reclaiming the 3.3 MB leak per launch on macOS arm64.
3aecc760b7f2eb5b3f737c9b534697cd05b317a0.evidence: New file `cli/src/utils/opentui-native-library.ts` defines `ensureRenderLibrary`, `installRenderLibrary`, `sweepLeakedRenderLibraryCopies`, and `bunExtractionTempDir`, and is imported in `cli/src/index.tsx` where `ensureRenderLibrary` is called before `createCliRenderer`, with `sweepLeakedRenderLibraryCopies` scheduled in a `setTimeout(0)`. `cli/src/types/env.ts` and `cli/src/utils/env.ts` add `BUN_TMPDIR` to the CLI env type and reader.
3aecc760b7f2eb5b3f737c9b534697cd05b317a0.unknowns: The change does not show whether the fatal-crash telemetry path has been wired to report the reason tag of `RenderLibraryLoadError` versus the previous `Failed to initialize OpenTUI render library` string, and no rollout flag gates the new behavior. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

3aecc760b7f2eb5b3f737c9b534697cd05b317a0.text: The Freebuff CLI now handles terminal rendering more reliably by first trying the normal startup path, and if that fails because the system's temporary folder is full, locked, or doesn't allow running programs, it installs a backup copy of the renderer into its own config folder and uses that instead. It also cleans up leftover copies of this renderer that each previous launch was secretly leaving behind in the temp folder, which on macOS was wasting about 3.3 megabytes per startup. Freebuff users on supported systems will either see a clear, actionable error message explaining exactly what to fix if all loading attempts fail, or otherwise notice no difference on typical machines where the temp folder works normally.

7f957e9d65768a7b5bfd994df8d7eac8891bbfb2.text: Solar Pro 4 has returned to the list of AI models you can choose from in Freebuff, rejoining Solar Mini 4 on September 25. You can now pick Solar Pro 4 in both full and limited access tiers, where it is available at no cost for full-access users and priced at 10 Freebucks for others. This gives you access to a larger, more capable model from Upstage alongside the faster, lighter option, adding more choice to your daily coding sessions without changing your existing settings or limits.

c3d72c61d37fd4193573c8facd2b9bdf892ad472.text: Solar Pro 4 is now available for free as a temporary promotion in the Unlimited section of the model picker. When using a personal API provider, errors about local connection problems now display specific, safe messages instead of generic failures. The release improves how your project instruction files are recognized by the AI to avoid conflicts. Two other updates in this version are not described here because the release notes were incomplete.

701e755d067753d205fc4fe643bdeb60de1c3fe5.text: Freebuff now offers a fast mode for its DeepSeek model that splits coding work across multiple assistants running at once, which is available only to users with full access. When prices are higher during peak hours, the model picker now shows you exactly when the cheaper rate resumes so you can choose to wait. This new option and pricing notice appear in the English and Chinese documentation and the terminal interface for users with full access; users in limited regions or without full access do not see this model.

3b7ce89c8102761014eafbe97cced66d9a22ec88.text: Freebuff now includes OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol in its list of available AI models for coding and research tasks. This new option is free for users in the United States, while users in other countries must have a paid subscription to access it. For everyone, the model carries a temporary promotional price, which the interface highlights with a badge so you know the cost is not permanent.

e4a960f781aeb3023a406e4990b741212d0cafce.text: Version 0.1.0 of the free coding assistant adds two new types of in-terminal advertisements. The first is a single line of text in a specific brand color that appears above your typing area if you mention pull requests, merges, or reviews in your draft; it also appears below the review command when that menu is open. The second update corrects the promotional ads for paid subscriptions to accurately describe the daily and monthly usage limits, using clear time-based units instead of vague numbers. To prevent these ad sections from cluttering your screen, they automatically hide if your terminal is too narrow to display them legibly or if you are in the middle of another action like a form or a help menu. The release also adjusts an internal database health warning threshold from 1 million to 10 million transactions, which reduces false alarm notifications for the service operators. Finally, the test scripts have been updated to recognize the assistant's new start-up screen, which now opens directly into a chat prompt rather than a traditional model picker.

95ecda2ed3026dfa12214335ce0a2b6f4732208d.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.14 adds DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Fast to the free model picker for full-access users, enabling a coding mode that splits large tasks across multiple parallel helper agents to handle many files at once. The model picker now groups available AI models into three clear categories (Unlimited, Optimized, Powerful) instead of a single flat list, making it easier to see what each model is for. The file-finding helper agents that support the main coding agent now run on GPT-6 Luna instead of a Gemini model, improving how the assistant locates relevant files in your code. When a paid plan is paused due to a failed payment, the CLI now displays a clear warning with a link to update your card so you know why your plan is not active. When you are paying for a model at peak hours, the model picker now shows you when the cheaper off-peak price will resume so you can decide whether to wait. Note that the server-side switch to make DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Fast live for all users is currently off, so it is only available on client builds that include the new code and are connected to a server that has the switch enabled.

bff551a315b23d079d428c40bd9e30c93aa4257c.title: Freebuff 0.2.13 ships ad engagement and adoption tracking
bff551a315b23d079d428c40bd9e30c93aa4257c.summary: Freebuff CLI version 0.2.13 introduces post-click adoption tracking and expanded ad client context signals for the terminal. The release adds a new module, cli/src/ads/ad-adoption.ts, which monitors agent shell commands for package installations matching a clicked ad vendor and reports a boolean adoption flag. The ad client context in cli/src/ads/ad-client-context.ts is extended with new telemetry buckets for system resources, app metadata, typing behavior, and network latency to enrich advertiser training features. These changes are wired into the engagement registry and auction request flow to provide richer client-side signals without altering core agent logic.

bff551a315b23d079d428c40bd9e30c93aa4257c.text: Freebuff 0.2.13 adds detailed tracking of how users interact with ads and the assistant, capturing data such as typing patterns, tool usage, and system performance to improve advertising models. The update introduces a post-click adoption watch that monitors whether the assistant installs a package from a vendor whose ad was just clicked, recording the event without storing the raw command. Additional system metrics, including CPU load, memory usage, disk space, and network latency, are now gathered as coarse buckets to contextualize the user's environment. The release also refines the skill registry to distinguish between a successful load with zero skills and a failed load. These changes focus on enriching the data available for ad engagement analysis while ensuring no raw or identifying information leaves the machine.

0cb910451c1b774876b017cf60f059ed6e9f2e82.text: This release adds the Space Bunny Alpha model to the limited-access free tier, making it available to users in regions with restricted access or those using a VPN. The daily streak bonus for Freebuff now counts days based on your local timezone rather than Pacific time, so your rewards reset at your local midnight instead of a fixed server time. The Desktop app now supports full-screen image ad placements called billboards in the sidebar and right panel, which display visual creative from advertisers. Windows users will notice improved detection for Git and Bash tools, allowing the assistant to find these programs even if they are not added to your system path. Several retired AI models, including MiniMax M3, have been fully removed from the free service, and users attempting to access them will be prompted to update their app. The release also includes an internal test for a new ad-ranking experiment that sorts sponsored content based on pre-calculated user preferences, though this feature is not yet active for users.

03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.11 release with deferred update adoption
03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.summary: Freebuff CLI release 0.2.11 ships a launcher mechanism to adopt staged updates that previous sessions failed to install due to terminal closure or file locks. The launcher now writes a `staged.json` manifest with SHA256 hashes for downloaded binaries and Tree-Sitter WASM files during the deferral window. On subsequent startup, `adoptOrphanedStagedUpdates` scans the configuration directory for staging directories owned by dead processes, verifies file integrity against the manifest, and installs the update before spawning the main binary. This prevents users from being stuck on outdated builds when they close the terminal window instead of exiting the CLI gracefully.

c5c0acc93f8fec48e0f7f78c536c4ed6dea74a2c.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.7 ships followup nudge, streak time label, and image
c5c0acc93f8fec48e0f7f78c536c4ed6dea74a2c.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.2.7 packages three changes spanning the agent runtime, shared core, and CLI. The agent runtime now checks the agent's to-do list when a turn ends on `suggest_followups` and nudges the model to continue if tasks remain open, bounded by `MAX_FOLLOWUP_TODO_NUDGES`. In the shared core, `getFreebuffModelImageSupport` now consults `getFreebuffModelPolicyOverlay` to resolve multimodal capability for server-only catalog models, preventing raw image data from reaching text-only upstreams. The CLI streak status line labels clock times with "(your time)" to disambiguate reader-local reset hours from server time, falling back to a compact label when terminal width is constrained.

Member 86909c74 adds `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/followup-todo-nudge.ts` and modifies `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` to invoke `decideFollowupTodoNudge`. Member 79da3da8 modifies `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` in `getFreebuffModelImageSupport` to consult `getFreebuffModelPolicyOverlay`.

dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.9: SDK DNS pinning, landing ads, and sponsored git

Additionally, sponsored run command refusals now fail closed on deep wrapper nesting and judge git subcommands to prevent history-moving operations.

03df0d8b1f0fb0d9a00ec7994c4eb57f3fc516cc.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.11 ensures you no longer stay on an outdated version if you quit the app by closing your terminal window instead of typing an exit command. When a new update was ready but the terminal closed, the program previously left the new files sitting in a temporary folder that no one would ever install. This version now checks for those leftover updates at your next startup and installs them, so you receive the latest features without manually waiting for the update to finish. If the install cannot complete because the files are locked by your computer, the program saves its progress so you do not have to download the update all over again on your next launch. Additionally, the release includes new internal tests to confirm that external coding tools receive the correct instructions on how to send their required settings, preventing errors when those tools run.

dfec4965e1fca35dbd60e69e1ce8d3f2ac90a605.text: Freebuff 0.2.9 tightens security protections across its CLI and developer tools. The URL reading feature now locks each connection to a specific address verified in the same step, blocking a trick that could swap a safe address for an unsafe one, and adds four more private network ranges to its blocklist. Sponsored tasks that run on your machine have stricter command checks: they now block shell tricks that hide or obfuscate destructive actions, block specific Git commands that move history, and fail safely if a command is too complex to verify. Terminal output is sanitized before display to strip hidden control codes that could change your clipboard or window. The Freebuff landing screen shows ads only when your terminal window is tall enough to display them, avoiding wasted data. Finally, the developer SDK no longer includes source maps, keeping the underlying source code out of the published package.

05b8302ce19e998ea16f2f38c400c62c94d974b7.text: The free coding assistant now includes its next update for people who use the free terminal, web, or desktop versions. This routine step keeps the tool current with the latest fixes and improvements from the recent development cycle. There is no new visible feature, setting change, or action required for you to install this version; it simply marks the next available release.

c5c0acc93f8fec48e0f7f78c536c4ed6dea74a2c.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.7 stops the AI assistant from ending a task prematurely when you have unfinished to-do items, and adds a label to time-based streak messages so you know they refer to your local clock. If the assistant pauses to show follow-up options while your personal task list is half done, the system now nudges it back to continue the work instead of making you type 'continue' manually, up to three times per request. For users with a 7+ day streak earning Freebucks, the status message under the perk note now explicitly adds '(your time)' next to odd-hour reset times (like 3:00 PM tomorrow) to clarify that it is your local time, not server time. In narrow terminal windows, this label is dropped to keep the line from wrapping, but the message itself remains visible. The release also fixes a crash where text-only models were receiving image data they could not process, causing entire conversation threads to fail when screenshots were replayed later in the chat.

055e9c3cd792ca332c6838f1f47c12415c638f54.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.5 release

The verification path displays an ID verification message without a reset time, while the spend-limited path retains the existing midnight Pacific reset notice.

055e9c3cd792ca332c6838f1f47c12415c638f54.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.5 introduces a new ID verification requirement for some accounts and improves how the app handles login errors. When your account needs identity verification, the app now shows a clear notice with a link to complete that step, instead of displaying a generic daily limit message. To prevent the app from filling up its error log with thousands of duplicate lines, it now records each login failure only once. The app also tightens security on the file that stores your login details, making sure only you can read it on non-Windows systems.

44c800d2617286631654dfd4d3c7b2b0e8e4d6b4.text: The default AI model for Freebuff has changed to MiMo 2.6 Flash, which balances performance with image support and costs 10 Freebucks per hour, while GLM 5.3 Flash remains the cheapest option at 5 Freebucks per hour. Users in limited access regions now see a wider selection of models, including those that require a paid plan, which appear locked until a plan is purchased. The CLI now signs network requests with a unique security key generated on your device, ensuring that only your specific installation can access your account's model catalog. This security measure prevents other users from reusing your access credentials and ensures that model requests are tied to your individual device.

985c872eb8d43f538ab77d933ef7c43125d100ff.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.3 with history navigation from recalled draft

8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.summary: The `FreebuffSessionAdmissionResponse` in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` now carries three new optional fields: `verificationCanChangeAccess`, `verificationReason`, and `countryUpsell`. These fields let the server tell the client whether a country-verification prompt is still useful for this account and, when it is not, offer a paid-plan upsell built from the server's catalog. A new type `FreebuffPlanUpsell` defines the shape of that offer, including the recommended plan, its daily Freebucks, and a `plansUrl` tagged for attribution.

8067376238835ba774fd0a5f761ff1c298f1711f.text: The Freebuff CLI now fetches its list of available AI models directly from the server, meaning new models can appear and prices can change without waiting for a software update. If a model you saved previously has been replaced by a server-managed version, the app automatically links your saved choice to the new one so your preference is preserved. For users in regions where Freebuff offers limited access, the app now shows why verifying your location will not unlock more features and offers specific paid plan details to help you decide on an upgrade. Finally, your login security token is now stored in your operating system's secure credential vault instead of a plain text file, reducing the risk that other programs on your computer could read it.

985c872eb8d43f538ab77d933ef7c43125d100ff.text: The Freebuff CLI now lets you keep paging through your previous commands after you have recalled one from history, instead of switching to text editing the moment the field is filled. Previously, once a remembered command was loaded into the text box, the up and down arrow keys moved your cursor within that text rather than showing older or newer history items. Now, as long as you have not typed new characters or moved the cursor yourself, the arrow keys continue to step back and forth through your history list. This applies to both normal command history and terminal command history. The release evidence covers only this specific navigation behavior; one additional change was omitted because its summary failed verification.

5d02de3e8d4e79daafd09162f66356696ce4d15a.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.16 enables fast mode for users and improves how the terminal interface loads on your computer. The release activates a new fast mode option on the server, making it visible in model pickers for users with full access, while keeping the underlying technology ready for other clients. To fix a startup crash that occurred when a computer's temporary folder was full or blocked from running programs, the tool now saves a backup copy of its visual components in a dedicated settings folder and automatically cleans up old leftover files. Additionally, when the system cannot record the results of a command due to storage issues, it now gives a clear, specific error message instead of failing silently, and stops repeating identical requests that the server has explicitly refused. The 'base2' agent definitions were updated to display human-readable model names in prompts, and a new test suite ensures that every agent definition shipped with the tool remains valid even when custom user agents are present, preventing the entire interface from freezing.

64e8d89a859503189b368484b0a43f37db4a1d11.text: Freebuff now sends a compact, privacy-conscious description of your terminal environment and typing habits to the server, and it provides clearer guidance when a model blocks a request for cybersecurity reasons. The client reports details like which terminal you use and whether you are running inside a secure shell, but it shares only fixed labels and counts, never your actual prompts or file paths. It also tracks how you typed your last message (such as the number of characters you typed versus pasted) to help the service understand usage patterns. If a model refuses to process a request because it flagged the content as a potential cybersecurity risk, the assistant now explains that retrying the same conversation on that specific model will fail and suggests switching to a different model instead.

e675e2ef35e2b55f3338ee522fb12cfd263470d9.text: This update adjusts how free compute credits are tracked and adds a new question to the new-user setup. The reasoning depth for the Muse Spark and Gemini 3.8 Flash AI models has been capped to manage cost and speed, and GPT-6 Luna now runs without its top reasoning level. GPT-6.1 Sol is currently available at a temporary promotional price. A new option to shuffle survey answers was added for setup questions about user roles, projects, and subscriptions.

2cde35ae5aa49b2646042d97c6d7113102d1836e.text: This release clarifies error messages for your own AI provider connections so you understand exactly what went wrong. If your saved model name is not listed by your server, the tool now shows the available names immediately. You can also change which variable holds your security key when updating a connection's address, preventing the key from being sent to a new server by accident. If your daily limit for a model is reached, the tool now stops the session instead of switching you to a different model. Finally, the tool can now recover from broken multi-line pastes when you enter provider setup commands.

e99feb7a839f91163e4dae51c0ab017b40f82563.text: This release protects your files from being accidentally damaged if the AI's response gets cut short. It includes two new checks: if a file edit is cut off, the program now refuses to apply it rather than saving a broken version. It also recognizes when an AI command is incomplete and stops it instead of trying to guess the missing parts. If these checks trigger, you will see a message explaining that nothing was written to your files, so your work remains exactly as it was before the attempt.

f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.title: Freebuff CLI 0.1.10 adds subscription MRR and billing cadence types
f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.summary: This release bumps the Freebuff CLI version to 0.1.10. It adds shared subscription-cadence helpers and types that power the admin subscription dashboard. The change includes two distinct additions in the shared constants and types, plus the release manifest bump. In `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts`, `freebuffSubscriptionBillingInterval` maps the free-text `billing_interval` column to `monthly` or `yearly`, and `freebuffSubscriptionMrrUsd` computes monthly recurring revenue per subscriber by dividing yearly plans by 12 and returning 0 for grants or unknown tiers.
f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.evidence: Diff in `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts` adds `freebuffSubscriptionBillingInterval` and `freebuffSubscriptionMrrUsd`; `common/src/types/subscription-costs.ts` adds `SubscriptionBillingIntervals`; `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumps version to 0.1.10.
f8c7a1ad8f21d84791d5bfd94277c937aa6d9f3f.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side admin endpoint that consumes `SubscriptionBillingIntervals` or `freebuffSubscriptionMrrUsd`.

changes.what: Adds billing interval normalization and MRR calculation helpers for subscription tiers
Adds `SubscriptionBillingIntervals` type for admin dashboard aggregation by billing cadence
Bumps Freebuff CLI release version from 0.1.9 to 0.1.10

afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.title: GPT-6.1 Sol added with daily session cap and release 0.1.9
afe1bfdf35f46fa3a26160855494e968ed5420c7.summary: GPT-6.1 Sol is added to the free model picker as a paid-only row with a one-per-day session limit enforced by `FREEBUFF_DAILY_SESSION_LIMITS`. New agent definitions `base3-free-gpt-6-1-sol` and `base2-free-gpt-6-1-sol` are registered in the CLI and Web surfaces to support the model, along with a dedicated code reviewer. The Freebuff CLI release manifest is bumped to 0.1.9 to package these changes.

The release members include `common/src/constants/freebuff-sol-promo.ts` which introduces `GPT_61_SOL_MODEL_ID` and `FREEBUFF_DAILY_SESSION_LIMITS`, and `agents/base3-free-gpt-6-1-sol.ts` which adds a new agent definition.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.title: CLI partner ads gain a launch-intent composer row
f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.1.8 adds a second partner ad slot, `CLI-Partner-Composer-Launch`, that triggers when the user's draft mentions launch-related keywords instead of pull-request terms. The change splits the previous `showComposerPartnerAd` gate into a shared `composerPartnerRowAllowed` check and a placement selection that prioritizes PR intent over launch intent so a draft about both still shows the PR slot. Four other changes are bundled in this release, including removal of the tier-change notice and Muse Spark OpenRouter routing constants.

f93daaf339a2cd84e01d8695bd8e091a6d2dc0ad.unknowns: The diff does not show which advertiser is currently contracted to the launch-intent slot.

Exports `LAUNCH_INTENT_KEYWORDS` and `mentionsLaunchKeyword` alongside the existing PR trigger
Registers the two new launch-intent partner slots in the placement catalog with labels

38cd1ed44428f573c4754d8e0cee868f2875b54e.title: Move CLI claim prefix to shared constants for version 0.0.204
38cd1ed44428f573c4754d8e0cee868f2875b54e.summary: Release 0.0.204 centralizes the Freebuff CLI purchase-protocol identity by moving the `'cli:'` instance prefix into `common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts` as `FREEBUFF_CLI_CLAIM_PREFIX`. The CLI package now imports this shared constant instead of maintaining a local duplicate in `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-identity.ts`. This ensures the server and client use the same prefix to distinguish CLI execution claims from Desktop tabs under the versioned opt-in single-use protocol. Three file changes support this release, covering the constant definition, its CLI consumer, and the packaging manifest bump.
38cd1ed44428f573c4754d8e0cee868f2875b54e.evidence: In `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-identity.ts`, the local constant `CLI_MULTI_SESSION_PREFIX` is replaced by an import of `FREEBUFF_CLI_CLAIM_PREFIX` from `@codebuff/common/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions`. The constant `FREEBUFF_CLI_CLAIM_PREFIX` (value `'cli:'`) and the helper `isFreebuffCliClaim` are added to `common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts` in the same commit, and `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumps the version from 0.0.203 to 0.0.204.
38cd1ed44428f573c4754d8e0cee868f2875b54e.unknowns: The diff does not show if `isFreebuffCliClaim` is consumed by server-side logic in this snapshot, only that it is exported for future or external use.
